The essential message of the Lord’s teaching is that devotion from the heart of the spiritual master, in the form of transcendental knowledge, enters the heart of a devotee, wherein it manifests as faith and further activates the internally existing bhakti.This transfer of devotion from guruto disciple is known as gifting the seed of the creeper of devotion.

The Lord continues:

*mali hana kare sei bija aropana*  
*sravana-kirtana-jale karaye secana*

**“When a person receives the seed of devotional service, he should take care of it by becoming a gardener and sowing the seed in his heart. If he waters the seed gradually by the process of sravanaand kirtana\[hearing and chanting\], the seed will begin to sprout.”**

We now call the reader’s attention to the following:

When the process of chanting and hearing about Krsna waters that seed, bhaktiproportionately spreads its influence throughout the devotee’s body, empowering his acts with devotion. The effect of bhaktiupon the sincere devotee’s senses is to spiritualise them and cause them to attain a qualitative oneness, tad-bhavaor tadat-myam, with bhakti’s nature. In this way corporeal activities done for Krsna become devotional service.

Copper wire is transformed by the electricity it conducts; similarly, the activities of a practitioner are made spiritual by the strength of his devotion. The transformation brought about in a devotee's body and mind has already been explained in relation to the spiritualisation of karma,offences, and false ego. However, we should note that the effectiveness of spiritualisation is dependent on the strength of a practitioner’s faith; there is a proportional relationship between the two. Lord Krsna explains this to Brahma:

*dharman anyan parityajya*  
*mam ekam bhaja visvasan*  
*yadrsi yadrsi sraddha*  
*siddhir bhavati tadrsi*

**“Abandoning all meritorious performances, serve Me with faith. The realisation will correspond to the nature of one’s faith.”**

The arguments above were in response to the first doubt about the definition of sadhanawhich was: how spiritual bhaktiis generated by physical actions. In summary our answer is:

**Bhaktiis not generated by physical acts. Rather, a devotee’s senses and activities are surcharged with the devotion radiating from his heart, and it is that devotion which transforms activities into devotional service in proportion to the nature of the practitioner’s faith.**

\* \* \* \*

While we have shown how bhakticorrelates to a devotee’s acts of devotion, we have yet to answer the question how those acts generate bhava.We shall give our response in this section.

The principle of bhaktya sanjataya bhaktya,when applied to the question of how sadhanacauses bhava,can be understood by a phenomena known as circular causality. In essence, circular causality is known as:

The mutual interaction of cause and effect.

More explicitly, it is a link between a cause and its effect, in which the effect circles back to reinforce the cause. In the ideal, circular causality represents perpetual motion.

Applied to how sadhana-bhaktigenerates bhava-bhakti,circular causality looks like this:

**The operative cause bhakti,received from the guru, awakens eternal bhaktiin the disciple’s heart, which as the immediate cause inspires an effect in the form of the devotee’s acts of sadhana-bhaktithat are further energised by bhaktifrom the devotee’s heart.**  
**This bhaktias effect then feeds back to further purify the sadhaka’sheart, increasing the flow of bhaktiin the form of cause, which then inspires more significant bhaktieffects in the form of bhakti-imbued acts of devotion. This cycle of bhaktiin the heart causing bhakti-saturated acts to release increased bhakti from the heart, eventually leads to the awakening of bhava-bhakti,which then becomes the cause of bhava- inspired acts. These activities of bhava-bhaktifeed back and cultivate bhavawhich in a similar way quickly awakens premaand its acts of devotion, thus perpetuating a circular causality of bhakti,ad infinitum.**

So, to the doubt that questions how the physical activities of sadhanacan generate transcendental bhava-bhakti,the summary response is:

**The dynamic of circular causality enables bhavato be awakened, not by the physical acts of sadhana-bhakti, but by the devotion that is inherent in and inspires those acts.**

The presentation above may require patience and attentive reading. However, upon careful introspection a devotee will see how it, too, is in conformity with the axiom, bhaktya sahjataya bhaktya.

It is understandable that a new devotee does not immediately understand the process of the circular causality inherent in sadhana.He will be unaware that devotional service can only be performed by spiritual senses and that such devotion has descended upon him by the mercy of guruand Krsna. Instead, a neophyte devotee generally thinks that bhaktiis a product of his corporeal or mental activities, the external functions of his material body.

Sanatana Gosvami suggests that this belief in a beginner need not be discouraged. By thinking, “My own tongue is vibrating the names of God and my own ears are hearing them,” a devotee develops faith and thus gradually surrenders his independence. By the association of saints, the neophyte eventually realises that devotional activities like sankirtanaare simply the expressions of the Lord’s mercy on him, mercy manifest through the agency of Krsna’s own *bhakti-sakti*.

Thus the devotion-saturated acts and thoughts of a sadhaka gradually purify the heart, remove obstacles to pure devotion, and allow the purely transcendental nature of ecstatic devotion to manifest its full power.

In our arguments above we have highlighted the way a sadhaka’s devotion transforms his acts to sadhanaand how that sadhana awakens bhava.There are, however, other sources of bhaktiin addition to the practitioner’s that contribute to these processes. The spiritual master and the Supreme Lord continue to shower the sincere devotee with their bhakti-sakti.

How the Lord, for example, is further involved in this process, manifesting His mercy in response to the effort of the sadhaka,is one of the first truths spoken of in Srimad-Bhagavatam:

*srnvatam sva-kathah krsnah*  
*punya-sravana-kirtanah*  
*hrdy antah stho by abhadrani*  
*vidhunoti suhrt satam*

**“Sri Krsna, the Personality of Godhead, who is the Paramatma \[Supersoul\] in everyone’s heart and the benefactor of the truthful devotee, cleanses desire for material enjoyment from the heart of the devotee who has developed the urge to hear His messages, which are in themselves virtuous when properly heard and chanted.”**

In this way, although devotional service can be performed only with spiritual senses, a conditioned soul becomes qualified for bhaktiby the mercy of Krsna and His servants. And by that same mercy a practitioner eventually becomes sufficiently purified to begin transcendental hearing and chanting of the names and pastimes of the Lord.

Having thus attained the stage of bhava,a devotee’s body becomes completely spiritualised; thus, almost like the residents of Vaikuntha, his limbs and senses are of the same spiritual quality as pure devotion. We say that the body of a pure devotee in the material world is “almost” like that of devotees in Vaikuntha, because in the material world material bodies are spiritualised, whereas in Vaikuntha bodies are purely spiritual.

At the stage of ecstatic devotion, the circular causality of bhaktya sanjataya bhaktyais highly accelerated, and spiritual advancement very rapid. And, after attaining the transcendental abode of the Lord, a devotee fully realises the wonderful nature and variegatedness of devotional service. Situated in his eternal constitutional position, a devotee enters into an endless cycle of spiritual growth in which devotional acts cause the further development of bhakti,giving ever-increasing pleasure to both Krsna and His servant.

Thus we have responded to the challenges of how corporeal acts of sadhanacan be called devotion and how they can awaken bhava.While the answers above are conclusive, our arguments can be clarified further by viewing them from a different perspective. The following chapter is dedicated to further substantiating Rupa Gosvami’s definition of sadhana-bhakti.

\* \* \* \*

In the following section we shall review the stages of sadhana-bhaktiand examine how and to what degree bhava,ecstatic devotion, is invoked at each stage. Keeping in mind the circular causality described earlier, we shall now see that the kindling of the fire of bhavatakes force at ruci,and even more so at asakti.

In the gradual development of bhakti,starting with faith and concluding in love, sadhana-bhaktistarts at the stage of bhajana-kriya.Only after the seed of devotion is planted within the heart, and the company of pure devotees reinforces faith in the truths of bhakti,can a person earnestly embark upon the path of practice.

That path, however, is not without its obstacles. Reactions to past sinful and pious acts, as well as the reactions to offences against bhaktiand the holy name, make a devotee’s initial efforts unsteady. This unsteadiness is characterised by struggling with uncontrolled senses, difficulty in upholding vows, and an artificial show of self-confidence. It is also visible through symptoms like distraction during bhajanaand attraction to bad habits. In Madhurya-kadambini,Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura describes six kinds of unsteady practice, anistha-bhajana-kriya,and their five visible symptoms.

Only the association of pure devotees and the guidance of spiritual masters keeps an unsteady devotee on the path of bhajana, a path that sometimes feels to him like crossing a stormy ocean in a rowboat. Yet the power of the nine limbs of devotion—or even the power of just one—shines through the clouds of unwanted habits to gradually dissipate a practitioner’s troubles. Caitanya Mahaprabhu says,

*sadhu-sanga haite haya ‘sravana-kirtana’*  
*sadhana-bhaktye haya ‘sarvanartha-nivartana’*

**“When one is encouraged in devotional service by the association of devotees, one becomes free from all unwanted contamination by following the regulative principles, and chanting and hearing.”**

When disturbances caused by piety, sin, and errors in bhaktiare completely extinguished, and the majority of offences to the name are subjected to systematic eradication, at that time devotional practice becomes steady. This steady devotional service is known as nistha-bhajana-kriya,or nistha.

The above-mentioned stepwise development of devotional service is described as anistha-bhajana-kriya, anartha-nivrtti, and nistha-bhajana-kriya.Visvanatha CakravartI Thakura cites Srimad-Bhagavatamin support of this sequence:

*srnvatam sva-kathah krsnah*  
*punya-sravana-kirtanah*  
*hrdy antah stho hy abhadrani*  
*vidhunoti suhrt satam*

*nasta-prayesv abhadresu*  
*nityam bhagavata-sevaya*  
*bhagavaty uttama-sloke*  
*bhaktir bhavati naisthiki*

“Sri Krsna, the Personality of Godhead, Who is the Paramatma \[Supersoul\] in everyone’s heart and the benefactor of the truthful devotee, cleanses desire for material enjoyment from the heart of the devotee who has developed the urge to hear His messages, which are in themselves virtuous when properly heard and chanted.  
By regular attendance in classes on the Bhagavatamand by rendering of service to the pure devotee, all that is troublesome to the heart is almost completely destroyed, and loving service unto the Personality of Godhead, Who is praised with transcendental songs, is established as an irrevocable fact.”

The desirability of steadiness is in its consistency to purify the practitioner through devotional activities performed by the mind, body, and tongue—especially through nama-sankirtana.Meanwhile, the liability of residual offences to the holy name results in a devotee’s concentrated efforts focusing more on removing obstacles than tasting the ecstasy of the holy name. Sukadeva Gosvami explains how offences obstruct tasting the sweetness of Krsna’s names:

*tad asma-saram hrdayam batedam*  
*yad grhyamanair hari-nama-dheyaih*  
*na vikriyetatha yada vikaro*  
*netre jalam gatra-ruhesu harsah*

**“Certainly that heart is steel-framed which, in spite of one’s chanting the holy name of the Lord with concentration, does not change when ecstasy takes place, tears fill the eyes, and the hairs stand on end.”**

Although a steady devotee only occasionally experiences attachment and ecstasy, in time his resolute efforts are rewarded by the appearance of taste, ruci.Lord Caitanya says, nistha haite sravanadye‘ruci’ upajaya:

**“When firm faith in devotional service awakens, a taste for hearing and chanting also awakens.”**

In the devotee’s journey to bhava,the devotional stage of ruciis significant in many ways.

With this attainment, inner purification frees a devotee from all unwanted things other than obstacles arising from offences. Indeed, rucihas such force that reactions to nama-aparadha,in their entirety, are subjected to eradication. The result is an extraordinary relish for hearing and chanting, a relish that dwarfs the taste for anything else. It can be said that a devotee who has risen to this stage of devotion becomes addicted to the practice of devotional service, as a result of which he is freed of fear, lamentation, and illusion.

One may argue that attention to bhaktiat nisthais already unflinching. However, attention at ruciis different, and that difference is found in the underlying cause of ruci.

At steadiness, a devotee is generally attentive in order to free himself from obstacles to attaining bhava.Such motivation, however, is a characteristic of regulated devotion and so does not yet reflect the spontaneity characteristic of pure love—indeed, it restricts it.

By contrast, at taste, natural attraction for hearing, chanting, and remembering are a devotee’s motivation, a motivation that is also the primary characteristic of bhakti,its svarupa-laksana.Thus at taste, a devotee’s attention is not only natural, but also the unequivocal sign of the dawn of bhava-bhakti.

As with every stage of devotion, taste is realised in varying degrees. When ruciattains a substantial depth, a wonderful transition takes place: the object of one’s attraction shifts from bhajana to Krsna.

That transition heralds the next stage of devotion called attachment, or asakti.Whereas at rucithe inspiration for bhakticame from the acts of devotion, at asaktiinspiration comes primarily from the object of devotion, and secondarily from devotional practices. Lord Kapila describes asaktiin this way:

*cetah khalv asya bandhaya*  
*muktaye catmano matam*  
*gunesu saktam bandhaya*  
*ratam va pumsi muktaye*

**“The stage in which the consciousness of the living entity is attracted by the three modes of material nature is called conditional life. But when that same consciousness is attached to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, one is situated in the consciousness of liberation.”**

As mentioned previously, the original gift of bhaktiis received by a devotee in the form of the seed of the creeper of devotion. That seed, which is cultivated through subsequent stages of sadhana-bhakti,is also known as the seed of affection because it is the original source of transcendental emotion that is known as bhavaor rati.The Supreme Lord comes under the control of such affection.

When devotion is raised to the stage of asaktiit becomes especially glorious, for it hints at the transcendental attachment that will soon appear at bhava.In other words, at attachment the seed of ecstatic devotion begins to sprout, and as it does, it signals the divine transformations that take place at the subsequent stage of ecstasy. Lord Caitanya says, asakti baite citte janme krsne prity-ankura:

**“From that attachment the seed of love for Krsna grows in the heart.”**

Attachment may be regulated, spontaneous, or a combination of the two. However, the stage of asaktiis certainly favourable soil in which to cultivate a natural inner attraction for following the residents of Vraja, while simultaneously conducting oneself externally as a neophyte. If truth be told, such attachment is like a forceful river that sweeps the mind of the practitioner away from material thoughts, while simultaneously polishing the recesses of the heart.

As attachment intensifies, so too does a devotee’s desire to serve Krsna in one of the five mellows of devotional service. And because Krsna comes under the control of such devotion, the seed of love, bhavankura,blossoms by Krsna’s grace, making itself known in the form of bhava.

The indication that the seed of transcendental emotion has matured within a devotee’s heart will be visible in his conduct. A devotee’s disposition will then be characterised by nine symptoms, such as detachment, an absence of false prestige, and care that time is never wasted.

The grace that makes the seed of attachment blossom generally manifests through a Vaisnava or Vaisnavas. The traditional understanding of the followers of Srimad-Bhagavatamis this:

Just as one receives the seed of the creeper of devotion from a devotee, similarly one advances through every stage of Krsna consciousness by the grace of devotees.

Caitanya Mahaprabhu says,

*krsna-bhakti-janma-mula haya ‘sadhu-sanga’*  
*krsna-prema janme, tenho punah mukhya anga*

**“The root cause of devotional service to Lord Krsna is association with advanced devotees. Even when one’s dormant love for Krsna awakens, association with devotees is still most essential.”**

In summary, the purification of unwanted things in the heart takes place through assiduous chanting and hearing of Krsna’s names, qualities, and pastimes. Bhaktivinoda Thakura calls anartha-nivrtti the “test of the development of devotional service” and the “preliminary symptom” of the awakening of love.

Freedom from gross material contamination leads to firm faith, which in turn allows one to scientifically scrutinise the truths of devotion and the means to attain them. Nisthais also the inspiration that nurtures the progressive desire for ecstatic devotion. Through nama-sankirtana,a steady devotee manifests a partial token of bhavain the form of taste, and the subsequent fondness for devotional service helps his bhaktimature into attachment. At asaktithe seed of bhavais fully present in the heart, its influence visible in a devotee’s eagerness for Krsna and in his saintly conduct. That seed of bhavaneeds only the touch of transcendence to make it sprout, a divine intercession made possible by the grace of Krsna, His devotees, and His holy names.

## Chapter Eight

**Questioning the Definition Further**

Reading Chapters Six and Seven, a thoughtful reader may have further questions regarding the definition of sadhana.While the logic of circular causality gives one perspective on how physical activities in time and space transform into transcendental devotion, there are other perspectives. To provide a comprehensive view of the definition of sadhana-bhakti,this chapter raises further relevant questions, and then answers them. While part of this procedure may be a repetition of earlier material, the format of this presentation will offer a more systematic perspective of sadhana-bhakti.In that way we hope to assist the reader’s access to the primary objective of this book —the determination to achieve love.

Here again is the definition of sadhana-bhakti:

*krti-sadhya bhavet sadhya-*  
*bhava sa sadhanabhidha*  
*nitya-siddhasya bhavasya*  
*prakatyam hrdi sadhyata*

**“When transcendental devotional service, by which love for Krsna is attained, is executed by the senses, it is called sadhana-bhakti,or the regulative discharge of devotional service. Such devotion eternally exists within the heart of every living entity. The awakening of this eternal devotion is the potentiality of devotional service in practice.”**

The two pivotal words above are sadhyaand sadhana,the goal and the means to attain it, the prayojanaand the abhidheya,the goal of life and functional duties.

Rupa Gosvami’s definition makes clear that this goal is bhava-bhakti and that bhava-bhaktiexists eternally, is eternally perfect, and is only awakened within the heart by sadhana,not created by it.

The process of sadhana-bhaktiis also described as those system atic and regulated activities of the senses that enable the potentiality of bhavato manifest in the practitioner.

A wonder of sadhana-bhaktiis that it achieves its purpose by emulating the sensual activities by which bhavaexpresses itself, such as speaking about Krsna. In this way bhaktimanifests through the senses and gives rise to bhaktiwithin the heart, thus remaining consistent with the principle of bhaktya sanjataya bhaktya, bhaktigives rise to *bhakti*.

Commentators on Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu,like Jiva Gosvami and Cakravarti Thakura, raise and answer certain objections that the analytical mind may pose in response to Rupa Gosvami’s definition. Those and other arguments now follow.

\* \* \* \*

A devotee who contemplates the definitions of bhaktiand sadhana-bhakti may wonder about the relationship of these spiritual practices with the material body and therefore ask:

**“Bhakti has already been defined as an eternal and transcendental potency of Krsna. How then can activities of the material senses, that are performed in time and space, qualify as bhakti?”**

This question expresses a standard paradox that goes back to the Western philosophy of Cartesian dualism, which first defined what it called the “mind-body problem.” It is an enigma that challenges philosophers who still cannot unravel how transcendence can interact with the temporal. However, the Bhagavad-gitaand Krsna’s acaryashad addressed that question in millennia past. We answer in the following way:

**“We have already explained that bhaktireceived from the guruthrough the seed of the creeper of devotion transforms activities into bhakti.**

**“Additionally, acaryasargue that rudimentary activities like collecting wood and other ingredients for a yajna—while different from rituals like chanting mantrasand pouring oblations—are also indispensable aspects of a fire sacrifice and so are part of it. Similarly, because they lead to bhavaand prema,the activities of sadhana—although different from transcendental devotion—are considered bhakti.”**

Wanting further clarification to his question, a person may respond:

**“In the definition, the word bhavais referred to with words like sadhya,“acquired,” and sadhyata,“the state of being attained” or “the state of being manifested.”**

The implication is that sadhanaactually produces bhava,which is contradictory to bhava’seternal nature as described by the phrase nitya-siddhasya.How is this incongruity resolved?”

A valid enquiry indeed, one that highlights the complexities and challenges involved in communicating spiritual dynamics with the limitations of language. Again we answer:

**“Sadhana does not cause bhava.Rather, sadhanaqualifies a practitioner, purifies his heart, and awakens feelings of intense hankering for bhava.But it is not the cause. It is the catalyst. Due to the limitations of language, however, we express ourselves by saying that the catalyst sadhanamanifests bhava.**

**“A fire is not caused by the spark from striking together two pieces of flint. Fire is already latent within the firewood. The spark merely initiates a condition in which the dormant fire is manifest or attained. It is the same with the effect of sadhanaon bhava.”**

Not satisfied with the above answer a reader may think:

**“Still the wording of the definition gives the impression that sadhanacreates bhava."**

A definition must be concise and cannot immediately address every question related to it. This difficulty is further complicated when the definition is given in the precise spiritual language of Sanskrit and translated into the temporal English. In light of this, we shall do our best to answer this query:

**“The wording is precise and unambiguous!**

**“Rupa Gosvami says that bhavais nitya-siddha,eternally existent or eternally accomplished. Moreover, he says prakatyam hrdi,that it is awakened within the heart. Thus the proper contextual understanding of sadhyaand sadhyatais Srila Prabhupada’s use of the word ‘potentiality,’ which makes clear that sadhana simply uncovers that which is already present in its fullness.**

**“In order to clarify, Srila Prabhupada gives a clear example: the walking capacity is within every child, and by practice a child learns to walk. The actions of learning to crawl and balance, and repeatedly standing and falling, do not themselves give a child the ability to walk, they simply extract the walking potential. Were that potential not there—for example, were the child handicapped—then no amount of effort would make walking possible.**

**“Cakravarti Thakura gives another example: Krsna takes birth in the prison of Kamsa. But that does not mean that Krsna did not exist before His birth. Indeed, we know that Krsna is eternal. And so it is with bhava-bhakti.**

**“In conclusion, and as will be seen in the following chapter, the role of sadhana-bhaktiis even more passive than its definition first conveys. No matter how good the sadhana,no matter how qualified the sadhaka, bhava-bhaktiis independent of both. Efforts do not occasion its appearance. Bhava-bhaktiappears by the agency of the potencies of divine cognisance and pleasure, by Krsna’s svarupa-sakti.It is the mercy of the Lord that is the cause of the appearance of bhava.**

**“Citing Lord Brahma, Gopinatha Acarya explained to Sarvabhauma Bhattacarya that ultimately Krsna can be known only by His mercy, there is no other way:**

*athapi te deva padambuja-dvaya-*  
*prasada-lesanugrblta eva hi*  
*janati tattvam bhagavan-mahimno*  
*na canya eko ’pi ciram vicinvan*

**“My Lord! If one is favoured by even a slight trace of the mercy of Your lotus feet, he can understand the greatness of Your personality. But those who speculate in order to understand the Supreme Personality of Godhead are unable to know You, even though they continue to study the Vedas for many years.”**

\* \* \* \*

Having heard the conclusions of the acaryasand sastra,the reader may be satisfied yet still have some questions about the definition of sadhana.After all, this is not an easy topic. But for one serious about practising devotional service it is an indispensible one:

**“Accepting that bhavais not created but rather lies dormant in all living entities, can we say that sadhana develops and cultivates bhavafrom an imperfect to a perfect state?”**

This question is relevant because it shines light on the nature of the goal of sadhanaand how it is acquired. We answer:

**“Rupa Gosvami discounts every possibility that bhava is anything but perfect, eternally perfect. He says nitya-siddhasya bhavasya prakatyam hrdi sadhyata,‘The awakening of this eternal devotion \[bhava\] is the potentiality of devotional service in practice.’**

**“Sadhana-bhaktiis neither the cause nor the refiner of bhava.Rather, it awakens something that is already perfect and complete, in the same way ministers awaken their king in the morning. The awakening process has nothing to do with the king’s long-standing monarchical competence.”**

A reader may interject:

**“How can you say bhavais not refined when we see that bhava-sadhakasexperience development in their Krsna consciousness as they gain further entrance into the realm of love?”**

To this competent question we reply:

**“To understand the answer, let us revisit Srila Prabhupada’s analogy of a child awakening to his walking potential:**

**“The walking ability is awakened by practice, but once a child can walk, he or she can develop almost endless varieties of walking, like strolling, jogging, running—each to a different stage of perfection.**

**“Similarly, while bhavais awakened by sadhana,once it is, the devotee enters into the realm of transcendence wherein devotional activities propel him forward through stages of ecstatic devotion, on to prema,and to what Cakravarti Thakura calls further stages of ‘ever-increasing love.’**

**“Thus what appears to be development in transcendence is actually a devotee’s progress through the eternal stages of ecstasy and love, a progress that takes place by divine grace.”**

For further clarification on the characteristics that actually distinguish the process from its attainment, another question arises:

**“Activities like nama-sankirtanaor arcana,when accomplished either in sadhanaor in bhava,appear the same. What then is the actual difference between the two?”**

This intelligent question is relevant in ways too numerous to describe in detail and so we answer it in summary. At its heart, the question probes the distinction between the practising and perfected devotee:

**“As explained previously, activities of the senses in sadhana-bhaktiare a means to invoke bhava;by contrast, the activities of bhava-bhaktiare expressions of bhava.The former is a means to attain the goal, the latter is a consequence of having attained it.**

**“If the reader bears in mind that sadhana-bhaktiemulates the activities of transcendental devotion, the difference between the two kinds of activities becomes clear: one is aspiring to awaken spiritual emotion, the other is an expression of awakened spiritual emotion. The external activity may appear the same, but the cause is different.”**

Following from this question is another, which helps us clarify the difference between these two types of devotees:

**“How can one distinguish between sadhana-bhaktiand bhava-bhakti,and devotees’ similar conduct at those two stages of devotion?”**

To this we answer:

**“The distinction between the two kinds of devotion is established by the phrase sadhya-bhava,which makes clear that sadhanais that by which bhavais achieved.**

**“The general characteristic of a bhava-bhaktais that he hides his spiritual emotions. Therefore, because of the similarity in their external conduct, it is difficult for practising devotees or even for scholars to distinguish between the two kinds of devotees. Even Lord Caitanya admits that it is difficult to properly identify those in whom love has awakened. He says,**

*yanra citte krsna-prema karaye udaya*  
*tanra vakya, kriya, mudra vijneha na bujhaya*

**‘“Even the most learned man cannot understand the words, activities, and symptoms of a person situated in love of Godhead.**

**“Therefore, only one who is steeped in devotion himself will be able to distinguish a practitioner from a transcendentalist. It takes one to know one.”**

When we answer that it is difficult to recognise a bhava-bhaktaby his conduct, the reader may still persist in wanting some clues as to how accomplished Vaisnavas are distinguished from their juniors and so raise the question:

**“Since the essence of bhavais spiritual emotion, wouldn’t a true bhava-bhaktastop all external activities on the temporal platform and instead internalise them in meditative trance?”**

This is another way of saying that a devotee in whose heart prema has awakened should recluse himself and meditate on Krsna’s pastimes. We answer this query as follows:

**“This question implies that sensual activities performed with the perishable body are material, and the emotions that inspire those acts are what is spiritual.**

**“However, this is a misunderstanding.**

**“The activities of sadhanaare eternal because it is an eternal process, and also because the seed of bhakti in a devotee’s heart spiritualises even those activities. They are not material. At bhavathose same activities are fully transcendental because they are under the control of the internal potency. A suitable example is how an iron rod placed in fire becomes fiery. Prahlada Maharaja calls the process by which the body and mind have been empowered by spiritual qualities bhava-nukrtasayakrtih.His full instruction on the matter is:**

*tada puman mukta-samasta-bandhanas*  
*tad-bhava-bhavanukrtasayakrtih*  
*nirdagdha-bijanusayo mahiyasa*  
*bhakti-prayogena samety adhoksajam*

**‘“The devotee is then freed from all material contamination because he constantly thinks of the Lord’s pastimes and because his mind and body have been converted to spiritual qualities. Because of his intense devotional service, his ignorance, material consciousness, and all kinds of material desires are completely burnt to ashes. This is the stage at which one can achieve the shelter of the Lord’s lotus feet."'**

“Therefore the answer is that while an advanced devotee may internalise his spiritual emotions and taste them in meditation, expressing those emotions with his limbs and senses is equally spiritual; indeed realised authorities generally consider them superior. How expressing devotional activities through the senses is generally superior to meditating upon them is elaborately explained in Brhad-bhagavatamrtaby the Vaikuntha-dutas. Readers may refer to that invaluable source of knowledge.”

\* \* \* \*

A relevant question, and one connected to the prominent verse spoken by Sukadeva Gosvami beginning with vikriditam vraja-vadhubbir,may also be raised:

**“Can pure bhaktireally appear at sadhanaor at bhava if lust is still present to varying degrees within the heart?”**

We preface the answer to this important question by confirming that in the neophyte and intermediate stages of practice, lust, the greatest enemy of spiritual life, will be present to some degree in almost every devotee. Although at asaktiand bhavalust from past sinful activities is eradicated, nonetheless, lust as a result of offences may still be present. So the question is relevant even to bhava-bhaktas.Having said that, we answer in this way:

**“Scriptures like Srimad-Bhagavatamand great authorities like Rupa Gosvami elaborately establish that faith is the only qualification for devotion. Therefore the answer is, ‘Yes! Bhaktiis unobstructed by the presence of lust.’**

**“Not only does bhaktiappear in the presence of lust, but it also drives lust away. We can consider the following statement of Sukadeva Gosvami:**

*vikriditam vraja-vadhubhir idam ca visnoh*  
*sraddhanvito ’nusrnuyad atha varnayed yah*  
*bhaktim param bhagavati pratilabhya kamam*  
*hrd-rogam asv apahinoty acirena dhirah*

**“Anyone who faithfully hears or describes the Lord’s playful affairs with the young gopisof Vrndavana will attain the Lord’s pure devotional service. Thus he will quickly become sober and conquer lust, the disease of the heart.”**

**“Once again faith is established as the qualification for devotional service, which then appears, pratilabhya, even in the presence of material lust. Indeed, this verse emphasises that pure faith is the harbinger of devotion imbued with love, bhaktim param,or prema-bhakti, which then systematically eradicates all unwanted things from the heart. The understanding is that bhakti, like Krsna, is independent of material conditions, and just as Krsna can appear in a prison, bhaktican appear in an impure heart.**

**“Further evidence of this truth, among many others, is the story of Ajamila; another from Krsna’s assurances to Uddhava:**

*badhyamano ’pi mad-bhakto*  
*visayair ajitendriyah*  
*prayah pragalbhaya bhaktya*  
*visayair nabhibhuyate*

**‘“My dear Uddhava! If My devotee has not fully conquered his senses, he may be harassed by material desires, but because of his unflinching devotion for Me, he will not be defeated by sense gratification."’**

With the above concern allayed, a different question follows. Devotees are always curious about the external symptoms of their advancement, and often ask the following:

**“Since love is already present in the heart of a devotee, are there any visible indications of its dawning during practice?”**

This topic is addressed at great length in later parts of this book. At present we offer this condensed answer:

**“Steady transcendental emotion awakens only at bhava, and so the activities of sadhana-bhaktiare generally not accompanied by deep emotion except for those occasions when the Lord bestows His special mercy.**

**“But as a devotee’s consciousness becomes increasingly spiritualised, faint indicators of spiritual emotion—like the first rays of the sun shining through clouds—make themselves known in the form of taste and attachment.**  
**Ruciindicates an awakening of desire for Krsna and asaktia softening of the heart, mind, and intellect. By these qualities, a devotee’s heart becomes an indication of, and a suitable place for, the dawning of bhava."**

Readers looking for a succinct and simplified definition of sadhana- bhaktimay ask:

**“In essence, what is the relationship between sadhana and bhava?"**

To this question we offer a concise answer:

**“Sadhana-bhaktiprepares the heart to become a place suitable for the independent appearance of bhava-bhakti.”**

While the definition of sadhana-bhaktiis meant for serious seekers, it may pose questions relating to others, such as:

**“Sadhana-bhaktiis defined as a purposeful activity. If acts of sadhanaare done unintentionally—like a nondevotee saying Krsna’s name in jest—is it sadhana,and does that kind of activity awaken bhava?"**

Scriptures like Srimad-Bhagavatamaddress the subject of people who perform apparent acts of devotion with no real intention of doing so. We summarise the conclusion of sastrain this way:

**“Since sadhana-bhaktiis defined as the intention to attain bhava,activities of sadhanawhen done unintentionally are not sadhana-bhakti,but are a kind of bhaktiknown as bhakti-abhasa,the shadow of bhakti.**

**“Although the performers of bhakti-abhasamay even feel a shadow of ecstasy, Rupa Gosvami opines that their activities cannot lead to real bhava. The value of such bhaktiis that it may eventually lead to real sadbana.”**

While the definition of sadhana-bhaktimakes clear its relationship with bhava,it does not set out certain details for the fruition of bhava.Thus a reader may ask:

**“What are the conditions for sadhana-bhaktito bear the fruit of bhava?”**

By way of answer we suggest that the following three should be given due consideration:

**“First, one must actually receive the seed of devotion, and that through the disciplic succession.**

**“Next, sadhanamust be based on the definition of pure devotion given in the verse beginning with anyabhilasita-sunyam. That means sadhanaundertaken with a desire for enjoyment or for liberation, or sadhanaimproperly performed, will not result in bhava.**

**“Lastly, sadhana-bhaktishould be executed under the guidance of a realised spiritual master.”**

And a final question is:

**“How and why does bhavafinally make its appearance?”**

Dear reader! That is the subject of the next chapter, and so we shall now conclude our questions and answers. We hope that your concerns on the definition of sadhana-bhaktihave been allayed.

## Chapter Nine

**The Appearance of Bhava**

By way of introduction to this topic, let us recall that devotional service in practice is of two types, regulated and spontaneous. These divisions are based on the nature of a devotee’s inner impetus for service. If the impetus is based on the directions of scripture and guru,the service is regulated, and if the impetus is due to a natural attraction to follow Krsna’s associates, the service is spontaneous.

After passing through the stages of ruciand asakti,both these kinds of bhaktigive rise to bhava.Rupa Gosvami explains:

*tatra sadhanabhinivesa-jah*  
*vaidhi-raganuga-marga-bhedena pankirtitah*  
*dvividhah khalu bhavo ‘tra sadhanabhinivesajah*  
*sadhanabhinivesas tu tatra nispadayan rucim*  
*harav asaktim utpadya ratim samjanayaty asau*

**“Bhava,arising from absorption in sadhana,will be discussed first. Bhavaarising from sadhanahas two types: arising from vaidhi-sadhanaand arising from raganuga-sadhana.Absorption in sadhana\[nistha\] produces ruci,then asakti,and then ratior bhavafor the Lord.”**

Acaryassay that bhavaarising from regulated service is somewhat weaker than that arising from spontaneous service. The reason is that for a regulated devotee, the dearth of natural attraction somewhat weakens the transition to bbava—spontaneity itself. Nonetheless, once transcendence is attained, the joy of devotion compensates for whatever initial disparity may be there, as confirmed by Krsna Himself when He says, yoga-ksemam vahamy aham:

**“I carry what they lack, and I preserve what they have.”**

This phrase is an important assurance to both types of devotees who, in their own way, worship Krsna with love. Devotees who have attained ecstatic love for Krsna will not fall short in any way, as the full verse suggests:

*ananyas cintayanto mam*  
*ye janah paryupasate*  
*tesam nityabhiyuktanam*  
*yoga-ksemam vahamy aham*

**“But those who always worship Me with exclusive devotion, meditating on My transcendental form—to them I carry what they lack, and I preserve what they have.”**

\* \* \* \*

Having introduced the two kinds of sadhanafrom which bhava awakens, let us respond to the final question of the previous chapter, which asked for further elaboration on the actual awakening of bhava.

The question was:

**“How and why does bhavamake its appearance?”**

As we delve into the truths of bhava,we find that these two questions are so intertwined that they are answered simultaneously.

If we are to answer them in brief we would say:

**“*****Bhava*** **appears by the grace of Krsna in a heart that has been purified and made eager for perfection by pure** ***sadhana-bhakti*****.”**

That said, to further clarify this answer let us enter a more in-depth analysis of ecstatic devotional service, gleaned from scriptures and acaryas.Having done so we can give a more comprehensive answer to the questions posed.

We begin by reminding the reader of the well-established principle of bhaktya sanjataya bhaktya,and so we know that bhava- bhaktimust be occasioned by bhaktiitself.

However, while sadhana-bhaktihas the potential to awaken bhava,nowhere is it said that sadhanais the cause of bhava. Indeed, statements that say bhavais awakened by the mercy of devotees or by the mercy of Krsna further indicate that the awakening process is not exclusively a function of practice.

Sadhana-bhakti qualifies a devotee for the awakening of bhava, and so in a very general way it is said to “awaken” it. But if we are to be specific, there must be some other form of bhaktithat is the actual cause of the awakening of bhava.Since the only form of devotion other than bhava-bhaktiis sadhana-bhakti—which has been eliminated as the actual cause of bhava—the logical conclusion is that bhava-bhaktiis the cause for its existence and for its awakening.

Clearly when we speak of bhava-bhaktias its own cause, prema-bhaktiis also inferred. Ecstatic love is but a spark of prema,and so the awakening of bhavamay be occasioned either by ecstasy or by love.

Commenting on Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu,Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura writes,

**“This bhava-bhaktiis not obtained by any means of sadhana.Rather, by continual performance of sravana, kirtana,and other angasof bhakti,when such bhakti attains maturity, it automatically cleanses all misgivings from the heart of the sadhaka,at which time bhava-bhaktimanifests itself in the transparent heart by the mercy of Sri Krsna or His devotees.”**

Thakura Bhaktivinoda also confirms that bhavaappears by its own will:

**“One cannot attain that eternal perfection by his own effort. In the beginning the stage called sadhanais manifested in the heart, and persists until the time that eternal perfection \[bhava\]appears of its own accord. It should be understood that one cannot force the appearance of ecstatic devotion, it must come of its own will.”**

To further understand how bhava-bhakti“manifests,” “appears of its own will,” or “awakens in the heart,” it is instructive to review how authorities define bhava.

In His teachings to Sanatana Gosvami, Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu has explained that bhavais a constitutional part of every living entity. He says,

*nitya-siddha krsna-prema ‘sadhya’ kabhu naya*  
*sravanadi-suddha-citte karaye udaya*

**“Pure love for Krsna is eternally established in the hearts of the living entities. It is not something to be gained from another source. When the heart is purified by hearing and chanting, this love naturally awakens.”**

Srila Prabhupada repeatedly cites this verse to emphasise that bhavais a “permanent” feature of all jivas,“already there in the heart of everyone.” Due to forgetfulness, bhavais covered, but by perfecting the chanting and hearing process it can be “aroused.”

**“Where is** ***bhava*** **aroused?”**

**“In the** ***jiva*** **itself!”**

And it is aroused because bhavais already present within the soul. It is the eternal ecstatic condition, sthayi-bhava,of every living entity, and it manifests by the touch of Krsna’s spiritual energy.

Krsna confirms this understanding when He calls the jivaHis amsa,or fragmental part, which means that the living entity is also a manifestation of His svarupa-sakti.Unfortunately, because of its minute size, the jivasometimes falls under the influence of the external potency, maya:

*mamaivamso jiva-loke*  
*jiva-bhutah sanatanah*  
*manah-sasthanindriyani*  
*prakrti-sthani karsati*

**“The living entities in this conditioned world are My eternal fragmental parts. Due to conditioned life, they are struggling very hard with the six senses, which include the mind.”**

In the struggle with the material energy, the spiritual nature of the soul remains covered, but in contact with the svarupa-saktimanifesting through pure-hearted Vaisnavas, the soul’s spiritual nature is gradually revived.

This means that by sadhana,the influence of the svarupa-sakti latent in pure devotional service progressively increases in a devotee, its presence becoming stable at the stage of nisthaand increasingly robust at the stages of ruciand asakti.The development of this spiritual strength depends on careful practice, primarily in the form of nama-sankirtana.And as already discussed, devotees are engaged in pure devotion because the awakening of the svarupa-saktisystematically transforms their bodies.

\* \* \* \*

Although readers will have by now surmised a general definition of bhava,let us refer to Rupa Gosvami's all-encompassing and perfect version:

*suddha-sattva-visesatma*  
*prema-suryamsu-samya-bhak*  
*rucibhis citta-masrnya-*  
*krd asau bhava ucyate*

**“When devotional service is executed on the transcendental platform of pure goodness, it is like a sunray of love for Krsna. At such a time, devotional service causes the heart to be softened by various tastes, and one is then situated in bhava\[emotion\].”**

The phrase suddha-sattva-visesatmarefers to the living entity at the permanent transcendental stage of pure goodness. As described previously, suddha-sattvaindicates both the samvitand hladinipotencies, as well as their most wonderful combination. When these potencies are increasingly concentrated through ecstatic chanting and hearing, they transform bhavainto prema,and premainto its increasingly elevated stages of perfection, such as mana.As bhava condenses, it increases and intensifies the desire to please Krsna, a mindset that is the natural disposition of His eternal associates.

Readers may take note that the initial stage of bhavais not the same as its final stage. Like sadhana-bhakti,which progresses through a variety of stages, bhavais first immature, and then, by the strength of devotional activities, it systematically matures until its final blossoming into prema.

The next phrase, prema-suryamsu-samya-bhak,indicates that bhavais like a sunray of love for Krsna. In the analogy that prema is the sun and bhavaa ray of sunshine, Rupa Gosvami suggests that not long after the faint dawning of bhava,the glowing sun of premaappears. The relationship between bhavaand premais also described by the rasacarya:

*samyan-masrnita-svanto*  
*mamatvatisayankitah*  
*bhavah sa eva sandratma*  
*budhaih prema nigadyate*

**“When that bhavasoftens the heart completely, becomes endowed with a great feeling of possessiveness in relation to the Lord, and becomes very much condensed and intensified, it is called prema\[love of Godhead\] by learned scholars.”**

As a ray of love, bhavais also transcendental, otherwise how could it dwarf the happiness of liberation and preview a vision of the Lord? Moreover, it is a constant feature of the Lord’s eternal associates, and thus in a bhava-sadhakait brings about a mental disposition similar to that of the Vraja-vasis.

The term rucibhis citta-masrnya-krdmeans that bhavasoftens the mind with desires for meeting, serving, and cavorting with the Lord. Ruciimplies three kinds of taste:

**Meeting Krsna, rendering Him favourable service, and entering into a friendly relationship.**

The softening of the mind is a clear distinction between sadhana and bhava-bhakti.In the former, gross bodily activities are prominent, which in the latter are complemented with the addition of subtle mental meditations that result in an intense hankering for perfection. Thakura Bhaktivinoda says that bhava-sadhakasusually take shelter of nama-sankirtanato fulfill their coveted purpose.

The last phrase of the definition, asau bhava ucyate,reiterates that the softening of the heart is called bhava.That softening of the heart, masrnya,is the specific characteristic of loving devotion, more so than physical acts done either to waken it or that are a consequence of it.

Softening of the heart, like the stage of bhava,is also called bhava,and is defined in the following way:

*sarirendriya-vargasya*  
*vikaranam vidhayakah*  
*bhavavirbhava-janitas*  
*citta-vrttaya iritah*

**“Bhavasare a variety of conditions of the mind, produced through a relation between a subject and an object of love that produce transformations of the body and senses.”**

Thus readers may note that the word bhavahas multiple uses in Vaisnava theology. It means the stage of ecstasy, material and spiritual emotion, and also a stage of prema.

This definition makes clear that bhavatakes place as a transformation of a devotee’s state of mind. When the mind or heart of a devotee is electrified by the combined hladiniand samvitpotencies manifesting from eternally perfect bhakti, bhavahas awakened. The presence of bhavais attested to by a variety of ecstatic condi tions within the devotee’s mind, conditions that are all favourable to Krsna.

Interestingly, while it is bhavathat is ecstasy incarnate, through the instrument of the mind it appears as the cause of ecstasy. While in one sense this is the case, in another it is not—bhavais both ecstasy and the cause of it, both cause and effect. In the domain of transcendence such phenomenon co-exist, while in the realm of mediocrity they cannot.

The appearance of bhavain the mind is aggressive. It takes possession of the mind. And while bhavais self-evident, because it appears in the mind, the indication is that it has arisen from it. However, from everything written in this chapter and those preceding it, that obviously cannot be the case.

Of the two aspects of bhakti—those performed by the senses, cesta-ruðṁ,and those experienced in the mind, bhava-rupa—bha- va-bhaktiis of the nature of the latter. But because bhavaalso results in acts of the senses like nama-sankirtana,and because it is difficult to know the mental state of a devotee, it is difficult to ascertain a devotee’s spiritual attainment. That difficulty is further compounded by a devotee’s spiritual chastity, which impels him to hide his spiritual advancement. Narottama Dasa Thakura advises devotees in this way:

*apana bhajana-katha na kahiba jatha tatha*  
*ihate haiba sabadhana*  
*na kariha keha rosa na laiha mora dosa*  
*pranamaha bhaktera carane*

**“In the matter of personal bhajana,be careful to keep your attainments confidential. If you do not, people will either find fault with you or be upset with you. Better that your inner heart remains distant from them.”**

Considering these things, it is not surprising that bhavais generally not visible in the conduct of an exalted devotee. Only in the case where a devotee has lost control over his ecstatic condition would the assiduous observe and recognise a sadhaka’sgood fortune.

\* \* \* \*

Hearing these wonderful truths of bhava-bhaktione may be curious to know more, and so ask:

**“Why does this good fortune arise? Why does a devotee receive Krsna’s mercy?”**

The answer is:

**“In exceptional cases mercy is causeless, but the general case is that it descends in reciprocation with a sadhaka’s sincere effort and attachment.”**

Sometimes scripture gives examples of someone who has not done any sadhanabecoming the object of a great devotee’s mercy, such as Narada converting a snake into a devotee. This is to show the potency of great devotees, and the potency of their love. However, the same scriptures promote the path of practice and expect devotees to seriously adopt that path in order to attract the blessings of bhakti.

To better understand how mercy appears, readers may again consider the example of how fire is started by rubbing together two pieces of wood.

Fire is latent within the wood. So, by the sadhanaof rubbing two pieces of wood together, they become more and more eligible to catch fire.

When does the fire take place? Only when the first spark of fire appears.

Similarly, bhavais latent within the heart of all living entities, and one becomes eligible to taste that bhavaas a consequence of his sincere sadhana.But it takes divine grace in the form of a spark of bhava, suryamsu,to induce the bhavain the heart to flare up.

It is the opinion of authorities like Sanatana Gosvami that such awakening generally takes place while a devotee is hearing and chanting Krsna’s names. That is because nama-sankirtanais the yuga-dharmaand the ultimate benefactor of devotees. Sanatana Gosvami says that the Lord’s names and pastimes have a “magical power to awaken prema.” Once again, this magical power is the blessings that Krsna’s names and pastimes voluntarily bestow upon the worthy recipient.

**“Why does nama-sankirtanahave such magical effects?”**

**“Because it is especially dear to Krsna.”**

The Vaikuntha-dutas explain,

*sriman-nama prabhos tasya*  
*sri-murter apy ati-priyam*  
*jagad-dhitam sukhopasyam*  
*sa-rasam tat-samam na hi*

**“Dearer to the Lord than even His own beautiful form, His easily worshipped holy name benefits the entire world. Indeed, nothing is as full of nectar as the holy name of the Lord.”**

So, to the question:

**“How and why does** ***bhava*** **awaken?”**

We have answered:

**“Such a divine transformation is made possible by the mercy of Krsna, His names, His devotees, or by** ***bhava*** **itself.”**

To be more specific, let us summarise what has been said so far and so elaborate on the answer above:

**“How and why does** ***bhava*** **awaken?”**

We answer:

**“When a devotee seriously applies himself to the science of sadhana-bhaktiwith the aim of attaining love for Krsna, his devotions purify his being and energise the bhavathat eternally lives within him. In this way he becomes a candidate for the mercy of the Lord.**

**“When Krsna, His pure devotee, or His holy names are satisfied with a sadhaka’spurity, humility, and eagerness for love—his asakti—then they bless him with their mercy. That means that love from their hearts touches the heart of the sadhakaand empowers his own bhava to burst forth and take full dominion over his mind and senses, elevating him to the stage ecstatic devotion.**

**“That is “how”** ***bhava*** **awakens!**

“

**And bhavaawakens because the Lord, His devotee, His holy names, or** ***bhava*** **itself are satisfied with the intense desire and** ***sadhana*** **of a** ***sadhaka*****, and are thus impelled to bless him in the way described above.**

**“That is ‘why’** ***bhava*** **awakens!”**

Again, bhavaappears by divine grace when the possessors of grace are inspired to enable bhava’sappearance within the accomplished sadhaka.

\* \* \* \*

If we reflect further we see that, in addition to the attainment of bhava,literally everything is Krsna’s mercy. Even the illusion of materialists is made possible by the mercy of the Lord, what to speak of the liberation of His devotees. Living entities, conditioned or otherwise, are helpless without supreme grace. Everywhere and everything is evidence of Krsna’s mercy. As Krsna says:

**“I am the life of all that lives.”**

**“Of all that is material and all that is spiritual in this world, know for certain that I am both the origin and the dissolution.”**

In a Vaisnava’s spiritual development we see that he meets a guruand receives the seed of bhaktiby Krsna’s mercy. The seed of bhaktiis nurtured and grows into a creeper by Krsna’s mercy. The process of sadhana-bhaktiis Krsna’s mercy. And similarly, the mature creeper finally bears flowers of bhavaand premaall by Krsna’s mercy. In other words, without Krsna’s mercy, a conditioned soul would have no chance for liberation. He would remain in bondage eternally.

We see the example of Lord Brahma as the first created being who attained bhavaby the grace of the Lord. And the actual blessing that transformed the creator from a conditioned to a liberated soul is recorded thus in Srimad-Bhagavatam:

*yavan aham yatha-bhavo*  
*yad-rupa-guna-karmakah*  
*tathaiva tattva-vijnanam*  
*astu te mad-anugrahat*

**“All of Me, namely My actual eternal form and My transcendental existence, colour, qualities, and activities—let all be awakened within you by factual realisation, out of My causeless mercy.”**

By Krsna’s grace Brahma received the seed of bhaktithrough the word tapah,learned the science of bhagavad-bhakti,and attained bhava.In the same way and by the same grace, we sadhakasmay also realise the many stages and varieties of devotional service. That is Krsna’s guarantee!

*raga-dvesa-vimuktais tu*  
*visayan indriyais caran*  
*atma-vasyair vidheyatma*  
*prasadam adhigacchati*

**“But a person free from all attachment and aversion and able to control his senses through regulative principles of freedom can obtain the complete mercy of the lord.”**

And since bhaktiis a divine potency that is inseparable from Krsna, it may also be said that bhavaappears by the mercy of bhakti. Similarly, because that same bbaktiresides within great devotees, ṝ may be further said that bhavaappears by the grace of devotees. And finally, because bhavais also an eternally perfect aspect of bhakti,it may be said that it appears by its own grace.

The topic of divine grace and its descent will be discussed in greater detail in the final part of this book, Part Eight.

We must add that evidence of how bhavamanifests by supreme grace may be supported by how bhaktimanifests in a similar way by the grace of Vaisnavas, even by the grace of neophytes.

For example, we see how a non-devotee like Mrgrari the hunter can be converted to a devotee by Narada Muni. We also see how, in Srila Prabhupada’s Krsna consciousness movement, new devotees preach to non-devotees and inspire them to take up bhakti. In both cases—the first, of the great Narada, and the second, of the young preacher—bbaktiappears from the heart of a devotee to spiritually transform a recipient by divine grace. Whether one considers that grace to be of Narada, the young preacher, Srila Prabhupada, or Gauranga Mahaprabhu, it is a fact that divine grace and bhaktican appear through anyone and take up residence in any recipient. So it is with the appearance of bhava.

To summarise, we quote the great Sanatana Gosvami:

**“To attain Vaikuntha one must be favoured with the blessings of bhakti.”**

We should thus allay all misconceptions that bhavais created in any way. Rather, it is more favourable to consider the perspective of great devotees.

**“What is that perspective?”**

**“Those who are absorbed in the perfections of loving devotion do not even think that the services they do are actions under their own control. Rather, they consider their every movement and service to be expressions of Krsna’s supreme mercy.”**

In other words, real devotees never see anyone as a doer, they simply see Krsna’s mercy as the cause of all things. An example is when Narada’s mother was bitten by a snake and he, a young boy, was left all alone. How did he react?t

*ada tad aham isasya*  
*bhaktanam sam abhipsatah*  
*anugraham manyamanah*  
*pratistham disam uttaram*

**“I took this as the special mercy of the Lord, who always desires benediction for His devotees, and so thinking, I started for the north.”**

In conclusion, bhavais never created but eternally exists, its self-manifest appearance being accomplished by the:

**“Actions of the most excellent transformations of the Lord’s svarupa-saktis, hladiniand samvit.”**

Let us close by embracing Jiva Gosvami’s succinct and unequivocal words on this topic:

**“Though this bhavais seen in the eternal associates of the Lord, the mental conditions of the devotees within this world become similar, by the mercy of the Lord and His devotees. By this mercy alone it shall appear.**

**There is no need to elaborate further.”**

## Part Three

**The Sankhya of Sankalpa**

## Chapter Ten

**Introduction: The Agents of Sankalpa**

In the first two parts of this book we introduced and defined sadhana-bhakti,the ultimate science of perfection. The definition of sadhanaestablished its purpose as bhava,ecstatic love. With that clear objective in mind and with the spiritual rewards that objective bolds, sadhakascan move forward from their current level of advancement with enthusiasm.

The many steps towards bhavaare known as sankalpas,or determinations. And many steps there will be. After all, it is rare that success can be accomplished in one giant step—such as a single sankalpa—from bhajana-kriyato bhava.It is true that Caitanya Mahaprabhu immediately exhibited ecstatic symptoms upon taking initiation, but He was the Supreme Lord. And we generally see that even great devotees require many steps and many years to attain or to disclose their perfection. It is therefore not unreasonable to assert that the journey to Krsna is not an overnight affair.

In Their Dvaraka pastimes, Srimati Radharani solicits from Krsna a blessing that His determined practitioners will one day see Him face to face. In so doing, She admits that such attainment will take a “long time” and that those desirous of it must sustain a “steady heart:”

*cirad asa-matram tvayi viracayantah sthira-dhiyo*  
*vidadhyur ye vasam madhṝrima-gabhire madbu-pure*  
*dadhanah kaisore vayasi sakhitam gokula-pate*  
*prapadyethas tesam paricayam avasyam nayanayoh*

**“Still, please grant this one benediction: to those devotees who reside in the profoundly sweet land of Vrndavana and who for a long time yearn with a steady heart to someday attain You, please Î master of Gokula, appear before their eyes as their youthful friend.”**

To realise this blessing that Radha secured will take time and repeated initiatives on the part of the resolute sadhaka.Each step will require a clear vision of both its goal and its means. A sankalpais successful when a devotee’s means and goal are well defined, and when he perseveres not only with the challenges he faces, but with the many steps he must take.

The obvious vehicle for a sankalpais the material body and its powerful senses. It was with the material body that one became entangled, and with that same material body one can make his spiritual life successful; it is just a matter of how the body is employed.

With our ears we hear Krsna’s holy names, with our eyes we see the deity of the Lord, and with our hands we serve the Vaisnavas. Devotees may take a lesson from Maharaja Ambarisa on how to fully and systematically engage their senses on their journey to Krsna. Sukadeva Gosvami describes the king’s glories in this way:

*sa vai manah krsna-padaravindayor*  
*vacamsi vaikuntha-gunanuvarnane*  
*karau harer mandira-marjanadisu*  
*srutim cakaracyuta-sat-katbodaye*

*mukunda-lingalaya-darsane drsau*  
*tad-bhrtya-gatra-sparse ’nga-sangamam*  
*ghranam ca tat-pada-saroja-saurabhe*  
*srimat-tulasya rasanam tad-arpite*

*padau hareh ksetra-padanusarpane*  
*siro hrsikesa-padabhivandane*  
*kamam ca dasye na tu kama-kamyaya*  
*yathottamasloka-janasraya ratih*

**“Maharaja Ambarisa always engaged his mind in meditating upon the lotus feet of Krsna, his words in describing the glories of the Lord, his hands in cleansing the Lord’s temple, and his ears in hearing the words spoken by Krsna or about Krsna. He engaged his eyes in seeing the Deity of Krsna, Krsna’s temples, and Krsna’s places like Mathura and Vrndavana; he engaged his sense of touch in touching the bodies of the Lord’s devotees, he engaged his sense of smell in smelling the fragrance of tulasioffered to the Lord, and he engaged his tongue in tasting the Lord’s prasada.**  
**He engaged his legs in walking to the holy places and temples of the Lord, his head in bowing down before the Lord, and all his desires in serving the Lord, twenty-four hours a day. Indeed, Maharaja Ambarisa never desired anything for his own sense gratification.**  
**He engaged all his senses in devotional service, in various engagements related to the Lord. This is the way to increase attachment for the Lord and be completely free from all material desires.”**

But the senses are not independent agents. They are directed by a common master known as the mind, which is also part of the body, a subtle part. And it is the mind that poses the greatest challenge to the spiritual aspirant. It poses a challenge because for the conditioned soul, the mind can be the aspirant’s greatest enemy. The Lord discloses this spiritual challenge to Arjuna:

*uddhared atmanatmanam*  
*natmanam avasadayet*  
*atmaiva hy atmano bandhur*  
*atmaiva ripur atmanah*

**“One must deliver himself with the help of his mind, and not degrade himself. The mind is the friend of the conditioned soul, and his enemy as well.”**

Reading the above verse one will be prompted to ask:

**“How can the mind be an enemy?’**

It can be an enemy when it directs the senses to sense gratification or when it meditates on sense gratification. Both these actions are obstacles to spiritual growth, and the devotee who entertains them while doing sadhanais on the slow boat to bhava.Inattention on the path of progress leads to frustration, and if not corrected, a likely failure.

To make determinations successful, the mind has to be sympathetic to properly scheduled spiritual pursuits. And for the mind to be on its best behaviour, it must be controlled. This will ensure that both it and its subordinates, the senses, are co-operating with the efforts of the sincere practitioner.

Krsna re-emphasises the dual nature of the mind while providing the toggle switch that transforms the mind’s inimical conduct to a friendly one. That toggle is the ability to control or conquer the mind:

*bandhur atmatmanas tasya*  
*yenatmaivatmana jitah*  
*anatmanas tu satrutve*  
*vartetatmaiva satru-vat*

**“For him who has conquered the mind, the mind is the best of friends; but for one who has failed to do so, his mind will remain the greatest enemy.**

But conquering the mind is a science. It is an undertaking that is made possible by empowering another controlling agent, the intelligence. Success in determinations is conditional on a purified intelligence gaining the upper hand over the mind. Krsna makes this necessity clear in no uncertain terms:

*yo vai van-manasi samyag*  
*asamyacchan dhiya yatih*  
*tasya vratam tapo danam*  
*sravaty ama-ghatambu-vat*

**“A transcendentalist who does not completely control his words and mind by superior intelligence will find that his spiritual vows, austerities, and charity How away just as water Hows out of an unbaked clay pot.”**

By contrast, when the intelligence is empowered by the practice of pure devotion, it becomes successful in guiding a sadhakatowards his desired destination. The Lord reassures us with the following words:

*tasmad vaco manah pranan*  
*niyacchen mat-parayanah*  
*mad-bhakti-yuktaya buddhya*  
*tatah parisamapyate*

**“Being surrendered to Me, one should control the speech, mind, and life air, and then through loving devotional intelligence one will completely fulfil the mission of life.”**

The next few chapters are dedicated to understanding how the bewildered and forgetful intelligence can be rectified in order to win control over the unruly mind.

A part of that assignment is to recognise another agent in the hierarchy of control over the senses, and that is the false ego. The challenge of the sadhakaincludes converting the false ego to its original identity as Krsna’s servant. It is only with the self-conception of “I am Krsna’s servant” that devotees can hope to attain love. It is selfless service alone that gives devotees entrance into the domain of love. To expose the falsity of bodily identification, Krsna explains the different forms in which the false ego manifests and how by devotional service false ego is rectified:

*amulam etad bahu-rupa-rupitam*  
*mano-vacah-prana-sarira-karma*  
*jnanasinopasanaya sitena*  
*cchittva munir gam vicaraty atrsnah*

**“Although the false ego has no factual basis, it is perceived in many forms—as the functions of the mind, speech, life air, and bodily faculties. But with the sword of transcendental knowledge, sharpened by worship of a bona fide spiritual master, a sober sage will cut off this false identification and live in this world free from all material attachment.”**

The interaction of the above-mentioned agents and how they are made favourable to devotional service is a matter of relationship, sambandha.And if the senses, mind, and intelligence sound like a crowded playing field, they are not the only contestants involved. Within the body is also the contaminated consciousness, as well as the living entity, the soul, while outside the body are the modes of material nature and the age, and agents, of Kali.

How do all these factors interact and how do they influence a sankalpa,favourably or otherwise? How are these agents made favourable for a sankalpa,and how are they all, including the mind, brought in line with the sadhaka’saspiration? The knowledge with which one can answer these questions is called sambandha-jnana.And Part Three of Sankalpa-kaumudidives deeply into the nectar ocean of this foundational knowledge.

\* \* \* \*

We have made the attempt, and taken the liberty, of presenting this analytic study with the conviction that understanding the mechanics of how the mind, intelligence, senses, and ego participate in making a determination towards advanced devotion is helpful in grasping the theme of this book.

While these chapters may be technical, we recommend that readers not skip over them—which readers sometimes do—simply because they may pose a challenge. What follows is part of the sankhyaphilosophy that Srimad-Bhagavatamso eruditely presents, and its reading is the kind of intellectual exercise Kaviraja Gosvami supports:

*siddhanta baliya citte na kara alasa*  
*iha ha-ite krsne lage sudrdha manasa*

**“A sincere student should not neglect the discussion of such conclusions, considering them controversial, for such discussions strengthen the mind. Thus one’s mind becomes attached to Sri Krsna.”**

While it is true to say that this entire book is of the nature of an analytical study, sankhya,the chapters comprising this part of the book fall even more so in that category.

**“What is sankhya?”**

From the perspective of Srimad-Bhagavatam:

**“The study of the elemental categories of the material world is known as sankhya,and applying that study to attain liberation is celebrated as sankhya-yoga.”**

This type of categorical analysis of sankhyais what western scholars refer to as metaphysics, and which Encyclopaedia Britannica defines as:

**“The philosophical study whose object is to determine the real nature of things—to determine the meaning, structure, and principles of whatever is insofar as it is.”**

By comparison to its western counterpart, sankhyais somewhat more detailed for it literally means “numeral,” from the root khya and the prefix sam,meaning “to count.” Sankhyacounts the elements and minutely catalogues the cause and effect principles underlying the unfolding of the material nature, from the microscopic to the macroscopic.

The whole purpose of such an analysis is to distinguish matter from spirit, and having done so, to further understand the nature of conditioned souls, the dynamics of their bondage, and their path to liberation through service to the one supreme soul.

Sankhyais one of the elemental building blocks of Krsna consciousness that Srila Prabhupada introduced to his first students in 1966:

“Perhaps some of you or most of you know what is sankhya-yoga,metaphysics, by Kapila, sankhya-yoga. Sankhya-yogameans analytical study of these material elements.

**“Now what is the use of analytical study of this material world? Simply understanding that this material world is working in twenty-four elements. The eleven senses, ten senses, five working senses, and five knowledge-acquiring senses, and the mind. Eleven. Eleven elements. And panca-maha-bhuta. Panca-maha-bhuta means the material elements just like earth, water, fire, air, and ether. Eleven and five, it becomes sixteen. Then subtle elements, just like manab, buddhih, ahankara:mind, intelligence, and false ego. False ego.**  
**So sixteen and three. Nineteen. And five, I mean to say, sense objects. Sense objects means rupa,form; rasa,taste; form, taste, rupa, rasa; gandha,smell; rupa, rasa, gandha,then sabda,sound, sound. You have got ear. You require sound to hear. In this way, the sankhya-yoga,they have analysed the whole material world into twenty-four elements. That is sankbya-yoga.”**

Krsna also introduces His teachings in the Bhagavad-gitaby analysing the difference between the material body and the life force moving it. And then in later chapters He teaches how to apply sankhyaas a yogaprocess that ultimately leads to bhakti-yoga.The Lord Himself uses the word sankhyain the following verse:

*esa te ’bhihita sankhye*  
*buddhir yoge tv imam srnu*  
*buddhya yukto yaya partha*  
*karma-bandham prahasyasi*

**“Thus far I have described this knowledge to you through analytical study. Now listen as I explain it in terms of working without fruitive results. Î son of Prtha, when you act in such knowledge you can free yourself from the bondage of works.”**

Furthermore, Srimad-Bhagavatamrepeatedly teaches primary and secondary phases of creation through the science of sankhya. One such presentation is that of Lord Kapila, the acaryaof devotional sankhya,who also elaborately describes the science of sankhya-yogaas it relates to pure devotional service.

And finally, even the biography of Caitanya Mahaprabhu, Sri Caitanya-caritamrta,includes a review of cause and effect as relating to the creation. Hence this kind of approach to devotional topics is one that studious devotees will be familiar with.

This third part of Sankalpa-kaumudi,therefore, presents an overview of how the fundamental components of sankalpainteract. It thereby lays the foundation for understanding the dynamics of sankalpa,a foundation that will hopefully inspire sadhakasto boldly progress step by step to bhava.

## Chapter Eleven

**Taming the Mind**

The previous chapter explained the need to understand the dynamics of sankalpasin light of a critical analysis of the decision making process and the components which facilitate decisions. The first component under review in this chapter is the mind, that all powerful opponent of spiritual progress.

We begin our study of the mind by hearing about the secondary creation known as visarga,and how the subtle and gross senses evolve by the mystic potency of the Supreme Lord:

The unmanifest eternal aggregate of twenty-four material elements, in which the modes of material nature are in equilibrium and which is the state of material nature prior to its manifestation, is called pradhana.

The twenty-four elements as explained by Lord Kapila are as follows:

*pancabhih pancabhir brahma*  
*caturbhir dasabhis tatha*  
*etac catur-vimsatikam*  
*ganam pradhanikam viduh*

**“The aggregate elements, namely the five gross elements, the five subtle elements, the four internal senses, the five senses for gathering knowledge, and the five outward organs of action, are known as the pradhana.”**

Of these twenty-four elements, the four internal senses are the mind, intelligence, false ego, and contaminated consciousness, the latter being also known as mahat-tattva.It is interesting to note that the material elements are counted differently by different sages in different Vedic texts. The reason for such variance is given by Lord Krsna Himself in Appendix Three.

Lord Kapila explains that, like our external senses, these four internal senses can only be distinguished from each other by their different functions. This is a very important point for readers to consider and to remember in their battle with the unruly mind. The Lord explains it in this way:

*mano buddhir ahankaras*  
*cittam ity antar-atmakam*  
*caturdha laksyate bhedo*  
*vrttya laksana-rupaya*

**“The internal, subtle senses are experienced as having four aspects in the shape of mind, intelligence, ego, and contaminated consciousness. Distinctions between them can be made only by different functions, since they represent different characteristics.”**

For example, the five knowledge-acquiring senses are the eyes, ears, tongue, nose, and skin, through which we see, hear, taste, smell, and touch, respectively. While these senses have general physical appearances by which they can be distinguished, their primary distinctive characteristics are their functions such as seeing, hearing, and tasting. However, since the internal senses are not physically perceivable, they can be distinguished from each other by their functions, such as thinking, discerning, and perceiving, these being attributable to the mind, intelligence, and false ego, respectively.

\* \* \* \*

To understand the functioning of the mind, it is advantageous to appreciate the evolution of the subtle body from the point at which the living entity comes into contact with material nature. That description now follows:

When the unmanifest combination of material elements, pradhana,becomes manifest, it is known as prakrti,or the material nature. The Lord places the living entities, along with their individual destinies, into the womb of this material nature, and then agitates the modes of nature by His potency of time.

Thus activated, material nature gives birth to the effulgent mahat-tattva,which is the seed of the universe in which the modes of nature become dominant, and which is represented in the body by consciousness.

When the mahat-tattvais infused with the energy of the Lord, then false ego, ahankara,is manifested in three features—goodness, passion, and ignorance. These threefold aspects of false ego, endowed with the three modes of nature, are the source of the other internal senses known as the antah-karana,as well as a further twenty elements, the visible ingredients of creation.

The modes of nature effect the false ego in different ways:

**When the false ego is dominated by goodness it gives rise to the mind; when dominated by passion, to intelligence; and when dominated by ignorance, to the gross and subtle elements.**
