The fruits of these seeds include affinity for wealth, prestige, followers, and sex. If this offence is not quickly uprooted, a devotee can easily become illusioned by temptation and abandon his efforts at pure devotion. In such a fallen condition he becomes either a pseudo-guruor an out-and-out sense enjoyer. Needless to say, the offence of distraction makes a devotee all the more neglectful in chanting.

If by some good fortune, either by his own intelligence or by the prompting of well-wishers, a devotee realises the implication of his distracted sadhana,he should immediately act to reform him self. He must banish all impure thoughts and allurements from his mind by consigning himself to Vaisnava culture and tradition. The following paragraphs elaborate on how this may be accomplished.

The implicit psychology of distraction is that there is something more interesting and valuable than that offered by the Vaikuntha worlds of service to Krsna. The solution to distraction is deep immersion in Vaisnava lifestyle, including attire, tilaka,meals, and a daily spiritual regimen. Thakura Bhaktivinoda emphasises the mesmerising potency of Vaisnava festivals when they are strictly observed, and he selects these celebrations as a panacea for the distracted mind. Vaisnava culture also includes regular attendance at temple functions and faithful worship of the Lord’s deity form.

The Vaisnava calendar is replete with events celebrating the Lord’s incarnations, pastimes, and associates. Included amongst these are the vow of Ekadasi and the appearance day of Krsna, Janmastami. During such observances the wayward sadhaka should avoid eating and drinking, and in the company of pure devotees, chant and hear the names and glories of Lord Krsna. If possible, these events may be celebrated in a Gaudiya dhama,but if not, then in a temple where saintly devotees congregate.

By wholehearted participation in such festivities, a devotee will gradually regain his good fortune and rekindle his taste for Krsna’s names and pastimes. From the insignificant distractions of maya, his attention will be brought back to the significant, ever-sweet names of Krsna. Rupa Gosvami describes how such a devotee revives his taste for chanting and thereby his attention to the same:

*syat krsna-nama-caritadi-sitapy avidya-*  
*pittopatapta-rasanasya na rocika nu*  
*kintv adarad anudinam khalu saiva justa*  
*svadvi kramad bhavati tad-gada-mida-bantri*

**“The holy name, character, pastimes, and activities of Krsna are all transcendentally sweet like sugar candy. Although the tongue of one afflicted by the jaundice of avidya\[ignorance\] cannot taste anything sweet, it is wonderful that simply by carefully chanting these sweet names every day, a natural relish awakens within his tongue, and his disease is gradually destroyed at the root.”**

As part of a repentant offender’s re-immersion in Vaisnava culture, we should not neglect to mention the need for deity worship, arcana.

The worship of Krsna’s deity form is compulsory for both neophytes and householders. Indeed, it is so spiritually beneficial that intermediate and even advanced devotees often serve personal deities.

Caitanya Mahaprabhu instructed Sanatana Gosvami to write in detail about the importance and the process of deity worship. The acaryafulfilled the Lord’s order by compiling Hari-bhakti-vilasa, worshipping the deity of Madana-mohana, and constructing the first temple in Vrndavana.

Sri Narada Muni is considered the acaryaof arcana, and he has compiled instructions for regulated worship in his Narada pancaratra.His path of worship is known as the pancaratriki marga,which Prahlada Maharaja included as one of the nine limb of pure devotional service.

The process of deity worship is especially recommended for a devotee new to the path of worship taught in the Srimad-Bhagavatam,the bhagavata-marga.The main aspects of the bhagavataschool are nama-sankirtana,hearing from saints, and remembering the Lord. Thus, for someone who is struggling with being attentive to bhagavat-vidhi, pancaratriki-vidhiis compulsory.

Deity worship—which includes dressing the deity, cooking Them a meal, and offering Them arati—brings devotees into such spiritual proximity to the Lord that even the hardest heart will melt. Such inner experiences revive a devotee’s attraction to chanting and eradicates the spiritually ruinous habit of distraction. Krsna assures the repentant devotee that even though crossing the reset voir of offences is an ordeal, by worshipping His deity the sadhaka will be successful:

*evam kriya-yoga-pathaih*  
*puman vaidika-tantrikaih*  
*arcann ubhayatah siddhim*  
*matto vindaty abhipsitam*

**“By worshipping Me through the various methods prescribed in the Vedas and tantras,one will gain from Me his desired perfection in both this life and the next.”**

Indeed, not only will the sincere devotee become free of offences, but if he continues to worship without the desire for fruitive results, he will be blessed with pure devotion. Krsna continues:

*mam eva nairapeksyena*  
*bhakti-yogena vindati*  
*bhakti-yogam sa labhata*  
*evam yah pujayeta mam*

**“But one who simply engages in devotional service with no consideration of fruitive results attains Me. Thus, whoever worships Me according to the process I have described will ultimately attain pure devotional service unto Me.”**

In the ways mentioned above, the inattentive devotee gradually overcomes his bad habit, be it caused by indifference, laziness, or distraction. The result of such a victory is that the sadhakarelishes the taste of pure devotion as being infinitely more attractive than the allure of sense gratification. And in time, he begins to detest even the thoughts of maya’sappeal. As the great Yamunacarya wrote:

*yadavadhi mama cetah krsna-padaravinde*  
*nava-nava-rasa-dhamany udyatam rantum asit*  
*tadavadhi bata nari-sangame smaryamane*  
*bhavati mukha-vikarah susthu nisthivanam ca*

**“Since I have been engaged in the transcendental loving service of Krsna, realising ever-new pleasure in Him, whenever I think of sex pleasure I spit at the thought, and my lips curl with distaste at the thought.”**

Such wonderful transformations take place when the offenceless vibration of Krsna’s names enters the devotee’s ears and fills his mind with waves of nectar, flushing out all mundane thoughts and saturating it with thoughts of Krsna. In such a state of Krsna consciousness the devotee again chants in an attentive mood, spontaneously relishing the joyous and peaceful path of taste and attachment that leads to the kingdom of bhava.

We should add that without the mercy of the Lord, singlehanded effort at chanting will not bear the fruit of attentiveness. To attain that mercy Caitanya Mahaprabhu recommends that a sadhakashould practise the fourfold path of humility, which we have already described. Therefore, while cultivating attentiveness in a way that corresponds to his weakness, a devotee must continually pray to the Lord for shelter and beg the holy name for forgiveness, In the preceding sections we have underscored the fault of inattentive chanting and offered remedies for the three ways such offence manifests. However, this chapter is about attentiveness. If from the beginning of his devotions a practitioner recognises this secret of spiritual advancement, he will remain enthusiastic and alert to warding off the slightest glimmer of apathy, laziness, or distraction.

A wise sadhakaknows that if he falls into the snare of inattentive nama-sankirtana,even if he is free of other offences, inattention will continue to frustrate any sankalpathat he undertakes In this regard, therefore, it is better for a sadhakato be proactive than to suffer the painful consequences of recapturing lost enthusiasm and rebuilding the eroded foundations of his spiritual life. Therefore a practising devotee inscribes the Vaisnavas’ motto In his heart, and morning, noon, and night he quietly whispers, sadhu savadhana, sadhu savadhana:

**“O sadhu!Always remain attentive! Always remain attentive!”**

## Chapter Twenty-Six

**Attentive Bhajana**

The latter part of the previous chapter explored the consequences of inattention during nama-sankirtana,the result of which is anything but a pretty picture of robust sadhana.Considering the challenges Kali-yuga already poses for the average sadhaka,devotees are better off not creating additional problems for themselves by ignoring their very means of salvation. Better that they take the trouble-free path to perfection and carefully cultivate attentiveness in nama-sankirtanaand the other limbs of sadhana.

The following chapters are meant to assist the thoughtful sadhakain cultivating attentiveness, especially in the more advanced stages of nama-smarana,which scriptures consider to be the very essence of bhakti-yoga.We shall see that such cultivation by stages is what lies at the very heart of sadhana-sankalpa,and a devotee who is adept in this spiritual science reaches bhavamuch faster than one who is not. Learned transcendentalists say that attentiveness makes the transition through sankalpassmooth and their results prompt.

We can take lessons from the example of little Prahlada when he was brought forward to pacify Lord Nrsimhadeva. Ushered before the Lord by the fearful demigods, he became very attentive, and with a mind fixed on his mission he began to offer prayers to the Lord. In his commentary to this pastime Srila Prabhupada writes,

**“The ability to fix the mind in this way is a result of yoga-siddhi, mystic perfection.”**

It rakes practise to attain the kind of samadhifrom which Prahlada could fulfil his sankalpaof glorifying the Lord with prayers. And from this young devotee we have an example of how attentiveness facilitates determinations.

Another example is Lord Siva instructing the Pracetas. In prefacing their initiation, the Lord emphasised the connection between attentiveness and the speed of attaining the goal. He was concerned that the brothers not falter in their determination to chant their diksa-mantra.That foremost amongst Vaisnavas said,

*atbedam nityada yukto*  
*japann avabitah puman*  
*acirac chreya apnoti*  
*vasudeva-parayanah*

**“A devotee of Lord Krsna whose mind is always absorbed in Him, who with great attention and reverence chants this** ***stotra*** **\[prayer\], will achieve the greatest perfection of life without delay.”**

The phrase acirac chreya apnotitranslates as “achieve auspiciousness very soon.” The word acirenameans “very soon,” and it is also found in the well-known verse beginning with *vikriditam vraja-vadhubhir idam ca visnoh*. Both these verses indicate that attentiveness yields quick results.

This productive sadhanastands in stark contrast to what we have already explained, which is that inattentive chanting yields agonisingly slow results. Indeed, the eventual result of inattentive bhaktiis never bhava.Rather, the best effect of offensive chanting is that it gradually brings sobriety to a sadhaka,and sobriety in turn gradually inspires him to control his mind and make his sadhanaattentive. As for the worst effect, Kaviraja Gosvami warns his readers that the snail-pace of careless chanting could span many lifetimes, *bahu janma*. Knowing the outcome of negligent sadhana, what intelligent devotee would want to risk protracting his already beginningless hardships in the material world! Better to cultivate attentive, conscientious chanting with the assurance that the treasure of bhava-bhaktais close at hand.

Let us now move forward to attentiveness in progressive sadhana.

The importance of one-pointed attention to the holy names really comes to the fore when devotees advance to the stage of remembrance, smarana, which scriptures praise as being the very essence of bhakti. Padma Paranasays,

*smartavyah satatam visnur*  
*vismartavyo na jatucit*  
*sarve vidhi-nisedhah syur*  
*etayor eva kinkarah*

**“Krsna is the origin of Lord Visnu. He should always be remembered and never forgotten at any time. All the rules and prohibitions mentioned in the sastrasshould be the servants of these two principles.”**

The purpose of attentiveness is to enable us to remember Krsna in the way that we now remember so many things unrelated to Him—spontaneously. The goal is laulyam,greed for Krsna. In its absence, a devotee must learn to remember Krsna, and learning remembrance is a science, as the following pages will reveal.

Commenting on Prahlada Maharaja’s qualification to offer prayers to the Lord, Srila Prabhupada further writes,

**“His mind and attention became saturated in transcendence.”**

Sri Prahlada’s level of attention is known as samadhi.In his purport His Divine Grace goes on to explain that the degree of attentiveness that a devotee is able to muster is dependent upon the purity of that devotee’s heart. Prahlada’s heart was pure, and so his one-pointedness carried him to the last stage of smarana.The lesson to be learnt is that a sadhaka’sattentiveness depends upon his level of spiritual advancement; there is a proportionate relationship between the two.

The step-by-step exertion for the goal of bhavarequires incrementally greater and greater attentiveness, which in turn rewards the sadhakawith a deeper and longer connection with the transcendental vibration of the maha-mantra.The composite result is an increasingly purified heart, enabling the devotee to climb the stairway of smaranamleading to bhava.Thus we see that attentiveness enables purity and purity enables further attentive ness. The two are intrinsically related.

Krsna reassures His devotee that progress through stages of devotion, when overseen by an attentive mind, are always effective:

*ista-purtena mam evam*  
*yo yajeta samahitah*  
*labhate mayi sad-bhaktim*  
*mat-smrtih sadhu-sevaya*

**“One who has executed sacrificial performances and pious works for My satisfaction, and who thus worships Me with fixed attention, obtains unflinching devotional service unto Me. By the excellent quality of his service, such a worshipper obtains realised knowledge of Me.”**

Followers of Caitanya Mahaprabhu know well that the attentive sacrificial performances of which Krsna speaks are twofold: one is the practice of bhaktiand the other its dispensation. According to the Lord’s teachings and example, the healthy balance of the two enables the rare attainment of bhava-bhakti.

Attentiveness in the dispensation of bhaktimeans attentiveness in the sankirtana-yajna.Devotees who have participated in book distribution, street chanting, or prasadamdistribution know well that steadiness in these services requires concentration of mind, without which a practitioner cannot undergo the austerities involved. Thus attentiveness in sankirtanais as important as attentiveness in bhajana.Indeed, it is the same controlled mind that makes both successful.

And so one may ask:

**“How is such attentiveness accomplished”**

The Lord answers:

**“By constant effort!”**

In the same accessible and straightforward language with which He solves the problem of mind control a few verses later, Krsna lays out the sadhanafor attaining attentiveness:

*yato yato niscalati*  
*manas cancalam asthiram*  
*tatas tato niyamyaitad*  
*atmany eva vasam nayet*

**“From wherever the mind wanders due to its flickering and unsteady nature, one must certainly withdraw it and bring it back under the control of the self.”**

Thus we hear that attentiveness is achieved by a constant effort in bringing the unruly mind to heel. In Lord Caitanya’s movement that effort means engaging the mind and senses in the purifying process of bhakti,both in sadhanaand in sankirtana.When the mind is progressively absorbed in these services it is purified, and purification empowers progress, which in turn enables greater levels of attentiveness. With increased attentiveness the degree of purification also increases, and the horizons of Krsna consciousness expand without limit.

\* \* \* \*

Let us now look into how attention develops in stages to one- pointed attention, ekagrata,the kind of attention that fully absorbs a devotee in thoughts of Krsna.

When a devotee is cultivating attentiveness in sadhana,then attentiveness becomes part of the primary limb of bhakti, smarana. As the sadhakasystematically develops remembrance of Krsna, attentiveness becomes one of the indicators of how he is progressing in Krsna consciousness.

It should be made clear that attentiveness is the tatastha-laksana of smarana,and purification of the heart is the svarupa-laksana. By attentive chanting a sadhaka’sheart is cleansed and he systematically moves forward to the goal of bhakti,not looking back at the sense enjoyment he left behind, Sukadeva Gosvami describes progressive nama-sankirtanain this way:

*natah param karma-nibandba-krntanam*  
*mumuksatam tirtha-padanukirtanat*  
*na yat punah karmasu sajjate mano*  
*rajas-tamobhyam kalilam tato ’nyatha*

**“Therefore one who desires freedom from material bondage should adopt the process of chanting and glorifying the name, fame, form, and pastimes of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, at Whose feet all the holy places stand. One cannot derive the proper benefit from other methods, such as pious atonement, speculative knowledge, and meditation in mystic yoga,because even after following such methods one takes to fruitive activities again, unable to control his mind, which is contaminated by the base qualities of nature, namely passion and ignorance.”**

Purposeful sadhanais also known as bhajana.This stage of devotional service is a mature cultivation in which a sadhakais keenly aware of the distance separating him from bhava,and so he shoulders a systematic and proactive effort to attain his goal. If he is not yet free of offences, such a sadhakawill soon become so, after which he enters the stage of clearing unwanted things, and the spiritually rewarding stage of pure chanting.

A serious practitioner sees all aspects of his Krsna conscious life, be it chanting Hare Krsna or honouring prasada,as means to his goal. That said, all limbs of devotion must be accompanied and enhanced by nama-sankirtana.Because chanting Hare Krsna is the life of devotional service, our acaryasevaluate systematic advancement in bhakti by a devotee’s proficiency and purity in nama-sankirtana.Following the lead of our predecessors, we shall focus our study of attentive determinations in smaranaas they manifest in a sadhaka’scompetence in chanting Krsna’s divine names.

We now take the opportunity to re-emphasise that the nature of the smaranaof true Gaudiya Vaisnavas is neither the remembrance practised by yogisnor that proposed by pseudo-Vaisnavas. Rather, it is remembrance inspired and empowered by nama-sankirtana.

The better a devotee’s kirtana,the better his remembrance of Krsna and all things related to Him. We request the reader to keep in mind this important truth.

It has been explained previously that there are two kinds of sadhakas:

**The devotees practising regulated devotion and those practising spontaneous devotion.**

Both types of practitioners can ascend to bhavaalong their own preferred path. However, it should be understood that aside from the purely regulated and the purely spontaneous devotees, there will be devotees whose devotion ranges over a blend of regulative and spontaneous. Jiva Gosvami confirms that generally for sadhakaswho have not attained attraction, namely ruci, even the best raganuga-bhaktiis mixed with some elements of *vaidhi-bbakti*. Thus we find that there is a spectrum of practitioners—from the purely spontaneous at one end of the spectrum, to the purely regulated at the other. However, for our purposes we shall call the mainly-regulated half of the spectrum “regulated devotees,” and the other half “spontaneous devotees.”

Let us review the characteristics of both the regulated and spontaneous devotees who journey to, and attain, ecstasy.

The vaidhi-sadhakaenters the domain of smaranaand ascends its stages under the direction of revealed scriptures and his spiritual master. His object of worship is Krsna, the opulent Supreme Personality of Godhead, the cowherd prince, King of Dvaraka, and source of countless incarnations. During nama-sankirtana,such a sadhakagenerally meditates on the beautiful sound of the holy names, and his reading of scripture is not dedicated solely to the pastimes of Vraja, but to all of Krsna’s pastimes. Such a sadhaka’s humble self-conception is that he is a spirit soul, an eternal servant of Krsna. He has no specific role model to follow, or if he does, it is not necessarily a resident of Vraja.

An example of this kind of regulated bhajanais spoken of by the son of Vyasa:

*tasmad bharata sarvatma*  
*bhagavan isvaro harih*  
*srotavyah kirtitavyas ca*  
*smartavyas cecchatabhayam*

**“O descendant of King Bharata, one who desires to be free from all miseries must hear about, glorify, and also remember the Personality of Godhead, who is the Supersoul, the controller, and the saviour from all miseries.”**

We qualify the above by reminding the reader that the description of the regulated devotee is a general one. By the grace of the holy names, any of the regulative qualities mentioned can be enhanced with degrees of spontaneity.

Let us now follow the characteristics of the raganuga-sadhakain his bhajana.

There are two kinds of raganugapractitioner:

**Those who have a level of natural attraction from a previous life, and those who have acquired such attraction in their current life, generally at the stage of taste, ruci.**

We write that raga“generally” appears at ruci,because it may arise at any stage of devotion. However, the majority of devotees who awaken to spontaneous devotion do so when their bhaktimatures to ruci.After all, ragaand ruciare in many ways synonymous. And because the majority of sadhakasdevelop ragain this life, rather than an earlier one, we shall be referring to them as our template for raganuga-sadhakas.

The spiritual impetus for this kind of devotee starts in the way it does for any regulated practitioner. But by association with an advanced devotee, his inspiration for practice shifts from obedience to guruand sastrato attraction for vraja-lila.That does not mean that a devotee does not follow guruand sastra.He does! What it does mean is that the dominant cause of his efforts in sadhanaare his attraction to Krsna, not his obligation to authorities.

The unique quality of a spontaneous devotee is that he worships Krsna exclusively as the son of Nanda and Yasoda. As he progresses in his bhajana,meditation on the sound of the holy names will develop to meditating on Krsna’s form, then His qualities, and finally His pastimes. In pastime meditation, this devotee will progress from the mantropasanaform to the svarasikiform. The former is absorption in one scene or one pastime of Krsna, the latter is absorption in a flowing sequence of pastimes.

The sustenance of a raganuga-sadhaka’smeditation is the subject matter he reads or shares with others. His primary attention is on Krsna’s Vrndavana pastimes, and as he begins to covet a certain type of relationship, then his attention becomes more concentrated by following a certain kind of servant, like the cowherd boys, and then a certain cowherd boy, like Subala.

As a practitioner’s sravanabecomes increasingly focused, so loo does his spiritual identity. He does not simply see himself as Krsna’s servant, but rather he aspires to be a follower of a Vraja associate of Krsna, and that intense aspiration sketches his self-conception. For example, by reading books like Govinda-lilamrta or Vilapa-kusumanjali,a devotee will be attracted to serve Radha-Krsna in the way of the manjarisand he will hanker to become like them, as their follower. The outline of raganuga-bhajanais summarised by Rupa Gosvami in the following verse:

*krsnam smaran janam casya*  
*prestham nija-samihitam*  
*tat-tat-katha-ratas casau*  
*kuryad vasam vraje sada*

**“The devotee should always think of Krsna within himself and should choose a very dear devotee who is a servitor of Krsna in Vrndavana. One should constantly engage in topics about that servitor and his loving relationship with Krsna, and one should live in Vrndavana. If one is physically unable to go to Vrndavana, he should mentally live there.”**

Both the successful vaidhi-and raga-sadhakaswill attain bhava. However, in keeping with the principle that devotional practice and perfection correspond, a vaidhi-bhaktawho attains bhava must also attain greed for vraja-bhaktiin order to qualify as a raganuga-bhava-sadhaka.Such greed will most likely come by associating with an advanced devotee steeped in spontaneous love Additionally, a vaidhi-bhava-sadhakamust read the scriptures that nourish and teach the proper sadhanafor raganuga-bhakti.These things cannot be neglected.

In the absence of greed, even if a devotee has some spontaneous attachment to Krsna, he will be promoted to serve the Queens îf Dvaraka, not the Queen of Vraja. This is the teaching of Rupa Gosvami. Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura adds that a devotee who worships Radha-Krsna in vaidhi-bhaktibut who does not have greed for the forbidden love of the gopisattains the perfection of Vaikuntha-Goloka. That is the place in Goloka where Radha and Krsna are worshipped in majesty, not in sweetness.

An example of a regulated devotee attaining bhavais found in Narada’s description of his ascension through ruciand asaktito love. This elaborate narration is found in Srimad-Bhagavatam. And the example of a spontaneous devotee attaining bhavais in the less well-known description of a Gandharva girl, Candrakanti, who was raised to bhavaby dancing for Krsna. This narration is found in the Padma Purana.

Although a devotee can also attain bhavaby mercy, because such perfections are rare and because this book is about sadhana,we refer readers interested in the subject to Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu.

We shall now describe how, with the assistance of attentive sankalpas,a sadhakacan make the ascension through the stages of nama-bhajana.Our description in this chapter will be general, with subsequent chapters offering a more detailed rendition. Our hope is that these explanations will be of help in the reader’s own bhajana.

\* \* \* \*

We begin with a short overview of how the eightfold yogasystem facilitates meditation. Such study will show the similarity of vaisnava-bhajanato its traditional yogacounterpart in which the depth of meditation corresponds to the depth of attention.

The eightfold system of yoga, astanga-yoga,teaches attentiveness based on the principle of regulating the life airs, which in turn is instrumental to mind control. When meditation on the Supersoul is included in such sadhana,then it gains additional spiritual strength.

The first four stages of astanga-yoga—namely yama, niyama, asana,and pranayamia, or prohibitions, recommendations, sitting postures, and breathing exercises—are regulative practices. They are meant to qualify the yogito enter into the realm of meditation, which is fulfilled by the other four stages, just as the stages of faith to anistha-bhajana-kriyaqualify devotees to begin bhajanain earnest at the stage of steadiness.

At the fifth stage, known as pratyahara,the yogiis able to withdraw from sense objects and place his attention on the object of meditation. This is followed by dharana,which entails a more concentrated absorption, and then dhyana,in which the yogihas attained a proficiency of lengthy meditation that knows no distraction from outside sources. The perfection of such meditation is the eighth stage, which is samadhi.At the culmination of trance, a yogi’sattention is so focused on the object of meditation that he has no awareness of himself, or that he is meditating.

While smaranain bhakti-yogahas similarities to astanga-yoga, our acaryashave extensively described a five-stage development in attentiveness, which culminates in the perfection of going back to Godhead. Because the cultivation of attentiveness in smaranais so important to successful advancement culminating in love, we request our readers to give it special scrutiny, even though the subject is somewhat technical.

In The Nectar of Instruction,Srila Prabhupada quotes Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura’s commentary in which the Thakura enumerates four stages of development up to and including prema. However, in both Jaiva-dharmaand Harinama-cintamani, Bhaktivinoda Thakura repeatedly lists five. The first three stages of both versions correspond, but Sarasvati Thakura appears to combine the last two stages into one, which Bhaktivinoda Thakura calls bhavapana-dasaand prema-sampatti-dasa—the attainment of ecstasy and then of love. Since this book does not go beyond sadhana-bhakti,it is not essential for us to resolve the two differing versions. And since Sarasvati Thakura also names the fourth stage sampatti-dasa,for our limited purposes we propose that his version of this stage also includes Bhaktivinoda Thakura's bhavapana-dasa. In this book we shall refer to the five stages of attentive bhakti presented by Bhaktivinoda Thakura. These stages of absorption in nama-sankirtanaare:

Sravana-dasa,the stage of hearing; varana-dasa,the stage of acceptance, or desiring; smaranavastha,or smarana-dasa,the stage of remembering; bhavapana-dasa ,the stage of attaining ecstasy; and prema- sampatti-dasa,the stage of life’s perfection, prema-bhakti.

Of special interest for our study are the five subdivisions within remembrance, which are:

**Smarana,recollection; dharana,absorption; dhyana, meditation; anusmrti,constant remembrance; and samadhi,trance.**

**Before studying the divisions of sadhanaand smarana,let us review the verse and purport in which they are cited.**

Sri Upadesamrtameans the “nectar of instruction,” and Rupa Gosvami says that verse eight is upadesa-saram,“the essence of all advice or instruction.” The implication is that a close study of this verse reveals rupanuga-bhakti-sadhanain a nutshell. We shall undertake that study in the context of Srila Prabhupada’s purport and the commentary of Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura. That analysis will reveal a clear perspective of bhakti-bhajanaand the qualification for it. Let us first see the verse and translation:

*tan-nama-rupa-caritadi-sukirtananu-*  
*smrtyoh kramena rasana-manasi niyojya*  
*tisthan vraje tad-anuragi jananugami*  
*kalam nayed akhilam ity upadesa-saram*

**“The essence of all advice is that one should utilise one’s full time—twenty-four hours a day—in nicely chanting and remembering the Lord’s divine name, transcendental form, qualities, and eternal pastimes, thereby gradually engaging one’s tongue and mind. In this way one should reside in Vraja \[Goloka Vrndavana-dhama\] and serve Krsna under the guidance of devotees. One should follow in the footsteps of the Lord’s beloved devotees, who are deeply attached to His devotional service.”**

We may note that the first seven verses of Upadesamrtadiscuss the proper conduct of a Vaisnava. The seventh verse addresses those who are afflicted by ignorance—in other words, those who have not yet reached nistha.And the concluding verses of the book, nine to eleven, deal with the good fortune, residence, and bhajanaof the bhava-bhakta.Therefore, verse eight is the bridge between nistha and bhava,and it describes the sadhanathat leads from the former to the latter. To see Srila Prabhupada’s illuminating purport on this verse we refer the reader to Appendix Five.

Sarasvati Thakura prefaces the meaning of the slokaby encouraging neophytes to abandon bad habits through the purificatory process of regulated sadhana.The whole purpose of such practice is to train the mind to think of Krsna, because absorption of the mind governs a devotee’s conduct, his sadhana,and his future destination. Srila Prabhupada cites Krsna’s rule of thumb on mind control, which begins with the phrase yam yam vapi smaran bhavam.

The attainment of mind control is indicated by the word su-kirtana,specifically by the prefix su,which Srila Prabhupada translates as “nicely.” Chanting is nice when it is offenceless, and freedom of offence indicates the stage of nistha.Moreover, because the verse is in the imperative, it initially speaks to the vaidhi-sadhaka.

\* \* \* \*

The following sequence of questions and answers sheds further light on the message of this verse:

**“What happens to the regulative practitioner when he attains steadiness?”**

**“He should train his mind in systematic remembrance through nama-sankirtanaof Krsna’s names as expressed by the phrase, sukirtananu-smrtyoh kramena!While he may not have much taste for the process, he has the requisite purity of mind.”**

**“And what should he be remembering?”**

**“He should remember Krsna’s name! And as he becomes proficient in that, the sadhakawill remember Krsna’s form, qualities, and pastimes as expressed by the phrase, nama-rupa-caritadi.”**

**“How should that sadhanabe practised?”**

**“The devotee should live in Vraja either physically or within his mind. And under the guidance of a devotee experienced in the ways of devotion, he may internally aspire to follow the example of an eternal resident of Vraja, a ragatmika-bhakta.”**

**“What will the development of a devotee’s sadhana look like?”**

**“It is individual and will vary from devotee to devotee! After fulfilling the qualifications of sravana-dasa,a learned sadhakawill come to the conclusion that vraja- bhavais his aspiration. That is varana-dasa.Thereafter follows real sadhanaby the process of remembrance through nama-sankirtana,which is explained in the sections to follow.”**

**“Is it compulsory to embrace vraja-bhakti?”**

**“This verse offers advice! One can choose to worship some other form of Krsna. However, Rupa Gosvami,**

**Srila Prabhupada, and Sarasvati Thakura recommend that one become a follower of a vraja-vasi.That is emphasised by the phrases tisthan vrajeand tad-anuragi jananugami.”**

**“How does raga-bhaktimanifest as one passes through the five steps of smarana-dasa,from smaranato samadhi?”**

**“As mentioned earlier, the sadhakawill begin as a regulated devotee. When he reaches the stage of ruci or asakti,he will probably awaken greed and enter the realm of spontaneous devotion.”**

In support of the answer above we quote Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura:

**“When one has developed such attachment, he can spontaneously serve the lotus feet of Krsna even without following the regulative principles. This stage is called raga-bhakti,or devotional service in spontaneous love.”**

This transition of mood is also confirmed in Srila Prabhupada’s explicit translation that begins with,

**“The essence of all advice is that one should utilise one’s full time—twenty-four hours a day.”**

To be continually absorbed in Krsna in thought and deed is possible only in raganuga-bhakti.

In the prose beginning with tad evam tat-tad-abhimana-laksana- bhava-visesena,Jiva Gosvami also says that the practice of hearing about the devotees of Vraja awakens and develops raganuga- bhakti.

**“When a devotee attains ragadoes his sadhana change?”**

**“While external practices remain the same, the internal meditation develops in many ways. Most notably the earlier general acceptance of vraja-bhaktibecomes very specific at varana-dasa,wherein the sadhakaselects the mood of bhavafor which he aspires, a mood such as friendship or conjugal love.”**

**“What happens if, during sadhana,a devotee’s vaidhi attitude does not change to raga?”**

**“Then he continues according to his inclination. When the regulated devotee attains bhavawithout greed, he will require spiritual guidance to facilitate his transition to raganuga-bhakti.With the help of a raga-guruhe will awaken the desire for a mood of vraja-bhaktiand learn how to concentrate on it.”**

In this regard it should be clear that without raga,one cannot enter Vraja. This principle is recorded by Kaviraja Gosvami as vidhi-marge na paiye vraje krsna-candra:

**“One cannot obtain Krsna in Goloka-Vrndavana simply by serving the Lord according to regulative principles.”**

By regulated worship of Krsna, one may attain the Vaikuntha planet or the liberation of one’s choice. This is because bhakti-yoga is all-powerful and because Krsna very mercifully reciprocates with the desire of His devotees. He says,

**“By performing such regulated devotional service in awe and veneration, one may go to Vaikuntha and attain the four kinds of liberation.”**

But readers should note that a sadhakawill only achieve a perfection that corresponds to his sadhana.It will not be otherwise. Previously we wrote about the qualification and attainment of the vaidhi-sadhakas.For emphasis, and to clarify the misconception that all devotional practices lead to the same destination, we again cite the version of acaryason this subject:

**Rupa Gosvami explains that those attached to vaidhi-sadhana but attracted to the mood of conjugal love will attain a bhava that qualifies them as a Queen of Dvaraka or as an attendant of a queen:**

*riramsam susthu kurvan yo*  
*vidhi-margena sevate*  
*kevalenaiva sa tada*  
*mabisitvam iyat pure*

**“A devotee who serves on the path of vaidhi-bhaktiwith a desire for a conjugal relationship with the Lord and a high position, but without desire for the gopis’type of love, after some time becomes a queen in Dvaraka.”**

In his commentary to this verse, Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura adds that a vaidhi-sadhakawho is more specific in his desire, and who aspires for the service of Radha-Krsna in Vraja, attains a bhavathat qualifies him for service in the portion of Vraja where the Divine Couple are worshipped in wedlock, and in awe and reverence. That part of Goloka-Vrndavana is known as Krsna-vaikuntha-goloka, or simply as Goloka.

And finally, those devotees who worship Radha-Krsna according to the regulative principles and who want to attain raga,but for some reason do not or cannot, will, upon the attainment of ecstasy, have the opportunity to develop the suitable spontaneous mood and advance towards service of the Divine Couple in Vraja.

Thus, in addition to the general attainment of Lord Narayana’s Vaikuntha planets, these are the three perfections available to regulated devotees.

The questions and answers now continue to their completion:

**“Why do you say that a devotee who has attained bhavawill cultivate a mood of bhakti? Is he not already at a perfectional stage?”**

**“A bhava-bhaktais still a sadhaka,a practitioner. Although he has realised his spiritual identity, that identity must develop through stages of bhavaand prema until the attainment of mature devotional mellow, rasa. Such development takes place through cultivation and can be understood from the following example:**

**“Sadhana-bhaktiis like a child in the womb. Bhava- bhaktiis when the child takes birth and has a manifest form. Prema-bhaktiis when the baby grows to adolescence and matures physically and psychologically. And devotional mellow, rasa,is when that adolescent is established in his varnaand asramaand thus has a mature social identity.”**

**“Is there any difference in progress between vaidhi- sadhanaand raga-sadhana?”**

**“There are several, a notable one being the speed at which the practitioner reaches bhava.The path to bhavathrough vaidhiis more protracted than that through raga—it is longer.”**

**“Why is that?”**

**“Because when greed arises in a devotee, he becomes eager for the mood of the vraja-vasis,and thus he more easily abandons material desires. And when greed becomes overpowering, there is absolutely no room for material desires. In this way ragafacilitates the rapid attainment of bhava.”**

**“What happens at the attainment of bhava?"**

**“We have earlier given the explanation with the example of a baby in the womb growing into a fully mature adult: by expert bhajanaand divine grace, the sadhaka rises to bhavapana-dasa,where he attains the actual perfection for which he hankered in the stage of bondage. In this liberated stage he continues his nama-bhajanaand very quickly realises all the aspects of his eternal relationship with Krsna. He develops full prema and enters into his relationship either as a gopaor gopi. That is called sampatti-dasa.”**

Our questions and answers on this topic are now complete.

In our summary of the Upadesamrtaverse and its commentaries, we have attempted to show the roles of both the stages of devotion and the stages of remembrance. A thoughtful devotee will recognise that while Krsna consciousness embraces and encourages all manner of devotion, the gift of Caitanya Mahaprabhu was raganuga-bhakti.It is that cultivation, either in the stage of bondage or liberation, that leads a sadhakainto the company of Krsna’s most dear associates, His vraja-bhaktas.

The distinguishing characteristic of Krsna’s Vrndavana associates is their absolutely spontaneous love for Him. That love is so natural that it submerges all awareness of Krsna’s divinity, knows Him only as the Prince of Vraja, and makes Him a dancing doll in the hands of His devotees. To accept the path to such perfection is the essence of all knowledge, the essence of the Vedas, the essence of all advice.

\* \* \* \*

In Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu,Rupa Gosvami delineates the stages of bhaktibeginning with faith, and lists eight subsequent stages that conclude in prema. Srimad-Bhagavatamemphasises that within these stages, real practice begins with nistha.Devotion from faith to the eradication of most bad habits clears the way for pure faith, and for pure cultivation. In the well-known verse quoted below, the sequence of stages in devotion are sraddha, rati, and bhakti:

*satam prasangan mama virya-samvido*  
*bhavanti hrt-karna-rasayanah kathah*  
*taj-josanad asv apavarga-vartmani*  
*sraddha ratir bhaktir anukramisyati*

**“In the association of pure devotees, discussion of the pastimes and activities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is very pleasing and satisfying to the ear and the heart. By cultivating such knowledge one gradually becomes advanced on the path of liberation, and thereafter he is freed, and his attraction becomes fixed. Then real devotion and devotional service begin.”**

Srila Prabhupada’s purport and the traditional understanding of acaryasis that Srimad-Bhagavatam’sstages sraddha, rati,and bhakticorrespond to Rupa Gosvami's nistha, bhava,and prema. While determinations are relevant from the first stirrings of faith, when faith is firm and when a devotee is purified, then sankalpas really make a significant impact on devotion. A dedicated practitioner then cultivates these effective aspects of sadhana,namely steadiness, taste, and attachment.

Sometimes devotees have a misunderstanding that bhavacan be attained without the proper sequence of cultivation, a sequence that necessitates the development of taste and attachment. Rupa Gosvami describes the compulsory sequence of attainments as follows:

*sadhanabhinivesas tu*  
*tatra nispadayan rucim*  
*harav asaktim utpadya*  
*ratim samjanayaty asau*

**“Absorption in sadhana, nistha,produces ruci,then asakti,and then ratior bhavafor the Lord.”**

To clarify the acarya'sintent, Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura gives his commentary to the verse:

**“Sadhanagives rise to nistha.Without developing ruci and then asakti,how will bhavaarise? This verse answers by saying that one must go through those stages.”**

We will now present this proactive cultivation, which is prefaced by sravana-dasa,begins at varana-dasa,progresses through smarana- dasa,and concludes with bhavapana-dasa.

These stages and their various subdivisions are best seen as steps for sankalpaswhose constant perspective and ultimate goal is ecstatic devotion. And while attentiveness is but a feature of sadhanaat the stages of hearing and acceptance, it is the very substance of sadhanaat the stage of remembrance. More will be said on that topic later.

Readers may remember the unique role of nama-sankirtanain sadhana.The three most important limbs of bhaktiare chanting, hearing, and remembering, the other six being included within these. Similarly, of these three primary limbs, nama-sankirtanais the most important, since hearing and remembering are included in and integral to it. Thus the pre-eminent position of nama-sankirtana makes it the cardinal medium for the cultivation of devotion.

Let us begin by exploring the truths of sravana-dasa,the beginner’s stage of hearing.

Hearing is the foundation of Krsna consciousness. By somehow hearing about Krsna, a person acquires piety, and piety eventually develops into faith. When faith goes beyond a cursory interest, a person develops some enthusiasm to hear about Krsna from advanced Vaisnavas, and that kind of hearing continues to nurture a devotee’s faith until he is willing to act on what he has heard. While such initial inspiration may be weak, and while the devotee may stumble in his resolve to distance himself from maya, the intention is laudable, and it will gradually bear fruit. Krsna explains this to Uddhava:

*badhyamano 'pi mad-bhakto*  
*visayair ajitendriyah*  
*prayah pragalbhaya bhaktya*  
*visayair nabhibhuyate*

**“My dear Uddhava, if My devotee has not fully conquered his senses, he may be harassed by material desires, but because of his unflinching devotion for Me, he will not be defeated by sense gratification.”**

Bhakti-sastrasdescribe that as the seed of devotion begins to sprout, it brings with it many symptoms of auspicious life. Foremost of these symptoms is a devotee’s increasing resolve to hear about Krsna, His teachings, pastimes, and devotees. And to the degree that the practitioner hears, to that extent his faith continues to grow and he engages in service and sadhanaaccordingly.

Ideally a devotee is an ardent hearer. We say “ideally” because that is not always the case in ISKCON. Indeed, experience shows that it may rarely be the case! However, among devotees who are ardent hearers, there are two kinds of sravana:

Methodical hearing and random hearing.

Bhaktivinoda Thakura says that methodical hearing also has different stages, but for the sake of brevity we shall communicate only its general principles.

Methodical hearing is that form of sravanathat is done with a systematic plan and for a specific goal. Of course, both making a plan and setting a goal will vary according to a devotee’s level of advancement. But a plan must be there. As Benjamin Franklin said, “If you fail to plan, you plan to fail.”

An example of methodical hearing for devotees in general is Srila Prabhupada’s temple regimen of studying Srimad-Bhagavatamin the morning and Bhagavad-gitain the evening. This was known as the “iskcon sandwich.” Another example is the books that he translated to further his mission. Those four main books —Bhagavad-gita, Srimad-Bhagavatam, The Nectar of Devotion, and Sri Caitanya-caritamrta— paint a complete, concise, and easily understandable picture of the science and purpose of Krsna consciousness.

A more specific example of methodical hearing is when a devotee desires to understand the ultimate purpose of Krsna consciousness and how to attain it. He makes a plan to systematically study Srila Prabhupada’s books starting with Bhagavad-gita,then Srimad-Bhagavatam, then The Nectar of Devotion,and concluding with Sri Caitanya-caritamrta.Additionally, he hears from and associates with devotees who have a similar interest, and better yet, with those who are realised in such study.

Methodical hearing continues when, having understood that the mission of Caitanya Mahaprabhu was to reveal the long-hidden science of raganuga-vraja-bhakti,a devotee makes a plan to methodically learn how raganuga-bhaktiis practised. To this end he reviews relevant books like Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhuand hears from Vaisnavas steeped in the practice, primarily his own spiritual master.

Furthermore, if that devotee finds himself drawn to the activities of manjaris,then he will study how they serve by reading the books of our acaryasand taking guidance from his spiritual master. Srila Prabhupada indicates methodical hearing in his translation of this verse of Narottama Dasa Thakura:

*rupa-raghunatha-pade hoibe akuti*  
*kabe hama bujhabo se yugala-piriti*

**“When shall I be very much eager to study the books left by the Six Gosvamis, headed by Srila Rupa Gosvami and Srila Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami? By their instruction I shall be able to properly understand the loving affairs of Radha and Krsna.”**

Following this systematic approach to sravana,a devotee studies and hears relevant subject matter and associates with Vaisnavas who share his goal. The more a devotee advances spiritually, the more he becomes determined in sadhana,specifically in his methodical hearing. The advantage of such systematic hearing is that it gives the devotee increasing exposure to Krsna’s pastimes and to devotional mellows, rasas.Spiritual master permitting, the sadhaka may begin hearing Krsna’s eightfold daily pastimes known as His asta-kaliya-lila,as it is described in books like Govinda-lilamrta.

By hearing Krsna’s pastimes, devotees increasingly taste their sweetness, and for some, the inspiration for spontaneous devotion will arise. For others it may do so later, or not at all!

Regulated devotees will show great respect for Krsna’s pas times and will be slower to progress in hearing of His confidential dealings, especially with the gopis.Even if they feel attraction toward vraja-bhakti,fear of not deviating from the path and concern for the opinion of others will curb the inclination to develop vraja-bhakti.The destination of such devotees has already been explained in the previous section.

For those devotees who are enchanted by the loving devotion of the cowherd boys or the young gopis,an eagerness will gradually awaken in their hearts, as will the desire to someday attain a similar service and affection for Krsna. These will be the raganuga-sadhakas,who will then continue to take further systematic guidance from their realised spiritual master. The steady yearning for vraja-bhaktiwill guide the sadhakaalong the path leading to the fulfilment of that yearning.

\* \* \* \*

The following verse of Srimad-Bhagavatamemphasises the importance of methodical hearing, as does Srila Prabhupada’s commentary:

*ya yah katha bhagavatah*  
*kathaniyoru-karmanah*  
*guna-karmasrayah pumbhih*  
*samsevyas ta bubhusubhih*

**“Those who are desirous of achieving complete perfection in life must submissively hear all topics that are connected with the transcendental activities and qualities of the Personality of Godhead, Who acts wonderfully.”**

Srila Prabhupada comments:

**“The systematic hearing of the transcendental activities, qualities, and names of Lord Sri Krsna pushes one towards eternal life. Systematic hearing means knowing Him gradually in truth and fact, and this knowing Him in truth and fact means attaining eternal life, as stated in the Bhagavad-gita.Such transcendental, glorified activities of Lord Sri Krsna are the prescribed remedy for counteracting the process of birth, death, old age, and disease, which are considered to be material awards for the conditioned living being. The culmination of such a perfectional stage of life is the goal of human life and the attainment of transcendental bliss.”**

Thakura Bhaktivinoda says that in order to properly engage in the further stages of sadhana-bhakti,a devotee must have heard methodically. It is to state the obvious when we say that methodical sravana-dasais attentive devotion. It is attentive because of the systematic effort a devotee must exercise to practise it, and it is attentive because a devotee carefully assimilates the message that Srila Prabhupada and our acaryasteach.

In our earlier dissertation on sambandha-jnana,we emphasised that the foundational knowledge of relationships is essential to understanding the truths of sadhanaand to putting those truths into practice. Such sambandha-jnanais therefore the foundation of systematic hearing.

We now come to random hearing, the other kind of sravana- dasa.

When reading is done without a systematic plan or purpose other than to “become Krsna conscious,” that is called random sravana.

Practitioners who read in this way will study Srila Prabhupada’s books out of a sense of duty or taste, and if they do that regularly, their reading may transform to a methodical mode. But because random sravanayields a distant perspective of the goal, such practitioners also risk losing their enthusiasm for hearing altogether.

Thus random sravanalacks the determined effort of systematic hearing. Moreover, because the connection with Krsna’s pastimes is not conscious, prolonged, and properly understood, random hearing rarely awakens eagerness for any serious devotion, what to speak of an eagerness for raganuga-bhakti.Keeping in mind Bhaktivinoda Thakura’s assertion that only methodical sravana leads to progressive sadhana,random sravanaat its best leads to its counterpart. Until that time, a devotee’s sadhanaremains restricted. In other words, while hearing about Krsna is always purifying, the speed of purification varies greatly between methodical and unsystematic hearing.

It is hard to categorise random hearing as being attentive. Although a devotee may be hearing or reading with attention, because he does not assemble the contents of what he hears into a structured sadhana,full attentiveness and its benefits allude him. As already mentioned, the true gain of random sravanais that it qualifies and purifies a devotee for methodical sravana.In the absence of that good fortune, random hearing over a prolonged period of time places a sadhakaat risk.

In his Krama-sandarbha,Sri Jiva Gosvami explains that Srimad-Bhagavatamis not meant for casual study or random hearing. He defends the supreme dominance of the paribhasa-sutra, which begins with ete camsa-kalah pumsah,and which dictates the perspective from which not only the Srimad-Bhagavatambut the entire Vedas should be understood.

Once Krsna, Who appeared and played in Vrndavana, is accepted as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, then it follows that His pastimes, associates, and loving exchanges, as well as the means to know these, are both peerless and the goal of all knowledge. Thus, hearing is a systematic process that should be recognised and sought out. Jiva Gosvami writes, parama-artba-vastu-parvatvac ca sri-bhagavatasya tatrapy arthikatvac ca tasya paribhasayah:

**“Srimad-Bbagavatamdescribes the ultimate phase of the Absolute Truth and the supreme goal of life. It is not a loose collection of nice stories for casual reading. The weightiness of the subject matter of the Srimad-Bhagavatamdemands that it be prefaced by a paribhasa-sutrato explain the subject matter to follow.”**

We have described the two categories of sravana-dasaand the two types of devotee who hear of Krsna. From that description it is clear that there is little hope of progressive devotion for the devotee who does not fit into either category—the devotee who has little or no interest in hearing. Needless to say, the non-reader remains in the neophyte sphere until that time as he is somehow prompted to become more serious in spiritual life.

The stage of sravana-dasa,especially methodical hearing, may be said to correspond to the first five stages of bhakti—sraddha, sadhu-sanga , bhajana-kriya, anartha-nivrtti,and nistha.It is a staircase to advanced sadhana.Obviously making each step requires one or multiple sankalpas,and how well each sankalpais made will determine how accurately a sadhakaprogresses and how easily he grasps the next spiritual challenge ahead of him.

And so it is until, by the continued hearing of Krsna’s pastimes, a devotee becomes intensely desirous of entering them. Having ascended to the summit of sravana-dasa,the sadhakaenters the next phase of his journey to bhava,the phase delineated by varana-dasa.

To summarise, sravana-dasais about a devotee hearing from sadhu, sastra,and guru.The purpose of the hearing is to acquire a clear picture of what his path to bhavais and what major sankalpashe will have to make to reach bbava.Until that maturity of knowledge is attained, a practitioner’s chanting and meditations are limited in their development. Both regulated and spontaneous devotees advance to their goal. However, the ideal is that a sadhaka awakens to spontaneous service, which is both efficient and effective in attaining perfection. Whichever the case, inspired by knowledge or by attraction, both vaidhi-and raga-sadhakasarrive at the culmination of sravana-dasawhen they resolutely desire to enter the pastimes of the Lord through systematic hearing. How a practitioner continues his journey is presented in the following chapter.

## Chapter Twenty-Seven

**Acceptance and Remembrance**

What follows is an overview of the stage of varana-dasa.As the stage of acceptance that precedes smarana,remembrance, varana-dasais the foundation for a practitioner’s nama-bhajana.

The devotee who is attentive in sravanareaches a conclusion, which then leads him to the most significant sankalpaof his devotional career. That determination is something like:

**“As a servant of the Lord, I am keen to serve like a cowherd boy!”**

The stage of varanais where a devotee embraces a relatively specific spiritual identity, in which he serves and follows an eternal associate of the Lord. This is the process outlined by Rupa Gosvami with the words tad-anuragi jananugami:

**“One should follow in the footsteps of the Lord’s beloved devotees, who are deeply attached to His devotional service.”**

Needless to say, the phrase “I am keen to serve like a cowherd boy” is not like the childish speculation of a boy who dreams of being an airplane pilot or a football star. After studying sastraand hearing from saints, after understanding the conclusion of what he has learned, and after being inspired by a specific kind of service to a form of Krsna, a devotee decides that that is the kind of perfection after which he aspires, and so he adopts a sadhanaconsistent with that aspiration.

The words “acceptance” and “desiring" are quite symbolic of the meaning of varana.

The word varanais based on the verbal root vrwhich means “to choose,” “to desire,” and “to enclose.” When a devotee intensely desires a thoughtfully chosen identity within which he fully encloses himself, he has reached the stage of acceptance.

To give added clarity, a similar noun from the verbal root vr, varnameans “colour,” “appearance,” and “form.” When a sadhakais coloured by a self-conception in which he aspires after a spiritual form and mood similar to that of his role model, he has reached varana-dasa.

A sadhakawill, at varana-dasa,embrace an attainment corresponding to his current aspiration. We say “current” because despite its eminence, varana-dasais still a stage of bondage, and thereat the desires of a devotee—be he regulated or spontaneous- are subject to error. Only at the stage of bhavado those desires become fine-tuned and correspond with transcendental reality.

The following is an example of a very specific varanathat has deep personal significance for Caitanya Mahaprabhu, and which His followers enthusiastically embrace:

*naham vipro na ca nara-patir napi vaisyo na sudro*  
*naham varni na ca grha-patir no vana-stho yatir va*  
*kintu prodyan-nikhila-paramananda-purnamrtabdher*  
*gopi-bhartuh pada-kamalayor dasa-dasanudasah*

**“I am not a brahmana,I am not a ksatriya,I am not a vaisyaor a sudra.Nor am I a brahmacari,a householder, a vanaprastha,or a sannyasi.I identify myself only as the servant of the servant of the servant of the lotus feet of Lord Sri Krsna, the maintainer of the gopis.He is like an ocean of nectar, and He is the cause of universal transcendental bliss. He is always existing with brilliance.”**

The following paragraphs exemplify varana-dasaand explain the restriction on the process being described.

In his Hari-nama-cintamani,Thakura Bhaktivinoda describes how a raganuga-sadhakawho comes to know of the eleven attributes, ekadasa-bhavas,of the Vraja-vasis, enters the stage of varana-dasa.

A Vraja-vasi is identified by eleven characteristic traits that apply equally to gopasand gopis,which are:

**Relationship, age, name, form, group, garments, service, residence, fidelity \[to a group leader\], highest aspiration \[for mercy\], and underlying nature.**

For details on these bhavaswe refer the reader to Bhaktivinoda Thakura’s Jaiva-dharma.

When a pure-hearted practitioner expresses an attraction to follow a resident of Vraja, his spiritual master will consider whether his disciple is qualified or not. If the disciple is eligible, the fully-realised guruwill empower his disciple with a specific set of ekadasa-bhavas.Acceptance means that the sadhakaembraces these eleven attributes as the basis for his spiritual identity and subsequent meditations. Vaisnava writings describe how such a confidential exchange took place in times past.

But, that is no longer the case!

Why that is so requires some attention, and before we continue our study into varana,this brief diversion is necessary, because while revelation of the eleven bhavasis authentic, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura and Srila Prabhupada deemed the process unsuited to preaching Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s mission. They favoured an equally authentic approach that was also approved of by Bhaktivinoda Thakura, which was to encourage devotees to engage in bhajanaand service of the holy names.

There are good reasons why Srila Prabhupada and Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati discontinued this process for their institutions and considered it too risky for the guru-disciple relationship.

The practice of bestowing the eleven bhavas,also known as siddha-pranali,requires that the spiritual master actually realises his own eternal form, and that the disciple is suitably pure in spontaneous devotion.

However, in a worldwide preaching mission all spiritual masters will not be siddhas.Indeed, because uttama-adhikarisare rare, they will be the exception and not the rule. And yet Srila Prabhupada would say that to bring Krsna consciousness to the world “we require many millions of gurus." That means that both kanistha- and madhyama-adhikarismay take up the service of guru,but they cannot offer the eleven bhavas.To do so would be nothing but unproductive imitation.

Additionally, disciples generally lack the requisite qualification to receive such a meditation. And even if qualified gurusand disciples did exist, were those gurusto give the eleven bhavasto some and not to others, the preaching effort would be soiled with envy, com petition, cheating, and endless ills.

Unfortunately, the historical reality is that by the unqualified application of this siddha-pranaliprocess, malpractice appeared in Gaudiya Vaisnavism soon after Lord Caitanya’s departure. And over the centuries, authentic acaryasrepeatedly had to save the sampradayafrom the influence of such deviants. That influence and its dangers continue to the present day. Thus, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura offered a safer form of bhajanafor his disciples and followers, and he made known his opinion of those who still stuck to the sacred and confidential path of siddha-pranali:

**“Those who have attained perfection in their bhajana have realised their own constitutional position. But nowadays in the Gaudiya Vaisnava sampradayasome immature pancaratrika-mantratraders are presenting imaginary material names and forms as the goal of life and the path of perfection (siddha-pranali); in this way they gratify the minds of their disciples as well as disclose their own foolishness and ignorance of the Vaisnava literatures.”**

What is the approved alternative for sadhakaswho are eager to accept vraja-bhakti,or other forms of devotion?

The answer is given in Srimad-Bhagavatam.Constant chanting and service to the holy name of the Lord, sankirtana,will be the process that reveals all necessities to attain ecstasy, including the eleven bhavas:

*krsna-varnam tvisakrsnam*  
*sangopangastra-parsadam*  
*óajnaih sankirtana-prayair*  
*yajanti hi su-medhasah*

**“In the age of Kali, intelligent persons perform congregational chanting to worship the incarnation of Godhead Who constantly sings the names of Krsna. Although His complexion is not blackish, He is Krsna Himself. He is accompanied by His associates, servants, weapons, and confidential companions.”**

While this verse may be satisfying to most readers, some may require further elaboration. We shall offer the same, based on the overall context presented in the verses preceding and following it.

Readers will recall that this verse is spoken by Karabhajana Rsi in response to Maharaja Nimi’s enquiries, which include kena vidhina pujyate:

**“By what process is the Lord worshipped?” The answer given is:**

**“Congregational chanting of the Lord’s names.”**

But one may doubt whether this process of worship includes the very confidential sadhanathat results in vraja-bhava.

In a subsequent verse the sage continues to address such a doubt by saying, yatra sankirtanenaiva sarva-svartho ’bhilabhyate:

**“...all perfection of life can easily be achieved by the performance of sankirtana.”**

We may note here that “all perfection,” sarva-sva-artha,can be attained by chanting the holy names. The singular word “all” must certainly include all and any perfection a worshipper may desire. Moreover, these verses are in the Eleventh Canto, whereat Srimad-Bhagavatamhas already described perfections in vaidhi-bhakti, raganuga-bhakti, vraja-bhakti,and gopi-bhava.Thus there can be little doubt that “all perfections” includes every perfection narrated.

To reaffirm that “all perfections” includes the highest perfection, Karabhajana then concludes his train of thought:

*na hy atah paramo labho*  
*dehinam bhramyatam iha*  
*yato vindeta paramam*  
*santim nasyati samsrtih*

**“Indeed, there is no higher possible gain for embodied souls forced to wander throughout the material world than the Supreme Lord’s sankirtanamovement, by which one can attain the supreme peace and free oneself from the cycle of repeated birth and death.”**

With the echo of the phrase na by atah paramo labho,“Indeed, there is no higher possible gain,” is there any room left to doubt that nama-sankirtanacan fulfil any perfection desired by any sadhana?

For the reasonable devotee the answer will be, “There is no doubt that nama-sankirtanaoffers every perfection!”

And yet some so-called seekers or sadhakaswant something that outwardly appears more esoteric or mystical.

These devotees are impatient. Having heard of subject matter that they should not have heard and which they do not understand, they want to enter a realm of bhajanafor which they have no eligibility. If such devotees actually embark on this premature sadhana, they also inherit the honorific title of sahajiya,a person who takes things cheaply. Srila Prabhupada would say, “Sahajiyameans persons who take things very easily.”

To “take things very easily” means to want something without paying the actual price for it, like buying a diamond with loose change. But the principle of bhakti,indeed of life, is sve sve ’dhikare ya nistha,that one has the right to that for which one has qualification. In Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura’s words, “First deserve, then desire.” Unfortunately, some obstinate neophytes contravene this law of devotion, and of course there are charlatans who are ready to pamper their illusions with promises of ekadasa-bhava, asta-kaliya-lila smarana, svarupa-siddhi,and manjari-bhava.The result is a potpourri of sahajiya-cheatersand sahajiya-cheated. Thakura Bhaktivinoda gives a list of thirteen varieties of such deviant practitioners: aula, baula, karttdbhaja, neda, daravesa, sani, sahajiya, sakhibheki, smarta, jata-gosani, ativadi, cudadhari,and gauranga-nagari.

\* \* \* \*

As previously mentioned, the original process of smaranaand other confidential perfections, such as ekadasa-bhavaor manjari-bhava, are not unauthentic or foreign to Gaudiya Vaisnavas. Indeed, these practices were first introduced and practised by Gaudiya acaryas.The earlier cited verses of Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhuare evidence of this.

Furthermore, Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s conversation with Kamananda Raya indicates that siddha-deha smaranaand adopting gopi-bhavawere practices predating even Rupa Gosvami's composition. For example, in his conversation with the Lord, Ramananda Raya said,

*ataeva gopi-bhava kari angikara*  
*ratri-dina cinte radba-krsnera vihara*

**“Therefore, one should accept the mood of the gopisin their service. In such a transcendental mood, one should always think of the pastimes of Sri Radha and Krsna.**

*siddha-dehe cinti’ kare tabanni sevana*  
*sakhi-bhave paya radha-krsnera carana*

**“After thinking of Radha and Krsna and Their pastimes for a long time and after getting completely free from material contamination, one is transferred to the spiritual world. There the devotee attains an opportunity to serve Radha and Krsna as one of the gopis.**

*gopi-anugatya vina aisvarya-jnane*  
*bhajileha nahi paya vrajendra-nandane*

**“Unless one follows in the footsteps of the gopis,he cannot attain the service of the lotus feet of Krsna, the son of Nanda Maharaja. If one is overcome by knowledge of the Lord’s opulence, he cannot attain the Lord’s lotus feet, even though he is engaged in devotional service.”**

In his purport to the above verse, Srila Prabhupada does not hide Gaudiya Vaisnavas’ support for the sambandhaand prayojanaof vraja-bhaktiand the means of its attainment. He writes,

**“One can worship Laksmi-Narayana by the process of vidhi-marga,worshipping the Lord with regulative principles according to the instructions of the sastra and the spiritual master. But the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Radha-Krsna, cannot be directly worshipped by this process. The dealings between Radha and Krsna and the gopisare devoid of the opulences of Laksmi-Narayana. The process of vidhi-marga,following the regulative principles, is utilised in the worship of Laksmi-Narayana, whereas the process of spontaneous service—following in the footsteps of the gopis,who are the denizens of Vrndavana—is transcendentally more advanced and is the process whereby Radha and Krsna are worshipped. One cannot attain this elevated position while worshipping the Lord in His opulence. Those attracted by the conjugal love between Radha and Krsna must follow in the footsteps of the gopis. Only then is it possible to enter into the Lord’s service in Goloka Vrndavana and directly associate with Radha and Krsna.”**

What is at the heart of contention for the followers of Sarasvati Thakura is the abhidheyaby which vraja-bhaktiis made available to people today through a worldwide preaching mission. What may have been practised or even commonplace in the past cannot automatically be transplanted to the twenty-first century. The blind implementation of spiritual practices is against the very spirit of Vedic injunctions, which serve to offer an authorised process of purification that is most applicable to the peoples of a specific time, place, and circumstance.

Through the four ages, the core religious principle changes from meditation in Satya-yuga to sankirtanain Kali-yuga. What worked for everyone in the golden age works for no one in the iron age. In Kali-yuga people do not have the life duration, peaceful environment, or sattvikanature required for successful meditation; the process for self-realisation has changed from a regimen of silence and inactivity to one of music and dance. And yet the outcome of both remains the same.

Similarly, with each age, and perhaps even within the division of ages, circumstances may change in ways that require adjustment to the details of the abhidheyaenabling liberation. Making such adjustment is the duty and the right of an acarya.This was the example shown our paramparaby Caitanya Mahaprabhu. Kaviraja Gosvami writes,

*saba nistarite prabhu krpa-avatara*  
*saba nistarite kare caturi apara*

**“Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu appeared in order to deliver all the fallen souls. Therefore He devised many methods to liberate them from the clutches of maya.”**

Five hundred years ago, most sadhakasof India may have been pious enough and cultured enough to adopt raganuga-sadhanaand lila-smarana.Today Indians have lost those assets, and so, like the rest of the world, they are encouraged to engage in vaidhi-sadhana and nama-sankirtana.However, when performed systematically and purely, the result of these two practices is the same as that of raganuga-sadhanaand lila-smarana:they lead to mature bhavain the wake of the Vraja-vasis. Vaidhimanifests spontaneous devotion in sadhana,and nama-sankirtanadoes so in bhava.What must be common to both is proper knowledge of sambandha, abhidheya, and prayojana,and diligent fidelity to sadhana.Should there be a lack in those, then practitioners cannot expect their desired sadhya

And that is the core message of this book: a devotee must be knowledgeable in and attentive to the science of sadhanaand the conscientious sankalpashe has to make to cultivate sadhanato its perfection. If a devotee is flying blind and does not know where hr is going, a best-case scenario is he ends up in one of the Vaikuntha planets.

Having emphasised the practice of educated vaidhi-sadhanafor most devotees, this book must also bring to the reader’s attention that raganuga-sadhanacannot be outlawed in iskcon.

If spontaneity arises in a devotee’s heart, it must be embraced as good fortune and not exorcised as heresy. As long as sadhanacor responds to qualification, spontaneous devotion may be accepted as the natural outcome of past piety, good practices, and serious study.

Those who are not inspired in a spontaneous way should none theless be knowledgeable in and respectful of the existence of such a spiritual reality. Moreover, devotees of both persuasions should hear from Srila Prabhupada’s books, for His Divine Grace’s writing are replete with teachings and pastimes meant to awaken in devotees an eagerness for vraja-bhaktiat some point in their journey to Krsna.

In the sections above we have attempted to warn the reader that varana-dasais not a matter of immature speculation. The stage of acceptance is for learned devotees who have reached the stage of nisthaor ruciand come to a conclusion on how they would like to serve Krsna eternally. The majority, vaidhi-bhaktas,will embrace their service with a sense of reverence, while the rarer, raganuga-bhaktas,with a sense of intimacy. In either case, these devotees will be qualified to enter the stage of smarana,the keenly attentive chanting of Krsna’s holy names.

\* \* \* \*

We have reviewed both sravana-dasaand varana-dasaas the first two steps of devotional service leading to smarana-dasa,the stage of remembrance. To have a well-rounded picture of how a devotee cultivates remembrance to the stage where it is his reality, the following pages outline seven characteristics of smarana.These are:

Remembrance facilitated by and through nama- sankirtana;the principles of smarana;how remembrance is cultivated; the five stages of cultivation; the mood of cultivation—separation; the bestowal of divine grace; and, ultimate perfection.

This current part of this book, Part Six, will describe the first four of these characteristics, Part Seven the mood of cultivation, and Part Eight the last two. In this way Sankalpa-kaumudiis complete.

The way in which nama-bhajanaguides a practitioner to bhava is described by Krsna in the following verse:

*yatha yathatma parimrjyate ’sau*  
*mat-punya-gatha-sravanabhidhanaih*  
*tatha tatha pasyati vastu suksmam*  
*caksur yathaivanjana-samprayuktam*

**“When a diseased eye is treated with medicinal ointment it gradually recovers its power to see. Similarly, as a conscious living entity cleanses himself of material contamination by hearing and chanting the pious narrations of My glories, he regains his ability to see Me, the Absolute Truth, in My subtle spiritual form.”**

How much attention a devotee gives to chanting the names of Krsna is the degree to which his consciousness becomes pure and his perception of transcendental reality clear. This is also confirmed by Lord Caitanya with the words ceto-darpana-marjanam.

In our presentation of smarana-dasawe shall follow the outline of Bhaktivinoda Thakura as found in Jaiva-dbarmaand Harinama-cintamani.However, those books concentrate on raganuga-sadhakas,whereas this book addresses both the regulated and the spontaneous practitioners—the latter being in the minority.

While devotees will practise attentiveness from the very beginning stages of bhakti,real smaranawill be effective at the stage of firm steadiness. A practitioner should he qualified by dint of his service and surrender, and more or less freed of past bad hah its. This is a reliable standard for both regulated and spontaneous devotees.

The English word “remembrance” does not fully capture the meaning of smarana.Generally it is used to indicate awareness of someone or something from the past. But smaranais very much about a happening in the present. It is about absorption in an activity, primarily chanting or hearing. Indeed, part of attentiveness is to not be distracted by the past. Of course, in another way remembrance can be used to recall He Whom we have long forgotten Krsna. However, that is a secondary usage.

The word smaranahas smras its verbal root, which means “to remember,” “to recollect,” and “to bear in mind.” The suffix ana transforms it to a noun, meaning remembrance, in the way that the root kirtis transformed to kirtanaor sruto sravana.In terms of nama-bhajana,the concept of “bearing in mind” suits the import of smaranawell. Srila Prabhupada even translated it as “memoris ing,” which means to embed something within the mind. Highly suitable!

For Gaudiya Vaisnavas at the stage of smarana-dasa,remembrance is when the mind becomes the instrument with which, and in which, Krsna’s attributes are minutely studied. Krsna gives this idea as a general definition;

*etavan yoga adisto*  
*mac-chisyaih sanakadibhih*  
*sarvato mana akrsya*  
*mayy addhavesyate yatha*

**“The actual yogasystem as taught by My devotees, headed by Sanaka-kumara, is simply this: having withdrawn the mind from all other objects, one should directly and appropriately absorb it in Me.”**

Such absorption enables a practitioner to approach his desired goal of ecstatic devotion. Indeed, it is said that Krsna gives Himself to the devotee who remembers His lotus feet. Obviously such benefit means that Krsna will also give any losser attainment, and that includes unlimited opulence and even liberation. Pure devotees, however, have no interest in such things. They only want Krsna.

And while remembrance may entail scrutinising study of and deliberation on scripture, or absorption in the form and pastimes of the Lord, Jiva Gosvami emphasises that the best and indispensable way to practise smaranais immersion in Krsna’s holy names.

Progressive stages of smaranarequire mature and educated determinations, the principles of which have been described in earlier chapters. We refer again to our role model, Gopa-kumara, who progressed to his objective by repeated absorption in his diksa-mantra,which was comprised of the names of the Lord.
