Remembrance of, remembrance in, and remembrance with nama- sankirtanais, in the words of Srimad-Bhagavatam,“the doubtless and fearless way of success for all.” The following two sections will now explore the pre-eminence of nama-sankirtanain the stage of smarana-dasa.

Caitanya Mahaprabhu descended to make known the glories of chanting the Hare Krsna maha-mantra.He summarised those truths in His own Siksastakaand instructed His followers to elaborate on it more fully. In pursuance of those teachings, a devotee is introduced to chanting from the very beginning of his spiritual life, and he continues to do so through the stages of devotion—sravana, varana, smarana, apana,and sampatti.And while the mantra remains the same, the quality and depth of chanting—one measure of which is attentiveness—matures.

During the stages of sadhana,chanting is meant to awaken bhava,however at apana-dasa,the chanting is a result of both effort and ecstasy. And when perfection, sampatti,is attained, sankirtana is the effect of an ever-increasing and constantly over-pouring love.

In Bhakti-sandarbha,Jiva Gosvami shines the spotlight on nama-sankirtanaas the source of empowerment for all forms of devotion, including smarana.

The acaryawrites, yad anyapi bhaktih kalau kartavya tada tat-samyogenaivety uktam:

**“If one performs any other type of bhaktiin Kali-yuga, it should be accompanied by kirtana.”**

While chanting the holy names is equally potent in every age, in Kali-yuga it has been given special significance by the Lord Himself, in that it must accompany all other limbs of bhakti Returning to our earlier reference of Karabhajana Rsi’s response, to Maharaja Nimi, the word prayaihin the phrase yajnaih sankirtana-prayairindicates that even when other services are being offered to the Lord, they must be accompanied by sankirtana. Thus chanting enables and empowers smarana.

A very important point should now be made!

To succeed in smaranaa devotee need not make any artificial efforts at remembrance. The lotus of smarana-dasawill natural!) unfold by attentive hearing of the maha-mantra.We emphasise this point because while some devotees may make conscious efforts in stages of remembrance, many will prefer to simply meditate on the beautiful sound vibration of Krsna’s names. Those devotees should be reassured that by this one attentive activity, they will be trails ported by the vimanaof nama-sankirtanathrough the airways of smarana.

In his commentary on Srimad-Bhagavatam,Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura makes a relevant and important comment to the following verse:

*srnvatah sraddhaya nityam*  
*grnatas ca sva-cestitam*  
*kalena natidirghena*  
*bhagavan visate hrdi*

**“Persons who hear Srimad-Bhagavatamregularly and are always taking the matter very seriously will have the Personality of Godhead Sri Krsna manifested in their hearts within a short time.”**

The acaryawrites,

**“Effort in remembering Krsna is not necessary for the devotee who hears and chants. Even without great effort, the Lord spontaneously enters into the heart. Hearing and chanting here indicates remembering.”**

Further evidence of the supremacy and independence of nama-sankirtana can be seen by the power invested in the holy name.

The Lord says, “Without a doubt, I forgive millions of offences of a person who chants My name with faith.”

If the holy name nullifies offences to other limbs of devotion, then it is clearly both superior to and independent of them. Veritably, it is the king of devotion that governs over its subjects, Conversely, if a devotee makes an offence to the holy name, no act of atonement or devotion—not even Krsna Himself—can nullify the offence. Only the holy name can forgive offences to itself.

Readers may question why they should delve into the details of smarana,such as the five stages described by Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati, if hearing the holy name fulfils and accomplishes everything.

The answer is twofold.

Firstly, there are some sadhakaswho want to cultivate smarana. Secondly, to fully benefit from chanting a mantra,practitioners should know the truths underlying the mantra:its sadhanaand its sadhya.That is called mantrartha-cintana.

Both Srila Prabhupada and his Guru Maharaja emphasised that a foundation for successful sadhanastarts with a well-rounded understanding of sambandha-jnana.Without a grasp of Bhagavad-gita,a devotee would be at a loss to chant offencelessly, what to speak of with true feeling. The same can be said about abhidheya and prayojana.There is a science to the cultivation of nama-sankirtana just as there is a science to the purpose of chanting. Chanting is not a lazy man’s business!

\* \* \* \*

Another indispensable aspect of nama-sankirtanathat should be mentioned is praying for the mercy of the holy names.

Chanting itself is a prayer for service, and as such it is to be voiced in a prayerful and reverential way. Furthermore, in the realm of the absolute there is no difference between Krsna and His names. Praying to the name of the Lord is as indispensable an aspect of a devotee’s sadhanaas prayer to Krsna. Srila Prabhupada encouraged devotees to precede their sankirtanawith a prayer to the holy name, citing the following verse of Rupa Gosvami:

*narada-vinojjivana*  
*sudbormi-niryasa-maidhuri-pura*  
*tvam krsna-nama kamam*  
*sphura me rasane rasena sada*

**“O life of Narada’s vina! O flood of the waves of sweet nectar! O Holy Name of Lord Krsna! Please manifest your enchanting, nectarean sweetness on my tongue.”**

Based on the foundations of knowledge and mercy, sincere effort in nama-sankirtanacertainly yields all perfections. That is the assurance of Srimad-Bhagavatam.

By offenceless chanting the false ego is systematically dissolved the sadhakarealises his siddha-deha,and he becomes eligible for spontaneous asta-kaliya-lilameditations. This is the import of the verse cited earlier beginning with yatha yathatma parimrjyate ’sau.Because perfected devotees, siddhaslike Haridasa Thakura, embraced nama-bhajanaas their path, pranali,to perfection, chanting Hare Krsna is the flawless siddha-pranaliof Gaudiya Vaisnavas.

We should clarify that sankirtanaof the maha-mantrais not “another” siddha-pranali.According to Caitanya Mahaprabhu it is the “only” siddha-pranalifor people in general in Kali-yuga.

This truth is exemplified by a pastime in the Caitanya-bhagavata in which the Lord enjoins the residents of Navadvipa to chant the maha-mantra.Indeed, the Lord speaks the words of the mantra and proclaims it the “maha-mantra.” Thereafter He makes the following statement in which He affirms that chanting grants all perfection, and that nothing else is required:

*iha haite sarva-siddbi haibe sabara*  
*sarva-ksana bala’ ithe vidbi nabi ara*

**“By doing so everyone will attain all perfection. Always chant, there is no other prescription.”**

In his Saranagati,Thakura Bhaktivinoda discloses the details of how this perfection unfolds. Because of its beauty and the wealth of conclusive truths contained within it, we include the entire song below:

*krsna-nama dhare koto bal*  
*visaya-vasananale, mora citta sada jvale,*  
*ravi-tapta maru-bhumi-sam*  
*karna-randhra-patha diya, hrdi majhe pravesiya,*  
*varisoya sudha anupam*

**“What power does the name of Krsna possess? My heart constantly burns in the fire of worldly desires like a desert scorched by the rays of the sun. Entering through the holes of my ears to the core of my heart, the holy name showers unparalleled nectar upon my soul.**

*hrdoya hoite bole, jihvara agrete cale,*  
*sabda-rupe nace anuksan*  
*kanthe mora bhange svara, anga kanpe thara thara,*  
*sthira hoite na pare caran*

**“The holy name speaks from within my heart, moves onto the tip of my tongue, and constantly dances on it in the form of transcendental sound. My throat becomes choked up, my body violently shivers, and my feet cannot remain still.**

*cakse dhara, dehe gharma, pulakita saba carma,*  
*vivarna hoilo kalevara*  
*murchita hoilo man, pralayera agaman,*  
*bhave sarva-deha jara jara*

**“Rivers of tears flow from my eyes, perspiration completely soaks my body, my skin thrills with rapture, my hairs stand on end, and my complexion turns pale and discoloured. My mind grows faint, I experience devastation, and my entire body is shattered in a flood of ecstatic emotions.**

*kori' eto upadrava, citte varse sudha-drava,*  
*more dare premera sagare*  
*kichu na bujhite dilo, more to' batula koilo,*  
*mora citta-vitta saba hare*

**“While causing such an ecstatic disturbance, the holy name showers liquid nectar on my heart and drowns me in the ocean of divine love of God. He does not allow me to understand anything, for He has made me truly mad by having stolen away my mind and faculties.**

*loinu asroya ja’r, heno vyavahara ta’r,*  
*varnite na pari e sakal*  
*krsna-nama iccha-moy, jahe jahe sukhi hoy,*  
*sei mora sukhera sambal*

**“Such is the behaviour of He in Whom I have taken shelter! I am not capable of describing all this. The holy name of Krsna is independent and thus acts according to His own sweet will. In whatever way He becomes happy, that is also the way of my happiness.**

*premera kalika nam, adbhuta rasera dham,*  
*heno bala karaye prakas*  
*isat vikasi’ punah, dekhay nija-rupa-guna,*  
*citta hari' loya krsna-pas*

**“The holy name is the bud of the flower of divine love, and the abode of astonishing mellows. The power of the name is such that when it further blossoms, it reveals His own mysterious form and qualities. Thus, my heart is abducted and taken directly to Krsna.**

*purna vikasita hoiya, braje more jaya loiya,*  
*dekhay more svarupa-vilas*  
*more siddha-deha diya, krsna-pase rakhe giya,*  
*e dehera kore sarva-nas*

**“Blossoming fully, the flower of the holy name takes me to Vraja and reveals to me His own love-dalliance. The name blesses me with my eternal spiritual body, keeps me right by Krsna’s side, and completely destroys everything related to my mortal frame.**

*krsna-nama-cintamani, akhila rasera khani,*  
*nitya-mukta suddba-rasa-moy*  
*namera balai jata, saba lo’ye hoi hata,*  
*tabe mora sukhera udoy*

**“The name of Krsna is a transcendental touchstone, a mine of all devotional mellows. It is eternally liberated, the embodiment of pure rasa.When all impediments to the pure chanting are destroyed, then my happiness will know true awakening.”**

Beautiful!

Up to now our reference to nama-bhajanahas been mainly in the context of japa.However, sankirtanahas much broader connotations than depicted by a picture of solitary chanting of the maha- mantrain Vrndavana.

Firstly, sankirtanaalso includes loud public chanting of Hare Krsna; singing songs praising Krsna’s qualities, form, pastimes, and associates; and chanting diksa-mantras,like the Kama-gayatri.

Secondly, sankirtanameans making the holy name available to others in ways that conform to Rupa Gosvami's principle of yukta-vairagya.This does not only mean chanting in the streets to the accompaniment of mrdangasand karatalas.It also means to beat the brhad-mrdanga—to print literature that describes the importance of and the truths relating to nama-sankirtana.According to Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura, that sound vibration “does not vanish into thin air.”

And that is not all: any other medium that fulfils the mission of Lord Caitanya to take the chanting of Krsna’s names to every town and village—internet, prasadamdistribution, and opening temples—is also an aspect of nama-sankirtana.

This two-faceted aspect of nama-sahkirtana—practice and preaching—is important to grasp, because it often eludes both the reclusive bhajananandiand the careless gosthanandi.

The oversight takes place in the former because he assumes that perfection in nama-bhajanais attained by effort alone, and in the latter because he assumes that perfection is attained by ḍṛñṇ alone. The bhajananandineglects the Lord’s mission for solitary meditation, and so is bereft of Gaura’s special mercy. And the care less gosthanandineglects the Lord’s sadhanain the name of preach ing, and he is bereft of Bhakti-devi’s mercy. Both are mistaken for emphasising only one of the two aspects of the sankirtana-yajna.

However, Caitanya Mahaprabhu did both: He practised and preached. When Advaita Acarya contemplated calling the Lord to appear, He thought,

*apani sri-krsna yadi karena avatara*  
*apane acari’ bhakti karena pracara*

**“If Sri Krsna were to appear as an incarnation, He Himself could preach devotion by His personal example.”**

And of course, the Lord did appear, and He taught devotees to chant the holy names and to distribute them, because the two activities are transcendentally and intrinsically linked. Preaching purifies and qualifies a practitioner, making him an object of the Lord’s mercy. In that way the sadhakais blessed with indispensable ingredients for a successful sadhana.Krsna repeatedly affirms His obligation to the preacher. But the Lord emphasises preaching not as an alternative to efforts in sadhana,but as a complementary practice. They are the two sides of the touchstone coin of sankirtana-yajna .

For example, upon concluding His extensive teachings to Uddhava, the Lord says He gives Himself to the preacher, an indication that the attainment of bhavais facilitated by preaching. But the Lord then explains the connection between preaching and sadhanain this way:

*ya etat samadhiyita*  
*pavitram paramam suci*  
*sa puyetahar ahar mam*  
*jnana-dipena darsayan*

**“He who loudly recites this supreme knowledge, which is the most lucid and purifying, becomes purified day by day, for he reveals Me to others with the lamp of transcendental knowledge.”**

Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura was explicit in emphasising the connection between preaching and spiritual attainment. He encouraged his followers by saying that congregational chanting will not only awaken in the preacher his spontaneous devotion, but also his svarupa.

Our Srila Prabhupada also taught this understanding, emphasising to devotees the need to concentrate on being free of bad habits and to trust in the power of nama-sankirtana.He encouraged his followers to benefit the ignorant in the way that they themselves had been blessed, for by doing so they would strike the right balance in service. Thus, even in Kali-yuga they could show others the way to perfection by attaining it themselves. As Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura summarised in a letter:

**“But if we want to show all these prakrta-sahajiyas who are mired in their misconceptions—lamenting like a cow stuck in mud—the real glory of raganuga-bhakti, we ourselves must become expert in the art of bhajana, whereby others may be benefited.”**

## Chapter Twenty-Eight

**Bhajana Of The Holy Names**

In this chapter we review the underlying principles of nama- bhajanain remembrance, thereby highlighting the basic sankalpasa sadhakamust undertake to perfect chanting Hare Krsna. The contents of this chapter are an introduction to the rest of Part Six, which elaborates in detail on the stages of remembrance and the specific determinations needed to smoothly pass through them to their perfection.

At the stage of sravana,determinations were mostly external, bringing the senses in line with the standards of sadhana-bhakti. But now, at the all-important stage of smarana, sankalpasare mostly internal, focused on increasing the mind’s absorption in the holy name.

To effectively make those determinations, a devotee must be free of most impurities and have full control over his mind and senses. A devotee who is not thus qualified will be unable to properly apply himself to nama-bhajana,what to speak of systematic remembrance. He should therefore continue to hear and chant as before with the confidence that when his heart is sufficiently clean, his chanting will transform into real bhajana.

That said, the devotee at smarana-dasamust also be further purified of material contamination, a process of purification that is complete only with the attainment of bhava.However, the strong faith and the purity of intent symptomatic of such a steady devotee enables him to practise pure sadhanaand to be called a pure devotee—at least in terms of his aspiration, if not in terms of his attainment.

True to His word, Krsna reciprocates with His devotee in a variety of ways, gradually transforming the sadhaka'svision of ecstatic devotion from an intellectual concept to a perceptible one. This takes place in the same way that the first light of dawn harkens the arrival of the sun. Krsna explains His reciprocation with this well-known analogy:

*yatha yathatma parimrjyate ’sau*  
*mat-punya-gatha-sravanabhidhanaih*  
*tatha tatha pasyati vastu suksmam*  
*caksur yathaivanjana-samprayuktam*

**“When a diseased eye is treated with medicinal ointment it gradually recovers its power to see. Similarly, as a conscious living entity cleanses himself of material contamination by hearing and chanting the pious narrations of My glories, he regains his ability to see Me, the Absolute Truth, in My subtle spiritual form.”**

As the sadhakais purified, his mind becomes increasingly peaceful and increasingly co-operative in meeting the challenge to unlock the treasure-chest of nama-sankirtana.For the raganuga-sadhaka, the natural attachment of the mind is an added advantage, his level of greed determining the efficacy of his bhajana.By contrast, in the absence of eagerness for vraja-bhakti,the vaidhi-sadhakais fully dependent on the strength of his practices.

Thakura Bhaktivinoda offers sound advice to the devotee ascending the rungs of smarana-dasa.He suggests that a practitioner chant a fixed number of rounds daily, and at a time and place free of any external disturbance. The morning hours after mangala-arati are an ideal time, either in a temple or in a solitary place in one’s home. Chanting japahere and there, at any time of the day, will hardly lead to quality bhajana.

Additionally, the Thakura emphasises that a devotee keep his mind free of mundane thoughts. This instruction might appear elementary, considering that nama-sankirtanais about focused attentiveness. Yet it should be taken as a word from the wise. Sagacious sadhakasnever let down their guard, no matter how satisfying their progress appears. In glorifying the activities of Maharaja Rsabhadeva, Sukadeva Gosvami says,

*nityam dadati kamasya*  
*cchidram tam anu ye 'rayah*  
*yoginah krta-maitrasya*  
*patyur jayeva pumscali*

**“An unchaste woman is very easily carried away by paramours, and it sometimes happens that her husband is violently killed by her paramours. If the yogigives his mind a chance and does not restrain it, his mind will give facility to enemies like lust, anger, and greed, and they will doubtlessly kill the yogi.”**

A devotee should try to increase the number of rounds of harinama that he chants. Srila Prabhupada would use the term “numerical strength” to connect the potency of japato the number of rounds a devotee chanted. In other words, as regards nama-sankirtana,quality is refined by quantity: purity in chanting can be enhanced by increasing the number of rounds. Thus it was no coincidence that His Divine Grace requested his followers to chant a “minimum of sixteen rounds daily.” The word “minimum” indicated that as far as possible, a devotee should organise his life in a way that he can increase his dedication to chanting Hare Krsna.

To the above four submissions a sadhakamay add three further practices that are the ingredients of success for nama-bhajana. These are:

**Keeping good association, refraining from a worldly lifestyle, and confident enthusiasm.**

Much has already been spoken about the indispensable benefits of associating with advanced Vaisnavas and avoiding those posing a spiritual handicap.

To achieve these ends, a devotee must position himself carefully in both his social circle and his relationships. The most important feature of association is those advanced devotees who are fully competent to guide a sadhakaon his journey. Additionally, sadhu-sanga should harmonise with one’s own mood of devotion.

For example, a spontaneous devotee should seek out raganuga-bhaktaswith the same inclination: if he is a follower of the cow herd boys, then among spontaneous devotees he should seek out someone with the same mood. Rupa Gosvami summarises this selection process in the following way:

*srimad-bhagavatarthanam*  
*asvado rasikaih saha*  
*sajatiyasaye snigdhe*  
*sadhau sangah svato vare*

**“One should taste the meaning of Srimad-Bhagavatam in the association of pure devotees, and one should associate with the devotees who are more advanced than oneself and who are endowed with a similar type of affection for the Lord.”**

The next best practice after good association is to live in a way that is supportive of spiritual progress.

While some devotees can seclude themselves in Vraja, most cannot. Most will have to work to maintain their families. That said, since a devotee’s activities influence his thought process, which in turn comes to the surface in his meditations, a Vaisnava should arrange his life to be as uncomplicated as possible. And while that is not easy in our increasingly convoluted world, the path of smaranadoes entail an uncomplicated mindset. Thus, one of the qualities of a pure devotee is simplicity. Indeed, adhering to the twenty-six good qualities of a Vaisnava defines what a favourable lifestyle entails. A devotee will accept material obligations with out being attached to them and solely as a means to facilitate his spiritual awakening. Progress in nama-bhajanawill also insulate him from unavoidable material affiliates, such as family, home, and so on.

\* \* \* \*

This brings us to the last necessity for successful bhajana,which is confident, intelligent enthusiasm.

Srila Prabhupada defines enthusiasm as:

**“Endeavour executed with intelligence in Krsna consciousness.”**

And confidence means faith in the truths of bhakti-yoga.Thus confident, intelligent enthusiasm means:

**Faithful endeavour guided by Krsna conscious intelligence.**

Success in bhajanaobviously depends on both faith in the process and on intelligence to make that process work. But most importantly, a qualified devotee must be convinced that he can attain the goal of bhava.In defining the characteristics of the stages of bhakti, Rupa Gosvami says that bhava-bhaktiis not easily attained, for two reasons:

*sudurlabha—*  
*sadhanaughair anasangair*  
*alabhya sucirad api*  
*harina casv adeyeti*  
*dvidha sa syat sudurlabha*

**“Bhaktiis difficult to attain in two ways; if undertaken with great effort but without attachment, bhakticannot be attained even after a long time, and even if practised with attachment, Krsna does not give bhaktito the practitioner immediately.”**

We have already discussed the necessity of developing asakti. However here we see that even if a devotee develops taste and attachment, Krsna is still slow in awarding bhava.Why? Because by doing so He gradually comes under the control of His devotee. This means that a sadhakamay be doing everything right and may have attachment, but ecstasy still does not come. Nonetheless he must persevere, and he must do so with enthusiasm. Why? Because sooner or later, Krsna will be merciful. Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura comments,

**“He does give bhava,but after a delay.”**

We are, after all, talking about acquiring the commodity that brings the Supreme Personality of Godhead under control. That attainment is not like buying a bag of rice. It is the most valuable commodity, and so a devotee must be willing to pay the price for it. Krsna delays because He wants to be convinced that a devotee values Him with determination and enthusiasm. From the sadhakasside, he must be equally convinced that with the blessings of pure devotees his efforts will in time bear fruit. That is confident intelligent enthusiasm.

Although securing bhavais a painstaking process, the effort itself has its rewards. Strong, faithful devotion increasingly attracts Krsna’s mercy, and that mercy fills the sadhaka’sheart with the happiness known only to one situated in goodness. The taste of that joy inspires a devotee to redouble his commitment to sadhana and particularly to the holy name.

As the sadhakasystematically ploughs forward in bhajana,affection for his means of progress—the holy name—simply increases and increases. In that frame of mind, the devotee becomes pos sessive of his bhajanain the way that a greedy person hoards his wealth. The devotee thinks, “the name is mine.”

Enthusiasm, combined with a sense of possessiveness of and attachment to the holy name, gives encouragement for a devotee to project his aspired mood of devotion on his bhajana.Bhaktivinoda Thakura calls this practice a helpful “imposition.”

This imposition is a reference to Rupa Gosvami's recommendation of following a resident of Vraja. By identifying with a mellow of devotion, a devotee expresses a preliminary desire which only later, at bhava,becomes a real identity. Because that aspiration gives a practitioner a sense of spiritual identity and direction, it contributes to enthusiastic bhajana.This mood is natural for the raganuga-sadhakaand less so for the vaidhi-sadhaka.That said, the latter will have an increased inclination for it after attaining the stage of asakti.

Readers will bear in mind that a sadhakamust be systematic in advancing towards bhavapana-dasa,and so he must pass through the stage of asakti,attachment. Without attachment, there is no question of love. And attachment is not just about fondness for Krsna, but a certain kind of fondness. Is that fondness similar to the love of the Vraja-vasis, the Dvaraka-vasis, or the Vaikuntha-vasis? The mood of attachment may be natural, regulated, or a combination of the two; whichever one it is, it is an individual affinity that is cultivated through sadhanaand then manifest through a corresponding mood of love at bhava.

Being individuals, serious devotees will have their own nuanced approach to sadhana.Some will try to systematically cultivate vraja-bhakti,others will prefer to meditate exclusively on the maha-mantra,and still others may have a unique attraction to Caitanya Mahaprabhu. These practitioners may be regulated or spontaneous. But one characteristic common to them all is that they are good sadhakas:they constantly keep themselves absorbed in chanting, hearing, and remembering. They are not dawdlers!

We shall now speak about the attraction of the regulated devotee for vraja-bhakti.

While the raganuga-bhaktaspontaneously follows his role model based on his study of scripture, the vaidhi-bhaktawill dutifully revere that ideal. He certainly cannot be indifferent to it! His reverence for a role model comes from spiritual realisation, which comes from studying the truths of devotional service as a requirement to go back to Godhead, to Goloka-Vrndavana. In this regard Krsna says,

*janma karma ca me divyam*  
*evam yo vetti tattvatah*  
*tyaktva deham punar janma*  
*naiti mam eti so ’rjuna*

**“One who knows the transcendental nature of My appearance and activities does not, upon leaving the body, take his birth again in this material world, but attains My eternal abode, O Arjuna.”**

Through hearing from advanced devotees, a vaidhi-bhaktaeventually aspires for vraja-bhakti,even though he lacks a spontaneous attraction for it. Yet entering Krsna’s Vrndavana pastimes is his researched goal. A minority of regulated devotees may have an inclination for some other form of the Lord, and so their sadhana and their mood of devotion will correspond to that attainment. We have spoken about this previously.

To conclude on these principles of smarana-dasa,we may reiterate that a sadhaka’saspiration and his mood of bhaktiis the devotional outpouring of a conditioned soul. Guidance from the spiritual master during smaranaand the liberating effect at bhava will either fine-tune or correct imperfections in those sentiments.

Devotional service to Krsna is an unlimited ocean. In this section we have attempted to present some of the fundamental principles underlying the stage of remembrance. In the following section we shall say something about the principles underlying the cultivation of remembrance.

\* \* \* \*

Pure devotional service in practice is defined as a “cultivation” by the word anusilanam,and as “practice” by the phrase krti-sadhya bhavet. Smarana-dasais pure devotion in practice, and so it demands quality cultivation for success.

There are two ways in which cultivation of remembrance takes place:

**Either by attentively hearing nama-sankirtana,or by attentively hearing the holy names while making a natural effort at further cultivation that does not interfere with the hearing process.**

It is an individual choice that each practitioner makes for himself, although Srila Prabhupada and acaryasmake their choice evident.

It should be clear by now that both processes necessitate that a devotee discard all offences to the holy name. And that means the sadhakamust pronounce the syllables of the maha-mantradistinctly. Real cultivation in smaranabegins when chanting is pure. With such quality kirtanathe mind will be sufficiently purified to actually be one-pointed, ekagra.

In describing the glories of pure chanting, Caitanya Mahaprabhu told Satyaraja Khan,

*diksa-purascarya-vidhi apeksa ñṁ kare*  
*jihva-sparse a-candala sabare uddhare*

**“One does not have to undergo initiation or execute the activities required before initiation. One simply has to vibrate the holy name with his lips. Thus even a man in the lowest class \[candala\] can be delivered.”**

While the truth of the Lord’s words is unassailable, acaryashave emphasised that a neophyte devotee needs a spiritual guide to efficiently unlock the mysteries of nama-bhajana. And commitment to a guruis firmed up through diksa.Therefore, while the holy name is not dependent on initiation, it is seen that all but the liberated sadhakaare.

Additionally, the pancaratrikisystem of deity worship is also embraced by Gaudiya Vaisnavas in order to purify devotees for nama-bhajana.By service to the deity, firm faith is fixed in the sadhaka’sheart. And for deity worship, a devotee must be an initiated brahmana.Thus he must embrace diksa.Jiva Gosvami gives a crystal-clear explanation in his Sandarbha:

*yadyapi sri-bhagavata-mate pancaratradi-vat arcana-*  
*margasya avasyakatvam nasti, tad vinapi saranapat-*  
*tyadinam ekatarenapi purusartha-siddher abbihitatvat,*  
*tathapi sri-naradadi-vartmanusaradbhih sri-bhagavata*  
*saha sambandba-visesam diksa-vidhanena sri-guru-*  
*carana-sampaditam cikirsadbhih krtayam diksayam*  
*arcanam avasyam kriyetaiva.*

*yadyapi svarupato nasti, tathapi prayah svabha-*  
*vato dehadi-sambandhena kadarya-silanam viksipta-*  
*cittanam jananam tat-tat-sankoci-karanaya srimad-rsi-*  
*prabhrtibhir atrarcana-marge kvacit kvacit kacit kacin*  
*maryada sthapitasti.*

**“It is Srimad-Bhagavatam’sopinion that the process of deity worship is not actually necessary, just as the specific prescriptions of the Pancaratraand other scriptures need not be followed. The Srimad-Bhagavatamenjoins that even without practising deity worship one can achieve complete success in human life by any of the other devotional processes, such as simply offering oneself at the Lord’s feet for protection. Nonetheless, a Vaisnava following the path of Sri Narada and his successors endeavours to establish a personal relationship with the Lord by receiving the grace of a bona fide spiritual master through initiation. And in this tradition the devotee is obliged to begin deity worship at the time of initiation.**

**“Although deity worship is also not essential, the material conditioning of most candidates for devotional service requires that they engage in this activity. When we consider their bodily and mental conditions, we find that the character of candidates is impure and their minds are agitated. Therefore, to rectify this material conditioning, the great sage Narada and others have at different times recommended various kinds of regulations for deity worship.”**

Readers must remember that the maha-mantrais not a combination of letters. The Absolute Truth, the Supreme Lord, is concealed behind the curtain of these sixteen names. And that cur tain can only be drawn back by a pure devotee who is steeped in the truths and the cultivation of nama-sankirtana.If a devotee is not pure enough to draw that curtain himself, then he must take shelter of a guruwho is willing to share his realisation with his sincere follower. The words of the mantra,combined with the divine blessings of the spiritual master, constitute the foundations of nama-bhajana.

In his advice to the practitioner, Sanatana Gosvami quotes Mantrarnavaon the six aspects of mantracultivation. The verse says,

*manah-samharanam saucam*  
*maunam mantrartha-cintanam*  
*avyagratvam anirvedo*  
*japa-sampatti-hetavah*

**“Controlling the mind, striving lor purity, observing silence, contemplating the meaning of the mantra, exhibiting peacefulness, and showing eagerness for chanting are the six acts of cultivation that yield mature benefit from japaof the maha-mantra.”**

The phrase manah-samharanamdirects the sadhakato focus his mind on the transcendental sound vibration and withdraw it from all other sense objects. This is the one-pointed attentiveness of which we have spoken at length, and will not elaborate on further.

External cleanliness and purity, sauca,refers not so much to the qualifications for taking up chanting, but the lifestyle of one engaged in nama-bhajana.The reason a devotee must accept a guru and take Vaisnava initiation from him is to encourage and enforce these practices while simultaneously refraining from un-Vaisnava conduct.

While absolute silence, mauna,is not a Vaisnava practice, avoiding idle talk and speaking only about things related to Krsna are. All kinds of unnecessary talk and sound vibration, like television, movies, internet, and talk of sports, are frivolous practices that Rupa Gosvami calls prajalpa.He warns that such idle chatter spoils one’s devotional service and the chance to attain the mercy of the name. From this perspective, maunais recommended.

In his booklet Nama-bhajana,Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura emphasises that repeated remembrance of the meaning of the maha-mantra,as explained by acaryaslike Gopala Guru Gosvami, will remove all inauspicious obstacles from the path of bhajana.The acaryaadds that such meditation will, in time, invoke the personality of the name before the sadhaka’sspiritual eyes. This is mantrartha-cintana,meditating on the meaning of the mantra.

While the reader is encouraged to look at the many word-for-word explanations of the maha-mantragiven by acaryas, we give a summary here:

**The name Hari indicates He Who frees one of all sin and from the threefold miseries, or it denotes that irresistible person Who steals the minds of all living entities, including of His own incarnations. In the vocative, Hari is expressed as Hare, which also means Hara, or Radha, the feminine aspect of the Absolute, Who bewilders Krsna’s mind to no end. The name Krsna indicates the Supreme all attractive person. The two syllables of Rama drive all sins from the heart and prevent them from ever returning, and Rama also refers to Radha-ramana, the lover of Sri Radha.**

Different sadhakaswill be drawn to different explanations of the maha-mantra.It will be a matter of devotional taste. However, the meaning of their choice will form part of the foundation of then nama-bhajana.

The word avyagratvaindicates a state in which a devotee is not distracted. This may refer to a secluded place, and time dedicated to quality cultivation, as well as to attentiveness referred to by manah-samharana.It is closely connected to the word ekagrata, as it contains the same word, agra.Needless to say, all five sub-stages of smarana-dasaare dependent on both suitable circumstances and proper focus.

And finally, anirvedameans “no indifference.” The meaning “no indifference” is a warning. No one becomes intimate with an indifferent person. Affection breeds affection. Similarly, to attain the mercy of the holy name a devotee should chant with loving feeling. If such emotion has not yet manifest, then the practitioner must at least draw the name into his heart by extreme humility and firm devotion.

\* \* \* \*

We have mentioned that there are two kinds of sadhakas,those who cultivate smarana,and those who do not. Whether they do or do not, the sequence of development for both efforts means a pro gressive meditation in bhajanaon Krsna’s names, then His form, followed by His qualities, and finally His pastimes—nama, rupa, guna, lila.The difference between the two is that in the former, meditation manifests by effort; in the latter, by grace of the holy name.

There is a question that devotees often ask:

**“Does cultivation mean that a sadhakamust make a systematic effort to go through the sequence of nama, rupa, guna, lilato finally enter asta-kaliya-lila smarana? Or is it enough to just hear the mantraf”**

The answer is:

**“To relish the nectar of Krsna’s pastimes, meditation on the names of the maha-mantrais enough. There is no obligation to practise a simultaneous meditation on Krsna’s form and so on.”**

Some devotees may make a separate effort to meditate on Krsna’s form, qualities, and pastimes. But such effort is optional, and successful only for the experienced. The standard, safe, and recommended practice is that devotees attentively hear Krsna’s holy names. By the grace of the names, the adept sadhakawill naturally ascend the rungs of remembrance. There is no requirement for separate effort. All acaryashave given this as their conclusion. Srila Prabhupada himself said,

“The purification of chanting harer namameans as soon as you chant the holy name of Krsna, immediately you will see the form of Krsna, you will realise the qualities of Krsna, you will immediately remember the pastimes of Krsna. That is pure chanting of Hare Krsna mantra.In his commentary Srila Jiva Gosvami says that a pure devotee who chants Hare Krsna mantraimmediately sees all these manifest—ndma, rupa, guna, lila, parikara, vasistha.

“Simply by chanting the name you will feel the form of Krsna: ‘Here is Krsna.’ Nama, rupa, guna.‘Here are the qualities. Oh! Krsna is so qualified. He is so kind. He is so magnanimous.’ So many qualities you will remember. Nama, rupa, guna, lila.Then His pastimes. ‘Oh! Krsna instructed Arjuna. Krsna played with His cowherd boys. Krsna had very nice talks with the gopis, with His mother, Yasoda.’ These things will be remembered. That is factual perfection of chanting.”

And while meditation on Krsna’s name accomplishes all perfections, the progression always starts with the name and passes in sequence to Krsna’s form, qualities, pastimes, and abode. This applies especially to the devotee who makes a separate effort to invoke these aspects of the Lord.

Jiva Gosvami admits that it is not impossible for a sadhakato jump the sequence to attain perfection, but it is a rarity. The general path, whether by separate effort or singular meditation on the name, is that a devotee will follow the standard order of things.

The transition through the sequence is, like all things devotional, scientific. A devotee begins by learning to attentively hear the syllables and names of the maha-mantra.Offenceless chanting results in effective purification of the heart, and when that purification matures, then Krsna’s form appears in the devotee’s heart.

The eager practitioner who proactively seeks after the form can either search out Krsna in his mind or chant before the deity, meditating on His beautiful features.

Krsna and His form, like His name, are identical.

The more clearly the sadhakachants the name, the more bhajanaproceeds with the accompaniment of Krsna’s form. And as the name and form take prominence, the influence of the modes of nature, including goodness, is nullified. The maturity of this meditation, either by effort or by the grace of the name, takes place when the name and form become inseparable. That means that as soon as a devotee says the name “Krsna,” he perceives the form of Krsna within his mind—and vice versa.

By attentive meditation on Krsna’s name and form, His qualities, as listed by Rupa Gosvami, gradually manifest in the same way as did His form.

As bhajanaproceeds, Krsna’s qualities become increasingly present, and they join with the name and form to further increase Krsna’s presence. Krsna’s fullness includes His name, form, qualities, pastimes, associates, and abode. He is never separated from these. Thus, the more that these attributes are cultivated, the more is the Lord perceived.

Finally, nama-sankirtanainvokes Krsna’s pastimes, with which appear His associates and abode.

A deep and natural meditation, in which the name literally dances on the tongue, brings unimaginable delight to the sadhaka. Pastimes are of two kinds, known as mantramayiand svarasiki:

**Individual pastimes, and those pastimes connected in a sequence, respectively.**

Devotees eager to meditate on Krsna’s pastimes may do so, but only after the name, form, and qualities of the Lord have sufficiently manifest. This type of meditation is commonplace when chanting diksa-mantrassuch as the Gopala mantra or the Kama-gayatri. Both mantrasfacilitate meditation which, depending on the sadhaka’sadvancement, may invoke a single or a series of pastimes.

At the conclusion of Gopa-kumara’s story, the sage Jaimini recounts to Janamejaya a series of verses which he regularly chants to taste the sweet ecstasies of scriptural conclusions. These verses are a rasayana,or tonic, which devotees of bygone times used as meditations while chanting Hare Krsna. A practitioner begins with mantramayimeditation in which he remembers a single pastime, or even a single scene. In that way he tastes the glories of the Lord and His devotees. The Gopala-tapani Upanisaddescribes this process in relation to meditation on the Gopala mantra:

*tam ekam govinda sac-cid-ananda-vigraham panca-*  
*padam vrndavana-sura-bhuruha-atalasinam satatam*  
*samarud-gane’ham paramaya stutya tosayami*

**“With eloquent prayers, I and the Maruts please Lord Govinda, Whose form is eternal, full of knowledge and bliss, and Who stands beneath a desire tree in Vrndavana as the embodiment of the five-part mantra \[klim krsnaya govindaya gopijanavallabhaya svaha\].”**

Another verse for mantramayimeditation that is cited by Jiva Gosvami and well-known to devotees is the Brahma-samhita sloka beginning with venum kvanantam. This verse paints a picture of Krsna’s pastime of playing His flute, while detailing His bodily features in a way that gives ample fuel for meditation.

When mantramayimeditation is fully adorned with the mature name, form, and qualities of Krsna, a devotee will be eligible for svarasikimeditation, which is also known as asta-kaliya-lila meditation.

In the tenth verse of Upadesamrta,Rupa Gosvami says that such meditation is characteristic of the bhava-bhakta.However, raganuga devotees at the stage of asakti,who have strong greed for Krsna’s eightfold daily pastimes, may also be thus absorbed, although there will be a qualitative difference between the two. In the heart of the bhava-bhaktaKrsna will appear by the agency of his internal potency, whereas the raganuga-bhaktaperceives Krsna as a strong mental impression. The process of svarasikimeditation and its trailsition from trance to direct perception is glorified by Lord Brahma:

*tvam bhakti-yoga-paribhavita-hrt-saroja*  
*asse sruteksita-patho ñṁñu natha pumsam*  
*yad-yad-dhiya ta urugaya vibhavayanti*  
*tat-tad-vapuh pranayase sad-anugrahaya*

**“O my Lord! Your devotees can see You through the ears by the process of bona fide hearing, and thus their hearts become cleansed, and You take Your seat there. You are so merciful to Your devotees that You manifest Yourself in the particular eternal form of transcendence in which they always think of You.”**

An example of svarasikimeditation is found in the invocation to Govinda-lilamrta,where Krsnadasa Kaviraja Gosvami summarises Krsna’s eightfold daily pastimes in nine verses, the first one bringing to light the essence of the following eight:

*kunjad gostham nisante pravisati kurute dohanannasanadyam*  
*pratah sayam ca lilam vibarati sakhibhih sangave carayan gah*  
*madyahne catha naktam vilasati vipine radbayaddhaparahne*  
*gostham yati pradose ramayati suhrdo yah sa krsno ’vatan nah*

**“May that Krsna, Who daily returns from the groves to His village at the end of night, milks the cows and eats His meals in the morning and evening, Who plays with His friends and herds the cows in the late morning, dallies with Radha in the forest at midday and at night, returns to the village in the late afternoon, and pleases His friends in the late evening, protect us all.”**

Each of the eight verses serve as a mantramayimeditation, and when joined together they become a svarasikimeditation. Kaviraja Gosvami’s book details Krsna’s eightfold pastimes, which serve as both an inspiration and as ingredients for a devotee’s meditations. Govinda-lilamrtaand authorised books in the same vein are a great asset for the serious sadhaka.

Similarly, the verses of Brahma-samhitaare a description of Lord Brahma’s svarasikimeditation. Devotees in iskcon are fond of reciting these verses in their entirety and thereby sharing the ecstasy of the creator.

When manifest in their fullness, the svarasikipastimes of Krsna appear before the devotee like a constantly flowing river. In a way that a river flows naturally under the force of gravity and without any external agent, so Krsna’s eternal pastimes flow constantly within the heart of the accomplished devotee.

Jiva Gosvami likens svarasikirealisation to the flowing Ganga, and mantramayito the lakes within the Ganga. In the former the pastimes flow constantly, and in the latter individual pastimes fill one lake after the other. Although the eager devotee may practise a semblance of svarasikimeditation, it is the transcendentalist who can actually enter into its mysteries and directly see Krsna and His associates. Jiva Gosvami says that this kind of meditation is very elevated and difficult to achieve.

Nonetheless, a devotee who is determined, who has the blessings of his gurus,and who meticulously follows the process of smarana as outlined by authorities will eventually be blessed by absorption in Krsna’s eightfold daily pastimes. Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura says that the prema-ruruksudevotees, those whose existence is attaining prema,will “in a very short time” realise their heart’s desire.

By following his predecessors, the devotee’s nama-bhajana becomes sheer joy and his remembrance increasingly precise. With this acquired proficiency the chasm between sadhanaand sadhyacloses, and as it does, the sadhaka’sinner senses are spirit ually transformed and his svarupagradually takes shape. Thus, while chanting and remembering Krsna’s name with tears rolling down his cheeks, at some time divine grace descends and gives the sadhakaentrance to the realm of apana-dasa.

We conclude this section with an important summary of the different names that constitute nama-bhajana.

In his Kalyana-kalpataru,Thakura Bhaktivinoda describes the holy name in six features as it manifests according to a devotee’s attainment in sadhana, bhavaand prema.He names the features of the maha-mantra; nama, rupa-yukta-nama, guna-yukta-nama, lila-yukta-nama, rasita-nama,and sarva-rasa-sikta-nama.These correspond to chanting at the stage of:

**Faith, steadiness, taste, attachment, ecstatic devotion and loving devotion, respectively.**

The acarya’smessage is that according to his attainment in devotion, a devotee is qualified to chant a different kind of name of Krsna. By different we do not mean another name, but rather the same name, same mantra,which continually reveals different features and different realisations. Thus “different” means “increasingly enhanced.”

The smallest currency of sraddhapurchases the most basic form of the maha-mantrain which the name of Krsna appears before the chanter. This is followed at nisthaby the feature of the name that reveals the form of Krsna. As mentioned earlier, to the steady devotee nama-bhajanawill spontaneously reveal the form of the Lord. When a devotee attains the stage of ruci,the Lord’s name will further reveal Krsna’s qualities, which means nama-bhajana is imbued with both Krsna’s beautiful form and all-attractive attributes. At the final stage of sadhana, asakti,the Lord’s names also reveal Krsna’s pastimes, embellishing nama-bhajanawith Krsna’s name, form, qualities, and pastimes.

These are the features of the holy name revealed to the pure devotee up to the stage of samadhiin smarana-dasa.

At bhavapana-dasaand sampatti-dasathe holy name manifests its final feature: transcendental mellow, rasa.When the sadhakaattains bhava,then the lotus-bud of mellow appears in nama-sankirtana,and when premabecomes the right of the accomplished devotee, then the blossoming lotus of mellow reveals its full splendour, scattering the pollen of its treasures before the fortunate devotee.

If the stages of bhaktiare considered the currency with which to purchase a feature of Krsna’s names, then:

**Sraddhais the lowly paisathat purchases the semblance of the name; nisthais one-eighth of a silver coin by which one acquires rupa-yukta-nama; ruci is one-quarter of a silver coin, qualifying one for guna-yukta-nama; asaktiis one-half of a silver coin that purchases lila-yukta-nama; bhavais the full currency of the silver coin that buys the very rare rasita-nama; and premais the gold coin with which one acquires the treasure of fully manifest transcendental mellow.**

Such are the wonderful revelations that acaryaslike Bhaktivinoda Thakura share with aspiring sadhakas.Truly a shower of nectar.

\* \* \* \*

We will now examine the five divisions of smarana-dasa,which are smarana, dharana, dhyana, anusmrti,and samadhi:

Recollection, absorption, meditation, constant remembrance, and trance, respectively.

By now the astute reader will have concluded that the core theme of this book is understanding the sankalpasrequired to transit from one stage of smaranato the other. No doubt the determinations to reach smarana-dasaare essential, as they form the foundation for real sadhana.However, those sankalpasare relatively elementary by comparison to those required for remembrance, which is really the substance of nama-bhajana.Since smarana-dasacorresponds to significant and dynamic advancement in sadhana,the steps that effect a devotee’s progress from the first stage of recollection to the final stage of trance are to be given special attention. They are, after all, the five major steps leading to a sadhaka’sgoal in life.

In making these steps, attentiveness is as much about clarity of mind on what to do and how to do it, as it is about actually doing it.

Bhaktivinoda Thakura warns devotees that those who are expert in their determinations will transit through the stages in good time, while those who are not may journey for many lives. The lack of expertise is generally not due to bad karma,but to a lack of suitable guidance.

Gopa-kumara is an example of a pure-hearted devotee who, due to a lack of transcendental knowledge, took a long time to reach his destination. But because he was sincere, he received guidance that would enable him to make one sankalpaafter the other. The boy’s story reveals that guidance comes to the practitioner from two sources:

**From within himself, and from spiritual guides.**

From his first sankalpa—to leave home and search out the Lord of the universe—until he reached Brahma-loka, Gopa-kumara acted upon his spiritual instincts, which included signs from Lord Jagannatha. Then to make the step to the abode of liberation, the boy received the blessings of the Mahapurusa, and after that, he received guidance from superiors that corresponded to his ever-increasing levels of realisation. In this way he always knew the next step to take.

It is noteworthy to pause briefly and consider Gopa-kumara’s reasoning while he was making sankalpas.

His were rarely easy decisions.

The reason is that at whichever stage he was at, the boy had darsana of and service to some form of the Lord. Both these things gave him great pleasure, and so he always doubted whether moving on was the best thing to do. But he was able to actuate forward progress by comparing his existing situation to that depicted by his mantra. When he did, he could understand that he had not attained his destination, and eventually he mustered the spiritual courage to move on.

The conclusion is that knowledge of sadhyais essential for a devotee’s progress, especially in the realm of goodness where happiness and satisfaction are dominant and thus binding. This relentless drive to the goal is one of the four instructions given by Krsna to Brahma:

*etavad eva jijnasyam*  
*tattva-jijnasunatmanah*  
*anvaya-vyatirekabhyam*  
*yat syat sarvatra sarvada*

**“A person who is searching after the Supreme Absolute Truth, the Personality of Godhead, must certainly search for it up to this, in all circumstances, in all space and time, and both directly and indirectly.”**

With the word etavat,“up to this,” the Lord encourages all His children to continue on their path until they have reached the kind of love for Him that they covet. This puts in clear perspective the first three stages of bhakti: sravana-dasa,to know one’s personal destination in devotion; varana-dasa,to firmly commit to that destination; and smarana-dasa,the path that leads there.

With each successful sankalpa,Gopa-kumara was entering into ever-increasingly blissful stages of devotion which were ever-increasingly difficult to give up. Once he was in the realm of liberation, he could no longer make decisions on his own—neither did he have the spiritual qualification to do so. It required instruction from the Vaikuntha-dutas, Mathura brahmanas,and from his own diksa-guruto qualify him for entrance into Vaikuntha. As an aside, it is interesting to note how little instruction Gopa-kumara received from his initiator by comparison to that received from his siksa-gurus,most prominent of whom was Narada.

Once in Vaikuntha, from abode to abode the boy faced a common dilemma, which was the divine conflict between attachment to the deity of his mantra,Madana-gopala, and the form of Krsna he stood before—first Narayana, then Ramacandra, and finally Dvarakadisa. Each time, Gopa-kumara had to be prompted by either Narada, Uddhava, or the Lord to make the sankalpaappropriate for the next step of his journey.

The takeaway from Gopa-kumara’s example is that making the determinations to go from one stage of smaranato the next requires spiritual guidance. Indeed, it appears that the closer a devotee gets to bhava,the more subtle the sadhana,and the more extensive the required counsel. Again, guidance comes from Krsna as the Supersoul and as the spiritual masters. Without such help it is highly unlikely that a sadhakacould make any headway in Krsna consciousness. A devotee is therefore unlimitedly grateful for Krsna’s constant guidance, and that gratitude is a significant aspect of the impetus to serve the Lord. Uddhava expresses his indebtedness in this way:

*naivopayanty apacitim kavayas tavesa*  
*brahmayusapi krtam rddha-mudah smarantah*  
*yo ’ntar bahis tanu-bhrtam asubham vidbunvann*  
*acarya-caittya-vapusa sva-gatim vyanakti*

**“O my Lord! Transcendental poets and experts in spiritual science could not fully express their indebtedness to You, even if they were endowed with the prolonged lifetime of Brahma, for You appear in two features—externally as the acaryaand internally as the Supersoul—to deliver the embodied living being by directing him how to come to You.”**

As already mentioned, smaranais not restricted to japa.It takes place in other services such as chanting diksa-mantras,other forms of nama-sankirtana,preaching, and service in general. Absorption in these activities facilitates the stages of remembrance. In his last days Srila Prabhupada continued to emphasise the sales of transcendental literature as a means for benefiting non-devotees with bhaktiand benefiting the preacher’s smarana.He wrote,

**“The word kriyasu,meaning “by manual labour” or “by work,” is important in this verse. One should engage in practical service to the Lord. In our Krsna consciousness movement, all our activities are concentrated upon distributing Krsna literature. This is very important. One may approach any person and induce him to read Krsna literature so that in the future he also may become a devotee. Such activities are recommended in this verse. Kriyasu yas tvac- caranaravindayoh.Such activities will always remind the devotees of the Lord’s lotus feet. By fully concentrating on distributing books for Krsna, one is fully absorbed in Krsna. This is samadhi.”**

Initially, devotees without greed will find it easier to be absorbed in active service than in silent meditation on mantras.This is because active services engage all their senses, while mantra-smarana engages mostly the tongue and ears. Thus the mind may be more easily absorbed in the former than the latter. Some authorities say that steadiness is first attained in bodily services, then vocal activities, and finally in mental activities, meaning in smaranam.In any case, once attachment awakens, nama-bhajanabecomes as easy as other services, which, through their purifying effect, contribute significantly to such attainment.

\* \* \* \*

We will now say something about the correspondence between the sub-stages of smarana-dasafrom smaranato samadhi,and the stages of bhaktifrom nisthato asakti.While a general correlation between the two is evident, arguments can be made for alternate versions to that given below. Moreover, a slight variation arises between comparing smarana-dasato vaidhi-bhakti,and comparing it to raganuga-bhakti.

We have already suggested that nisthais a prerequisite for smarana.While a devotee may try for meditation, unless his mind is reasonably controlled it will not be effective. Of course, there is no harm in trying, and the effort itself will be purifying. However, until significant steadiness is achieved, remembrance will be flickering.

Efforts at remembrance under the tutelage of the holy name purify the heart and reveal the tastes of pure devotion, which in turn facilitate absorption. Thus the divisions of ruciand dharana are in general agreement.

This taste has significant depth, meaning that it too has further subdivisions. Cakravarti Thakura gives two main divisions, vastu-vaisisty-apeksiniand vastu-vaisisty-anapeksini:

**Taste that is dependent on the excellence of elements, and taste that is not.**

The former is the lower division, while the latter displays a qualitative and quantitative superiority of taste. Absorption followed by meditation, dhyana,becomes increasingly more effective as taste for nama-bhajanamatures.

The mature stage of sadhana-bhakti, asakti,may be said to correlate with anusmrti,constant remembrance, but in its superlative stage asaktimost definitely correlates with samadhi,trance. The characteristic of asaktiis natural attraction, the strength of which depends on the practitioner’s bhakti.However, that attraction is so strong that a devotee’s mind habitually turns to the holy names, just as at earlier stages it turned away from them towards mundane subjects.

With this general correlation between the two divisions of sadhana-bhakti,and the description of the six features of Krsna’s name, we conclude this chapter.

## Chapter Twenty-Nine

**Four Stages of Remembrance**

In this chapter and the next, we investigate the five divisions of smarana-dasa,described in the previous chapter as smarana, dharana, dhyana, anusmrti,and samadhi.These translate to recollection, absorption, meditation, constant remembrance, and trance, respectively. The English rendering of these divisions does not do justice to the fine nuances between them, which are so clearly expressed by the Sanskrit words. Obviously, unlike Sanskrit, the English language was not designed to communicate spiritual concepts or yogapractices. What follows is a basic review of the Sanskrit terms. Readers will immediately see how the words clearly express the gradation of spiritual absorption that leads a devotee to the gateway of bhava.

We begin with smarana.

The verbal root smrmeans, “to call to mind,” or “to recollect.” The suffix anaforms the noun “recollection,” or “remembrance.” To call to mind, or to recollect, indicates that the object of contemplation is not in the mind, but must be summoned back to the mind. Moreover, these terms further communicate a sense of repetition. The object is not recalled just once, but has to be repeatedly recalled or brought to mind. It is very much a beginner’s effort. Yet it is the effort of a pure devotee firmly situated in Krsna consciousness.

The next division of smarana-dasais dharana.

The verbal root dhrmeans “to hold,” “to support,” or “to contain.” By adding the suffix anaagain a noun is generated, meaning “the act of holding.” These words now give remembrance a more substantial meaning in that there is a clearly implied sense of permanence, a sense of possessing the object of meditation; hence it is called absorption. The reader achieves a lair idea of dharanaby thinking of how a sponge absorbs and retains water.

Next is dhyana.

This word comes from the verbal root dhyai,which means “to contemplate,” “to meditate,” or “to be thoughtful.” All three meanings take remembrance one step further. But it is neither about recalling nor being absorbed in the object, but about contemplating it and giving it profound consideration. Here we see the mind more actively involved in remembrance, as compared to the more passive involvement earlier. This is real meditation.

After meditation comes constant remembrance, anusmrti.

The verbal root is the same smras in smarana,remembrance, and the prefix anumeans “methodically,” or “lengthwise.” The meaning of anusmrtiis methodical remembrance, across the entire length of both the object of meditation and the effort of meditation. Therefore smaranais the practical application of absorption through a comprehensive, uninterrupted effort. This, we shall later see, means not an immobile meditation, but a dynamic one in the form of a developed meditation on Krsna’s pastimes. Additionally, methodical remembrance means that all other things are excluded.

Both Bhaktivinoda Thakura and Jiva Gosvami place an adjective before anu,and that is dhruva,extending the term into dhru-vanusmrti.The new addition gives the added meaning of “constancy,” and hence, in a purport to The Nectar of Instruction,Srila Prabhupada translates it as “constant remembrance.” So now as the fourth division of smarana-dasawe have methodical, constant remembrance that is oblivious to everything but its object.

The culmination of smarana-dasais samadhi,trance.

The noun is based on the verb dhawhich means “to place.” Two prefixes are connected, the first being sam,as in “together,” or “fully,” and the second a,as in “toward.” The sum of the two stands for “joining together,” thus in context with the first four divisions of smarana, samadhican be understood in two ways:

Joining all aspects of the object together, thereby bringing remembrance of it to a conclusion; or, joining all aspects of smaranatogether, to bring it to its conclusion.

In essence the two are the same. Srila Prabhupada gives a very simple meaning to samadhi,calling it “fixed mind.” This phrase is derived from the Sanskrit dictionary definition, samyag adhiyate 'sminn atma-tattva-yathatmyam:

**“When the mind is fixed for understanding the self, it is said to be in samadhi.”**

This Sanskrit analysis should give readers a preliminary insight into the characteristics of different divisions of nama-bhajana.These divisions will be elaborated upon in the following sections. With knowledge of their characteristics, a sadhakawill have a clear picture of the sankalpasthat he needs to make to progress from one division to the next.

We summarise the above five stages of smaranaby citing Jiva Gosvami:

*tad idam smaranam panca-vidham yat-kincid anu-*  
*sandhabam smaranam. sarvatas cittam akrsya*  
*samanyakarena manodharanam dharana. visesato rupadi-*  
*cintanam dhyanam. amrta-dharavad anavacchin-*  
*nam tad-ddhruvanusmrtih. dhyeya-matra-sphuranam*  
*samadhir iti.*

**“Remembrance unfolds in five stages: To somehow or another think of Krsna is known as smaranam,or remembrance; to withdraw the mind from external objects and concentrate it on the Lord is dharana,or concentration; to precisely reflect on the Lord’s name, form, and other attributes is called dhyana,or meditation; when remembrance proceeds without interruption like a continuous flow of nectar it is called dhruvanu- smrti,or constant remembrance; and when the object of meditation is manifest without awareness even of one’s own self, it is called samadhi,or trance.”**

\* \* \* \*

We shall now examine recollection, smarana,the first level of smarana-dasa.To avoid confusion readers are reminded that both the stage of bhakti, smarana-dasa,and its first division, smarana share the same name.

Recollection is the beginner’s stage of remembrance, which sometimes happens as much by circumstantial arrangement as by effort A circumstantial arrangement is seen in the following pastime: With Krsna standing before them at the time of death, Sisupala and Duryodhana saw Him in their minds, and so were cleared of all offences and liberated. What then is the wonderful destination of devotees who, while trying for nama-bhajana,recall Krsna's, name or form with devotional feelings?

Still, smaranais not a steady form of remembrance. A practitioner tries to hear the maha-mantra,but the next minute his mind and senses are elsewhere. Again, he focuses his mind, and again it imperceptibly slips away. And so it is, over and over again, and sometimes the sadhakadespairs. Yet the effort is pleasing to Krsna, and when there is success, it brings happiness to the practitioner. In this well-known verse, Srimad-Bhagavatampraises this humble attainment as the perfection of life:

*etavan sankhya-yogabhyam*  
*sva-dharma-parinisthaya*  
*janma-labhah parah pumsam*  
*ante narayana-smrtih*

**“The highest perfection of human life, achieved either by complete knowledge of matter and spirit, by practise of mystic powers, or by perfect discharge of occupational duty, is to remember the Personality of Godhead at the end of life.”**

In this slokathe sage Suka mentions jnanis, yogis,and followers of varnasrama,but not devotees. The perfection of these sadhakas does not lie in their effort at smarana,but in their desire to connect with the Lord. The further implication of the verse is that while this kind of smaranais glorious, devotees can easily advance beyond it. Furthermore, the recollection of a devotee gives a different result than that of the non devotee. The practitioner who attempts to do justice to chanting the maha-mantraquickly becomes absorbed by the grace of the holy name, which eventually reveals to him Krsna’s form of exquisite beauty.

Constant efforts at recollection remove inauspiciousness and expand a devotee’s good fortune by freeing him from material contamination. With further purification of heart a sadhaka’sdevotion grows, and as it does, so too does his knowledge, realisation, and renunciation. Spiritually empowered on all fronts and steadily practising smarana,recollection transforms into absorption, and the devotee practitioner enters the kingdom of dharana.

Jiva Gosvami gives the following verse as a description of absorption, dharana:

*visayan dhyayatas cittam*  
*visayesu visajjate*  
*mam anusmaratas cittam*  
*mayy eva praviliyate*

**“The mind of one meditating upon the objects of sense gratification is certainly entangled in such objects, but if one constantly remembers Me, then the mind is absorbed in Me.”**

As previously mentioned, the verbal root dhrmeans to hold. That stage of remembrance where the sadhakacan hold the holy name at the forefront of his mind is dharana.It begins with a weak form of absorption and intensifies with practise. This means that the mind is withdrawn from other things and is fixed at will on the sweet sound vibration of the mantra,its names, and syllables.

While absorption remains a general form of remembrance, its power is to develop systematic attraction to nama-sankirtana.This attraction means attraction to Krsna, or to Radha-Krsna, as the case may be. Some devotees will relish the words bare, krsna,and ramaas the names of Krsna, while others will consider that the Divine Couple have entered their minds through their ears.

Sometimes a devotee may attempt to meditate on the mantra and chant only within his mind. While this is an authorised form of dharana,it is not as effective as loud nama-sankirtana,which engages both internal and external senses. In either case, when dharanais achieved by steady, effective smarana,the symptom is an intense taste for chanting nama-sankirtanaand for hearing about Krsna. The nature of this taste is that it awakens an attraction for nama-bhajanathat is vastly greater than attraction for any thing else. This attraction is so powerful that a devotee absorbed in nama-sankirtanabecomes oblivious to the demands of the body, such as sleep, hunger, and thirst, his objects of meditation having expanded to both the form and qualities of Krsna. And taste is addictive. Therefore the sadhakafeels that he can never get enough of it, what to speak of give it up.

Rupa Gosvami wonderfully describes the awakening of ruciin dharanain the following words:

*syat krsna-nama-caritadi-sitapy avidya-*  
*pittopatapta-rasanasya na rocika nu*  
*kintv adarad anudinam khalu saiva justa*  
*svadvi kramad bhavati tad-gada-mula-bantri*

**“The holy name, character, pastimes, and activities of Krsna are all transcendentally sweet like sugar candy. Although the tongue of one afflicted by the jaundice of avidya\[ignorance\] cannot taste anything sweet, it is wonderful that simply by carefully chanting these sweet names every day, a natural relish awakens within his tongue, and his disease is gradually destroyed at the root.”**

With this awakening of taste comes a truly repentant attitude in which a sadhakalaments how he could have ever let himself be illusioned into the bitter taste of sense gratification. And so, like a prospector who strikes an endless vein of gold and so enters deeper into his mine, the devotee at dharanagreedily dives ever-deeper into the unfathomable nectarean ocean of nama-sankirtana.

\* \* \* \*

As a devotee becomes more proficient in nama-bhajana,the stage of remembrance expands in depth and focus to reach the eminent stage of meditation, or dhyana.

The ripening of absorption broadens the sadhaka’sperception of the holy name and fully reveals to a devotee the words of Padma Purana, abhinnatvan nama-naminoh:

**“There is no difference between the name of Krsna and Krsna Himself.”**

And Krsna means His attributes of form, qualities, and pastimes. The features of this expanded meditation are a subject for later discussion; first let us continue to explore the general aspects of dhyana.

Srila Prabhupada was fond of defining devotional meditation with a line from the Srimad-Bhagavatam, dhyanavasthita-tad- gatena manasa pasyanti yam yoginah:

**“He whom the perfected yogissee within their minds after fixing themselves in trance and absorbing themselves within Him.”**

Herein dhyanais that unwavering condition of the mind in which the yogisees Krsna within his heart. This manifestation of Krsna within is also known as sphurti.It is the progressive unfolding of the bud of the holy name, which reveals its ever-fresh and increasingly attractive features.

Whereas at dharanathe sadhakarelished taste from the sweetness of Krsna’s name, form, and qualities, at dhyanahe relishes the additional sweetness of Krsna’s pastimes. Jiva Gosvami says, visesato rupadi-cintanam dhyanam:

**“To specifically contemplate the Lord’s name, form, and other attributes is called dhyana,or meditation.”**

This intensified rucibecomes the fertile ground in which the creeper of attachment sprouts. The strong taste that results from nama-bhajanaat dhyanais the cause for remembrance being continuous, and for awakening spontaneity in a heart in which it was absent.

Sri Jiva Gosvami quotes the Nrsimha Puranawith the following, definition of dhyana:

*bhagavac carana-dvandva-*  
*dhyanam nirdvandvam iritam*  
*papino ’pi prasangena*  
*vihitam suhitam param*

**“Meditation on the two lotus feet of the Lord is beyond the influence of all dualities. Even if a sinner incidentally takes to meditation, he attains supreme welfare.”**

The word nirdvandvamindicates that meditation frees one from the dualities of the world, such as heat and cold, or happiness and distress. Such release from worldly troubles makes for increased attentiveness and strength in sadhana.It is like finally releasing the handbrake in an automobile that was driving with it on. The word iritamconfirms this understanding to be a true scriptural conclusion and not an excessive glorification.

While the Nrsimha Puranaverse gives the example of a sinner who meditates on the Lord, Srimad-Bhagavatamgives the example of the Pandavas, who in their meditation on Krsna attained a most extraordinary perfection:

**“Thus by pure consciousness due to constant devotional remembrance, they attained the spiritual sky, which is ruled over by the Supreme Narayana, Lord Krsna. This is attained only by those who meditate upon the one Supreme Lord without deviation. This abode of the Lord Sri Krsna, known as Goloka Vrndavana, cannot be attained by persons who are absorbed in the material conception of life. But the Pandavas, being completely washed of all material contamination, attained that abode in their very same bodies.”**

Clearly, the Pandavas’ perfection was assured. They were the Lord’s eternal associates, their consciousness was transcendental, and their forms were eternal. Nonetheless, this verse proclaims that the stage of dhyanais so glorious that even the Lord’s associates consider it a favourable conveyance for their journey to Vaikuntha. It is advanced devotion.

It has been mentioned previously that meditation is an expanded form of nama-bhajanathat incorporates within it Krsna’s form, qualities, and pastimes. Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura reminds us that the manifestation of these attributes is a natural result of nama-bhajana,they cannot be separated from the name, and they should not be meditated upon independent of the name:

*rupa-guna-lila-sphurti nama chada haya na*  
*rupa-guna-lila hoite krsna-nama haya na*

**“Revelations of the Lord’s transcendental form, qualities, and pastimes are never manifest in the absence of His holy name. The holy name of Krsna is never separated from His transcendental form, qualities, or pastimes.”**

Consequently, at the stage of dhyana,the devotee who is dedicated to quality nama-bhajanawill see the holy name expand to Krsna’s form, qualities, and pastimes. This development is systematic and follows a sequence which had its origins in the chanting of Krsna’s names, and which began at sravana-dasa.

Nama-bhajanabegins with offenceless chanting, namabhasa. Within namabhasaare different stages that correspond to the varying presence of bad habits and offences. The less the obstacles, the more advanced the namabhasa.When the sadhakais free of all obstacles, his chanting becomes pure, suddha.This suddha-nama also has further subdivisions according to the degree of the sadhaka’s purity. And even when the sadhakachants with love, there will be further stages of development that correspond to the maturing of bhavaand the unfolding of prema,which manifests fully with the attainment of rasa.

The point has been made that the holy name of Krsna reveals itself in stages through the divisions of smarana-dasa.As it does, nama-bhajanasuccessively reveals Krsna’s attributes from form, to qualities, to pastimes. Additionally, the maturing of the holy name increasingly manifests each consecutive attribute. In other words, as each feature of Krsna manifests, its presence grows from weak to strong with the progression of smarana.We show how this takes place with the burgeoning of one attribute, Krsna’s form:

At smaranathe name begins to reveal its divine form, and as the cultivation of the name passes through stages of maturing, the form of the Lord is also increasingly manifest. The initial appear ance of Krsna’s form is a partial presence within the mind, and its full-blown manifestation is His personal darsanaat the perfection of prema-sankirtana, sampatti-dasa.

A further factor should be considered:

**In addition to the name, there is another impetus that causes the Lord’s form to dawn. Just as the Lord’s name progressively mam fests itself by being heard, in a similar way the form of Krsna grad ually manifests by being heard of.**

Jiva Gosvami writes, suddhe cantahkarane rupa-sravanena tad udaya-yogyata bhavati:

**“When the heart is purified by nama-sankirtana,a devotee can hear about the Lord’s form, and by so doing, the heart becomes fit for revelation of the same.”**

That is to say, when a sadhakaregularly hears or reads glorification of Krsna’s mind-enchanting appearance, those descriptions impress themselves in his mind and increasingly come to life during nama-bhajana.Hearing about the form of the Lord also includes seeing the deity in the temple.

Moreover, a devotee’s preferred relationship with Krsna is reflected in the specific form of which he hears, such as the son of Yasoda, the friend of Subala, the beloved of Radha, or other Vaikuntha forms. This follows the principle that the result of an activity matches the discipline a devotee has practised. So a devotee will hear about the form of the Lord which he aspires to worship. This preference of a sadhakais beautifully described by the creator in the following verse:

*tvam bhakti-yoga-paribhavita hrt-saroja*  
*asse sruteksita-patho nanu natha pumsam*  
*yad-yad-dhiya ta urugaya vibhavayanti*  
*tat-tad-vapuh pranayase sad-anugrahaya*

**“O my Lord! Your devotees can see You through the ears by the process of bona fide hearing, and thus their hearts become cleansed, and You take Your seat there. You are so merciful to Your devotees that You manifest Yourself in the particular eternal form of transcendence in which they always think of You.”**

The natural advent of the Lord’s form will vary from devotee to devotee. Spontaneous practitioners will generally partake of an earlier and more distinct encounter than their regulated counterparts. As both these kinds of practitioners advance in chanting, so does the constancy and intensity of Krsna’s presence. And at a certain stage, these two attributes of name and form become inseparable. This means wherever one is present, the other is there.

Thereafter, meditation further cultivates the development of both the name and form until the heart becomes so saturated with their presence that it brings forth Krsna’s qualities.
