Another approach to this verse accepts the devotional given that Krsna is controlled by sadhya-bhakti.But because sadhana-bhakti gradually leads a devotee to the perfectional stage, logic demands that it, too, is part of the glorification in this verse. We are again led to conclude that the word bhaktialso refers to sadhana,which even with all a sadhaka’simperfections somehow controls the supreme controller. Because Krsna is so captivated and controlled by sadhana,the advanced devotee in trance is eminently qualified to see Krsna.

Whether Krsna shows Himself or not is another thing.

The example of a devotee who did see the Lord in his samadhiis Lord Brahma. He underwent severe penance, and while in trance he was not only able to see the Lord, but was touched by Him and received spiritual guidance.

And yet, meeting Krsna in trance is not a given. It is a possibility. When Gopa-kumara was in Tapaloka, the sage Pippalayana taught the boy the art of meditation. While speaking of how Krsna reveals Himself, the sage mentions the word kadacit,which means “sometimes.” This indicates that sometimes a bhakti-yogigets to see the Lord, an example being Narada in his last life. But “sometimes” means that it is an occasional event to which only some are privy. The sage’s actual words were:

*kadacid bhakta-vatsalyad*  
*yati ced drsyatam drsoh*  
*jnana-drstyaiva taj jatam*  
*abhimanah param drsoh*

**“If the Lord, out of compassion for His devotees, sometimes reveals Himself to their eyes, that vision actually occurs by the power of the mind; one only imagines the eyes to be the seers.”**

In giving examples of a practitioner’s trance, Jiva Gosvami cites the order the sage Narada gives Vyasa.

Narada instructs his disciple to repeatedly observe the pastimes of Krsna in samadhiand then record what he has seen:

*urukramasyakhila-bandha-muktaye*  
*samadhinanusmara tad-vicestitam*

**“You can think of the pastimes of the Lord in trance for the liberation of the people in general from all material bondage.”**

These are examples in which a devotee can sometimes see the Lord in samadhi.And while a devotee who is so attracted to Krsna is always eager to see his worshipable Lord, if he does not see Krsna in sadhanahe will certainly see Him in prema.The hankering for a darsanawill simply hone his love for Krsna and make vision of the Lord all the more relishable when it finally takes place.

Devotees sometimes wonder:

**“Does a sadhakasee Krsna with his eyes?”**

**“In the realm of bhakti,such things are always possible. But if the lesser vision within the mind is not assured, the greater vision with the eyes is at least as uncertain.”**

Kardama Muni saw the Lord before him, riding on Garuda and surrounded by confidential associates. And after King Mucukunda awakened from a long sleep, he also saw Krsna in a four-armed form.

As mentioned, in its own way sadhana-bhakticaptivates and controls Krsna. If a sadhakahas performed the kind of service and sadhanathat truly captures Krsna’s heart, then the Lord may be inclined to fulfil His devotee’s inner desire and give His darsana. Who or what can obstruct Krsna from doing what He wants!

And while yogisalso attain samadhi,they do so with great difficulty and with a realisation that depends upon their aspiration. For the most part, yogiswill fall away from their sadhana;by comparison, accomplished devotees will rarely, if ever, do so. This feature of bhakti-samadhinow follows.

\* \* \* \*

The yogiswho meditate on things of substance attain what is known as samprajnata-samadhi,of which there are two kinds. When the object of meditation is something gross, then it is not much more than an elevated form of mental speculation. However, when the object is the Supersoul, then that attainment is spiritual.

Then there are yogiswho have no object of meditation, and they can attain asamprajnata-samadhi.They lose all sense of awareness, even of their selves. This is the perfection of today’s non-Vedic meditation in which students are told to clear their minds of all thoughts.

Even if perfected, none of these yogisexperience the taste of pure service to Krsna. Moreover, they all undergo great difficulty for a paltry perfection that has a very low success rate. As a result, many unsuccessful yogisbecome professionals, attracting followers with their limited knowledge and attainments. Uddhava discloses an unspoken truth of yogapractice—that the majority of aspirants seeking samadhiabandon the process in frustration:

*prayasah pundarikaksa*  
*yunyanto yogino manah*  
*visidanty asamadhanan*  
*mano-nigraba-karsitah*

**“O lotus-eyed Lord! Generally, those yogiswho try to steady the mind experience frustration because of their inability to perfect the state of trance. Thus they weary in their attempt to bring the mind under control.”**

And even those few who do succeed in attaining samadhi,because they take pride in their accomplishment in yoga,they fail to take shelter of Krsna, as a result of which they are defeated by the illusory energy. Srila Prabhupada gives the example of Visvamitra Muni who, at the stage of samadhi,was allured into sex by the Apsara, Menaka.

On the other hand, by constant nama-bhajanaand absorption in pastimes, devotees who depend on Krsna’s blessings eventually reach their destination. The Lord emphasises that this success is not an exception, but the rule:

*vita-raga-bhaya-krodha*  
*man-maya mam upasritah*  
*bahavo jnana-tapasa*  
*puta mad-bhavam agatah*

“Being freed from attachment, fear, and anger, being fully absorbed in Me and taking refuge in. Me, many, many persons in the past became purified by knowledge of Me—and thus they all attained transcendental love for Me.”

To practise samadhi, yogisalways seek out secluded places when their attempts at trance will not be disturbed. On the other hand Vaisnavas in Lord Caitanya’s line generally preach, and so will often find themselves in crowded metropolises, not in unfrequented forests

**“How do preachers or devotees living in cities avoid disturbance?”**

**“By making the best possible arrangement, and then depending on Krsna to protect them from distractions.”**

This means a devotee selects a lifestyle that is favourable to his goals and rejects everything that is not. Otherwise he will not be peaceful enough to undertake nama-bhajana,what to speak of reaching its perfection. A sadhakamust be fixed in his determination, and not be distracted by unnecessary material objects that can entangle him into possessiveness and deviate him from sadhana.

We should keep in mind the injunction of Brahma-sutradiscussed in an earlier chapter. Its directive should be the rule of thumb for all Vaisnavas, whether they reside in a city or a forest. A devotee serious about sadhana-bhajanashould mould his life in pursuance of the following rule, yatraikagrata tatravisenat:

**“Krsna consciousness should be practised in the place, time, and condition where single-pointed concentration, ekagrata, of the mind is possible.”**

There is no arguing the fact that a secluded setting is superior to an urban area.

When Gopa-kumara found himself in Tapaloka, the peaceful atmosphere improved meditation on his mantra,and in turn the mantraexerted an increased influence on him. Srila Prabhupada wanted his followers to regularly visit Vrndavana and Mayapur to avail themselves of the spiritual atmosphere that pervades those places. And he told devotees that after a lifetime of preaching, they could retire to either place for nama-bhajana.Srila Prabhupada invited all his followers, everyone. He said,

“We should make our life so simple and easy that we can get our necessities of life without any hard labour and save time to advance in Krsna consciousness. That is perfect civilisation. This is not perfect civilisation.

There is every chance of being influenced by these lusty desires, and that is going on, especially in the Western country. For fulfilling these lusty desires there are so many clubs at night, nightclubs, bottomless and topless and so many advertisements. This is not civilisation. Civilisation is peaceful life, and we should be satisfied in simple mode of life and always think of Krsna. Therefore, Vrndavana life is like that, Vrndavana life, especially those who are engaged in devotional service. So we have opened this temple to give facility to the elderly section of the human being to come and live with us. We invite all elderly persons, especially retired person. They should come and live with us. We have got a nice guesthouse, and if required, we can construct many other guesthouses. At least those are retired. Everyone should retire after fiftieth year. That is the injunction of the sastras,that pancasordbvam vanam vrajet.After fifty years one should give up family life and vanam vrajet...vanammeans Vrndavana... Similarly, Prahlada Maharaja has advised:

*tat sadhu manye ’sura-varya dehinam*  
*sada samudvigna-dhiyam asad-grahat*  
*bitvatma-patam grham andha-kupam*  
*vanam gato yad dharim asrayeta*

**“Vanam gato. One should go in the vana,in Vrndavana. Then what to do there? Harim asrayeta.Otherwise, if we live in Vrndavana like monkeys and other animals, that will not be beneficial. Harim asrayeta.Come here, live here, and take shelter of Hari. That is the ultimate goal. Therefore, Hari personally says, Krsna,** ***sarva-dharman parityajya mam ekam saranam vraja.*** **Harim asrayeta.**

**“So we are not only inviting Indians throughout the whole world. Now we have got connection with the whole world. We invite everyone. At least after the age of fifty they should come here in Vrndavana. They should live peacefully and take shelter at the lotus feet of Krsna-Balarama and be happy in this life and get salvation in next life.”**

In Hungary we have established New Vraja-dhama and installed Radha-Syamasundara in a replica of Vrndavana, and with a similar purpose. After spending their lives in serving Srila Prabhupada’s mission in Hungary, devotees can come and live in Krishna Valley, chant Hare Krsna, serve Their Lordships, and be absorbed in samadhi.

We now conclude on conditions for the cultivation of samadhi. When attained, these attributes are characteristic of the Vaisnava who has attained strong attachment to Krsna, vaisnava-samadhi. The next chapter concludes our study of trance and our study of smarana-dasa.

## Chapter Thirty-Two

**In Praise of Samadhi**

It must be admitted that reaching and perfecting samadhi,the stage whereat a practitioner may knock on the door of ecstatic devotion, is neither easy nor quick. One needs to be spiritually adept and resolutely determined. We should remember that bhava-bhaktiis rarely achieved, and the trance of attachment is Krsna’s requisite lor it. But then, pure devotees are a rare and special breed among the multitude of seekers. Thus statistics, and more relevant, Lord Caitanya’s blessings, are on their side.

It can be done! They can do it! We can do it!

In the following verses, Krsna glorifies the stage of samadhiand encourages the sadhakato remain determined in his systematic efforts at perfection. While the Bhagavad-gitaspeaks to Prabhupada’s purports speak to devotees. Still, whatever applies to the lesser monistic hatha-yogisis applicable to the superior Vaisnavas. The advice of the Lord is applicable to all practitioners.

Surely some of our readers have duelled with doubts regarding their eligibility for perfection and their ability to go back to

Godhead in this life. In reading this book does the reader think:

**“While these pages are inspiring, is smarana-dasareally something I can practically refine to its finale of samadhi?And if I were to attain trance, will Krsna give me entrance into His kingdom of love?”**

Ascending the stages of smarana-dasarequires perseverance and a conviction that it can be done. That conviction is our faith in the promise of Krsna and Srila Prabhupada. And faithful perseverance brings its rewards, which in this case is samadhiin nama-bhajana,an attainment glorious to the extreme. Krsna praises that accomplishment in the following verses:

*yatroparamatecittam*  
*niruddham yoga-sevaya*  
*yatra caivatmanatmanam*  
*pasyann atmani tusyati*

*sukham atyantikam yat tad*  
*buddhi-grahyam atindriyam*  
*vetti yatra na caivayam*  
*sthitas calati tattvatah*

*yam labdhva caparam labbam*  
*manyate nadhikam tatah*  
*yasmin sthito na duhkhena*  
*gurunapi vicalyate*

*tam vidyad duhkha-samyoga-*  
*viyogam yoga-samjnitam*

**“In the stage of perfection called trance, or samadhi, one’s mind is completely restrained from material mental activities by practise of yoga.This perfection is characterised by one’s ability to see the self by the pure mind and to relish and rejoice in the self. In that joyous state, one is situated in boundless transcendental happiness, realised through transcendental senses. Established thus, one never departs from the truth, and upon gaining this he thinks there is no greater gain. Being situated in such a position, one is never shaken, even in the midst of the greatest difficulty. This indeed is actual freedom from all miseries arising from material contact.”**

Devotional trance attained by the grace of nama-sankirtanais characterised by complete absorption in the attributes of Krsna—His names, form, qualities, and pastimes. A devotee has no connection with the material aspect of life, for he is now fully dedicated to the fruits of nama-bhajana.By the grace of Krsna’s names a devotee is immersed in his identity as spirit soul, and may also have a strong inclination to his spiritual form and service.

Although not yet situated in the bliss of transcendence, a devotee in trance experiences pleasure that surpasses all sensual enjoyments.

The joy of being one in thought with Krsna’s divine sports creates such a deep impression within the heart that it is almost unheard of that a devotee would again revert to sense gratificanon. Elated by this unprecedented happiness, he looks back at the many years of effort and failure, at the hardships and sacrifices, and thinks, fully convinced,

**“It was all worthwhile. If I had to, I would do it again. There is nothing better than this.”**

And while the greatest challenge—rising to bhavapana-dasa—is yet m come, for now he basks in the happiness of his attainment. If Krsna has brought him this far, He will assist him to the next step, however difficult that may be. Again the devotee thinks,

**“Why would Krsna have brought me this far to then turn me back? Surely He will not withdraw His mercy now, as tricky and elusive as He, and love for Him, may be.”**

Such is the attainment of samadhi,wherein a devotee no longer suffers the threefold miseries of life. He now sees his material body being as distant from him as the bodies of others. It is but one of many in a far-off crowd.

\* \* \* \*

The resolute determination to gain shelter under Krsna’s lotus feet described above is rarely reached without the sadhakafording many rivulets of doubts. Even having read the glories of devotional trance, a sadhakamay have thought,

**“How is it possible for me to attain such perfection?”**

Taking compassion upon His devotee, one day Krsna speaks from within the sadhaka’sheart:

**“Have faith in Me and follow the path marked by the acaryas.”**

At first the devotee wonders whether he is hearing his mind, but as a special bliss spreads through his being he is convinced otherwise. And yet doubts continue to linger, and he asks:

**“O Lord! Is it really possible?”**

Krsna is patient. After all, He too has invested so much time to escort this jivato his current attainment. The Lord continues:

**“We—the acaryasand I—are not small men. What is difficult, we make easy; what is rare, we make abundant.”**

**“What do I have to do?”**

**“You must make every endeavour to free yourself of attachment and invest your everything in Me. Listen to what I have to say; listen to this:**

*sa niscayena yoktavyo*  
*yogo ’nirvinna-cetasa*  
*sankalpa-prabhavan kamams*  
*tyaktva sarvan asesatah*

*manasaivendriya-gramam*  
*viniyamya samantatah*

**“One should engage oneself in the practice of yoga with determination and faith and not be deviated from the path. One should abandon, without exception, all material desires born of mental speculation and thus control all the senses on all sides by the mind.”**

Sometimes the practitioner wavers in his efforts. From sravana-dasa through varana,and then smaranato samadhi,the steps are long, with many opportunities for disappointment.

When he is enthusiastic the devotee thinks:

**“Although it will take a long time, I am sure I can become a pure devotee.”**

And Krsna immediately replies:

**“Yes! Be determined and be faithful. Do not leave Me again.”**

Yet a lack of good sadhanaresults in spiritual weakness:

**“But sometimes I feel like giving up.”**

As the ultimate well-wisher Krsna continues His support:

**“Do not be disgusted with yourself, or with the challenges to your bhajana. Be certain that by My grace, you will succeed. That conviction is called anirvinna-cetasa.”**

Hearing this, the sadhakagains heart, but again after some time he thinks:

**“After so many years, I am still struggling with desires. Where is samadhi? Why has Krsna not recognised my efforts.”**

Smiling, the Lord, Who is often blamed for the bad choices of His children, replies:

**“Do not be faint of heart. It may appear that you are not getting anywhere, but I see it differently.”**

**“How do You see it?”**

Krsna’s voice is as sweet as honey and as smooth as ghee:

**“I see you like the little sparrow trying to empty the ocean. Do you know the story?”**

The devotee replies:

**“Yes, I do!”**

**“How much did the sparrow achieve in his attempt to retrieve his nest from the ocean?”**

**“Not much!”**

**“But then?”**

The sadhakacontinues:

**“Narada sent Garuda who threatened the ocean, and the sparrow got back his nest.”**

Krsna nods, slightly shaking His shark-shaped earrings:

**“And when I come, or when I send My associate, then the ocean of your sadhanawill become like the water in a calf’s hoofprint. You will step over it while dancing in sankirtana.”**

With these convincing words laced with the sweetest nectar, the devotee again takes heart:

**“Why am I so foolish to lament? I should count my lucky stars. After who-knows-how-many lifetimes, perfection is just a stone’s throw away. Let me try for it. And if I do not get it in this life, I will in the next.”**

With such determination the devotee takes shelter of nama-sankirtana,and as his heart becomes purified his mind comes under control, and so his senses enter Krsna’s exclusive service:

*sanaih sanair uparamed*  
*buddhya dhrti-grhitaya*  
*atma-samstham manah krtva*  
*na kincid api cintayet*

**“Gradually, step by step, one should become situated in trance by means of intelligence sustained by full conviction, and thus the mind should be fixed on the self alone and should think of nothing else.”**

The process of nama-bhajanais systematic. By constant effort in smaranathe practitioner gradually masters his mind and senses, and is able to be absorbed in Krsna’s name by fully concentrated intelligence, buddhya dhrti-grhitaya.This is the stage of dharana.

With the mind now a friend, it can be absorbed in further meditation on Krsna’s form, qualities, and pastimes, atma-samstham manah krtva. This is the stage of dhyana,meditation.

Then gradually, step by step, the devotee attains anusmrti,constant remembrance, and finally trance. Provided that he protects himself on all sides and does not get distracted by illusion, Krsna consciousness in trance becomes the devotee’s permanent state, uparamed.

These gradual steps towards bhava-bhaktiare the sankalpas which, like the waxing moon, increasingly illuminate with their rays the darkness of the directions. When the moon is full, it reveals Krsna playing His flute by the bank of the Yamuna. And as the sadhakalooks on in wonder, Krsna approaches, and smiling sweetly, says:

**“My beloved devotee! Did I not tell you that you would meet with success?”**

But the sadhakais speechless. Is he dreaming? Is this a vision in his mind? Is he seeing Krsna with his eyes, hearing Krsna with his ears?

The Lord teases:

**“Did I not tell you it would all be worthwhile?”**

Falling prostrate before the Lord, the sadhakatries to speak, but the words are stuck in his throat. Yet in his heart he manages to answer, an answer that becomes his love song:

**“Yes! It was all worthwhile. All worthwhile!”**

The moon always shines. At night it is visible, in the day it is not And so Krsna and His entourage also become invisible; all that is left are footprints in the sands by the Yamuna’s shore, the same footprints that are impressed within the sadhaka’sheart. And while the bliss of encountering Krsna enlivens the devotee’s being, that same bliss drives him forward for more.

But that “more” is not to be had in the realm of sadhana.It exists, par excellence,in the realms of prema,and it is to that abode of consciousness that he must now transition. Of all sankalpas,the one from samadhito bhavapanais the most challenging. It will be a sankalpathat is as much dependent on grace from above as the efforts of the sadhaka.

Thakura Bhaktivinoda writes,

**“Because vraja-bhaktiis the most desirable goal, it is the living entity’s eternal duty to cultivate it up to the stage of samadhiby following the mood of the residents of Vraja.”**

The reader may wonder:

**“Does this mean that a devotee should stop at the stage of smarana-samadhi?"**

The acarya’sanswer would be:

**“No!”**

The intent of the Thakura is to urge a sadhakato advance to the stage of trance in sadhana,and by the grace of nama-sankirtana proceed to taste the nectar of vraja-bhaktiin bhava-samadhi,and thereafter in prema-samadhi.When the Lord spoke in four verses the very essence of Srimad-Bhagavatam,He too encouraged Brahma to pursue cultivation to the far end of bhakti.He said,

**“You must never stop, but continue your quest until you reach this.”**

**“What is ‘this’?”**

**“Trance in prema!”**

Krsna taught Brahma:

*etavad eva jijnasyam*  
*tattva-jijnasunatmanah*  
*anvaya-vyatirekabhyam*  
*yat syat sarvatra sarvada*

**“A person who is searching after the Supreme Absolute Truth, the Personality of Godhead, must certainly search for it up to this, in all circumstances, in all space and time, and both directly and indirectly.”**

The goal of this quest may be a challenge. But then nothing of value is ever achieved without a corresponding effort. That effort is the way of bhakti-sankalpas,the same effort to which the Lord encouraged Lord Brahma at the conclusion of talks at the dawn of another creation:

*pramanais tat-sad-acarais*  
*tad-abhyasair nirantaram*  
*bodhayan atmanatmanam*  
*bhaktim apy uttamam labhet*

**“The highest devotion is attained by slow degrees by the method of constant endeavour for self-realisation with the help of scriptural evidence, theistic conduct, and perseverance in practice.”**

## Part Seven

**Sankalpa for Chanting with Emotions**

## Chapter Thirty-Three

**The Sankalpa of Bhava-Seva**

Parts One and Two of this book defined some of the main aspects of sadhana-bhakti.Parts Three, Four, and Five elaborated on the details, examples, and dynamics of sankalpa.The previous Part, Six, examined the determinations that take place in the process of attentive nama-bhajana,which culminates in samadhi.

In Chapter Twenty-seven we listed certain important characteristics of smarana-dasathat were elaborated upon in ensuing chapters, with two exceptions: the mood in which the holy name is cultivated—vipralambba-bbava;and how success in sadhanais made possible by divine grace—krpa.Because of the importance of these topics, they are presented in Part Seven and Part Eight respectively, followed by the Summary and Conclusion, a precis of each chapter.

This present chapter introduces an aspect of sadhanathat is integral to attaining bhava-bhakti,and that is practice with emotion, bhava-seva,also known as vipralambha-seva.

According to the following maxim, a practice and its goal must correspond:

*sva-sadbananurupam hi*  
*phala sarvatra sidhyati*

In the words of Bhaktivinoda Thakura:

**“One attains a perfection that corresponds to his meditation.”**

It stands to reason, therefore, that a perfection that is saturated with the emotion of love is attained by a practice with a mood of emotion.

Although the ultimate purpose of the Vedas is to bring everyone to loving devotion to Krsna, to achieve that, different parts of the Vedas propose different sadhanasand sadhyasto match the qualification of their followers. Narada instructs Gopa-kumara on this topic in this way:

*evam tat-tat-sadhananam*  
*ritir apy avagamyatam*  
*taj-jnapakanam sastranam*  
*vacananam ca tadrsi*

**“The methods of discipline and the scriptural statements that teach them should be understood to differ according to the different goals to be achieved.”**

Because the Vedas offer so many paths to so many perfections, their students are often confused about the goal of life, and so they rarely have a clear perspective on the consolidated message of scriptures. Even Krsna, the origin of the Vedas and its first professor, advises Arjuna to rise above the potpourris of sadhanasand sadhyasand understand the essential purpose of the scriptures.

By the grace of acaryaslike Rupa Gosvami and Srila Prabhupada, Gaudiya Vaisnavas know the distilled message of the Vedas to be loving devotion to Krsna, attained through sadhana-bhakti. Thus a devotee’s picture of spiritual perfection is going back to Godhead and participating in pastimes of love with Krsna’s eternal associates. But exactly how do we get there?

With a goal that clearly includes divine emotion, a contemplative sadhakawill eventually come to the conclusion that in order to correspond to its goal, his sadhanamust also be imbued with spiritual emotion. How to achieve that kind of practice will require a close examination of our scriptures: Srimad-Bhagavatam,the books of the Gosvamis, and Srila Prabhupada’s other books. Since they teach pure sadhana-bhakti,which culminates in loving devotion, those texts must also teach the cultivation of emotion as an integral part of a sadhaka’spractice. And they do! But a devotee must be well read to glean this aspect of their message.

For example, after Krsna tells Arjuna that the best kind of yoga is sadhana-bhaktiimbued with pure faith, He advises Arjuna to incorporate the emotion of attachment into his bhajana.The Lord says,

*mayy asakta-manah partha*  
*yogam yunjan mad-asrayah*  
*asamsayam samagram mam*  
*yatha jnasyasi tac chrnu*

**“Now hear, O son of Prtha, how by practising yogain full consciousness of Me, with mind attached to Me, you can know Me in full, free from doubt.”**

The spiritual science of awakening love for Krsna, of being always absorbed in affectionate thoughts of Him, is called abhidheya-jnana.Like sambandha-jnana—knowledge of our relationship with Krsna—it takes time for a devotee to fully assimilate and put knowledge of cultivation into practice.

Until a devotee has a full grasp of abhidheya-jnana,his sadhana is generally formulaic and mechanical. However, the proper cultivation of regulated sadhana-bhakti,matured by study of Srimad-Bhagavatam,leads a devotee to conclude that practice with spiritual emotion is an essential requisite to enter the realm of bhava.

It should be made clear that sadhanawith emotion is not an artificial imitation of the symptoms of love. That kind of exhibition is unauthorised and only takes its followers to the dead end of sahajiyaism. Instead, service with emotion is vipralambha-seva, or sadhanaperformed with the realisation that one is distant from Krsna, a distance that is a great misfortune.

Equally relevant is the realisation that others are distant from Krsna, in which case vipralambha-sevamanifests through acts of preaching and the awakening of a corresponding sentiment, compassion. In this case the development of compassion for those devoid of bhaktito Krsna gives rise to one’s own ever-increasing feelings of separation, and so the preacher becomes doubly qualified for Krsna’s grace—by preaching and by practice.

And so one will ask:

**“But how do we awaken spiritual emotion?”**

We answer:

**“Since emotion is spontaneous, efforts to experience it are inadequate. And yet the process of sadhanacan awaken spiritual emotion, just as it ultimately awakens eternal, transcendental emotion, prema.It is a matter of cultivation, as expressed in the basic definition of pure devotional service, krsnanusilanam.”**

The preceding chapters have emphasised two aspects of cultivation, namely sankalpaand ekagrata—determinations and attentive ness. When bhava-sevasprouts on the creeper of devotion, then sadhana-bhaktitakes on the full characteristics of separation. In the meantime, emotion is in a formative stage. But it is there—or rather, it should be.

**“How to kick-start that emotion if it is not present in sadhana?”**

**“By being attentive to the need of developing emotion.”**

As a devotee studies Srila Prabhupada’s books, and other books that are harmonious with Srila Prabhupada’s, he will become increasingly aware of the misery of material existence on one side, and the bliss of vraja-bhaktion the other. Chanting the maha-mantrain such a polarised condition, the mood of separation gradually awakens and intensifies in a practitioner. And when vipralambha-sevabecomes so exceedingly intense as to invoke Krsna’s mercy, a devotee is gifted with love in separation, a truth attested to by Sri Sukadeva:

*pibanti ye bhagavata atmanab satam*  
*kathamrtam sravana-putesu sambhrtam*  
*punanti te visaya-vidusitasayam*  
*vrajanti tac-carana-saroruhantikam*

**“Those who drink through aural reception, fully filled with the nectarean message of Lord Krsna, the beloved of the devotees, purify the polluted aim of life known as material enjoyment and thus go back to Godhead, to the lotus feet of Him \[the Personality of Godhead\].”**

The cumulative result of well-directed cultivation is that a devotee gives up all gross and subtle desires for liberation and sense enjoyment. While sadhanaundertaken with feeling manifests in every limb of bhakti,it is especially associated with, and especially relish- able through, nama-sankirtana.This has been extensively discussed in earlier chapters. The Visnudutas confirm to Gopa-kumara the supremacy of nama-sankirtanaover all other limbs of devotion:

*param srimat-padambhoja*  
*sadasangaty-apeksaya*  
*nama-sankirtana-prayam*  
*visuddham bhaktim acara*

**“Simply practise pure devotional service, mainly in the form of nama-sankirtana, with the hope of gaining the eternal contact of the Lord’s divine lotus feet.”**

As with every aspect of bhakti, vipralambha-sevahas its requisite qualification, which is either steadiness or taste. When that initial mood, bhava,is cultivated further, it matures to natural emotion at the stage of asakti.Whether a devotee has attained spontaneous devotion or whether he remains a regulated practitioner, his devotion should be coloured by feelings of separation.

During the initial cultivation of bhava-seva,emotion is an aspect of knowledge, abhidheya-jnana.When, however, emotion becomes more spontaneous, knowledge of it becomes a concomitant factor. Nonetheless, knowledge of service in separation is essential to the attainment of emotion. As Krsna says,

*vidusah karma-siddhih syad*  
*yatha naviduso bhavet*

**“Those who know what they are doing achieve success in their work, whereas ignorant people do not.”**

From what has been written above, it can be seen that cultivating vipralambhaincludes acquiring a grasp of abhidheya-jnana and the practices that correspond to it, keeping one’s sights on the goal while being attentive to one’s progress in sadhana,and finally rendering service with such heartfelt feelings that Krsna becomes obliged to bestow His mercy.

In the form of Caitanya Mahaprabhu, Krsna Himself taught us how to express this mood of separation in His Sri Siksastaka,praying to Krsna to be able to chant His holy names in ecstatic love:

*nayanam galad-asru-dharaya*  
*vadanam gadgada-ruddbaya gira*  
*pulakair nicitam vapuh kada*  
*tava nama-grahane bhavisyati*

**“My dear Lord! When will My eyes be beautified by filling with tears that constantly glide down as I chant Your holy name? When will My voice falter and all the hairs on My body stand erect in transcendental happiness as I chant Your holy name?”**

While all aspects of devotional service are the grace of Krsna, the more elevated the devotion aspired for, the more elusive the requisite grace. Yet we are fortunate that in this age Krsna appears in a form in which He is eager to distribute divine grace. Indeed, as Caitanya Mahaprabhu, Krsna freely distributes prema—the rarest spiritual treasure and the ultimate expression of mercy. Thus, by the grace of Gauranga, what was rarely attained in the past—and even then with great difficulty—is now secured with relative ease. We need only know the art of appealing to Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s kind heart.

\* \* \* \*

The subject of vipralambhais voluminous, and yet we have dedicated only a few chapters to its glories. Perhaps in the future a Vaisnava will do justice to the topic by writing a book on it. In the meantime we request our readers to recognise the importance of rendering service with emotion as a means of practising sadhanaand attaining bhava.

We employ the phrase bhava-sevaas the greater expression of emotions which include vipralambha-seva.The purpose is to emphasise the importance of emotion in sadhana.That said, later chapters on this topic will focus on feelings of separation; however, our starting point is at the more general service with emotion.

In the definition of pure devotional service beginning with anya-bhilasita-sunyam,the word anusilanam,cultivation, has two aspects:

An active form, cesta-rupa—which engages the body, mind, and words; and an emotional form, bhava-rupa—which consists of emotion.

These are the ways in which devotional service is cultivated.

By far the greatest emphasis in vaidhi-sadhana-bhaktiis on the active form of cultivation, cesta-ruðṁ,in which a devotee accepts things favourable to his service and rejects those which are unfavourable. The emotional aspect of cultivation, bhava-rupa,comes to prominence at bhava-bhakti,as the spiritual emotions generated by it are both transcendental and significant.

However, bhava-rupadoes not play an insignificant role in sadhana-bhakti.Emotions at sadhanaare not transcendental, but they are relevant emotions nonetheless, and thus are spiritual to the extent that spiritualisation of a sadhakahas taken place. These emotions come to the fore at the stage of taste and attachment, which Krsna makes a condition for the attainment of love. That being the case, emotions at less advanced stages of sadhanaare not inconsequential. Indeed they are imperative.

Let us recall the definition of bhava-bhakti:

*suddha-sattva-visesatma*  
*prema-suryamsu-samya-bhak*  
*rucibhis citta-masrnya-*  
*krd asau bhava ucyate*

**“When devotional service is executed on the transcendental platform of pure goodness, it is like a sunray of love for Krsna. At such a time, devotional service causes the heart to be softened by various tastes, and one is then situated in bhava \[emotion\].”**

The marginal characteristic of the stage of bhava-bhaktiis that the heart is softened by ecstatic emotions, and so the active forms of cultivation—like preaching, prasadadistribution, and temple service, for example—are a result of emotion. Thus a guiding feature of ecstatic devotion, bhava-bhakti,is bhava-rupa.Even though this form of bhava-rupais electrified by suddha-sattvain the form Krsna’s hladiniand sarhvitpotencies, it is the result of an original cultivation that took place at the stage of sadhana.

Tracing back the cause from the effect based on the principle of bhaktya sanjataya bhaktya,that bhaktigives rise to bhakti. we must infer that divine emotion is generated by another kind of emotion. And that other emotion is attachment, asakti,which Rupa Gosvami affirms to be an imperative prerequisite for bhava. Similarly, even earlier stages of sadhana,especially taste and less so steadiness, must also display corresponding degrees of emotion. These expressions of emotion in practice and their maturation in ecstasy are known as bhava-seva.

After reading the above, that divine emotion is generated by another emotion, readers may ask:

**“Is asaktinot a divine emotion, then?”**

The answer to that question is:

**“While not transcendental, asaktiis spiritual, as are the strong emotions of fondness for Krsna that it generates. We remind the reader that emotions at any stage of sadhana,like sadhanaitself, are not transcendental, but they are relevant emotions nonetheless, and thus are spiritual to the extent that spiritualisation of a sadhaka has taken place.”**

From the first contact a devotee has with Krsna consciousness, it is bhava-sevathat is the impetus to advance in spiritual life. Let us briefly view how that is the case.

The very beginning of spiritual life is unknown piety, ajnata-sukrti.Unknowingly a devotee renders service, and because bhakti begets bhakti,by an emotion such as curiosity he will connect further with Krsna consciousness.

Faith is the next emotion, followed by the feeling of belonging, belonging to the company of devotees. Along with practice comes many challenges, throughout which a devotee experiences a host of emotions, foremost of which is the conviction that he is doing the right thing. And through all this, faith is felt, belonging is felt, conviction is felt—all as an emotion.

Finally a devotee becomes steady in both active and emotional service, the latter being a sense of duty. And when he reaches taste and attachment, bhava-rupabecomes the helmsman of cesta-rupa. This is so much more true for the raganuga-sadhaka,who will have been inspired by emotions of eagerness or greed at even earlier stages of practice. And once divine grace gives the sadhaka entrance into ecstatic devotion, his mind is saturated by transcendental emotion, its effects permeating his body.

In summary, bhava-ruðṁboth exists and is important, even though it is not much emphasised in a society of regulated devotees. Indeed it is regrettable that we sometimes hear neophyte devotees relegating a peer’s valid feelings as sentimentalism or even worse.

And yet our deary asstress the cultivation of emotions! As we shall see, Srila Prabhupada gives great emphasis to devotees cultivating the feeling of separation from Krsna. What else is that but bhava-rupa?Indeed Srila Prabhupada concludes that his followers’ ability to succeed in sadhana hinges on their ability to enter the mood of separation.

That mood or feeling may first be activated by the mind, vocalised by the tongue, and further expressed through engagement of the working senses, but bhava-sevamust arise. Either it already begins with emotion, or expressions of separation awaken it, but emotion must be incorporated into nama-sankirtanafor it to be called effective sadhana.

To better understand what we mean by bhava-sevain general, let us take the success formula for bhaktigiven by Rupa Gosvami:

*utsahan niscayad dhairyat*  
*tat-tat-karma-pravartanat*  
*sanga-tyagat sato vrtteh*  
*sadbhir bhaktih prasidhyati*

**“There are six principles favourable to the execution of pure devotional service: being enthusiastic, endeavouring with confidence, being patient, acting according to regulative principles \[such as sravanam kirtanam visnoh smaranam—hearing, chanting, and remembering Krsna\], abandoning the association of non-devotees, and following in the footsteps of the previous acaryas. These six principles undoubtedly assure the complete success of pure devotional service.”**

In this verse the first three principles are features of emotion, and the latter three are a combination of emotion and action. The bottom line is that properly guided emotions are needed for spiritual success. Emotion is the life of activity. And bhaktiis not lifeless, it is full of life—it is life.

Let us examine the first symptom of success, enthusiasm, utsaha. It is an emotion.

Some people are enthusiastic by nature, others not. In either case a devotee must be enthusiastic. How does a devotee become enthusiastic, or increase his enthusiasm? Srila Prabhupada says,

**“The more you engage yourself in the service of the Lord, the more you become enthusiastic,” and, “The more they hear and talk, the more they become enthusiastic to hear.”**

Looking at the etymology of “enthusiasm,” Oxford English Dictionary says that it comes from the Greek enthousiasmos,which based on the root theosor god, and translates as “possessed by a god; inspired.” A good definition to keep in mind. Unfortunately the word currently has a more secular usage, but still means:

**“Intense and eager enjoyment, interest, or approval.”**

So here we see that the first principle of spiritual success is based on emotion. And so are other aspects of sadhanathat constitute bhava- rupa.After all, bhaktimeans the emotion of love. Rupa Gosvami defines the devotional love of Krsna’s associates in this way:

*iste svarasiki ragah*  
*paramavistata bhavet*  
*tan-mayi ya bhaved bhaktih*  
*satra ragatmikodita*

**“When one becomes attached to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, his natural inclination to love is fully absorbed in thoughts of the Lord. That is called transcendental attachment, and devotional service according to that attachment is called ragatmika,or spontaneous devotional service.”**

In this definition we find that the emotion of deep attachment is the primary characteristic of loving devotion, and the activity of absorption in thoughts of or service to Him is the marginal characteristic. In the realm of spontaneous love, bhava-rupadominates over cesta-rupa.

Similarly, of the twenty-six qualities of a Vaisnava, many—like being mild, humble, and compassionate—are aspects of the emotional state. Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhuencourages a sadhakato reveal his emotions to Krsna in the form of prayers and entreaties. Revealing one’s heart both mentally and verbally is a regulation of vaidhi-bhakti,and offering prayers is an injunction of nava-anga-bhakti.Such entreaties are characteristic of the devotee at practice and at ecstasy. Rupa Gosvami writes,

*samprarthanatmika dainya-bodhika lalasamayi*  
*ity adir vividha dhiraih krsne vijnaptir irita*

**“The wise have explained that there are various types of entreaties to Krsna, such as prayers, admission of incompetence, and expressions of longing.”**

Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura comments that samprarthanaare prayers from a devotee who has not attained the stage of bhava, while lalasastatements are from one who has.

We will conclude by reiterating that sadhana-bhaktimeans the cultivation of emotion, bhava-seva.This cultivation of emotion, specifically the emotion of separation from Krsna, takes prominence in the later stages of sadhana,and it is a cultivation that Srila Prabhupada called upon his followers to engage in. The following sections will explore why and how such cultivation takes place.

In the following pages the terms bhava-sevaand vipralambhaare sometimes used synonymously, and sometimes differently. Bhava sevais the all-encompassing concept of service with emotion, as well as the cultivation of spiritual emotion, which becomes specific in nama-bhajanawith vipralambha,feelings of separation. Thus vipralambhais the mature development and goal of bhava seva.The two are synonymous, the former being the part and the latter the whole. When true feelings of separation fully manifest in a sadhaka,then it is understood that all other spiritual emotions follow. For this reason we shall concentrate mostly on the cultivation of vipralambha,the perfection and guardian of bhava-seva.

\* \* \* \*

We begin by elaborating on how sadhana-bhaktimust be undertaken with feeling based upon the direction of a devotionally well-educated intelligence.

Spiritual education is a must for both regulated and spontaneous devotees. While raganuga-bhaktiis inspired by natural attraction and not the order of sastraand guru,the process of awakening and cultivating greed is well established by scripture and disciplic tradition, both of which must be known and followed.

The essence of Srila Prabhupada’s instructions on service in separation is that as Gaudiya Vaisnavas, our devotion must be saturated with feeling, the kind of feeling shown by Caitanya Mahaprabhu. In Srila Prabhupada’s words,

**“So we have to follow the footprints of the Gosvamis, how to search out Krsna and Radharani, Vrndavana, or within your heart. That is the process of Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s bhajana:feeling of separation, vipralambha, vipralambha-seva. Just like Caitanya Mahaprabhu, feeling the separation of Krsna, He was falling down on the sea. He was coming out of His rest room or His bedroom and going out at dead of night. Nobody knew where He has gone. So that was His searching. This process of devotional service is taught by Caitanya Mahaprabhu.”**

This is the standpoint of all our acaryas.Thakura Bhaktivinoda taught that the primary characteristic of sadhana-bhaktiwas to hear, chant, and remember Krsna with an affection that is expressed through feelings of separation from Him. Giving up karmaand jnanaare secondary characteristics of practice which, when combined with the primary characteristic described above, lead to prema.

When Gopa-kumara was in the realm of liberation and somewhat distracted by brahmananda,the Vaikuntha-dutas advised him to not only give up all ideas of liberation, but to give up the formality of his nama-bhajana.Gopa-kumara needed to learn to chant with feeling, with ecstasy, not just out of a sense of duty. But this would only be possible once he was adept in knowledge of the nine limbs of bhakti.By hearing Krsna’s pastimes from devotees steeped in Srimad-Bhagavatam,he would understand the nature of Vraja’s loving devotion and be competent to adopt that mood, the mood of separation. The Vaikuntha-dutas’ specific words were:

*param srimat-padambhoja*  
*sadasangaty-apeksaya*  
*nama-sankirtana-prayam*  
*visuddham bhaktim acara*

**“Simply practise pure devotional service, mainly in the form of nama-sankirtana, with the hope of gaining the eternal contact of the Lord’s divine lotus feet.”**

The words “with the hope of gaining the eternal contact” are significant in that they define both a distance between the worshipper and the worshipped, and the aspiration the former should feel for the latter. That aspiration is a mood of separation in which resides a hope of a future meeting.

Gopa-kumara did as he was told, and by the grace of his guru was able to achieve a semblance of perfection in nama-bhajana, which then transported him to Vaikuntha. But understanding the nuances of chanting in separation still escaped the boy. Only later, once in Dvaraka, did Gopa-kumara receive further instruction from someone who witnessed the Vraja-vasis’ ecstasies of separation— Sriman Uddhava Prabhu.

Uddhava explained that without utter humility, Gopa-kumara would be unable to awaken the kind of love he needed to enter Vraja. A desolate feeling of emptiness known as separation could only arise in Bhauma-Vrndavana, where Krsna remains unseen in the forests, rivers, and hills that were once His place of pastimes. Were Gopa-kumara to go there, to wander through that abode, he would gradually be overcome by lamentation, and with his heart burning with grief he would begin to search here, there, and everywhere for his beloved. That blissful misery of separation would then bring him to his knees and submerge him in dainya,the very illusive key to the vraja-premathat was his birthright.

This is the kind of separation that Lord Caitanya’s followers must acquire. To facilitate such acquisition, a devotee also receives diksa-mantrasthat are suffixed with words like pracodayator svaha,words which are meant to invoke separation, and which invoke the need for sankalpa.In this way vipralambha-bhava-seva defines the mood by which a devotee makes his determinations in advanced stages of sadhana.

Before proceeding to further understand the truths of nama-bhajana in the mood of separation, it will be helpful to understand in some detail what are vipralambhaand its polar opposite, sambhoga,meeting.

The basis of relationships is love. In the divine realm of Vaikuntha, love is a purely spiritual exchange, but in the material world that spiritual love is reflected as a mundane facsimile that knowers of truth have indifferently referred to as lust.

Material love reveals its joys when lovers are together, but it is full of anguish when the lovers are apart. However, the longer lovers remain united, the more their love wanes, and so a husband and wife divorce, friends fall out, and parents and children go their separate ways. The reason for this is that like all things worldly, material love is temporary, it becomes staid with time, and generally ends in unhappiness.

By contrast, love for Krsna is the headspring of many wonderful sentiments. When a devotee is fortunate enough to gain Krsna’s company, he tastes a joyous mellow called sambhoga-sukha.And when that devotee is inevitably separated from Krsna, his love blossoms into a wonderful emotion that displays the symptoms of intense unhappiness but gives the internal experience of a special transcendental bliss. This is vipralambha.

Rupa Gosvami describes this state of love in separation as follows:

*yunor ayuktayor bhavo yuktayor vatha yo mithah*  
*abhistalinganadinam anavaptau prakrsyate*  
*sa vipralambho vijneyah sambhogonnati-karakah*  
*na vina vipralambhena sambhogah pustim asnute*

**“When the lover and the beloved meet, they are called yukta\[connected\]. Previous to their meeting, they are called ayukta \[not connected\]. Whether connected or not connected, the ecstatic emotion arising due to not being able to embrace and kiss each other as desired is called vipralambha. This vipralambhahelps nourish emotions at the time of meeting.”**

The conditioned mind cannot comprehend how one can be simultaneously unhappy and happy. But that is the transcendental reality of love for Krsna. Like the two sides of a golden coin, which though embossed differently are of equal value, premahas two ecstatic features, meeting and separation. Citing a conversation between Paurnamasi and Nandimukhi, Caitanya Mahaprabhu glorified this inconceivable wonder as follows:

*pidabhir nava-kala-kuta-katuta-garvasya nirvasano*  
*nisyandena mudam sudha-madburimabankara-sankocanah*  
*prema sundari nanda-nandana-paro jagarti yasyantare*  
*jnayante sphutam asya vakra-madhuras tenaiva vikrantayah*

**“My dear beautiful friend! If one develops love of Godhead, love of Krsna, the son of Nanda Maharaja, all the bitter and sweet influences of this love will manifest in one’s heart. Such love of Godhead acts in two ways. The poisonous effects of love of Godhead defeat the severe and fresh poison of the serpent. Yet there is simultaneously transcendental bliss, which pours down and defeats the pride of nectar and diminishes its value. In other words, love of Krsna is so powerful that it simultaneously defeats the poisonous effects of a snake, as well as the happiness derived from pouring nectar on one’s head. It is perceived as doubly effective, simultaneously poisonous and nectarean.”**

On the occasions Caitanya Mahaprabhu visited Lord Jagannatha’s temple in Puri, He would be overwhelmed with the happiness of meeting. In the ecstasy of love He would think He was Srimati Radharani meeting Krsna on the battlefield of Kuruksetra. The Lord would stand at the entrance to the temple by the Garuda-stambha, and His tears of joy would create and fill a depression in the stone floor.

When Jagannatha’s araticeremony was over and the doors to the deity room closed, Lord Caitanya would return to His residence, overcome by the agony of separation from His beloved. In the mood of a distraught gopi,He would mark the ground with His fingers and express His sorrow to confidants like Svarupa Damodara:

**“Where is Vrndavana? Where is Krsna, the son of Nanda Maharaja? Where is that youth who plays the flute with such skill?”**

Throughout His stay in Jagannatha Puri, Caitanya Mahaprabhu would exhibit the twofold aspects of love of God. And in His final years, the Lord became mostly immersed in the mood of separation, displaying transcendental symptoms that remain unknown to even the Vedas.

\* \* \* \*

Devotees may wonder:

**“Why, when transcendental things are ever-fresh, is there a need for separation in the first place. Why is meeting not eternal?”**

The answer reveals the wonders of vipralambhaand the importance of cultivating it during sadhana-bhakti:

**“In short, even in the realm of eternity, separation makes meeting more enjoyable. Similarly, for the sadhakaseparation brings with it a spiritual bliss that in time transforms into the love which qualifies him to meet Krsna.”**

Now for a little more detail.

Synonyms for vipralambhaare virahaand viyoga,and their respective meanings are “parting,” “separation,” and “disjunction.” Let us look at just the etymology of vipralambha.

The verbal root labhmeans “to obtain” or “to meet,” and the corresponding noun, lambha,is “obtaining” or “meeting.” The prefix praadds an implicit emphasis to the Sanskrit, although the translations to both lambhaand pralambhaare the same. However, with the leading suffix vi,the meaning takes a contrary direction, making the word vipralambhamean “loss” or “separation.” Interestingly, pralabhand vipralabhalso mean “to deceive.” Thus vipralambhaalso means “deception.”

From this simple analysis readers can understand that vipralambhais that state in which people, or in the case of loving relationships, lovers, are separated or cheated of each other’s association. That separation invokes many emotions, and those too are implicit in the meaning of vipralambha.

The nature of transcendental love is such that when lovers of any mellow are unable to fulfil their desire to meet, their mutual love increases. The example is given that when red cloth is placed in red dye, it becomes all that much redder. Similarly, because vipralambhais another facet of love, when a devotee is immersed in it his love becomes greater, as does his enjoyment when meeting the beloved.

While far from being a transcendentalist the French author Francois de La Rochefoucauld nicely expressed emotions that rep resent certain aspects of vipralambha.He wrote,

**“Absence extinguishes small passions and increases great ones, as the wind will blow out a candle and fan a fire.”**

The truth of the matter is that without vipralambhathe enjoyment of sambhogawould be stifled and not fully appreciated. Separation is like a magnifying glass that makes the bliss of meeting a million times greater. And the ecstasy of meeting is like a tidal wave that carries on into separation, making vipralambhajust another form of ecstatic bliss.

That is how there is happiness in separation. The difference between the two is how happiness is tasted and displayed. In meeting, the bliss within is externally evident by corresponding symptoms such as smiling and laughter, but in separation, the bliss within is externally evident by contrary symptoms such as crying and moroseness.

As the depths of love increase with the hierarchy of mellows, so too does vipralambhabecome increasingly tasty, finding its pinnacle in madhurya-rasa.Indeed, love in separation is especially relishable in the unwedded conjugal love between Krsna and the young damsels of Vraja.

In the form of Caitanya Mahaprabhu, Krsna was able to relish the various tastes of separation that reached a pinnacle in wild expressions of madness like those displayed by Radha after Krsna’s departure for Mathura.

Krsna Himself makes countless arrangements to be separated from His associates. He does this for two reasons. One is that He is thus able to taste the bliss of separation that is due the object of a devotee’s love, and the other is that He is curious to observe the behaviour of a devotee in separation. By watching and hearing His devotee’s expressions, Krsna enjoys the devotee’s emotions through the agency of tad-bhava, in the way that a sadhakadevelops his own feelings through the same agency by hearing of the separation of Krsna’s associates. And so Krsna enjoys.

Someone may think that Krsna is cruel to put His devotee in a situation against the devotee’s liking. But the fact is that Krsna is doing His devotee a great favour. By hiding from His lover, Krsna is submerging His devotee is an ocean of nectar, a special bliss the devotee could never ever taste in His association. How inconceivable!

For the reasons mentioned above, at the height of His loving exchanges with the gopis,Krsna hides from them, and then later He even abandons Srimati Radharani. For the same reasons, Krsna hides in a cave from the cowherd boys, and, for the same reasons, He leaves Vrndavana and gives His eternal associates the experience of leading their lives without Him.

While the pastimes of separation know no limit, Caitanya Mahaprabhu categorises the types of separation into four:

*’vipralambha’ catur-vidha—purva-raga, mana*  
*pravasakhya, ara prema-vaicittya-akhyana*

**“Vipralambhahas four divisions—purva-raga \[separation before meeting\], mana \[separation caused by pique\], pravasa \[separation by distance—either short or long\], and prema-vaicittya \[apprehension of separation even while in Krsna’s company\].”**

There are various kinds of meeting that correspond to each type of separation. The joy of meeting blossoms to fullness and perfection after an extended separation, as when the Vraja-vasis and Krsna meet at Kuruksetra. That is known as sudura-pravasa-anantara.

To those who would fault Krsna for paining His devotees, Narada comes to His defence and explains,

**“No! By leaving His devotees Krsna is giving them the greatest pleasure.”**

To Gopa-kumara the great sage says,

*manye 'ham evam parama-priyebhyas*  
*tebhyah pradeyasya su-durlabhasya*  
*dravyasya kasyapi samarpanarho*  
*vadanya-mauler vyavahara esah*

**“This way of acting, I think, just befits the most generous, the most magnanimous person, for He presents to His dearmost friends the most desirable object, the most rarely obtained.”**

Once, in Navadvipa, Lord Ramacandra informed Sita-devi that Navadvipa would be the place of His appearance in Kali-yuga. Hearing about Gauranga, the goddess enquired,

**“O lotus-eyed one! Why will You make Your mother cry? Why will You give up Your wife and take sannyasa?What happiness is there in giving such sorrow to Your mother and wife?”**

**Sri Rama replied, “O dear one! You know everything.**

**But You are acting in this way just to teach the living entities. Listen, Sita!**

**“My devotees relish prema-bhaktiin two ways. In union with Me they enjoy sambhoga,and in separation from Me they enjoy vipralambha.My eternal associates desire sambhoga,but I mercifully give them vipralambha.**

**“Why? The devotees know that distress due to separation from Me is actually the topmost bliss. And after separation, when union occurs, they feel happiness so much greater than before—a million times multiplied. That is why I separate from those I love the most.”**

Fear of being separated from Her Lord made Sita-devi silent. But within, She was guardedly curious about the excessive bliss that could be tasted in separation. Knowing His beloved’s mind, Lord Ramacandra silently vowed that He would make Sita taste the bliss of vipralambha,and so He arranged for Ravana to kidnap Her in Pancavati forest.

The transcendental mysteries surrounding meeting and separation are endless. No doubt, to see Krsna with one’s eyes is the fruit of bhaktiand the bestower of a mercy and joy that cannot be had by seeing Him within one’s heart. Kardama Muni and Prahlada Maharaja are evidence of this. And the darsanaof Krsna is the true reward of sadhana,as it alone destroys all illusion and enables prema to prosper. But if seeing Krsna brings such transcendental delight, what can be said of gaining His eternal association, in which a devotee constantly delights in the rolling waves of the ocean of bliss.

And while Krsna’s associates abhor the thought, what to speak of the mention, of separation from Him, within their hearts they are eager for the special bliss that only separation brings. Knowing His devotees, and eager to share this singular rapture with them, Krsna makes arrangements to fulfil their mutual desire, all the while lamenting the loss of their company.

Love for Krsna is a treasure chest of divine bliss, while love in separation is the crown jewel of all ecstasies. Although vipralambhaappears to be the very antithesis for which a sadhakastruggles, it is the innate and internal facet of premaand of sambhoga.

Gaudiya Vaisnavas are the guardians of this confidential form of worship, a gift that was bestowed upon them by Caitanya Mahaprabhu. Indeed, the worship of Krsna in separation is the only way in which a devotee can find his way out of the teeming jungle of Kali. There is no other way!

After attaining the shelter of the holy name, when a sadhaka’s feelings of separation are extreme, he becomes truly qualified to meet Krsna. Calling upon the Lord with plaintive cries is the only way to catch Krsna’s attention and move His heart. And when Krsna’s heart echoes with the distressed calls of His devotee, only then does He make His appearance. This is the way of bhava-seva.

We now summarise the description of vipralambhaand its relation to meeting Krsna with Srila Prabhupada’s own words:

**“The spontaneous attraction of Sri Krsna for His dearest parts and parcels generates an enthusiasm that obliges Sri Krsna and the gopisto meet together. To celebrate this transcendental enthusiasm, there is need of a sentiment of separation between the lover and beloved. In the condition of material tribulation, no one wants the pangs of separation. But in the transcendental form, the very same separation, being absolute in its nature, strengthens the ties of love and enhances the desire of the lover and beloved to meet. The period of separation, evaluated transcendentally, is more relishable than the actual meeting, which lacks the feelings of increasing anticipation because the lover and beloved are both present.”**

## Chapter Thirty-Four

**Gauranga and Vipralambha-seva**

It would be impossible to cultivate nama-sankirtanain the mood of vipralambhawithout giving due respect to the personification and embodiment of separation, Caitanya Mahaprabhu. Lord Caitanya’s associates and His subsequent followers, up to our Srila Prabhupada, have revealed the identity of Sri Gauranga as Krsna Himself. Yet with one voice they emphasise the difference between the mood and pastimes of these two forms of Godhead.

Krsna and Gaura are undeniably one and the same person. In Vrndavana, blackish Krsna revels in pastimes of love, and He is the abode of sweetness and the object of affection for His servants, friends, parents, and girlfriends. In Navadvipa, fair Gaura is lost in nama-sankirtana,and He is the emblem of compassion and the leader of Vaisnavas like Advaita, Nitai, Gadadhara, and Srivasa.

Krsna’s mood is that of the supreme enjoyer; Gaura’s mood is that of the supreme enjoyed, Sri Radha.

Krsna adopting the mood of His Beloved is an extraordinary display of tad-bhava.Taking on the innermost characteristics of another person is something that actors do all the time. However, an actor’s absorption in a role is temporary, a daily routine, not an identity he permanently adopts, forgetting who he really is.

But Krsna is different! His absorption in Radha’s emotions is His life, and it is an absorption so intense that its external symptoms of identification can frighten even His closest companions. Additionally, because Radha is His unlimited spiritual potency, Krsna never gives up plumbing the depths of Her love for Him, and so His identity as Caitanya Mahaprabhu is also eternal, another feature of the Absolute Truth.

Thus there are two forms of the Supreme Lord:

**Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and Caitanya Mahaprabhu, the Supreme Personality of Servitor Godhead.**

Krsna is complete with His consort, Radha, and in two forms They constantly meet to enjoy conjugal love. As Gauranga, Krsna is complete with the mood of His consort, and in one form He tastes the mellows separation from Krsna. Thus Krsna manifests Himself as the Supreme Lord and as His own devotee.

In his commentary to Caitanya-bhagavata,Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura summarises these truths of the Divine Couple and Gauranga. He writes,

*asraya-visaya-dvaya, anyo 'nya-sambhoga-maya,*  
*radha-krsna madhurya dekhaya*  
*vipralambha-bhava-maya, sri-caitanya dinasraya,*  
*duye mili’ audarya vilaya*

**“In separate forms, Radha and Krsna, the shelter of love and its object, enjoy the bliss of Their union, and in so doing reveal to the world unlimited pastimes of sweetness. The combined form of Radha and Krsna, Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu, is the shelter of the fallen, the emblem of compassion, and the personification of service in separation.”**

Readers may do well to note the ontological difference between Krsna and Gaura, as pointed out in the verse above.

Krsna as the Supreme Lord is called the visaya,because He is the object and enjoyer of His devotee’s worship. Like Srimati Radharani, a devotee is the asraya,or shelter of love, the lover.

Although He is Krsna, Caitanya Mahaprabhu does not take the role of the visaya.He remains the asraya.Consequently, it is a great offence to intrude upon Lord Caitanya’s identity by attempting to impose upon Him the role of the visaya.Unfortunately, even at the time of Vrndavana Dasa Thakura, the first biographer of Caitanya Mahaprabhu, certain sects were mistakenly worshipping Gaura as the enjoyer and not as the enjoyed. One of these sects is known as the Gaura-nagari.No more need be said about them, other than warning readers to avoid such fallacious worship of Caitanya Mahaprabhu.

Real Vaisnavas understand that Caitanya Mahaprabhu is both the personification and the teacher of service in separation. He is the vipralambha-vigraha,the very form of love in separation. That same mode of worship is the life-force of the Lord’s followers.

For example, Gaura Kisora Dasa Babaji, the personification of renunciation, is also revered as vipralambha-rasambhode,one who is submerged in the mellows of the expansive ocean of separation. Similarly, in the way that people become strong by eating grains, Gaudiya Vaisnavas become spiritually fit by hearing of the Lord’s moods of separation and by becoming one with them.

Love in separation was Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s life; He had no oilier. Kaviraja Gosvami discloses this truth in his biography of the Lord, and hints to the devotee that his perfection is to be realised by embracing the mood of Caitanya Mahaprabhu:

*tate visvasa kari’ suna bhavera varnana*  
*ha-ibe bhavera jnana, paiba prema-dbana*

**“Please hear faithfully this description of Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s ecstatic emotions. Thus you will come to know of His ecstatic love, and ultimately you will achieve love of Godhead.**

*krsna mathuraya gele, gopira ye dasa haila*  
*krsna-vicchede prabhura se dasa upajila*

**“When Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu felt separation from Krsna, His condition exactly corresponded to that of the gopisin Vrndavana after Krsna’s departure for Mathura.**

*uddhava-darsane yaicbe radhara vilapa*  
*krame krame haila prabhura se unmada-vilapa*

**“The lamentation of Srimati Radharani when Uddhava visited Vrndavana gradually became a feature of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s transcendental madness.**

*radhikara bhave prabhura sada ‘abhimana'*  
*sei bhave apanake haya ‘radha’-jnana*

**“Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s emotions exactly corresponded to those of Srimati Radharani when She met Uddhava. The Lord always conceived of Himself in Her position and sometimes thought that He was Srimati Radharani Herself.**

*divyonmade aiche haya, ki iha vismaya?*  
*adhirudha-bhave divyonmada-pralapa haya*

**“Such is the state of transcendental madness. Why is it difficult to understand? When one is highly elevated in love of Krsna, he becomes transcendentally mad and talks like a madman.”**

Both Srila Prabhupada and Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati emphasised that Lord Caitanya never thought “I am Krsna;” rather He always thought “I am Krsna’s servant,” and generally, “I am Sri Radha.” The Lord’s abhimana,or self-conception, as Radha was so intense that His blackish complexion was covered by Srimati Radharani’s golden complexion. That external transformation is an indication of just how strong His internal identification was. After all, it is well known that emotions bring about physical transformations. This is also the case with the Lord.

An additional feature of Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s mode of worship should be noted—well noted. While Radha and Krsna’s pastimes of meeting and separation take place within the context of the mellow of conjugal love, Lord Caitanya’s savouring of the pastimes of meeting and separation are within a different context: they are based on the mellow of servitude, dasya-bhava.

When Caitanya Mahaprabhu was in Gaya to perform the rites for His deceased father, He met Isvara Puri and took initiation from him, receiving the ten-syllable mantra asHis worshipable deity. After meditating on the mantra,the Lord became emotional and began to weep, roll in the dust, and search for Krsna. In separation He called out,

*krsna re bapa re mora jivana sri-hari*  
*kon dike geld mora prana kari’curi*

**“My dear Krsna! O father! O Hari! My life and soul! Where did You go after stealing My heart?”**

Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati points out that addressing Krsna as “father” and so thinking of Himself as “son” reflects Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s mood of pure servitude, dasya.Moreover, in this verse and the ones that follow it in Caitanya-bhagavata,Lord Caitanya called out after Krsna, Who had dissappeared from the Lord’s meditation and stolen His heart. In this first expression of ecstatic separation the Lord lost complete control of Himself, and only with great difficulty did His surprised students pacify Him and straighten His dishevelled appearance. In other words, Lord Caitanya’s first display of ecstasy was one of separation.

In the ensuing years, both in Navadvipa and Jagannatha Puri, Caitanya Mahaprabhu continued to exhibit feelings of separation from Krsna, the emotions increasing in intensity in His final pastimes.

The Lord was subservient to His emotions. He was not in control of them. At night the pains of separation were so intense that He could not sleep. He would feel so uncomfortable that He would rise from His bed, then He would lie down again, but unable to sleep He would again rise and sit, staring off into a far distance from where He hoped Krsna would momentarily return.

In the way that enacting transcendental pastimes is an eternal feature of Krsna, separation from those pastimes and their cynosure is eternally present in Caitanya Mahaprabhu. And as much as the Lord was eager to taste ecstasy, He was equally eager to have others do so. As Sarvabhauma Bhattacarya wrote,

*kalan nastam bhakti-yogam nijam yah*  
*praduskartum krsna-caitanya-nama*  
*avirbhutas tasya padaravinde*  
*gadham gadham liyatam citta-bhrngah*

**“Let my consciousness, which is like a honeybee, take shelter of the lotus feet of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Who has just now appeared as Sri Krsna Caitanya Mahaprabhu to teach the ancient system of devotional service to Himself. This system had almost been lost due to the influence of time.”**

Caitanya Mahaprabhu appeared not only to relish love for Krsna but to teach that eternal system of devotion, a sadhanawhich had “almost been lost due to the influence of time.”

Moreover, the Lord was not discriminating in His distribution of love for Krsna. Whoever was willing to take it, could have it. Although spontaneous loving devotion was a carefully guarded secret of the Vedas, a perfection very rarely attained by the most attentive sadhaka,Lord Caitanya, the proprietor of vraja-bhakti, was willing to give it to anyone. Overcome by the kindly emotions of Srimati Radharani, Lord Caitanya was not only the personification of vipralambha,but the personification of audarya,magnanimity. In Rupa Gosvami's words, He is maha-vadanya,the most magnanimous incarnation.

\* \* \* \*

Srimati Radharani is always eager to increase service to Krsna. The more servants, the more and more varied the loving devotion to offer Krsna. This is always Her desire. And when Krsna enters the mood of His Beloved, He is overcome by the inclination to distribute devotion to Himself, freely and indiscriminately.

The obvious question arises:

**“By which sadhanawould people attain this treasure?”**

Of course we all know that answer today:

**“By chanting Krsna’s names, specifically by chanting the Hare Krsna maha-mantra."**

When Krsna appeared over five-thousand years ago, He did so to savour the unique mellows of loving exchange facilitated by the backgound setting of the material world. But He had another reason:

**To display spontaneous loving devotion and teach the path to it, raganuga-sadhana.**

Krsna thought,

*vrajera nirmala raga suni' bhakta-gana*  
*raga-marge bhaje yena chadi’ dharma-karma*

**“By hearing about the pure love of the residents of Vraja, devotees will worship Me on the path of spontaneous love, abandoning all rituals of religiosity and fruitive activity.”**

However, contrary to Krsna’s plan, people did not fully understand His purpose, His pastimes, or His teachings to Arjuna and Uddhava.

Although by hearing the Bhagavad-gitasome people were inspired to take up devotional service, they all followed a path of regulated sadhanathat did not lead to Vraja. Thus Krsna contemplated coming again! Introducing nama-sankirtanaas the religion for the age, He would also distribute the four mellows of service to Krsna. In these ways He would make the world dance in ecstasy.

But Krsna was experienced! He had already tried to teach vraja- bhaktiin Dvapara-yuga, and it was unlikely that the less-qualified people of Kali-yuga would understand His intention. He had to do something different.

**“I will become a devotee!”**

The Lord considered that by shedding His divinity for the role of a devotee, He would be more successful in teaching bhakti.Example was always better than precept. He thought,

**“Unless one practises devotional service himself, he cannot teach it to others.”**

And to teach spontaneous devotion to Himself, He would have to come Himself. His incarnations could re-establish religious principles, kill demons, and shelter devotees. But only He could teach and distribute vraja-bhakti:His incarnations could not.

With that intention, Krsna appeared as Caitanya Mahaprabhu and distributed access to loving devotion through the medium of nama-sankirtana.While doing so, He simultaneously fulfilled His inner purposes by assuming the role of Radha and thereby tasting the three features of Their loving exchanges. These three confidential reasons for Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s descent were disclosed by Svarupa Damodara and recorded by Kaviraja Gosvami:

*sri-radhayah pranaya-mahima kidrso vanayaiva-*  
*svadyo yenddbhuta-madburima kidrso va madiyah*  
*saukhyam casya mad-anuhbavatah kidrsam veti lobhat*  
*tad-bhavadhyah samajani saci-garbha-sindhau barinduh*

**“Desiring to understand the glory of Radharani’s love, the wonderful qualities in Him that She alone relishes through Her love, and the happiness She feels when She realises the sweetness of His love, the Supreme Lord Hari, richly endowed with Her emotions, appeared from the womb of Srimati Saci-devi, as the moon appeared from the ocean.”**

In reading this verse one would be prompted to ask:

**“In addition to chanting Hare Krsna, was there anything else that would enable devotees to easily enter the realm of vraja-bhakti,and Mahaprabhu to access the depths of Radha’s heart?”**

Our ṁcaryasanswer this question in this way:

**“Corresponding to a mantrais the mood and purpose with which it is chanted. By adopting and entering the divine mood of service in separation, Krsna would fulfil both purposes at once.”**

With a clearly laid-out strategy, Krsna again appeared; this time He was endowed with Radha’s sentiments and complexion. He distributed the nectar of nama-sankirtanain the Vraja-vasis’ mood of separation, and He simultaneously relished the bhavasof His devotees—primarily the madhurya-rasaof Srimati Radharani.

Radha’s mood of separation had reached its ecstatic climax when Krsna left for Mathura. Radha literally went mad. Speaking to Her intimate friends, Srimati Radharani would reveal Her heart, which was like a storm-tossed ocean, sometimes displaying happiness, sometimes despair. To a greater or lesser degree, Caitanya Mahaprabhu was always absorbed in similar moods.

During the day His mind was distracted by His associates, and so His consciousness veered towards the external world. But if t here was a lapse in that company then His mind would spontaneously merge into ecstatic emotion, which was either partially external or completely internal.

Kaviraja Gosvami says that Lord Caitanya exhibited three states of consciousness, bhava-magna, ardha-bahya-sphurti,and bahya-sphurti:

Totally merged in ecstatic emotion, partial external consciousness, and full external consciousness, respectively.

At night, with Svarupa Damodara and Ramananda Raya, Lord Caitanya was free of all inhibitions and He let loose ecstasies which sometimes seemed like wild, insane performances.

And while such confidential exploration of Radha’s innermost being was the sole prerogative of Caitanya Mahaprabhu, hearing of it along with the Lord’s teachings gives a template for the thoughtful practitioner’s bhajana.

Caitanya Mahaprabhu did not want His followers to imitate Him. But He wanted them to understand His message and apply it in their spiritual lives. Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura sum marised the purpose of Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s appearance as the enjoyer and teacher of vipralambha-sevain this way:

**“The transcendental symptoms that Sri Gaurasundara exhibited after meditating on His mantraare indicative of His feelings of separation from Krsna. In spite of being with Krsna, He sometimes felt that He had not achieved Him, so shedding tears became His principal activity. Feelings of separation alone are the means and nourishment for sambhoga,or union. In order to remove the illusions born of the false conclusions of those who accept sambhogarather than vipralambha as their sadhana,the Lord—who proudly considered Himself a servant afflicted with separation from Krsna—preached that the mood of separation is the only means of achieving the goal of life. Actually, the Lord descended from the spiritual world, Goloka, simply to preach the glories of the shining exalted mood of separation from the Krsna.”**

\* \* \* \*
