And so devotees cultivate feelings of separation for these two manifestations, as well as for Their associates, the vraja-janas.Since Radha and Balarama are inseparable from Krsna, separation from Them naturally includes and induces separation from Krsna.

Moreover, we should consider that Srimati Radharani is but the personification of Krsna’s pleasure potency, so in one sense She is also Krsna. Therefore attachment to Her naturally and spontaneously includes attachment to Krsna.

Narottama Dasa Thakura sings,

*krsna-nama-gane bhai radhika-carana pai*  
*radha-nama-gane krsnacandra*  
*sanksepe kahila katha ghucaha manera vyatha*  
*duhkha-maya anya-katha-dvandva*

**“O brother! By chanting Krsna’s name you can attain Radha, and by chanting Radha’s name you can similarly attain Krsna. With these few words I have summarily explained how you can dispel all sufferings from your heart. If you hear anything to the contary, know that entertaining such nonsense will only bring you pain.”**

Having explained how aspiring for Radha’s service leads to and is not different from aspiring for Krsna’s service, it must be admitted that some differences exist in the affection underlying the two aspirations.

To follow Radha means to follow one of Her girlfriends, or more generally to follow one of her maidservants, one of the manjaris.

A devotee who awakens spontaneous attraction to a gopilike

Rupa-manjari or Rati-manjari will be more inclined to Radha than to Krsna. Their attraction, and eventual love, is known as radha-snehadhika.This means attraction, sneha,that is slightly greater, adhika,for Radha than for Krsna. There will be other gopiswhose attraction for Krsna is slightly greater than that for Radha, which is known as krsna-snehadhika.Then there are those whose attraction to the Divine Couple is equal: radha-krsna-sama-sneha.

Of the many wonderful books, songs, and commentaries written about worship of Sri Radha in separation, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami's Vilapa-kusumanjaliis a particular favourite of devotees. The reason is that it embodies the ideal mood of service of a raganuga-sadhakaaspiring for the mood of a maidservant.

Rupa Gosvami explained the principles of mellows, a duty that was entrusted to him by Caitanya Mahaprabhu. However, it was his follower Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami who taught how an aspirant can enter these mellows by following the guidelines he had learned from Svarupa Damodara Gosvami while in Puri. Of the writings of Dasa Gosvami, Vilapa-kusumanjaliis particularly useful in that regard; Vraja-vilasa-stavais helpful in cultivating attraction to the residents of Vraja; and Visakhanandada-stotramguides advanced devotees in meditating on Krsna’s asta-kaliya-lila.

A sample of Dasa Gosvami's poetry that nurtures separation from Srimati Radharani is this oft-quoted verse:

*tavaivasmi tavaivasmi*  
*na jivami tvaya vina*  
*iti vijnaya devi tvam*  
*naya mam caranantikam*

**“O Radha! Please know that I am Yours! I am Yours alone and cannot live without You a moment longer. Knowing this, how can you hesitate to bring me to the shelter of Your lotus feet.”**

By embracing verses like this while chanting barinama,a devotee tastes the moods of separation from Radha and nurtures affection for the Divine Couple.

\* \* \* \*

We conclude on the topic of how to cultivate feelings of separation from Krsna by discussing how such cultivation removes obstacles on the path of the sadhaka’sprogress and thus contributes to his purification.

In earlier parts of the book, obstacles to devotion have been examined as being the unwanted habits caused by past karma and offences. Past karmameans pious and sinful activities, whereas offences means offences to bhaktiand to the holy names. Nama-sankirtanaimbued with feelings of separation is effective in freeing a practitioner from all resulting reactions and habits, albeit in proportion to the severity of the cause.

But there is another way in which separation purifies a practitioner’s nama-bhajana.This second way is when a sadhakahears of the effect that separation from Krsna has on advanced and perfected devotees: the effect of tad-bhava.

To enter the truths of this topic we cite a relevant passage from Srimad-Bhagavatamthat describes how meditation in separation from Krsna both purified sadhakasand qualified them to meet Krsna. This is relevant in the two ways mentioned above:

As the effect that vipralambhahas on the devotee who experiences it, and as the effect it has on a devotee who reads about the effect of vipralambbaon others.

When on the full moon night of the Karttika month Krsna invited the gopisfor confidential pastimes, they all responded to His flute- call, although a certain class of practitioners were restrained by their superiors. These gopiscould not leave their homes to meet Krsna.

About them Sukadeva Gosvami says,

*antar-grha-gatah kascid*  
*gopyo ’labdha-vinirgamah*  
*krsnam tad-bhavana-yukta*  
*dadhyur milita-locanah*

**“Some of the gopis,however, could not manage to get out of their houses, and instead they remained home with eyes closed, meditating upon Him in pure love.**

*duhsaha-prestha-viraha-*  
*tivra-tapa-dhutasubhah*  
*dhyana-praptacyutaslesa-*  
*nirvrtya ksina-mangalah*

*tam eva paramatmanam*  
*jara-buddhyapi sangatah*  
*jahur guna-mayam deham*  
*sadyah praksina-bandhanah*

**“For those gopiswho could not go to see Krsna, intolerable separation from their beloved caused an intense agony that burned away all impious karma.By meditating upon Him they realised His embrace, and the ecstasy they then felt exhausted their material piety. Although Lord Krsna is the Supreme Soul, these girls simply thought of Him as their male lover and associated with Him in that intimate mood. Thus their karmic bondage was nullified and they abandoned their gross material bodies.”**

The gopisreferred to in these verses were practitioners in their previous lives who had been promoted by yogamayato gopibodies in Krsna’s pastimes.

**As sadhakasthey had attained the stages of ecstatic devotion, bhava,with the notable exception of those who had only attained asakti.Because these girls were unable to associate with the eternally liberated gopis,they had not come to the stage of prema,nor awoken to purva-raga.As a result, in different ways they remained sullied by past conditioning. This meant that after being married, some of these gopishad intercourse with their husbands, and among those that did, some may have had babies. Whatever their situation, because they had not attained spiritual maturity, they did not have fully spiritual bodies and so they were not qualified to meet with Krsna.**

The analogy is clearly relevant to practising devotees who— while not concurrent with Krsna’s pastimes in the way of the gopls—are present with Krsna’s deity, name, and sankirtanamovement. Thus the subject of the gopis’purification and attainment correlates with those of any sadhaka.

A cursory read of this pastime may give the impression that the gopisattained liberation, but a thoughtful reader will understand that liberation was neither the interest nor destination of the gopis. By the agency of vipralambhathey experienced both pain and bliss, and in a trance of devotion they realised Krsna's embrace, which then enabled them to meet Him in person on another night.

The use of the word bandhanah,meaning karmic bondage, should be clarified.

The gopisdid not take birth in Krsna’s pastime as a product of their karma.No pious activity other than pure devotion qualifies anyone for such an attainment. However, they did carry with them certain subtle reactions to past activities that were both of a fruitive and a devotional nature. Indeed, Baladeva Vidyabhusana says that their bondage was the reactions already in effect, their prarabdha- karma.However, as we know, that kind of karmafor devotees is also not ordinary because it is a reaction given by Krsna, not maya.

Like the other girls of Vraja, these gopisalso heard the flute and were inspired to go to Krsna. Yet up until this time they had neither met Him nor endeavoured to do so, and thus they were neither fully purified nor fully qualified. The result was that they now faced obstacles to answering Krsna’s call, and those obstacles were their husbands and in-laws.

These relatives were like the personification of the gopis’impurities, impurities which also manifest in the material aspect of their bodies. The word virahaindicates that the gopishad already experienced some slight vipralambhaby having heard about Krsna, and that separation was now further heightened by Krsna’s personal invitation. The combination of the gopis’desire to meet Krsna and their family’s reproaches raised those feelings of separation to a fever pitch. The resultant passion was so extraordinary that the gopisfelt as if they had been cast into an intense, tivra,and intolerable, duhsaha,ocean of fire, tapa.

In the way that an expansive forest fire burns all things before it, the agony of the gopis’separation consumed all materially inauspicious things within their forms and consciousness. Thus the gopis became free of material contamination, and in a purified state they met Krsna in their trance of separation.

From this incident a sadhakacan infer that he can be freed of material contamination in proportion to the intensity of his vipralambha-bhajana .Moreover, as the material aspect of his being is consumed, the spiritual aspect is correspondingly manifest.

A practitioner’s body has a dual constitution that is similar to the spiritual-come-material body of the gopis.The adjective guna-mayamindicates that prior to hearing the flute, the gopis' bodies were twofold—spiritual bodies materially tainted. But when they heard the flute and felt its effects, their bodies became fully spiritual. Similarly a sadhaka’sbody is also twofold—a material body that is spiritualised. And by the strength of nama-sankirtana in separation, the sadhaka’sbody gradually becomes increasingly spiritual.

This dual identity, characteristic of both gopisand sadhakas, is explained by a Navayogendra in the following verse:

*bhaktih paresanubhavo uiraktir*  
*anyatra caisa trika eka-kalah*  
*prapadyamanasya yathasnatah syus*  
*tustih pustih ksud-apayo ’nu-ghasam*

**“Devotion, direct experience of the Supreme Lord, and detachment from other things—these three occur simultaneously for one who has taken shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, in the same way that pleasure, nourishment, and relief from hunger come simultaneously and increasingly, with each bite, for a person engaged in eating.”**

The degree to which a devotee is accomplished in vipralambha-seva determines the extent to which the spiritual aspect of his identity becomes prominent and the mundane aspect concealed. This evolution can be seen in the gopis,and in a less assertive way in any practitioner.

The gopisattained premaand the sadhakasattain ruci, asakti, and then bhava.When, by the power of their devotion, gopisand sadhakasalike destroy the grip of the three modes, at that time they attain a nature like that of the Lord, and by their prema become qualified associates.

Krsna asserts this principle while explaining to Uddhava the workings of the modes of nature:

*etah samsrtayahpumso*  
*guna-karma-nibandhanah*  
*yeneme nirjitah saumya*  
*guna jlvena citta-jah*  
*bhakti-yogena man-nistho*  
*mad-bhavaya prapadyate*

**“O gentle Uddhava! All these different phases of conditioned life arise from work born of the modes of material nature. The living entity who conquers these modes, manifested from the mind, can dedicate himself to Me by the process of devotional service and thus attain pure love for Me.”**

We have seen that the initial result of gopisbeing barred from meeting Krsna was a pain of separation which by its intenisty purified their inauspicious qualities. From this, a practising devotee can conclude that the distress he feels in his conditioned state will destroy his prarabdha-karmaand free him of offences.

Now we shall examine the subsequent result of the gopls’separation, which was the bliss they experienced, and how a sadhaka benefits from the pleasure of vipralambha-bhajana.

\* \* \* \*

Sukadeva Gosvami says that the gopisexperienced bliss, nirvrti, and the cause of that bliss was Krsna appearing within their trance of meditation, dhyana,where they embraced each other, praptacyutaslesa.

What the gopiswanted to achieve physically they secured mentally, within their hearts. When their husbands stood by the door with sticks, barring their exit, the gopismerely closed their eyes and, in defiance, meditated upon Krsna, Who, sympathetic to the their plight, became personally manifest to them. Thus the gopis fulfilled their long-standing desire to embrace Krsna, and the touch of His transcendental limbs filled them with endless bliss.

**“What was the influence of the bliss that they felt?”**

**“Whatever materially auspicious qualities, mangalah, that remained within the gopiswere reduced to nil, ksina.Thus the pain and joy of separation freed the gopisfrom all temporal effects, pious and impious.”**

We should note that the gopis’great delight was a consequence of meeting with Krsna and not an outcome of the nectarean effect of separation itself.

In the verse spoken by Sukadeva beginning with tam eva paramatmanam,mention is made of Paramatma.

One should not mistakenly think that this refers to the Supersoul or any expansion of Maha-Visnu. Such a conception would run contrary to corresponding devotional conclusions. The gopis'had no attraction for the Supersoul in previous lives, or in the current one. Why then would they think of Him, Whom yogisworship with neutrality, as their paramour, jara?The simple meaning is that Acyuta is the Supreme Soul, the Supreme Personality of Godhead Therefore even though the gopis’conduct was debased by material calculation, in connection with the Supreme it yielded the highest spiritual perfection.

From this example a sadhakacan rightly conclude that tin ecstasy of separation he tastes in meditation results not only in great delight, but in the removal of all auspicious qualities, such an attachment to goodness.

In this way the consequences of invoking moods of separation is that a devotee’s karmic bonds are nullified.

However, something more must be said about this statement.

A devotee is completely free of bad habits resulting from past karmaat the stage of steadiness, and at asaktithese habits are absolutely vanquished without a trace. Therefore when we say “karmic bonds” it cannot mean ordinary karma,but, in Sanatana Gosvami’s words, “subconscious habits.”

We have cited the example of Narada Muni, who in his last life had achieved premabut was disqualified from the Lord’s association because he had a trace of attachment to meditating in solitary places. In the way that Narada did not know that this was unfa vourable to his devotions, the gopisalso did not know that adhering to family obligations and the social traditions of Vraja should be renounced for prema-bhakti.Not having fully purified themselves in a previous life, some vestiges of subtle reaction accompanied them as they took gopibodies imbued with asaktior bhava. Those reactions then manifest in the form of attachment to social customs.

Similarly, as a practitioner transitions through the five stages of smarana-dasahe is freed of both gross and subtle reactions, provided that, unlike the sadhakaswho became the gopis,he expertly applies the principles of sadhana-bhakti.

Someone may argue:

**“The gopis’perfection ended with the demise of their body, as expressed in the words jahur guna-mayam deham.”**

To this we reply:

**“The idea that death would occur as a result of vipralambhawould be a most inauspicious intrusion into Krsna’s most auspicious rasa-lila.One can just imagine the chaos and sorrow that the simultaneous death of hundreds or thousands of housewives would cause.”**

While death is indeed the tenth aspect of vipralambha,it is rarely manifest, and when it is, only on occasions that are favourable for the Lord’s pastime, a time when pathos is meant to dominate. However, on the full-moon night of Karttika, abundant sweetness was dominant, and so neither the gopisnor Yogamaya would arrange any event that could result in a conflict of mellows, rasabhasa.

**“How then should the words of sage Sukadeva be understood?”**

Commentators are unified in the notion that when the gopiswere purified of pious and impious influences, they cast off any thinking that was not favourable to Krsna’s pleasure. Their conduct was reminiscent of the way that Brahma once relinquished one unfavourable mental body after the other. In a similar way, the material aspect of their being evaporated and they attained fully spiritual bodies fit for Krsna’s company.

This understanding is confirmed by Krsna Himself in the message that He sent the gopisthrough Uddhava. Krsna had sent His cousin to console the Vraja-vasis. To each relative and dear acquaintance He dedicated individual letters, which included separate messages to each group of gopis.

To those gopiswho were obstructed from meeting Him, He wrote,

*ya maya kridata ratryam*  
*vane ’smin vraja asthitah*  
*alabdha-rasah kalyanyo*  
*mapur mad-virya-cintaya*

**“Although some gopishad to remain in the cowherd village and so could not join the rasadance to sport with Me at night in the forest, they were nonetheless fortunate. Indeed, they attained Me by thinking of My potent pastimes.”**

Sukadeva Gosvami then says that the gopisreferred to in this message were thrilled to receive Krsna’s recognition and to have been reminded of pastimes with Krsna.

From this historical narration it is clear that the gopiswere not deceased, but very much alive. Moreover, the word kalyanyah, “fortunate,” implies that everything remained auspicious that night. Although the gopiswere of a mind to give up their bodies in the way Sati once did, they restrained themselves. They were aware that such an act would have been displeasing to Krsna.

Thus we answer by quoting acaryaVisvanatha’s summary on this topic:

**“Thus the conclusion is that they gave up their material bodies without dying. Parched by the intense heat of separation, their material bodies gave up their materiality and became purely spiritual, just like the bodies of great devotees such as Dhruva Maharaja. This is the meaning of the gopis’‘giving up their bodies.’”**

\* \* \* \*

The final aspect of this pastime of Vipralambha-sevaand how a sadhakais benefited by cultivating that same spirit will now be disclosed. It is this:

Those who hear and read about pastimes of vipralambha are especially blessed.

In their commentaries, both Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura and baladeva Vidyabhusana emphasise the tad-bhavaeffect of hearing about the ecstasy of the gopis’separation. By hearing of these pastimes, a similar effect is bestowed upon the hearer. Indeed, the same benefit ensues from hearing the many other pastimes of separation that our acaryashave narrated.

We quote again Prahlada Maharaja’s explanation of the mechanism of tad-bhavaupon a sadhakaabsorbed in devotional service, as explained to his classmates:

*tada puman mukta-samasta-bandhanas*  
*tad-bhava-bhavanukrtasayakrtih*  
*nirdagdha-bijanusayo mahiyasa*  
*bhakti-prayogena samety adhoksajam*

**“The devotee is then freed from all material contamination because he constantly thinks of the Lord’s pastimes and because his mind and body have been converted to spiritual qualities. Because of his intense devotional service, his ignorance, material consciousness, and all kinds of material desires are completely burnt to ashes.This is the stage at which one can achieve the shelter of the Lord’s lotus feet.”**

The line tad-bhava-bhavanukrtasayakrtihindicates that the nature of a sadhaka’scontemplation, bhava,transforms his body and mind, asaya-akrtih,in harmony with the topic in which he is absorbed, tad-bhava.Since that topic is very much in relationship to Krsna, bhavaalso indicates the mood of devotion which a practitioner aspires for—friend, parent, or lover.

A devotee may be concerned that his body is still very much immersed in the modes of nature. However, if he is regularly absorbed in spiritual practice, then both material intelligence and the impressions of past sense objects, anusayah,are burned up. Cakravarti Thakura says that eventually, the raganuga-sadhaka meets, sam,Krsna, in the relationship that he contemplated. This was the case with the gopis,and will be for those who follow their example through the process of aural reception.

Prahlada Maharaja further elaborates on how tad-bhavafrees the hearer of the effects of the modes and the pitfalls of material existance—pious and impious:

*adhoksajalambham ihasubhatmanah*  
*saririnah samsrti-cakra-satanam*  
*tad brahma-nirvana-sukham vidur budhas*  
*tato bhajadhvam hrdaye hrd-isvaram*

**“The real problem of life is the repetition of birth and death, which is like a wheel rolling repeatedly up and down. This wheel, however, completely stops when one is in touch with the Supreme Personality of Godhead. In other words, by the transcendental bliss realised from constant engagement in devotional service, one is completely liberated from material existence. All learned men know this. Therefore, my dear friends, Î sons of the asuras,immediately begin meditating upon and worshipping the Supersoul within everyone’s heart.”**

Srila Prabhupada’s translation and purport emphasise that constant hearing and chanting, alambham,of the Lord’s pastimes— what to speak of directly attaining Him—destroys, satanam,all material contamination. And if a devotee contemplates Krsna as his favoured object of love, alambhana,then contact with the Lord, Who is replete with all mellows of bhakti, hrd-isvaram,destroys both auspicious and inauspicious attributes.

Furthur study of the mechanism by which tad-bhavaliberates the sadhakawill be helpful in raising awareness of the importance of hearing topics concerning vipralambha.Let us now briefly look at that mechanism.

When the gopiswere barred from meeting Krsna, the anguish they felt was so overwhelmeing that all inauspicious things within the world were extinguished. Similarly, when they felt Krsna’s embrace, the bliss the gopisexperienced was so intense that its effects shrank both the auspicious things and the sense pleasures of the world—including the bliss of liberation—to insignificance.

That overwhelming anguish and that intense bliss continue to reverberate today in the words describing the gopis’feelings of separation. When a faithful devotee hears of that ecstasy it uproots the tree of his false ego, strips him of every misconception, and frees him of the reaction to past deeds, both pious and impious. But more importantly, narration of the gopis’ vipralambha-lilamakes the creeper of his devotion blossom with fresh buds of conjugal attachment to the Prince of Vraja. In short, those who read and hear of the gopis’affliction and bliss are freed of similar inebreities and blessed with similar attachment.

This conclusion is confirmed in the following verse, spoken by Narada to Vasudeva:

*sruto ’nupathito dhyata*  
*adrto vanumoditah*  
*sadyah punati sad-dharmo*  
*deva-visva-druho ’pi hi*

**“Pure devotional service rendered to the Supreme Lord is spiritually so potent that simply by hearing about such transcendental service, by chanting its glories in response, by meditating on it, by respectfully and faithfully accepting it, or by praising the devotional service of others, even persons who hate the demigods and all other living beings can be immediately purified.”**

We now conclude our summary of Krsna’s kindness to those gopis who retained a hint of identification with the world. Other sadhana siddha-gopisdid not face the same challenge in meeting with Krsna. They, like their nitya-siddhacounterparts, left home unobstructed or unnoticed.

In their previous lives as sadhakasthey had attained an advanced stage of ecstasy where every trace of materiality was cleansed from their consciousness and bodies. Because of their purity, Yogamaya arranged for them to meet the eternally liberated gopis,and by hearing from Krsna’s associates they developed purva-raga.As a result, they found no obstacle to fulfilling a meeting with Krsna when they heard His flute-song.

Yet both groups of gopisfinally attained Krsna’s company, and night after night they relished pastimes of love in fully spiritual bodies that were not only fit for Krsna but of no interest to family members.

To mature their love, yogamayawould continue to make these sadhana-siddhastaste separation after separation: first during the day when they stayed at home as Krsna tended the cows; then some time later when He left Vrndavana for Mathura; and finally in the many years that He was in faraway Dvaraka.

When the gopishad given up all hope that Krsna would return, they continued to drink through the chalice of vipralambhaan intoxicating blend of poison and nectar, which they would share with Krsna through letters like this:

*kalindyah pulinam pradosa-maruto ramyah sasankamsavah*  
*santapam na barantu nama nitaram kurvanti kasmat punah*  
*sandistam vraja-yositam iti hareh samsrnvato ‘ntah-pure*  
*nihsvasah prasrta jayanti ramani-saubhagya-garva-cchidah*

**“O Hari! Why is it that the soothing moonlight and the gentle breezes caressing the glittering shore of the Yamuna cannot cool the intolerable pain scorching our hearts?”**

When Krsna heard these words from a messenger, He began to sigh uncontrollably. Seeing His distraught condition, His queens’ possessive pride evaporated in the way that the morning mist dissipates with the sun’s appearance.

When a practising devotee reads such verses he, too, is blessed with the wonders of service in separation. How those blessings transform a devotee’s bhajanainto a blossoming desire tree yielding the fruits of love is difficult to express in words and can only be experienced. The words below of a Vaisnava poet describe that hearing about pastimes of separation is the guardian of the sincere sadhaka.May these pages describing Bhava-sevain its maturity of vipralambhabe of some small help in guarding the pure devotion of the reader. Sri Nila wrote,

**“Once a traveller passed through Vraja on his way to Dvaraka. Taking advantage of this messenger, the gopis composed a letter to Krsna, which He then opened with trembling hands. It said,**

*te govardhana-kandarah sa yamuna-kacchah sa cesto vato*  
*bhandirah sa vanaspatih sahacaras te tac ca gosthanganam*  
*kim te dvaravati-bhujanga hrdayam nayati dosair apity*  
*avyad vo hrdi duhsaham vraja-vadhu-sandesa-salyam hareh*

**‘“O debauchee of Dvaraka! Why do Govardhana’s caves, the Yamuna’s shore, Your favourite tree named Bhandira, the kadambatree by Kaliya Lake, Your friends like Subala, or Vraja village, never enter Your heart even to be criticised?’**

**“When Krsna read these words they entered His heart like a javelin, causing Him unbearable pain. May that javelin enter your hearts and protect you all.”**

May the inconceivable pastimes of Krsna’s vipralambha-bhava bless and protect this author and his readers.

## Part Eight

**Sankalpa for Divine Grace**

## Chapter Thirty-Seven

**The Sankalpas Corresponding to Grace**

The many determinations that guide a practitioner through the stages of sadhana-bhaktihave the attainment of bhavaas their raison d’etre.The motto of iskcon, “Back to Godhead,” can be realised only by loving devotion, of which ecstasy is the dawning. This state of transcendence is generally understood to be the limit of attainment made possible by the material body. Yet Cakravarti Thakura seems to indicate that the upper limit of attainment may be the first stage of prema,and it is the further development of love from snehato mahabhavathat requires a spiritual body like that of the sadhana-siddha-gopismentioned in the previous chapter.

An inevitable question to arise in a book dedicated to the steps leading to ecstatic devotion is:

**“What is the final sankalparequired to facilitate a sadhaka’selevation to bhava?”**

The following chapters reveal that the effort to attain bhavais not sufficient in itself. Exacting determination in nama-bhajanamust be accompanied by Krsna’s grace. Thus, the closing sankalpaof sadhanais that which invokes the mercy of the Lord.

So the answer in short, then, is:

**“The final determination is not the sadhaka’s,it is Krsna’s.”**

Divine intervention alone gives the practitioner entrance into the kingdom of love, into Krsna’s own heart. But Sukadeva Gosvami warns us, muktim dadati karhicit sma na bhakti-yogam:

**Krsna easily awards practitioners liberation, but He does not so readily share the treasure of direct service unto Him.**

Of course, practising devotees are no strangers to Krsna’s mercy. Devotional service and the aspects of practice, like chanting, are made of and are available by the Lord’s grace. However, the quality of mercy varies with service and attainment, and the standard of mercy that a sadhakaeyes in his attempt to reach bhavais, for him, without precedent. But for a devotee who has strived hard and long through years of sadhana,it is a must! After all, Krsna has repeat edly encouraged us:

*man-mana bhava mad-bhakto*  
*mad-yaji mam namaskuru*  
*mam evaisyasi satyam te*  
*pratijane priyo ’si me*

**“Always think of Me, become My devotee, worship Me, and offer your homage unto Me. Thus you will come to Me without fail. I promise you this because you are My very dear friend.”**

Krsna has promised us bhava.But He has also made conditions like man-mana,which indicates spontaneous attachment to Him. His mercy has a price.

In the many chapters preceding this, we have described the sadhanaof true Gaudiyas. Systematic meditation in nama-sankirtana braided with feelings of separation is the means by which devotees pass through the increasingly elusive stages of devotion from nisthd to advanced asakti.

The eminence of bhava-bhaktiis the regal crown worn by universal controllers like Brahma and Siva. This book is dedicated to the study of sadhanaand the attainment of bhava.It does not further examine the cultivation of bhavato premaand beyond. However, to understand what it means to accomplish the transition to bhava,we should review certain features of bhava-bhakti,beginning with its definition:

*suddha-sattva-visesatma*  
*prema-suryamsu-samya-bhak*  
*rucibhis citta-masrnya-*  
*krd asau bhava ucyate*

**“When devotional service is executed on the transcendental platform of pure goodness, it is like a sunray of love for Krsna. At such a time, devotional service causes the heart to be softened by various tastes, and one is then situated in bhava\[emotion\].”**

This verse describes bhavaas a beam of prema,the former being the smallest constituent part of the latter, in the way that a single ray of sunshine is an irreducible particle of the sun.

Bhavaalso goes by the name of ratiand is the bud of the permanent feature of love known as sthayi-bhava.Permanent ecstasy indicates one of the five mellows of devotional service, which blossom in fullness with the rising of the premasun. A bhava-bhakta attains the first transcendental insight into the mood of devotion for which he so hankered at practice.

The phrase suddba-sattva-visesarefers to the enchanting combination of two features of Krsna’s internal potency: knowledge, samvit,and pleasure, hladini.

This combination generates an intense desire to please Krsna, a desire that is the eternal characteristic of the Lord’s associates. In other words, the bhava-bhaktais naturally inclined to love and serve Krsna, indicating a maturing in spontaneous devotion. Combined with a softening of the heart, these conditions make a devotee very eager to meet the Lord, and they also invoke transitory ecstasies called sancari-bhavas.These transitory ecstasies are modest in intensity and meagre in number, but they are encounters with the divine nonetheless.

Caitanya Mahaprabhu lists three of these symptoms as sought after by the bhava-bhakta:

*nayanam galad-asru-dharaya*  
*vadanam gadgada-ruddhaya gird*  
*pulakair nicitam vapuh kada*  
*tava nama-grahane bhavisyati*

**“My dear Lord, when will My eyes be beautified by filling with tears that constantly glide down as I chant Your holy name? When will My voice falter and all the hairs on My body stand erect in transcendental happiness as I chant Your holy name?”**

At bhava,spiritualisation becomes unique. A sadhaka’ssenses are spiritually empowered; emancipated from the influence of the modes of nature, they seek out the sight, sound, and taste of Krsna’s form, flute, and lips. Yet due to his spiritual infancy, a devotee has limited ability to perceive the objects of his desire. He generally cries for its fulfilment, and attains it on occasion only to lose it again. Whether separated from or united with Radha or Krsna, the sadhakatastes an intense sweetness that pervades his days and nights, his consciousness absorbed more in his siddha-deha than in his external body.

Followers of Caitanya Mahaprabhu will have the son of Mother Yasoda as the object of their love, and spontaneous loving devotion as the character of their sthayi-bhava.While both raganugaand vaidhipractitioners will attain a mature stage of spontaneity, the attraction of the former will be somewhat richer and more forceful than that of the latter. With the development of bhava,the two eventually gain parity.

Fortunate is that rare soul in whom ecstatic devotion has awakened. In the way that he was attracted to the material energy as a conditioned soul, he is now attracted to Krsna as a liberated soul. Uninformed outsiders will see this conduct as brainwashing or contrived, but his natural state is to be attracted to Krsna in the way that iron filings are naturally attracted by a magnet.

When Prahlada Maharaja displayed allegiance to Visnu, his father’s sworn enemy, his teachers enquired as to who had spoiled his intelligence with devotional teachings. The young boy humbly replied,

*yatha bhramyaty ayo brahman*  
*svayam akarsa-sannidhau*  
*tatha me bhidyate cetas*  
*cakra-paner yadrcchaya*

**“O brabmanas!As iron attracted by a magnetic stone moves automatically toward the magnet, my consciousness, having been changed by His will, is attracted by Lord Visnu, who carries a disc in His hand. Thus, I have no independence.”**

Such is the exquisite nature of bhava-bhakti!

\* \* \* \*

Now that the final sankalpahas been disclosed, the overarching question becomes:

**“How to attain bhava?”**

Rupa Gosvami says it is rarely attained, and Sukadeva Gosvami says Krsna is reluctant to give it. Jiva Gosvami explains how bhava is accomplished:

**“By Krsna’s mercy alone!”**

**“And how to inspire Krsna to give that mercy?”**

**“Firstly, a devotee must give himself completely to the expert practice of sadhana.Secondly, he must be able to cry in separation and pray eagerly to be engaged in confidential service.”**

Krsna is a person, and if He sees that a sadhakawants Him more than anything and everything else, He reciprocates and bestows His mercy. That is the way!

And ecstatic devotion can appear in two ways:

**In response to the sincere sadhanamentioned, and without the prerequisite of such sadhana—out of an act of causeless mercy.**

Of these two, our attention is on the former, which is the standard way bhavaappears, the latter being the very rare exception.

It should be made clear, however, that in both cases, the grace of the Lord is essential. The difference is that in one case, grace is sincerely solicited and well earned, and in the other it is neither.

In glorifying Krsna, King Mucukunda explains that the awakening of true devotion takes place by the grace of devotee association:

*bhavapavargo bhramato óada bhavej*  
*janasya tarhy acyuta sat-samagamah*  
*sat-sangamo yarhi tadaiva sad-gatau*  
*paravarese tvayi jayate matih*

**“When the material life of a wandering soul has ceased, O Acyuta, he may attain the association of Your devotees. And when he associates with them, there awakens in him devotion unto You, who are the goal of the devotees and the Lord of all causes and their effects.”**

The above verse reverses a sequence of events for the sake of emphasis.

Actually, it is devotee association that terminates material entanglement, and not the unqualified cessation of fruitive life that culminates in the company of devotees. In any case, this good fortune is the marginal effect of saintly association, sat-sangamah,the primary effect being that it awakens pure devotion.

As previously mentioned, different devotees will affect conditioned souls in different ways. A regular practitioner can give faith, a bhava-bhaktahis own power, and a prema-bhaktiany level of devotion. But the transfer of spiritual potency takes place through the power of saintly association.

**“But what does it mean to get mercy by the association of saints? How does that association transmit mercy?”**

In the description of causeless mercy, Rupa Gosvami elaborates on three ways by which grace is bestowed, He writes, prasada vacikaloka-dana-hardadayo hateh:

**“Krsna’s mercy manifests through the words of the Lord, in the presence of the Lord, or through the heart.”**

The acaryalater adds that the same result also accrues from the mercy of the devotee. We shall later show that there is no difference between the two, Krsna’s mercy and His devotee’s mercy. They are one and the same.

Narada’s perfection is an example of how a devotee is blessed by the words of Vaisnavas. The sages staying near his home would instruct the young boy to sit down and hear their talks about Krsna. That instruction to “sit and hear,” and those transcendental discussions about the Lord’s pastimes, were the verbal form of the devotees’ mercy by which Narada attained taste, attachment, ecstasy, and love.

Elsewhere in the Naradiya Parana,Krsna tells Narada:

**“May you have undeviating bhava-bhaktifor Me.”**

A benediction like this, directly pronounced by the Lord, obviously bestows wonderful and immediate results.

Krsna’s presence through His direct appearance or through His deity form may also inspire bhava.An example is the Gandharva girl Candrakanti, who upon seeing Krsna’s deity attained spontaneous ecstatic devotion and danced in abandon all night. This pastime is described in the Padma Purana.

Jiva Gosvami cites the verse beginning smeram bhangi-trayaas another example of securing Krsna’s mercy simply by seeing Him.

Sukadeva Gosvami is the example of a devotee for whom bhava manifested within His heart. Jiva Gosvami explains that because Sukadeva had neither heard nor seen either the Lord or His devotee, his advanced devotion must have arisen from within himself.

An example of obtaining bhavaby the mercy of a devotee is seen in the transformation that took place in the hunter Mrgari.

By seeing and hearing Narada, he was transformed from a cruel hunter of animals to a fully accomplished Vaisnava.

In answer to the question regarding the mercy of great devotees, we reply:

**“Mercy through the association of saints means being in their presence and receiving their instructions.”**

As a consequence of that answer, we draw the reader’s attention to the following train of thought and its significant conclusion:

**For twelve years of his preaching pastimes Srila Prabhupada was personally visible, and in that time he repeatedly assured his followers that by offenceless nama-sankirtanathey would attain per fection. Additionally, for all time to come, His Divine Grace left Ins teachings primarily in the form of his transcendental writings, and secondarily in his recorded words.**

We may conclude that by his words and presence, Srila Prabhupada gave the blessings by which his direct disciples could attain bhava,and by those same instructions, succeeding generations of followers not initiated by him could also attain the same result. With the blessing of bhava,devotees could attain Krsna’s pastimes, and with further purification return to the spiritual world.

To summarise, a devotee will be able to attain bhavafrom a qualified spiritual master, or alternately through Srila Prabhupada’s books, followers, and presence.

It goes without saying that Srila Prabhupada expected his followers to work for mercy. He was not giving it unconditionally. He expected his followers to put his teachings to work for themselves and to serve Lord Caitanya’s mission by giving his teachings to others. When one of his sannyasisasked how they would know their siddha-dehaafter his departure, Srila Prabhupada replied,

**“When you are ready, I will come and reveal it to you.”**

We should make it abundantly clear that Srila Prabhupada’s posthumous blessing for a sadhakato attain bhavadoes not mean that anyone other than his directly initiated disciples are, or can be, initiated by him. Devotees must be properly initiated by a guru who is physically present. That is a law of bhakti.

Krsna Himself describes the result of seeing and hearing an empowered devotee like Srila Prabhupada—or even being cursed by him—with the example of the two sons of Kuvera. After freeing Nalakuvera and Manigriva from their confinement in the form of trees, Krsna said,

*sadhunam sama-cittanam*  
*sutaram mat-krtatmanam*  
*darsanan no bhaved bandhah*  
*pumso’ksnoh savitur yatha*

**“When one is face to face with the sun, there is no longer darkness for one’s eyes. Similarly, when one is face to face with a sadhu,a devotee, who is fully determined and surrendered to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, one will no longer be subject to material bondage.”**

By the grace of Narada the two demigods were endowed with Krsna’s darsana,and they attained not only ecstatic devotion, but loving devotion to the Lord. Such is the spiritual influence of great devotees like Narada and Srila Prabhupada—immeasurable!

\* \* \* \*

We have explained that either Krsna’s mercy or a devotee’s mercy is needed to rise from sadhanato bhava.To the reader it must be clear by now that to invoke the blessings of our well-wishers, not any kind of sadhanawill do. Sadhanamust be expertly accomplished, with a clear conception of its goal.

Earlier chapters showed that while a devotee’s sadhanamay at first be general, at varana-dasait assumes a conceptual form, and at smarana-dasathat concept is put to practice. And as a devotee progresses through the stages of smarana,his practices become increasingly exacting. Bhaktivinoda Thakura warns that carelessness in attempting to reach ever-elusive bhavamay consign a devotee to many lifetimes of effort. He says,

**“The ascension from the level of samadhiin smarana- dasato apana-dasais a delicate one. For the practitioner who is not expert, elevation through the five stages of smarana-dasato apana-dasamay require many yugas;for a dexterous sadhaka,it is accomplished quickly.”**

Our purpose in this chapter is to show the rationale that a sadhaka takes in clarifying the path of his sadhana.We have amply emphasised that sadhanais not just about chanting Hare Krsna, bun about chanting Hare Krsna with a clear conception of the process by which it is done, the mood with which it is done, and the goal for which it is done.

In short:

**How does a devotee chart his path?**

In answering this question our concentration will primarily be on the transition from dhyanato samadhi,which correlates to the development of taste and attachment. It may be noted that this study will relate to sadhana-bhaktiin which spontaneity, raga,is partially, if not fully, manifest.

And, as mentioned, our main emphasis is not so much on the actual mechanics of practice already described in earlier chapters as it is on the directional sankalpasthat a devotee striving for ragatmika must make. In other words, we shall point out to both regulated and spontaneous practitioners the choices that lead to raganuga-sadhana for Krsna, specifically in the mood of madhurya-rasa.

We begin with an overview of smarana-sadbana.

Krsna explains how material consciousness abandons its temporal nature and displays spiritual characteristics in proportion to a sadhaka’ssincere efforts. In other words, sadhana-bhaktiinfused with Krsna’s mercy transforms matter into spirit:

*yatha yathatma parimrjyate ’sau*  
*mat-punya-gatha-sravanabhidhanaih*  
*tatha tatha pasyati vastu suksmam*  
*caksur yathaivanjana-samprayuktam*

**“When a diseased eye is treated with medicinal ointment it gradually recovers its power to see. Similarly, as a conscious living entity cleanses himself of material contamination by hearing and chanting the pious narrations of My glories, he regains his ability to see Me, the Absolute Truth, in My subtle spiritual form.”**

The careful application of this verse requires ideal conditions on the part of the sadhakaas he passes through the stages of smaranato the doorstep of apana.The following are some such considerations:

In the verses beginning with trnad api sunicenaand na dhanam na janam na sundarim,Caitanya Mahaprabhu lays down a devotee’s external conduct for nama-bhajana.A practitioner must offer respect to everyone, be a humble servant of his spiritual master, and feel remorse for his fallen condition. Although Caitanya Mahaprabhu ordered everyone to preach and become guru,even if one adopts such a risky service, as a sadhakahe must shun recognition and worship, and see disciples as his spiritual masters.

In cultivating bhava-sevaand specifically vipralambha-seva,a practitioner’s sole means of deliverance and succour is the holy name. As he becomes mature in nama-bhajana,a devotee feels ever-increasing joy in chanting, especially after attaining raga, and Thakura Bhaktivinoda says that the bliss of chanting leads to a sense of possessiveness in which the sadhakathinks “the holy name is mine.” That sense of ownership or connection with the maha-mantrafurther results in an increasing sense of attachment to Krsna’s name, which naturally leads to attachment to Krsna, the two being non-different.

Because attachment to Krsna and those things related to Him arises from a purification effected by external practice, asakticultivated through smarana-dasamay be called an external imposition of bhava.Upon the exercise of divine will in the combined form of the hladiniand samvitpotencies, pure love within the heart becomes free of all material coverings and is able to manifest itself without hindrance. That attainment is bhavapana-dasa.And like a person who has been sick for many months and must again learn to walk and fend for himself, the liberated soul at bhava will once again learn to develop and express his unfettered loving propensities.

Let us now return to sadhanaand study more closely the direction in which a devotee’s sankalpasshould be steered to reach the destination of bhava.As we have summarised: how does a devotee chart his path?

To say it another way: by the practise of nama-sankirtanaa devotee aspires to attain bhava.And that aspiration needs to be intense enough to invoke Krsna’s mercy. But a cardinal question ensues:

**“What kind of bhavado we want?”**

When a person asks another for something, he is clear on what he wants. Similarly, the sadhakahas to be clear about what lie- means by “love for Krsna,” “spiritual identity,” and “going back to Godhead.” These general phrases are sufficient to inspire and guide a beginner, but not an accomplished practitioner.

The perspective of a sadhaka’sgoal must become increasingly clear as he progresses through smarana-dasa,in the way that the directions to a driver’s destination become increasingly specific as his arrival draws closer. It goes without saying that the driver knows where he is going. But it is not enough to know the district and town: the driver must know the street and house number, and even more specifically, he must know the residents of the house in order to gain entry. Similarly, the sadhakamust know where he wants to go; he must know what kind of bhavahe wants.

Now, how does the sadhakadetermine exactly at which address to find Krsna and which kind of bhavafor which he is beseeching Krsna?

For guidance on answering those question we turn to Srila Prabhupada’s commentary on Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s teachings about the progression of devotion from sadhanato bhava.

His Divine Grace writes,

**“After initiation, when one follows the regulative principles of devotional service, one becomes freed from all unwanted things. In this way one becomes firmly fixed and gradually develops a taste for devotional service. The more the taste grows, the more one desires to render service to the Lord. In this way one becomes attached to a particular mellow in the Lord’s service— santa, dasya, sakhya, vatsalya,or madhurya.As a result of such attachment, bhavadevelops. Bhava-bhakti is the platform of purified goodness. By such purified goodness, one’s heart melts in devotional service. Bhava-bhaktiis the first seed of love of Godhead.”**

Of special interest are the following sentences:

**“The more the taste grows, the more one desires to render service to the Lord. In this way one becomes attached to a particular mellow in the Lord’s service— santa, dasya, sakhya, vatsalya,or madhurya.As a result of such attachment, bhavadevelops.”**

Herein Srila Prabhupada says three things:

**At the stage of rucia devotee has a desire to serve Krsna, and that desire may be general, or inclined to a specific mellow Srila Prabhupada refers to in the next sentence.**

At the stage of asaktithe sadhakabecomes attracted to a mellow of devotional service. This is in accord with Rupa Gosvami’s directive to follow a resident of Vraja.

And when attachment is mature and a devotee is blessed by Krsna, he attains a bhavathat corresponds to the specific mellow of attachment that he cultivated, perhaps at ruci,definitely at asakti.

From Srila Prabhupada’s words it is dear that at dayana-smaranaa devotee should begin to clarify what eternal service to Krsna means for him. The later pages of this chapter show how that kind of research may transpire. Moreover, at anusmrti,and even more so at samadhi,a devotee should be cultivating attachment to a specific mellow of devotion, which means that he has awakened to some degree of spontaneity.

A thoughtful reader may well ask:

**“How do the temporal characteristics of sadhana-bhakti carry over to the spiritual characteristics of bhava-bhakti?”**

In other words, how, for example, is a raganuga-sadhakaassured that he does not attain vaidhi-bhava, and how is he assured that if he aspires to be a gopi,his identity will not be that of a gopa?”

We preface our answer by reminding the reader that one who has suitable guidance from both his guruand his intelligence will cultivate the sadhanasuited to his eternal bhava.If there is any disconnect between sadhanaand sadhyaat any stage of Krsna consciousness, Krsna will make sure that the sincere devotee is properly directed, yoga-ksemam vahamy aham:

**“I carry what they lack, and I preserve what they have.”**

Moreover:

**“Krsna, scripture, and acaryasstate that one attains that state of perfection which he practises.”**

For example, Krsna says that a devotee practising vaidhi-sadhana attains vaidhi-raga:

*aisvarya-jnane vidhi-bhajana kariya*  
*vaikunthake yaya catur-vidha mukti pana*

**“By performing such regulated devotional service in awe and veneration, one may go to Vaikuntha and attain the four kinds of liberation.”**

Additionally, we have previously described the different perfections attained by practitioners of various moods or combinations of moods.

And we have also explained that the following verse can be understood in terms of a person passing from one body to another, or of a devotee passing from one state of consciousness to another:

*yam yam vapi smaran bhavam*  
*tyajaty ante kalevaram*  
*tam tam evaiti kaunteya*  
*sada tad-bhava-bhavitah*

**“Whatever state of being one remembers when he quits his body, O son of Kunti, that state he will attain without fail.”**

Herein Krsna clearly establishes a correspondence between a devotee’s aspiration and his destination.

And finally, one of the cornerstones of this book is Sanatana Gosvami’s teaching that practice and perfection match:

*sva-sadhananumpam hi*  
*phalam sarvatra sidhyati*

**“In all spheres of activity, the results one achieves match the discipline one has practised.”**

*siddhasya laksanam yat syat*  
*sadhanam sadhakasya tat*

**“The practitioner and the means of practice should be in accord with their goal.”**

So to conclude on this question, we may rest assured that the nature of properly executed devotional service is such that practitioners will reach their appropriate destination.

However, our attention is primarily on how a devotee’s taste and attachment for Krsna unfold, and what the underlying truths to inspire that development are:

**What is a devotee’s worshipable deity? What kind of relationship does he have with the Lord? With which associates does he serve? And more.**

While for most devotees these questions are academic, iskcon is a worldwide institution, where devotees still seek out and have access to many Vaisnavas beliefs. The questions above must be addressed and the path a sadhakamust take should be crystal-clear. Thus we propose the following:

**To pass from dhyanato samadhiand from there to bhava,the sadhakamust have envisaged and realised a complete correlation between sadhanaand sadhya.**

The regulative devotee must have an intellectual appreciation of raga-bhaktiwhich when applied to his own practices becomes increasingly spontaneous as he approaches bhava.And the same truths that guide the vaidhi-bhaktamust apply in equal measure to the more progressive raganuga-sadhaka.

\* \* \* \*

It should go without saying that Krsna is the exclusive object of devotion in practice and perfection. That said, experience shows that due to a misunderstanding of Gaudiya Vaisnava teachings, some devotees worship Nrsimha, Ramacandra, or Narayana as their ista-devas.However, Sri Uddhava points out that it is Krsna who is meant to be the beneficiary of every sadhaka’sservice. Uddhava addresses his cousin with these words:

*namo ’stu te maha-yogin*  
*prapannam anusadhi mam*  
*yatha tvac-caranambhoje*  
*ratih syad anapayini*

**“Obeisances unto You, O greatest of yogis! Please instruct me, who am surrendered unto You, how I may have undeviating attachment to Your lotus feet.”**

Uddhava’s praise of Krsna is not familial bias, and neither is a Gaudiya Vaisnava’s veneration of Krsna a religious formulary. Rather, the verdict of Srimad-Bhagavatamis that Krsna is the original Supreme Person who embodies all the attractive features of His expansions and more. He is the most appealing form of Godhead in terms of beauty, sweetness, and opulence. Most importantly, one of Krsna’s most persuasive attributes is the unparalleled mercy that He alone bestows, mercy which is illustrated by pastimes in which even demons attain perfection, a quality no other incarnation displays.

Again, it is Uddhava who gives evidence of this remarkable trait:

*aho baki yam stana-kala-kutam*  
*jighamsayapayayad apy asadhvi*  
*lebhe gatim dhatry-ucitam tato ’nyam*  
*kam va dayalum saranam vrajema*

**“Alas! How shall I take shelter of one more merciful than Him \[Lord Krsna\], who granted the position of mother to the she-demon Putana although she was faithless and had prepared deadly poison to be sucked from her breast?”**

Sri Uddhava rightly argues that a devotee who contemplates Krsna’s extraordinary kindness will conclude that it does not make sense to take shelter of any form of the Lord, because they show less mercy than He. Dear readers! Please remember that our attainment of bhavais dependent on mercy, and since Kali-yuga practitioners have a hard time with the simplest spiritual requirement, their success is very much dependent on how gracious and sympathetic their worshipable object is.

As we have explained, a practitioner must have reached this understanding at the stage of dhyana,which is characterised by fixed meditation on the form of the Lord. That quality of concentration is only possible when the object of meditation is settled. Indeed, the earlier that a devotee decides on his worshipable deity, the smoother and speedier will be his progress through smarana, dharana, dhyana,and beyond.

Having concluded on the form of Krsna as the best meditation for him, a devotee needs to further refine his thinking to determine which of Krsna’s forms is most desirable—the one in Vrndavana, Mathura, or Dvaraka.

A comparison of these manifestations will lead a devotee to infer that Krsna manifests all qualities in full in Vraja, all qualities in part in Mathura, and only some qualities in Dvaraka. In this way He is known to be most perfect, more perfect, and perfect. In light of these considerations, Pariksit Maharaja came to the conclusion that Krsna and His pastimes in Vrndavana are the most fit topic for hearing and remembering. King Pariksit said,

*yena yenavatarena*  
*bhagavan harir isvarah*  
*karoti karna-ramyani*  
*mano-jnani ca nah prabho*

*yac-chrnvato ’paity aratir vitrsna*  
*sattvam ca suddhyaty acirena pumsah*  
*bhaktir harau tat-puruse ca sakhyam*  
*tad eva haram vada manyase cet*

**“My lord, Sukadeva Gosvami! All the various activities exhibited by the incarnations of the Supreme Personality of Godhead are certainly pleasing to the ear and to the mind. Simply by one’s hearing of these activities, the dirty things in one’s mind immediately vanish. Generally we are reluctant to hear about the activities of the Lord, but Krsna’s childhood activities are so attractive that they are automatically pleasing to the mind and ear. Thus one’s attachment for hearing about material things, which is the root cause of material existence, vanishes, and one gradually develops devotional service to the Supreme Lord, attachment for Him, and friendship with devotees who give us the contribution of Krsna consciousness. If you think it fit, kindly speak about those activities of the Lord.”**

And while Pariksit Maharaja cites the attractiveness of Krsna’s childhood form and pastimes, they too—like his boyhood pastimes—are not as complete as the form and pastimes of pre-youth, kaisora.

Moreover, the exchanges of love between Krsna and His different associates also develop in fullness from servanthood through friendship, parenthood, and conjugality. The mellow of conjugal love is the original relationship, and the others are its parts. Therefore the conjugal mellow is the fullest and most complete in attributes of loving exchange.

When Caitanya Mahaprabhu was in Prayaga, He heard these truths from Raghupati Upadhyaya and approved of them as the full consummation of Srimad-Bhagavatam’steachings.

In summary they are sung thus:

*syamam eva param rupam*  
*puri madhu-puri vara*  
*vayah kaisorakam dhyeyam*  
*adya eva paro rasah*

**“The form of Syamasundara is the supreme form, the city of Mathura is the supreme abode, Lord Krsna’s fresh youth should always be meditated upon, and the mellow of conjugal love is the supreme mellow.”**

We have, to this point, concluded that the most desirable form of worship is Krsna in Vrndavana in His form of fresh youth, and the most desirable mellow of worship is the conjugal mellow. Now let us further refine our perspective of the goal.

\* \* \* \*

As previously detailed, Srila Prabhupada indicates that the maturing of taste leads a devotee to become spontaneously attached to a particular relationship with the son of Nanda. Jiva Gosvami further explains that the seed of this attraction is dependent on the nature of the association and the nature of hearing to which a sadhaka is exposed. Hence, if a devotee hears of Krsna’s pastimes with the gopis,he will most likely develop an attraction to conjugal love, madhurya-rasa.

A reader may want clarification on the following subject:

**“How will spontaneous attraction awaken in a devotee in whom such feelings have not yet manifest, but who still displays a regulated attraction to Krsna?”**

While we have answered this in an earlier chapter, it remains a timely enquiry, and we repeat our reply:

**“He must become acquainted with the truths of spontaneous devotion, and he must regularly hear Krsna’s Vrndavana pastimes.”**

With proper guidance a vaidhi-bhaktawill respect the subject mat ter of such hearing and not reject it. Then he can add aspects of spontaneous devotion to his sadhana,and in this way his bhakti will gradually develop into a blend of vaidhiand raga.

**“What does that mix of regulated-spontaneous devotion look like?”**

Here is an example:

**“A devotee chants nama-sankirtanawith the conviction that the most fruitful meditation is to conceive of himself as a follower of a resident of Vraja engaged in services to the Divine Couple, as described in the books of the deary as."**

Even though the sadhakais not meditating out of spontaneous desire, he follows the activities of spontaneous sadhanaas an act of intelligence. By doing so he awakens an increased taste for the ways of the Vraja-vasis, and in time his regulated efforts assume the quality of spontaneity.

Jiva Gosvami explains the transformative power of spontaneous devotion in this way:

*yasya purvokte raga-visese rucir eva jatasti na tu*  
*raga-visesa eva svayam tasya tadrsa-raga-sudhakara-*  
*kardbhasa-samullasita-hrdaya-sphatika-maneh sastradi-*  
*srutasu tadrsya ragatmikata bhaktau paripatisv api*  
*rucir jayate. tatas tadiyam ragam rucyanugacchanti sa*  
*raganuga tasyaiva pravartate.*

**“When a person develops a taste for the aforementioned raga,even though that attachment has not awakened in him, the heart becomes like a glittering crystal reflecting the rays of the moon of raga. By hearing about this attachment from scripture or his guru,the sadhakadevelops a taste for the actions of the ragatmikaassociates who are but manifestations of ragatmika-bhakti.In this, way by adhering to the ragaof a particular associate to whom he is attracted, he then becomes known as a practitioner of raganuga-bhakti.”**

We should not fail to emphasise that pure raganuga-bhaktiis for Sri Krsna alone.

This understanding is derived from the verse beginning with kamad dvesad bhayat snehadand the verses following it. Even devotion to the King of Dvaraka falls in the category of regulated devotion. Jiva Gosvami points out that the consistent theme of Srimad-Bhagavatamis that raganuga-bhaktiis for the beloved of Radha alone.

For example, while speaking to Uddhava, Krsna’s mention of spontaneous devotion was only towards Himself, while descriptions of regulated devotion were always aimed at His four-armed form.

Thus a devotee who closely studies the teachings of Srila Prabhupada and his predecessors comes to the conclusion that on the path of spontaneous devotion, following the residents of Vrndavana is the only way to serve Krsna. Such spontaneous devotion is recommended by spiritual authorities, and is the stronger of the two kinds of sadhana, vaidhi,and raga.

Moreover, a devotee will note that acaryassuch as Bhaktivinoda Thakura, Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura, Rupa Gosvami, Sana tana Gosvami, Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami, Narottama Dasa Thakura, and their associates all wrote about the unwedded love of the gopisand made that mellow their own. In short, madhurya rasais the mellow most associated with raganuga-bhakti.

When Sukadeva Gosvami was describing the rasa-lila,some of those in attendance were confused how mixing illicitly with others’ wives was in keeping with the Lord’s exemplary character. The sage explained the transcendental position of Krsna and His devotees, and concluded by the following glorification of the conjugal mellow:

*vikriditam vraja-vadhubhir idam ca visnoh*  
*sraddhanvito ’nusrnuyad atha varnayed yah*  
*bhaktim param bhagavati pratilabhya kamam*  
*hrd-rogam asv apahinoty acirena dhirah*

**“Anyone who faithfully hears or describes the Lord’s playful affairs with the young gopisof Vrndavana will attain the Lord’s pure devotional service. Thus, he will quickly become sober and conquer lust, the disease of the heart.”**

In this verse the word paramindicates that the devotion depicted by the rasadance is both transcendental and superior to all others. By hearing and contemplating the rasadance and other similar pastimes, a devotee acquires a devotion comparable to that of the gopis,and his heart is quickly freed of lust.

Commentators emphasise that the sequence of events is as mentioned in the previous sentence: first one attains spontaneous devotion in wake of the gopis,and then the heart becomes completely pure. In other words, one need not be freed of all material desire to hear of Krsna’s pastimes with the gopis.In Srila Prabhupada’s words:

**“If a bona fide listener, hears of Krsna’s pastimes with the gopis, which seem to be lusty affairs, the lusty desires in his heart, which constitute the heart disease of the conditioned soul, will be vanquished, and he will become a most exalted devotee of the Lord.”**

Krsna’s exchanges with the gopisin Vraja represent one of His two conjugal pastimes, the parakiya-lila.The other is described in Srimad-Bhagavatam’slater chapters, which is His marrying sixteen thousand one-hundred and eight queens, the svakiya-lila.

Sometimes there is controversy which of the two conjugal pastimes—married or unmarried—is superior and original. The phrase bhaktim param,“supreme devotion,” answers that dispute. The devotion at the heart of Krsna’s love for the gopisis accepted by gaudiya-acaryasas the most excellent of the two. Even Jiva Gosvami, the occasionally reluctant proponent of wedded love, proclaims in his Sandarbhasthat unwedded love is the best of all. And Srila Prabhupada certainly made clear his unilateral opinion on this subject.

This standpoint should convince a sadhakaof the need to embrace the service mood of the gopisand his identity as their assistant.

But realising such an ambition is not without its price. To answer the call of Krsna’s flute, the gopisabandoned their families, homes, reputation, and children. A devotee must be willing to follow the gopis’lead. To court Krsna’s ultimate favour, he must be willing to make the ultimate sacrifice.

Somehow a practitioner must embrace the same resolve to serve the gopisas they did to serve Krsna when they declared,

**“We must become Your maidservants.”**

By this conviction a sadhakaattains the shelter of the gopis’mood of devotion, gopi-bhava,a mood that the Six Gosvamis shared.

We have refined our desired mood of bhavafurther, from a general one of conjugal attachment, to the more specific unwedded love of the gopis.We are getting further clarity!

\* \* \* \*

In hearing of and meditating on the mood of the gopisit is inevitable that a devotee will recognise Srimati Radharani’s pre-eminent position and the wonders of Her service. A corollary of follow ing the gopisis the awakening of a desire to serve Her. The Lord becomes pleased when a sadhakayearns after Radha’s service while chanting Krsna’s names and serving Gaura’s sankirtanamission Thus the practitioner’s spontaneous attachment goes from strength to strength.

There should be no doubt that service to Sri Radha is synonymous with and complementary to service to Krsna. Indeed, the wise say that Radha is the exclusive medium to serving Krsna in Vrndavana. All other efforts must complement Her service, and those that do not are futile.

Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami expresses this law of bhaktiin this way:

*anaradhya radha-padambhoja-renum*  
*anasritya vrndatavim tat-padankam*  
*asambhasya tad-bhava-gambhira-cittan*  
*kutah syama-sindho rasasyavagahah*

**“Without worshipping the pollen of Sri Radha’s lotus feet, without taking shelter of Vrndavana, which bears Her footprints, and without respectfully greeting the great souls whose hearts are filled with deep love for Her, how will one be able to plunge into the nectar ocean of love for Lord Krsna?”**

While this verse seems to say that Radha is the gateway of service to Krsna, the same author has taught its hidden meaning, which is that for Her maidservants and dear friends, Srimati Radharani is also the primary object of service and love. Yes, they love Radha more than Krsna! And that kind of devotion pleases Him the most.

Krsna is not envious of the worship of others, despite the biblical pronouncement:

**“I am a jealous God.”**

To the contrary, displaying His benevolence, Krsna says,

**“One who claims to be My devotee is not so. Only a person who claims to be the devotee of My devotee is actually My devotee.”**

After all, we must remember that in one sense, Srimati Radharani is not different from Krsna, for She is a manifestation of the aggregate of His divine potencies. Thus, serving Radha is serving Krsna.

With this conviction a sadhakamakes the lotus feet of Srimati Radharani the ultimate goal of his bhajana—indeed, of his existence. Thus his moods of devotion in separation will be directed at least as much, if not more, to Radha as they are to Krsna. Considering himself floundering in an ocean of pain, the practitioner will pray for shelter in the charming boat of Her lotus feet, the cooling nectar of a momentary glance, darsanaof Her divine form, and the tinkling of Her ankle bells.

With firm dependence on Sri Radha’s service, the sadhakagains an exclusive affinity that is both uniquely sweet and transcendentally advantageous. What to speak of succumbing to the opulences of Brahma, a devotee will not exchange service to the Queen of Vrndavana for direct service to Krsna, or even promotion to the station of becoming an intimate girlfriend, sakhi.

In his Vilapa-kusumanjali,Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami pre-empts and declines Srimati Radharani’s offer of a close friendship akin to that of Lalita. By doing so, he reveals a rarely-known service attitude that is not to be found even within the pages of the Vedas:

*padabjayos tava vina vara-dasyam eva*  
*nanyat kadapi samaye kila devi yace*  
*sakhyaya te mama namo ‘stu namo ‘stu nityam*  
*dasyaya te mama raso ‘stu raso ‘stu satyam*

**“O Devi! I shall never, never, ask You for anything other than the peerless service of Your lotus feet. Over and over again I offer my respects to the chance of becoming Your girlfriend, but I shall only aspire for the honour of being Your maidservant.”**

Exclusive service to Srimati Radharani is called radha-dasyam,and it is a unique blend of conjugal love and servanthood. The maid-servants who embody this mood are known as manjaris,and their attitude of devotion is also known as manjari-bhava.From the perspective of madhurya-rasa,when Rupa Gosvami says,

**“Follow in the footsteps of the Ford’s beloved devotees, who are deeply attached to His devotional service,”**

he means,

**“Follow in the footsteps of the manjaris.”**

Why is the mood of the manjarisweeter and more advantageous than that of a gopi-friend like Visakha?

The role of a maidservant places manjarisin a subordinate position in which Radha allows them to do services that She will not accept from Her girlfriends, such as massaging Her feet. Moreover, in many ways a servant becomes more intimate than a friend.

When Radha and Krsna are in a secluded grove sharing confidential pastimes, only the manjaris,and not other gopis,have access to Their service. The reason is that in some circumstances, Sri Radha will be shy before Her friends, whereas She is not so before Her maidservants.

As a servant, the manjarisare dependent on and maintained by Sri Radha, and so they are also referred to as palya-dasi.

Thakura Bhaktivinoda sings, vrsabhanu-suta-carana-sevane, hoibo ye palya-dasi:

**“To serve the lotus feet of the charming daughter of King Vrsabhanu, I will become Her sheltered maidservant.”**

Indeed, this palya-dasiidentity is one of the eleven essential traits of a manjari’sperfection. In consideration of these factors it is clear that a manjari'srole as servant, dependant, and confidante is full of pastimes and moods of sweetness that other gopisdo not share.

The role of a manjariis also more advantageous than that of a sakhi,because their love for Krsna is transcendentally more chaste.

While Radha’s friends indulge in physical contact with Krsna, the manjarisspurn all His advances, thinking themselves Radha’s exclusive property. One may think that this virtue is at the cost of being denied the bliss of Krsna’s touch and amour. But no! The manjaris'utter dependence on Sri Radha creates such a connection with Her that even at a distance they experience Radha’s every ecstasy of union with Him. Therefore Dasa Gosvami thinks,

**“Why should I settle for a lesser pleasure of being Radha’s friend, when I can taste the greater pleasure of being Her maidservant?”**

In his external conduct, a sadhakais known as a rupanuga,a follower of Rupa Gosvami. In his maturing internal identity as a manjari, he continues in the rupanugamould, but now as a follower of Rupa-manjari. Thus, both internally and externally he takes guidance from Sri Rupa, always thinking, rupa-manjari-mukhas ta dasikah samsraye:

**“I take shelter of those maidservants who have Rupa-manjari as their leader.”**

In honing the mood and goal of our sadhana,we have come to its general conclusion, which is that a serious practitioner will follow the young maidservants of Sri Radha. This general mood and goal are sufficient to make the transition from samadhito bhavapana-dasa—Krsna willing. Having done so, the more specific aspects of one’s svarupabecome increasingly manifest with continued cultivation at bhava.

Yes! With a similar process of thinking, a devotee may conclude that he desires to be in another mellow, that of a young friend or older parent of Krsna. However, that conclusion will respect the pre-eminence of the conjugal mellow and will be based on the instructions Caitanya Mahaprabhu gave to Rupa Gosvami in Prayaga.

We now continue and conclude with our sadhaka’sjourney.

The natural progression of a devotee’s internal meditation blossoms with the fragrance of many pastimes of service to the Divine Couple. Malayan breezes carry the aroma of sandalwood over mountains, through forests, and across waters. Similarly, divine fate carries Radha and Krsna through pastimes of love from the caves of Govardhana, through the groves by the Yamuna, to the waters of Radha’s lake. In a meditation uninterrupted by either external circumstances or his external identity, always retaining his identification as a maidservant, the sadhakamerges into these pas times in the way that a river flows into the ocean.

Surrounding the shore of fragrant Radha-kunda are charming groves filled with the pleasing sounds of birds and bees. In the courtyard of one grove, Radha and Krsna share humorous talks with Her girlfriends, the echo of their laughter further ornament ing the forest gardens. When the rays of the sun become excessive, Krsna entices Radha and Her passionate friends to join Him in water sports, and the waves from their splashing mix with the waves of their laughter, creating high tide in the ocean of their pas times. Caitanya-caritamrtadescribes how Caitanya Mahaprabhu became so absorbed in this pastime that He envisaged Himself to be one of the manjaris.

To embrace Radha-Krsna’s noonday pastimes is to submerge in an ecstasy a thousand times greater than the bliss of the nocturnal rasadance by the Yamuna’s shore. This is the opinion of our acaryas.Named after a girl who is a dancing arena of divine love for the moon of Vraja, a girl who is the crown jewel of celestial gopis,Radha-kunda is the shelter of the followers of Rupa-manjari. To that fragrant lake, which is filled with the waters of pure love, a sadhakaardently prays,

*vraja-bhuvi mura-satroh preyasinam nikamair*  
*asulabham api turnam prema-kalpa-drumam tam*  
*janayati hrdi bhumaṝ snatur uccair priyam yat*  
*tad ati-surabhi radba-kundam evasrayo me*

**“For the eager person who bathes in its fragrant waters, Radha-kunda immediately creates in the land of the heart a desire tree of pure love rare even among the gopibeloveds of Mura’s enemy. May that diadem of Vraja be my shelter.”**

because vraja-bhaktiis the most desirable attainment, Jiva Gosvami enjoins all sadhakasto cultivate it up to the stage of samadhi. And because madhurya-bhavais the pre-eminent mood of service to the son of Nanda Maharaja, it is the mellow of devotion most glorified by scriptures and saints, and most preferred by practitioners.

If, however, a sadhakabecomes sensually agitated while hearing about the gopis,then he should leave aside such meditation in favour of those pastimes for which he has both qualification and inclination. The same course of action should be taken if a devotee is more attracted to pastimes of Krsna’s childhood or boyhood. He should meditate on pastimes that correspond to his attachment and not intrude into the confidential exchanges of love between Krsna and His beloveds. Such misconduct will result in a conflict of mellows and an obstacle to nama-bhajana.This is the final teaching of Bhakti-sandarbha.

\* \* \* \*

In the preceding pages we have charted a course for a smarana-sadhaka.It is not the only course, but the one described and practised by most of our acaryasand many of their followers. It is their understanding of the conclusive teaching of Srimad-Bhagavatam.

As a devotee engages in nama-bhajanahe must follow a similar cultivation which begins with an intellectual understanding at smaranaand becomes part of meditation at dhyana.Thereafter, at anusmrtiand samadhi,meditation transforms into a sense of identity, which the sadhakaardently prays after to become a manifest reality. In time, by practising a sadhanasuited to his aspiration, a devotee attracts Krsna’s mercy and is blessed with bhava.These are the sankalpasleading to divine grace. We have earlier quoted Srila Prabhupada’s description of this path. We do so again:

**“In this way one becomes firmly fixed and gradually develops a taste for devotional service. The more the taste grows, the more one desires to render service to the Lord. In this way one becomes attached to a particular mellow in the Lord’s service—santa, dasya, sakhya, vatsalya,or madhurya.As a result of such attachment, bhavadevelops. Bhava-bhaktiis the platform of purified goodness. By such purified goodness, one’s heart melts in devotional service.”**

The journey is not easy, but at some point in his bhajanaa sadhaka meets with good fortune in the form of the grace of Krsna, which descends upon him in a way suited to divine fate. His bodily identification dwindling to nil, his spiritual identity a blossoming reality, a practising devotee loses himself in the bliss of Krsna’s pastimes. His feelings of ecstasy rise and fall like the waves on the sea, his eyes fill with tears of separation, his voice becomes hoarse from crying, and his heart yearns painfully for divine shelter.

True to His word, Krsna gives His devotee admittance into the spiritual realm, and having attained bhavapana-dasa,the sadhaka begins another journey through the enchanting forest-garden of love of God. In that forest he eventually encounters the Divine Couple and is given entrance into Their pastimes under the tutelage of Their eternal associates. Having attained such a perfection, a devotee may take a final glance back to offer respect to the worshippable path of bhajanawhich brought him to his destination. It was not an easy path.
