Still, free of doubt, fully convinced, he whispers, yam labdhva caparam labham:

**“Upon attaining this, there is no greater gain.”**

## Chapter Thirty-Eight

**The Truths of Grace**

If one were to observe an advanced sadhaka,it may seem that one day, bhavaappeared in the practitioner solely as a result of his intensive sadhana.Such a conclusion, however, would be erroneous. While rigorous sadhanais a must to purify the consciousness, in and of itself sadhanais not sufficient to attain bhava. Ecstatic devotion may appear to have manifest by the activities of a devotionally saturated mind, but the truth is that bhavaappears by divine grace.

In describing the advent of bhava,Rupa Gosvami says,

*avirbhuya mano-vrttau vrajanti tat-svarupatam*  
*svayam-prakasa-rupapi bhasamana prakasyavat*  
*vastutah svayam asvada-svarupaiva ratis tv asau*  
*krsnadi-karmakasvada-betutvam pratipadyate*

**“Appearing within the functions of the mind, bhava assumes the condition of the mind itself. Although bhavais self-manifesting, it appears to be manifest by the devotionally saturated mind. Moreover, although the essential nature of bhavais taste itself, it also acts as a cause of tasting the pastimes of Krsna, His associates, and His pastimes.”**

Rupa Gosvami makes clear that bhavais self-manifesting. It appears in response to sincere and favourable sadhana,but the cause of bhava’sappearance is not sadhana.

**“How then does bhavafinally manifest within the heart and mind of the sadhaka?”**

**“Bhavaappears by its own will! It is self-manifesting! It may be the bhavain Krsna, the bhavain a great devotee, or even the bhavain the heart of the sadhaka; whichever it is, bhavamanifests by its own will through any one of those divine agents.”**

In the definition of bhavabeginning with suddha-sattva-visesatma Rupa Gosvami makes clear that Krsna’s potencies of cognisance, samvit,and loving devotion, hladini,descend into the heart of the sadhaka,wherein they combine and forcibly make the devotee delight in Krsna as the object of love:

*suddha-sattva-visesatma*  
*prema-suryamsu-samya-bhak*  
*rucibhis citta-masrnya-*  
*krd asau bhava ucyate*

**“When devotional service is executed on the transcendental platform of pure goodness, it is like a sunray of love for Krsna. At such a time, devotional service causes the heart to be softened by various tastes, and one is then situated in bhava\[emotion\].”**

In other words, although premais dormant within every living entity, through the actions of Krsna’s internal potency, suddha- sattva,it is brought to life in a heart made ready by pure devotional service. In the way that a seed sprouts by the agency of exterior forces like rain and sunshine, so the seed of love sprouts as bhavaby the grace of pure goodness comprised of divine cognisance and love. For that reason, Caitanya Mahaprabhu calls it the sprout of love, premankura.

The verse above refers to bhavaas a sunray of love, prema-suryamsu,and paints a picture of the rising sun. Before the sun manifests its full presence, it is heralded by an initial sunbeam that then grows in strength and size into sunrise. Similarly, bhavais the first stream of prema.Like the sun, which appears in part or whole by its own agency, ecstatic devotion appears by its own volition through the power of the sun of love, suddha-sattva.

And so one asks:

**“From where does this beam of suddha-sattva descend?”**

**“From the heart of a great devotee who is empowered to bestow such love. Love from the heart of the siddha awakens love in the heart of the sadhaka.”**

**“What is the reason a great soul blesses a practitioner in this way?”**

**“His mercy! Krsna’s mercy!”**

**“But what is that oft-spoken mercy of Krsna, mercy of Krsna’s devotee, which is the sole cause for the appearance of bhava?And why and how does it appear?”**

**“The purpose of this chapter is to study how saints and scriptures answer these questions, and what they have revealed about the mysteries of divine grace.”**

In describing how Vaisnavas are the cause of devotion for non-devotees, Jiva Gosvami defines mercy as krpa-rupas ceto- vikaro hi para-duhkhasya sva-cetasi sparse saty eva jayate:

**“Mercy is a transformation of consciousness which occurs only when the suffering of another person touches one’s own heart.”**

In light of this definition, mercy may be based on remembrance of one’s own past suffering, or if one is a stranger to suffering, then mercy is based on simply seeing the struggles of another.

Because the suffering of conditioned souls is due to ignorance of the bliss of pure devotion, when devotees are moved by the suffering of others, mercy is manifested in acts of giving others bhakti.

Since mercy is only completed by action, a full definition of mercy is:

**“A transformation of consciousness which occurs only when the suffering of another person touches one’s own heart, compelling one to distribute devotional service to materially afflicted souls.”**

Based on the principle of bhaktya sanjataya bhaktya,“devotion begets devotion,” the mercy which induces a Vaisnava to offer someone bhaktimust itself be an aspect of bhakti.

Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura makes clear that mercy is a potency of Krsna known as krpa-sakti,and that it is the emperor who rules over all other divine energies. Since devotion is Krsna's pre-eminent potency, in one sense the two, bhaktiand krpa,are synonymous; in another sense, how they act is different: one is loving devotion itself, the other is the inspiration to bestow loving devotion.

It may be asked:

**“Does Krsna feel the suffering of others?”**

The answer is:

**“Yes and no!”**

Krsna feels the troubles of His devotees, but He does not experience the suffering of non-devotees.

The key to understanding Krsna’s interaction with His own krpa-saktiis to recognise the connection He does and does not have with His potencies.

Krsna elaborates on this subject in the following verse:

*samo ’ham sarva-bhutesu*  
*na me dvesyo ’sti na priyah*  
*ye bhajanti tu mam bhaktya*  
*mayi te tesu capy aham*

**“I envy no one, nor am I partial to anyone. I am equal to all. But whoever renders service unto Me in devotion is a friend, is in Me, and I am also a friend to him.”**

When Krsna says that He is “equal to all,” He refers to His relationship with non-devotees and with the material energy, which elsewhere He calls His “separated” energy. The material energy, its modes of nature, and the conditioned souls who have taken shelter of both are all separated from Krsna. As such, the material happiness and distress of non-devotees are not felt by the Lord. Therefore it is said that the Lord does not feel the sufferings of the world.

However, when Krsna says He is a “friend to him,” He refers to His relationship with His devotees and with the spiritual energy, specifically His bhakti-sakti.Because loving devotion is Krsna’s very heart, He is therefore very much connected to the heart and feelings of His devotee, be they sadhakaor siddha.

In the pastime of binding Lord Damodara, despite His displays of magic, Mother Yasoda exhibited extraordinary determination to bind her son. Witnessing Yasoda’s loving devotion, Krsna’s krpa-saktimelted His heart, turned it butter-soft, made Him submit to her will, and forced Him to be bound. This is an example of how Krsna feels the anxiety of His pure devotee.

But Krsna is captivated not only by loving devotion, but by devotion in practice as well. In describing the yogasystem to Uddhava, Krsna speaks of the glories of both sadhanaand sadhya-bhakti.

In the verse below He shows that both kinds of bhaktienchant His heart:

*na sadbayati mam yogo*  
*na sankhyam dharma uddhava*  
*na svadhyayas tapas tyago*  
*yatha bhaktir mamorjita*

**“My dear Uddhava, the unalloyed devotional service rendered to Me by My devotees brings Me under their control. I cannot be thus controlled by those engaged in mystic yoga,Sankhya philosophy, pious work, Vedic study, austerity, or renunciation.”**

Kardama Muni worshipped the Lord with a desire for a suitable wife. In that sense he was still a practitioner. While narrating how Kardama met the Lord by Bindu-sarovara, Maitreya Muni revealed that the lake was so named because:

**“Drops of tears had fallen there from the eyes of the Lord, who was overwhelmed by extreme compassion, krpaya samparitasya,for the sage, who had sought His protection.”**

In summary, it is well known that Krsna is always full in bliss and remains untouched by even the slightest scent of distress, what to speak of the ignorance of non-devotees. Although the origin of mercy, and even while He leaves His abode to deliver conditioned souls, Krsna does not undergo any of their sufferings, inasmuch as darkness cannot touch the sun. And because Krsna does not feel the suffering of conditioned souls, He is not moved to directly give them mercy. Instead, He gives His mercy through His representatives, the devotees. More will be said about this later.

But Krsna’s relationship with His devotees is a different story.

The bliss of the Lord is made possible by His internal potency, the essence of which is loving devotion. And loving devotion is what defines a devotee. Thus, the Lord and His servant are bound together by the bond of devotion. When bhaktiin the heart of the devotee melts the heart of the Lord, it induces Him to show mercy in proportion to His servant’s devotion and humility. This is how Krsna gives mercy to His devotee, a secret He taught to Durvasa Muni and summarised in this beautiful verse:

*sadhavo hrdayam mahyam*  
*sadhunam hrdayam tv aham*  
*mad-anyat te na jananti*  
*naham tebhyo manag api*

**“The pure devotee is always within the core of My heart, and I am always in the heart of the pure devotee. My devotees do not know anything else but Me, and I do not know anyone else but them.”**

When Krsna shares the transcendental sorrow of His associate— such as at the time of their separation—the pangs of despair are also an aspect of His internal potency and are but another facet of transcendental bliss. In this way His eternally blissful nature remains undisturbed.

\* \* \* \*

Readers may well ask:

**“If Krsna is the source of mercy, and yet He does not give mercy to non-devotees, how does someone become a devotee without mercy? And if non-devotees do get Krsna’s mercy, how do they do so if He does not give it to them?”**

These important topics should be understood by devotees, since their ascent to bhavais dependent on grasping the truths of the krpa-sakti.

In summary, the answers to the two questions are:

**“It is not possible to become a devotee without getting the Lord’s mercy.**

**“But it is the devotee of the Lord, specifically the madhyama-adhikari,who makes Krsna’s mercy available.”**

The intermediate devotee is known to be of two kinds:

**“The sadhakawho has ascended from the neophyte stage, and the siddhawho has descended from the advanced platform.”**

While the latter is clearly more qualified than the former, both are impelled by their corresponding level of devotion to manifest mercy upon conditioned souls. Vasudeva explains that magnanimity is the nature of devotees, sadhavo dina-vatsalah:

**“Sadhusare merciful to the fallen.”**

A relevant point requires clarification:

**“Is the mercy theirs or Krsna’s?”**

**“Both!”**

Krsna is the source of the krpa-sakti.It is His mercy. But He gives the power of attorney over His mercy to His devotee, who is free to do with it as he likes. The devotee can choose to distribute it, or to not. The decision to give others Krsna’s mercy is the mercy of the devotee. In this way, mercy is both Krsna’s and the devotee’s.

When the demigods were glorifying the Lord in Devaki’s womb, they conveyed an insight into the relationship between the mercy of the Lord and the mercy of His devotee. They said,

*svayam samuttirya sudustaram dyuman*  
*bhavarnavam bhimam adabhra-sauhrdah*  
*bhavat-padambhoruha-navam atra te*  
*nidhaya yatah sad-anugraho bhavan*

**“O Lord, Who resembles the shining sun, You are always ready to fulfil the desire of Your devotee, and therefore You are known as a desire tree \[vancha-kalpataru\].When acaryascompletely take shelter under Your lotus feet in order to cross the fierce ocean of nescience, they leave behind on Earth the method by which they cross, and because You are very merciful to Your other devotees, You accept this method to help them.”**

In this verse Krsna is referred to as dyuman,the independent transcendental sun who illuminates the world with the rays of His mercy. Devotees are blessed with that mercy, accessible to them in the form of the shelter of the Lord’s feet. That shelter is devotional service, which is the boat by which devotees cross to the far shore of the ocean of material existence.

Usually when one crosses water, the vessel in which one crossed remains at the landing point. But the demigods say that the mercy of the devotees is that the boat with which they crossed is both at the starting and landing point. And so, by the grace of Vaisnavas, what was received by them continues to be available to those who want it.

In his purport to this verse, Srila Prabhupada explains that a form that the devotee’s mercy takes are the books he writes describing the path of devotional service. This is a traditional way in which conditioned souls are able to access Krsna’s mercy through the mercy of the devotee. Therefore, writing and distributing books is the family business of merciful Vaisnavas.

Srila Prabhupada’s translation also features another wonderful interaction between the mercy of the Lord and the mercy of His devotee. His Divine Grace describes the boat moored at the starting dock in this way:

**“They leave behind on Earth the method by which they cross, and because You are very merciful to Your other devotees, You accept this method to help them.”**

The meaning is that the acaryamay make adjustments to the details of how his followers can take shelter of Krsna’s lotus feet.

Srila Prabhupada gives the example that his followers were instructed to chant sixteen rounds because they were not able to chant sixty-four or more. That arrangement was Prabhupada’s mercy. Because Krsna accepts how devotees want to distribute the krpa-sakti,He accepted Srila Prabhupada’s adjustment. Thus, Krsna’s mercy wonderfully follows the mercy of His devotees in all ways because He is sad-anugraha:

**“Always kind and merciful to the devotees.”**

Another prayer taught by Lord Siva to the sons of King Pracina- barhi makes clear that by the Lord’s mercy one becomes fortunate enough to associate with pure devotees, the very personifications of mercy:

*athanaghanghres tava kirti-tirthayor*  
*antar-bahih-snana-vidhuta-papmanam*  
*bhutesv anukrosa-susattva-silinam*  
*syat sangamo ’nugraha esa nas tava*

**“My dear Lord! Your lotus feet are the cause of all auspicious things and the destroyer of all the contamination of sin. I therefore beg Your Lordship to bless me by the association of Your devotees, who are completely purified by worshipping Your lotus feet and who are so merciful upon the conditioned souls. I think that Your real benediction will be to allow me to associate with such devotees.”**

The word anugrahais a synonym for krpa.The verbal root of anugrahais grab,which means “to capture,” and the familiar prefix anumeans “to follow.” Together anugrahaindicates that some one’s heart is captured by the plight of another. This is the definition of true empathy.

Lord Siva says that the Lord’s grace is manifest in the form of the association of pure devotees, sangamo ’nugraha.

Jiva Gosvami gives two meanings to this phrase:

**The first is that the Lord is He whose mercy comes through the gateway of His devotees, and so only through them does He bless the unfortunate. The second meaning is that the Lord is He whose mercy is His devotees.**

The implication of both explanations is that Krsna’s mercy is available only by the association of pure devotees, and not in any other way.

The line bhutesv anukrosa-susattva-silinamdescribes the qualities, sila,of saintly devotees. They are situated in goodness, susattva,and they are very merciful, anukrosa,to ordinary living brings, bhutesu.The word anukrosaalso means mercy, krpa.The verbal root krusmeans “to cry.” The import of the word is that pure devotees

**“Follow the crying of suffering souls.”**

What do they do when they meet up with such distressed humans? Saints give them Krsna’s mercy in the form of their teachings and example, and thus relieve the torment of the spiritual pauper’s heart.

In the Bhagavad-gitaKrsna uses the phrase mat-prasadat,“by My mercy,” as in,

**“You will pass over all the obstacles of conditioned life by My grace.”**

Krsna says that devotees are the form of His mercy, and His mercy can be received only through the mercy of the devotee.

In the way that Krsna is independent, so too is His krpa-sakti. So much so that in damodara-lilait was the krpa-saktithat decided when Yasoda should bind Krsna, not He. He was too scared of being punished to think of such things. This is the excellence of Krsna’s independent potencies.

When Krsna hands over the power of attorney to His devotee, along with His mercy He also gives them complete independence to distribute mercy to anyone, anywhere, at anytime. That said, there are certain guidelines regarding what level of mercy should be given to whom, and if devotees are not mindful, they may incur very serious reactions for their oversight. One such transgression is the ninth offence to the holy name:

*asraddadhane vimukhe' py asrnvati*  
*yas copadesah siva-namaparadhah*

**“It is an offence to preach the glories of the holy name among persons who have no intelligence or no faith in the subject matter.”**

The message of this verse is that it is a namaparadhato give mercy beyond an aspirant’s qualification, or for that matter beyond the donor’s qualification.

\* \* \* \*

In addition to the above-mentioned truth regarding divine grace is another:

**Krsna and His energies follow the will of a pure devotee.**

Once while wandering over the universe unimpeded, the Nava yogendras came across Maharaja Nimi’s sacrifice, and of then own free will decided to give audience to the king and his retinue. Sukadeva Gosvami says, upajagmur yadrcchaya:

**“They approached according to their free will.”**

Thereafter the nine sages each spoke extraordinary words of wis dom, and so liberated their audience. This was an example of devotees distributing Krsna’s mercy according to their sweet will.

Lord Brahma gave another example of how Krsna is subservient to His devotees. Embarrassed for having tested Krsna’s powers, Brahma begged forgiveness with eloquent prayers that included the sentence asyapi deva vapuso mad-anugrahasya sveccha-mayasya:

**“Neither I nor anyone else can estimate the potency of this transcendental body of Yours, which has shown such mercy to me and which appears just to fulfil the desires of Your pure devotees.”**

The Lord further confirmed subservience to His devotees when Durvasa Muni was desperate for shelter from the Sudarsana cakra. The sage sought out the Lord’s mercy, thinking,

**“After all it is the Lord’s personal weapon. He can withdraw it.”**

But that was not to he! Lord Narayana admitted that He was not at liberty to annul an offence against His devotee. He had no independent authority over His pure devotee; to the contrary, He was but a subordinate, fully controlled by Ambarisa's devotion. His words eternally resound in the heart sincere Vaisnavas:

*aham bhakta-paradhino*  
*hy asvatantra iva dvija*  
*sadhubhir grasta-hrdayo*  
*bhaktair bhakta-jana-priyah*

**“I am completely under the control of My devotees. Indeed, I am not at all independent. Because My devotees are completely devoid of material desires, I sit only within the cores of their hearts. What to speak of My devotee, even those who are devotees of My devotee are very dear to Me.”**

No doubt there are examples when a devotee is seen to give mercy to a conditioned soul in response to the order of the Lord.

For example, Srimati Radharani was observing the wanderings of a Mathura brahmanawho was unclear about both the sadhana and sadhyaof pure devotion. She thus called Gopa-kumara—who is known as Sarupa in Goloka—and asked him to deliver Her devotee. The entire second part of Brhad-bhagavatamrtais the instructions that Gopa-kumara gives the brahmana.

And yet we know that if, for some reason, a devotee is averse to the opinion of the Lord and does not want to bless a person, then the flow of mercy is blocked. That is the import of the Gurvastaka verse beginning with yasya prasadad bhagavat-prasadah.

Sri Jiva summarises these truths by saying that in the case of the deliverance of a living entity, the mercy of the Lord is a secondary factor, the primary factor being the free will of the pure devotee.

Therefore, as regards saving a conditioned soul from maya, Krsna’s krpa-saktiis the ingredient cause, upadana-karana,and the mercy of the devotee the effective cause, nimitta-karana.In the way that raw clay is of no value as a plate without first being moulded and fired by a potter, the krpa-saktiis not helpful without being made accessible by a Vaisnava’s free will.

The role of the devotee in distributing mercy should not be seen solely as that of a delivery man.

While a Vaisnava does not change the content or meaning of the truths that he transmits, he does add his own personal touch, which may enhance the Lord’s mercy even further. For example, the Srimad-Bhagavatambegins by extolling its speaker Sukadeva Gosvami, who made that fruit of the Vedas even more tasty by his artful recitation, suka-mukhad amrta-drava-samyutam.

In his glorification of the Lord, Siva therefore prays for the “real benediction” of associating with pure Vaisnavas, implying that the sequence in which mercy descends is from the devotee first and from Krsna second. Moreover, if the devotee’s mercy is secured, Krsna’s is guaranteed to follow. The Lord admits that He is not independent but rather fully controlled by His devotee. If a devotee blesses, then so does He. This is confirmed by the words of Sri Rudra, cited earlier.

The eternally liberated devotees have never been touched by the material energy and thus they are moved by empathy, anugraha. However, the sadhakasand the sadhana-siddhascan recall their previous suffering in the way one remembers a bad dream. In that way they are deeply affected by what they see, and freely give their krpa.

In either case a devotee’s mercy is invoked when he sees the unfortunate condition of those bereft of bhakti, sadhavo dina-vatsalah:

**“Sadhusare merciful to the fallen.”**

Their mercy, unlike the reciprocation of demigods, is not dependent on their being worshipped or petitioned.

The blessings of a great devotee can also save offenders in the way that Narada nullified the offences of the two sons of Kuvera. However, in order to be freed of offence, a person must receive a special blessing in the form of forgiveness. In the absence of the special mercy of a sadhu,an offender will not attain devotion, meaning he will not reap the benefit of a great Vaisnava’s distribution of mercy. And to get forgiveness, an offender usually has to ask for it, as in the case of Nalakuvera and Manigriva.

Jiva Gosvami argues that while Krsna’s mercy may address an unlimited number of souls, His devotee can only bless those of whom he is conscious.

After his father had been killed by the Lord, little Prahlada was seen by the demigods as the only one qualified to pacify angry Nrsimhadeva. Thus the boy offered beautiful prayers to the Lord in which he expressed the welfare of all non-devotees, saying,

*prayena deva munayah sva-vimukti-kama*  
*maunam caranti vijane na parartha-nisthah*  
*naitan vihaya krpanan vimumuksa eko*  
*nanyam tvad asya saranam bhramato ’nupasye*

**“My dear Lord Nrsimhadeva! I see that there are many saintly persons indeed, but they are interested only in their own deliverance. Not caring for the big cities and towns, they go to the Himalayas or the forest to meditate with vows of silence \[mauna-vrata\],They are not interested in delivering others. As for me, however, I do not wish to be liberated alone, leaving aside all these poor fools and rascals. I know that without Krsna consciousness, without taking shelter of Your lotus feet, one cannot be happy. Therefore, I wish to bring them back to shelter at Your lotus feet.”**

In the above verse, Sri Prahlada expresses a desire to give his mercy to all conditioned souls. And yet we see that everyone did not become liberated. Why is that? Because Prahlada’s blessing was effective for the people he was able to think of, but not for others. And since the boy could not possibly think of the unlimited living entities of the universe, only those whom he had seen and heard of received his grace. This conclusion is drawn from use of the negated pronoun naitan,“not these,” which refers solely to objects or people close by.

By contrast, the Lord’s mercy is unfettered. Lord Nrsimha was exceedingly pleased with Prahlada Maharaja’s prayers and He gave the blessing that anyone can be liberated by recalling the exchange between He and the boy:

*ya etat kirtayen mahyam*  
*tvaya gitam idam narah*  
*tvam ca mam ca smaran kale*  
*karma-bandhat pramucyate*

**“One who always remembers your activities and My activities also, and who chants the prayers you have offered, becomes free, in due course of time, from the reactions of material activities.”**

Thus, while the mercy of the Vaisnava is the predominating factor in benefiting the ignorant, the number of souls reached by the Lord’s mercy is more extensive than that of His servant’s.

The mercy of Krsna and His devotee takes many forms. We have given evidence that the devotee is the personification of mercy and therefore the advanced devotee is known as His Divine Grace. Of all mediators of Krsna’s grace, Srimati Radharani is the foremost It is through Her that Krsna’s love is bestowed upon devotees To experience what it was like to be the mercy incarnate of the Lord, Krsna embraced Radha’s mood and appeared as Caitanya Mahaprabhu. Along with His associates He distributed mercy without discrimination.

Kaviraja Gosvami writes,

*patrapatra-vicara nahi, nahi sthanasthana*  
*yei yanha paya, tanha kare prema-dana*

**“In distributing love of Godhead, Caitanya Mahaprabhu and His associates did not consider who was a fit candidate and who was not, nor where such distribution should or should not take place. They made no conditions. Wherever they got the opportunity, the members of the Panca-tattva distributed love of Godhead.”**

This verse makes dear that what the sadhu bestows upon the fallen is his mercy. In this case, the Panca-tattva gave the greatest mercy, prema.

However, the process of sadhana-bhaktiis also a devotee’s mercy. The teachings on sadhanaare premain seed form, and they are given to a recipient with the expectation that he must bring the seed to fruition.

In addition to the devotee, his association, and his teachings, another form of mercy is service to Krsna, and to Vaisnavas. The ninefold limbs of devotion facilitate many kinds of service, including participation in the preaching mission and attending to the physical needs of the spiritual master.

By winning the company of a devotee, a fortunate soul will receive mercy in the form of both faith and the specific sadhana that corresponds to his saviour’s spiritual tradition. In other words, the taste of Krsna’s mercy is as varied as the devotees within the aithentic paramparathat they represent.

The preceding sections have mostly emphasised giving mercy to the non-devotee, which is beautifully summarised by King Mucukunda’s words:

**“When the material life of a wandering soul has ceased,**

**O Acyuta, he may attain the association of Your devotees. And when he associates with them, there awakens in him devotion unto You, Who are the goal of the devotees and the Lord of all causes and their effects.”**

The ultimate mercy upon a sadhakais to be blessed with a spiritual body corresponding to the mood he cultivated during his years of practice. In the previous chapter we have described an advanced devotee’s eligibility for bhava:his crystal clear vision of the path leading there. The attainment of bhavahas yet to be discussed, as it is the crowning glory of all sankalpas,and so of central interest to our studies.

\* \* \* \*

In the following sections we shall turn our attention to how the Lord and His associates give mercy to devotees, and especially to t he sadhakaeager for bhava.

Being distant from them, Krsna does not feel the happiness and distress of conditioned souls. But he is intimately bound to His pure devotee through the medium of pure devotional service, the essence of His internal potency. Bhaktiis in the heart of the Lord and in the heart of the devotee, and bhaktibrings the two together in a way that they appear to share one heart. Thus, whatever the devotee feels is felt by the Lord, and vice versa. In this way a devotee is the recipient of the Lord’s grace, and incredibly, the Lord feels Himself the object of His devotee’s mercy.

When Gopa-kumara arrived in Vaikuntha he was greeted by the Lord, whose affectionate words repeatedly indicated that He fell Himself blessed by the presence of His devotee.

Lord Narayana first said,

**“I am fortunate, most fortunate, to meet you here.”**

Recounting how He had observed Gopa-kumara’s wandering throughout countless lifetimes, the Lord revealed that He thought Gopa-kumara may never return to favour Him with mercy:

*tat te mayy akrpam viksya*  
*vyagro ’nugraha-katarah*  
*anadim setum ullanghya*  
*tvaj-janmedam akarayam*

**“You showed Me no mercy, and as I considered this I grew impatient, full of anxiety to receive your favour. So I transgressed My eternal code of conduct and arranged for you to take your current birth.”**

In this verse we find two references to mercy. The Lord considered Gopa-kumara’s escapades acts of mercilessness, akrpam,and yet hoping against hope He remained in anxiety that one day the boy would grace Him, anugraha.Reading Lord Narayana’s address, it is hard not to be moved by His extreme humility.

In the following verse Krsna reveals to Uddhava how, like Lord Narayana, He is eager for the mercy of His pure devotees. And as we will see, Krsna expresses even greater modesty than His expansion. The Lord says,

*nirapeksam munim santam*  
*nirvairam sama-darsanam*  
*anuvrajamy aham nityam*  
*puyeyety anghri-renubhih*

**“With the dust of My devotees’ lotus feet I desire to purify the material worlds, which are situated within Me. Thus, I always follow the footsteps of My pure devotees, who are free from all personal desire, rapt in thought of My pastimes, peaceful, without any feelings of enmity, and of equal disposition everywhere.”**

In this verse Krsna also shows His humility by thinking of Himself as a devotee of His devotees.

Visvanatha Cakravarti adds that a firmly established law of bhaktimandates that the bliss of devotion to Krsna can only be had by the grace of the devotees. Therefore, Krsna also wants to taste that bliss by being the object of His devotees’ mercy.

Sripada Madhavacarya adds a caveat. While Krsna walks behind His devotees, the dust of His feet is swept forward and gives His mercy to them. In this way there is a constant exchange of love between worshipper and worshipped, in which who is benefactor and who is beneficiary is transcendentally obscured.

Readers may be inclined to assume that Krsna’s heart-to-heart connection is with His eternal associates and the perfected devotees, but not with sadhakas.

Durvasa Muni had this same misconception when He approached the Lord for shelter. Knowing his mind, Lord Visnu made it explicitly clear that His subservience to devotees included both the practitioner and the perfect. He claimed that His heart was controlled not only by those who have abandoned liberation, but also by their servants and dependants, the sadhakas.

The Lord said,

*aham bhakta-paradhino*  
*hy asvatantra iva dvija*  
*sadhubhir grasta-hrdayo*  
*bhaktair bhakta-jana-priyah*

**“I am completely under the control of My devotees. Indeed, I am not at all independent. Because My devotees are completely devoid of material desires, 1 sit only within the cores of their hearts. What to speak of My devotee, even those who are devotees of My devotee are very dear to Me.”**

Reading this one may be curious:

**“How dear to the Lord are the devotees of devotees?”**

Krsna replies:

**“The pure devotee is always within the core of My heart, and I am always in the heart of the pure devotee. My devotees do not know anything else but Me, and I do not know anyone else but them.”**

Krsna’s expression of love is based on, among other things, devotees’ exclusive dependence on Him. When devotees know nothing else but Him, He is obliged to reciprocate in kind. When devotees make Him their all-in-all, He is impelled to do the same. And while there is a gulf of difference between the siddhasand sadhakas, Krsna remains closely bound to both, even as His reciprocation varies with the degree of their surrender.

There is a secret in this exchange that should be disclosed.

The mercy and attachment of a perfected devotee far excels those of a practitioner. Nevertheless, both kinds of devotees are possessed of a mercy in which Krsna is the object of devotion. When their attachment is enriched with mercy, it results in bliss that surpasses the pleasure that Krsna derives from His own Self. For this reason, to share the bliss that sadhakasand siddhastaste, to be showered by it, Krsna remains in their hearts. In that way He considers Himself the object of His devotees’ special mercy.

Being directly connected to His devotees, Krsna can and does bestow His mercy directly. But the time-tested law is that His mercy descends through and because of His representative. Devotees of every calibre, from beginner to eternally liberated, consider that Krsna's mercy descends through the disciplic succession to their spiritual master, and from their spiritual master to them.

The first verse of the Gurvastakadepicts Krsna as an ocean of mercy whose waters are drawn up into the cloud-like spiritual master, who then showers the waters of mercy on conditioned souls hurtling in the blazing fire of material existence:

*samsara-davanala-lidba-loka-*  
*tranaya karunya-ghanaghanatvam*  
*praptasya kalyana-gunarnavasya*  
*vande guroh sri-caranaravindam*

**“The spiritual master is receiving benediction from the ocean of mercy. Just as a cloud pours water on a forest fire to extinguish it, so the spiritual master delivers the materially afflicted world by extinguishing the blazing fire of material existence. I offer my respectful obeisances unto the lotus feet of such a spiritual master, who is an ocean of auspicious qualities.”**

While the verse indicates that the mercy of the guruis for nondevotees or neophytes—for it is they who suffer—the principle is accepted by all intermediate and advanced devotees as well.

The works of the Gosvamis and Vyasa are replete with expressions of gratitude to superior Vaisnavas. Kaviraja Gosvami offers respects to Rupa and Raghunatha at the end of each chapter of Caitanya-caritamrta,Sanjaya thanks Vyasa for being able to hear the Bhagavad-gita,and Suta Gosvami praises his guruSukadeva for disclosing Srimad-Bhagavatam.The list of exalted devotees who consider themselves dependent on the mercy of their spiritual master is endless. Indeed, Krsna rejects those who consider themselves His devotees, saying,

**“One who claims to be My devotee is not so. Only a person who claims to be the devotee of My devotee is actually My devotee.”**

Since Krsna considers Himself the servant of the devotees, He does not like to see anyone act otherwise. The humble attitude in which a devotee conducts Himself as the servant of the Vaisnavas pleases Krsna very much. And because Krsna’s mercy is the cause of devotion, such humble devotees are blessed with increased spiritual opulences.

There is a divine connection between a devotee’s humility and the amount of mercy that he receives.

Jiva Gosvami writes, sa evatra mama saranam ity adi-dainyatmaka bhakti-sambandhenaiva jayate.

The purport is that Krsna bestows mercy upon His devotee when his service is saturated with humility and expressions of surrender such as:

**“O Lord! You are my only shelter,” and “I am but the servant of my spiritual master.”**

The greater a devotee’s humility, the greater the mercy that Krsna bestows upon him through his spiritual masters. And when the first trace of utter humility, dainya,manifests in the heart, then a devotee becomes eligible for bhava.And when his dainyais fully manifest, so too is loving devotion.

Readers may note that humility is like a special potion which, when sprinkled upon the creeper of devotion, causes a devotee’s bhaktito blossom in wonderful ways. Among the fruits of that creeper is both the increased desire and the increased ability to bestow mercy upon non-devotees or beginners. Another fruit is that humble devotion melts Krsna’s heart and makes Him all the more inclined to bless His devotee. The Lord thinks,

**“This Vaisnava is worthy of My mercy.”**

A humble devotee considers himself to be made of, in equal measure, the mercy of his guruand the mercy of Krsna.

Srutisays,

*yasya deve para bhaktir*  
*yatha deve tatha gurau*  
*tasyaite kathita hy arthah*  
*prakasante mahatmanah*

**“Only unto those great souls who have implicit faith in both the Lord and the spiritual master are all the imports of Vedic knowledge automatically revealed.”**

because devotion is dependent on mercy, a devotee prays intensely to his well-wishers, imploring them to be merciful and to bless him with increased devotion. Kaviraja Gosvami gives an example of such a humble entreaty:

*prema-dhana vina vyartha daridra jivana*  
*‘dasa’ kari vetana more deha prema-dhana*

**“Without love of Godhead, My life is useless. Therefore, I pray that You accept Me as Your servant and give Me the salary of ecstatic love of God.”**

By contrast, those who do not pray for mercy do not get it.

Jiva Gosvami makes clear that a devotee must have a desire lor mercy. Someone may be self-satisfied or even free of material desires, but without mercy he will not advance in devotion, what to speak of advancing to loving devotion. Such mixed devotees are not attuned to Krsna’s heart, and thus they cannot control it.

But pure devotees who turn to Krsna as their only recourse can expect the Lord’s shelter. It is there for those who ask for it, who plead for it. In the words of the Bible:

“Ask and it will be given to you; seek and you will find; knock and the door will be opened to you. For everyone who asks receives; the one who seeks finds; and to the one who knocks, the door will be opened.”

Mercy is there for the taking. The more intent the plea, the greater the quantity, the more exquisite the quality of bestowment.

\* \* \* \*

Jada Bharata told Maharaja Rahugana that if someone wants to realise the Absolute Truth and become the object of Krsna’s mercy, he must be willing to smear his entire body with the foot dust of great devotees. Sometimes students of Srimad-Bhagavatamtake this injunction to be symbolic. But they are mistaken: it is literal. Sukadeva Gosvami says such doubters are like the living dead:

*jivan chavo bhagavatanghri-renum*  
*na jatu martyo ’bhilabheta yas tu*

**“The person who has not at any time received the dust of the feet of the Lord’s pure devotee upon his head is certainly a dead body.”**

Scriptures repeatedly illustrate how Krsna’s mercy remains distant from those not willing to sincerely humble themselves before advanced Vaisnavas. On the other hand, a devotee who worships his superiors and faithfully takes the dust of their feet, who eats the remnants of their food, and drinks the water that washed their feet, that devotee becomes the object of divine grace.

Vrtrasura attained perfection by desiring the dust of great Vaisnavas, Narada told Yudhisthira Maharaja to make such practice an administrative policy, and Kalidasa received the special mercy of Caitanya Mahaprabhu by honouring the food remnants of devotees. To show how mercy manifests through the body of devotees, we shall briefly summarise the events of Kalidasa’s perfection.

Kalidasa was an uncle of Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami. Once, when the Bengali devotees came to see Caitanya Mahaprabhu in Jagannatha Puri, Kalidasa was among them. He came from a cultured brahmanaVaisnava family and had taken a vow to eat the food remnants of Lord Caitanya’s devotees—all of them.

Kaviraja Gosvami narrates an incident wherein by a trick, Kalidasa acquired the food remnants of a low-born Vaisnava, Jhadu Thakura. Lord Caitanya was already mercifully disposed to Kalidasa because of his sankalpaof honouring Vaisnavas. But when the Lord came to know that this high-class brahmana ignored the mundane norms of society and respected the remnants of a Vaisnava below his social station, He became especially merciful.

Lord Caitanya would always wash His feet before entering Jagannatha’s temple. And He had given strict orders that no devotee was allowed to taste the water that had washed His feet. But when Kalidasa placed his cupped hands beneath the Lord’s feet, the Lord did not object and in this way Kalidasa could drink three palmfuls of water.

This was how Kalidasa received the extraordinary mercy of Caitanya Mahaprabhu. Kaviraja Gosvami narrates this pastime to illustrate how devotees should exhibit their humility before advanced devotees and the mercy they can expect by doing so.

The author of Caitanya-caritamrta“insists” that his readers have faith in the power of these three practices and,

**“Render service to them without hesitation.”**

A devotee who is determined to have bhavain this very life must make a sankalpato serve great devotees’ foot dust, food remnants, and foot wash.

Kaviraja Gosvami says,

**“The dust of the feet of a devotee, the water that has washed the feet of a devotee, and the remnants of food left by a devotee are three very powerful substances. By rendering service to these three, one attains the supreme goal of ecstatic love for Krsna. In all the revealed scriptures this is loudly declared again and again. Therefore, my dear devotees, please hear from me, for I insist again and again: please keep faith in these three and render service to them without hesitation.”**

He then concludes,

*tina haite krsna-nama-premera ullasa*  
*krsnera prasada, tate ‘saksi’ kalidasa*

**“From these three one achieves the highest goal of life—ecstatic love of Krsna. This is the greatest mercy of Lord Krsna. The evidence is Kalidasa himself.”**

It has already been explained how sadhana-bhaktiattracts Krsna While the resolute determination to perfect the activities of chant ing, hearing, and remembering attract Krsna’s attention, the attitude of humility expressed by menial service to sadhuand guru quickly wins Krsna’s mercy.

Earlier chapters have emphasised developing humility by cultivating feelings of separation. That is an internal practice. We then added the external practice of crying after Krsna’s mercy with heartfelt emotion. Now we add subordinating oneself before advanced devotees. A sadhakacan expect to get Krsna’s mercy in proportion to how successfully he perfects these celebrated active ties of devotion.

Someone may doubt whether his bad background, low birth, and intense attachments will allow him to attain success in devotion, even if he makes every endeavour for it. But scripture reassures us time and again that the power of devotional service in the form of service to devotees overrides and nullifies these handicaps. Verses like kirata-hunandhra-pulinda-pulkasaprove that regardless of one’s background, by taking shelter of those who have Krsna’s shelter, apasraya-asraydah,a practitioner becomes free of all contamination and is elevated to ecstatic devotion.

To allay any doubt that the power of Vaisnava association can deliver His mercy, Krsna gives the following extensive list of those whom He has blessed. They include demons, animals, demigods, men, women, His associates, gopis,and the yajna-patnis:

**“In every yugamany living entities entangled in the modes of passion and ignorance gained the association of My devotees. Thus, such living entities as the Daityas, Raksasas, birds, beasts, Gandharvas, Apsaras, Nagas, Siddhas, Caranas, Guhyakas, and Vidyadharas, as well as such lower-class human beings as the vaisyas, sudras,women, and others, were able to achieve My supreme abode. Vrtrasura, Prahlada Maharaja, and others like them also achieved My abode by association with My devotees, as did personalities such as Vrsaparva, Bali Maharaja, Banasura, Maya, Vibhisana, Sugriva, Hanuman, Jambavan, Gajendra, Jatayu, Tuladhara, Dharma-vyadha, Kubja, the gopisin Vrndavana, and the wives of the brahmanaswho were performing sacrifice.”**

There is a history associated with each of those named in the list. We share a summary of only those with whom practitioners eager for bhavacan resonate. In every case, those mentioned above served Krsna’s devotees, were blessed by His mercy, and secured the good fortune of the Lord’s company. Readers may consider the following:

**The demon Vrtrasura was King Citraketu in his previous life, during which he associated with Narada Muni and Angira Muni and by their grace attained premain one life. Prahlada Maharaja, while still in the womb of his mother, Kayadhu, heard Narada Muni and quickly reached bhava.Vibhisana was the brother of Ravana. After freeing Hanuman, He decided to abandon his sinful life and join Lord Ramacandra’s cause. Even then, it took the intercession of Hanuman to secure Lord Rama’s shelter and the company of other devotees.**

Among animals, the elephant Gajendra is known to have been the accomplished devotee Indradyumna, who by service to devotees overcame his unfortunate curse and was personally saved by the Lord from death. We all know how Jatayu, the vulture, sacrificed his life to save Sita. He became devoted by associating with Garuda and Maharaja Dasaratha. By giving his life in service, Lord Rama personally performed his funeral rites and sent him directly to Vaikuntha.

Kubja was condemned to be a hunchback, yet in a previous birth she was Ravana’s sister Surpanakha, and by pleasing Lord Siva and Narada Muni, she developed a unique love for Krsna that was fulfilled in Mathura.

Of primary relevance to a sadhakaare the gopismentioned here. While their origins are varied, they had one thing in common, and that is they secured the blessings of saints through service, and hence took birth in Vrndavana. As Krsna enacted His pastimes, the eternally liberated gopiswandered here and there either in play, or in fulfilling household obligations. In the process they befriended these sadhakas,and by the touchstone of their association mailt the newcomers into lovers of Krsna. Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura says that these new gopisalso had the opportunity to serve Vrnda-devi.

The main point to be noted is that whether a devotee was previously a demon, an animal, a sinful human, or a sadhaka,the power of service to Vaisnavas overcomes all obstacles and blesses one with loving devotion. Thus endowed, a devotee secures entrance into Krsna’s pastimes.

We now conclude this chapter. In the next chapter we continue this topic by studying the role of the Vaisnava, and specifically the spiritual master, in securing the grace of the Lord and ecstatic devotion.

## Chapter Thirty-Nine

**Krsna’s Grace Descends Through Vaisnavas**

In the two preceding chapters we explored the descent of divine grace upon devotees and non-devotees. The source of mercy is the Supreme Lord and the channel through which it manifests is the advanced Vaisnava. Mercy is a voluntary act of kindness by which the Supreme or His representative gift the priceless treasure of pure devotion to a needy soul. When saints see the suffering of materialists, they are moved to bless them with bhakti,and when the Lord hears a practitioner’s earnest plea for eternal service, He blesses the devotee with prema.The perfected devotees and eternally perfect devotees revel in an eternal downpour of mercy, in the land of mercy.

Understanding the causes and movements of divine grace, a sadhakacan learn to act in ways that makes him its recipient. Thus, by the empowerment of krpa-sakti,a devotee can traverse the stages of sadhanato its perfection, ecstatic devotion.

It is this last transition from sadhanato bhavathat poses the greatest challenge. Because it is the most difficult transition in bhakti,it requires the most extraordinary grace, which in turn requires a most unprecedented appeal for love on the part of the sadhaka.In short, nama-sankirtanaof the sadhaka,enhanced by his humble cries of estrangement from Krsna, must move the heart of the Lord as never before.

In this chapter we shall attempt to put into words the sublime realisations that transpire during the fulfilment of the purpose of sadhana-bhakti.

\* \* \* \*

It is inevitable that sincere devotees are eager to know how and when they will obtain the mercy of bhava-bhakti.

The means by which ecstatic devotion is accomplished is the same as the means by which any stage of devotion is reached: by the practice of bhakti.Devotion begets devotion, bhaktyd sanjataya bhaktya.By the practice of sadhana-bhakti, bhava-bhaktimanifests in due course.

Since it is very rare, we shall not consider bhavathat is fortuned by a grace devoid of the desire for it. That kind of perfection is the exception, and we are concerned with the general case: perfection through sadhana.

Whether it is accomplished through practice or mercy, ecstatic devotion cannot be had without mercy. So when we speak of bhavasecured through sadhana,we actually mean bhavasecured through sadhanaand krpa.And while every form of mercy in every stage of sadhanais spiritual, the mercy by which the perfection of sadhanais accomplished is special, as inherent in the following definition of bhava-bhakti:

*suddha-sattva-visesatma*  
*prema-suryamsu-samya-bhak*  
*rucibhis citta-masrnya-*  
*krd asau bhava ucyate*

**“When devotional service is executed on the transcendental platform of pure goodness, it is like a sunray of love for Krsna. At such a time, devotional service causes the heart to be softened by various tastes, and one is then situated in bhava\[emotion\].”**

This “sunray of love” has been already described in the previous chapters as the spirited combination of a fundamental element of both the cognisance and pleasure potencies. While bhavaexists eternally within the heart, it has lain dormant. But now the active form of bhavafrom the heart of the Lord or from His associate actuates the dormant bhavaof the sadhana,and so suffuses his being with spiritual energy.

The following example, which has also been mentioned in Chapter Eight, is appropriate.

Fire is dormant in every piece of wood, but until that inner fire manifests, the wood cannot burn to create heat and light. However, when a burning stick contacts a length of wood, then the latter is quickly set alight.

The limitation of this example is that the fire which burns a length of wood quickly consumes the wood and hence itself. But once bhavaawakens within a devotee, it continues to burn as its own flame while simultaneously transforming into the flame of prṛḍṁ. In that way two flames of devotion burn within a devotee, the flame of bhavaand the flame of prema.Moreover, these flames are never extinguished, for they are fed by the fuel of bhakti,which is eternal and endless.

We quote Rupa Gosvami's description of the appearance of bhavaand Srila Prabhupada’s comment on it. The rasacaryawrites,

*sadhanabhinivesena krsna-tad-bhaktayos tatha*  
*prasadenati-dhanyanam bhavo dvedhabhijayate*  
*adyas tu prayikas tatra dvitiyo viralodayah*

**“Bhavaappears in very fortunate persons in two ways: by absorption in sadhana,or by the mercy of Krsna or His devotee. Its appearance by sadhanais normal, and its appearance by mercy is rare.”**

Srila Prabhupada elaborates on the term sadhanabhinivesena, “absorption in sadhana," as,

**“Constant association with pure devotees.”**

His summary study further says,

**“One can develop to the stage of ecstatic love simply by the association of pure devotees. It is essential, therefore, that one constantly associate with pure devotees who are engaged morning and evening in chanting the Hare Krsna mantra.In this way one will get the chance to purify his heart and develop this ecstatic pure love for Krsna.”**

The context in which Rupa Gosvami and Srila Prabhupada describe this path to bhavais the same. They give the example of Narada Muni, who as a boy constantly served, heard from, and associated with a group of great devotees camped near his home during the months of the rainy season. By their grace Narada became advanced in ecstatic devotion.

From this we can assume that Srila Prabhupada’s mandate of constantly associating with pure devotees includes the association of advanced devotees. The reason for this will be apparent shortly.

Krsna explains to Uddhava that a sadhakawho keeps company with pure devotees brings the Lord under his control. This extraordinary revelation would make clear to any practitioner intent on loving devotion that he must search out and revere the fellowship of advanced devotees. Indeed, no other form of yogaor spiritual practice can even come close to pleasing Krsna as much as the process He outlines below:

*na rodhayati mam yogo*  
*na sankhyam dharma eva ca*  
*na svadhyayas tapas tyago*  
*nesta-purtam na daksina*

*vratani yajnas chandamsi*  
*tirthani niyama yamah*  
*yathavarundhe sat-sangah*  
*sarva-sangapaho hi mam*

**“My dear Uddhava! By associating with My pure devotees one can destroy one’s attachment for all objects of material sense gratification. Such purifying association brings Me under the control of My devotee. One may perform the astanga-yogasystem, engage in philosophical analysis of the elements of material nature, practice non-violence and other ordinary principles of piety, chant the Vedas, perform penances, take to the renounced order of life, execute sacrificial performances and dig wells, plant trees and perform other public welfare activities, give in charity, carry out severe vows, worship the demigods, chant confidential mantras,visit holy places, or accept major and minor disciplinary injunctions, but even by performing such activities one does not bring Me under his control.”**

In commenting on these verses we shall concentrate only on the advantages of devotee association and not the shortcomings of the other disciplines mentioned.

It has already been established that bhaktiis the only way to please and attain Krsna.

The primary limb of sadhanais association with saints, for without it one can neither hear, chant, nor remember Krsna. By serving Krsna in the company of devotees a sadhakais doubly blessed, and as he advances to the goal, purified of all attachment, Krsna comes under his control. So much so that when a devotee tearfully begs the Lord for ecstatic devotion, the purchased Lord is obliged to give it. This is the meaning of the two synonyms, rodhayatiand auarundhe,which Krsna speaks to emphasise that keeping quality association “brings Him under control.”

It is well known that Krsna is reluctant to give a sadhakalove, although He may readily offer material opulences and liberation. Therefore it is imperative that the Lord be brought to a state of compliance where He feels obliged to give bhava-bhakta.

We may note that the control being spoken of here with words like rodhayatiis not total, absolute control over Krsna. That is only possible for the siddha,the devotee possessed of condensed prema.That kind of devotion has as one of its characteristic sri-krsnakarsini,which means that Krsna addicted to prema,thus it brings Him under the devotee’s control.

But the control of the sadhaka—either at sadhanaor bhava—is not as complete. It is a conditional and partial constraint over Krsna, and therefore a devotee cannot dictate the terms of Krsna’s compliance in awarding bhava.Nonetheless, it is very much a control to be desired and accomplished.

Some authorities are of the opinion that the same result can he achieved by going on pilgrimage or residing in holy places. Krsna, however, does not share that view. No doubt these practices are purifying, but not as quickly or effectively as service to pure devotees. Krsna says,

*na hy am-mayani tirthani*  
*na deva mrc-chila-mayah*  
*te punanty uru-kalena*  
*darsanad eva sadhavah*

**“Mere bodies of water are not the real sacred places of pilgrimage, nor are mere images of earth and stone the true worshipable deities. These purify one only after a long time, but saintly sages purify one immediately upon being seen.”**

The reader may be startled to learn that Krsna considers association with sadhusto be more potent than worshipping His deity form. Considering that Krsna is fully present in His deity, this may sound puzzling.

But the simple explanation is that in His deity form, Krsna does not generally move or talk. He chooses to be passive. By contrast a sadhuis pro-active, and with the sword of his instructions he cuts down the tangled weeds of a sadhaka’sbad habits and plants the seeds of love. In this way saints make the Lord more quickly available than even Krsna’s deity form.

Going back to the verse beginning with na rodhayati mam yogo, Lord Krsna makes control over Him conditional on “destroying one’s attachment for all objects of material sense gratification,” sarva-sangapahah.This, too, results from the influence of saints.

Part Five of this book described how a sadhakamust overcome the frailties that arise from fear, meaning bodily identification, before he can achieve the kind of attachment in which he thinks of Krsna as a friend or beloved. That kind of affection is only possible if the practitioner has a strong desire to serve Krsna in the way of the gopasor gopis.While anarthasand offences exert their influence, a devotee will generally worship Krsna along the path of

regulations, revering Him as the Supreme Personality of Godhead. When those obstacles are overcome, Krsna gives the intelligence to approach Him with intimacy, in the way of His eternal associates:

*ananya-mamata visnau*  
*mamata prema-samyuta*  
*bhaktir ity ucyate bhisma-*  
*prahladoddhava-naradaih*

**“When one develops an unflinching sense of ownership or possessiveness in relation to Lord Visnu, or, in other words, when one thinks Visnu and no one else to be the only object of love, such an awakening is called bhakti by exalted persons like Bhisma, Prahlada, Uddhava, and Narada.”**

A sadhakacultivates attachment in the wake of such love by meditating on Krsna’s Vraja pastimes to the accompaniment of the sankirtanaof His holy names.

While his devotion remains regulated, the sadhakameditates by effort on Krsna’s form, qualities, and pastimes. In time his nama-bhajanatransforms through stages from dhyanato the more advanced anusmrtiand samadhi,where he longs after the promise of prema-sankirtana.Chanting with intense longing will be the means for achieving bhava,by which he realises the confidential truths of Krsna and His pleasure potency. This much has already been said. But here is a further, and key, point:

Such spiritual excellence can only be accomplished under the tutelage of experienced Vaisnavas who are very dear to Krsna.

Narada tells his ward Gopa-kumara:t

*ad-eka-rasa-lokasya*  
*sange ’bhivyaktatam svatah*  
*prayasyad api tad vastu*  
*gopaniyam prayatnatah*

**“In the company of people whose only taste is for devotional service in pure love, that love appears of its own accord. Yet one must try hard to keep it concealed.”**

Narada instructs Gopa-kumara that the most effective way to achieve love is to keep company with those devotees who know its value and so have no other goal in life. Association with devotees means association with first-class devotees, uttama-adhikaris,for it is they who have the power to stimulate premain an aspirant’s heart. This was the case with Narada, who was so fortunate as to be blessed with the service of Bhaktivedantas.

The verse above concludes with a warning to the novice in love: keep your love hidden. In his own commentary Sanatana Gosvami cites a proverb, gopayet matr-jara-vat:

**“One should keep premahidden, just as one would conceal the affairs of one’s mother with a paramour.”**

The humble conduct of a devotee is to conceal his attainments. Here premarefers to bhava,because only this immature stage of love can be controlled. Once it matures fully, there is no controlling prema.

\* \* \* \*

The Vedic tradition is to offer children from the age of six an opportunity for intense companionship and training through residence in the asramaof the village guru.This practice is less about academic learning and more about spiritual advancement. It is a timeless cultural norm established by Krsna with the purpose of qualifying the more perceptive sections of society for His ultimate mercy, thereby fulfilling the mission of the human form of life. Unfortunately, this tradition has been more or less lost, being replaced by academic education and a sensual environment that is the least likely place to find the mercy of the Lord.

Srila Prabhupada established iskcon as a means to again offer the opportunity to keep company with pure devotees, and to even reside with them. On occasion His Divine Grace emphasised the superiority of in-residence training, one of its obvious advantages being the opportunity to more quickly procure Krsna’s grace. The following humorous exchange during a morning walk is an example:

**\[Devotee\] “Srila Prabhupada, is it faster if one lives in the temple and goes on the sankirtanaparty. Is it faster?”**

**\[Srila Prabhupada\] “That depends on him. Even in the temple, if his mind is in a different subject matter, then how it will help him?”**

**“The temple authorities like to preach that anyone who’s living outside the temple is going to hell.”**

**“Generally!”**

**“But even devotees who are following. They like to preach that.”**

**“No, that is not. That is not. Just like even in ordinary business, if you transact business in the stock association, you get good business. And outside the stock association you don’t get. Because association is there, there are many purchaser and many seller. So if you have to sell, you get immediate purchaser. And if you have to purchase, there is immediate seller. That is... Therefore the stock exchange is there. That is the way, that if we live together in the stock exchange of devotional service, then you can help me; I can help you. So our business will go on nicely. And outside the market, you can live three hundred miles away from the stock exchange. You will not get so many business. Like that.”**

**“You’ll miss the opportunities?”**

**“Yes! Therefore it is helpful. If you want to do business, you must take the first opportunity, the greatest opportunity, do your business. That is intelligence. And if we think, ‘All right, I shall do slowly. In seven hundred lives I shall become perfect,’ that is another thing.”**

**“It is riskier to stay outside.”**

**“Oh, yes! Otherwise why you are opening so many centres and making arrangement that ‘We shall provide you with shelter, with food. These are the facilities. You live here, do whatever is your capacity. Don’t sleep, but work.’ This is our teaching. Satam prasangat,this is also, and Rupa Gosvami says, sato vrtteh sadhu-sange sadbhir bhaktih prasidhyati,‘If you live with the association of sadhu,devotee, then it will be quickly fruitful. And if you live with these ordinary men, then whatever you have got will be finished very soon. There is another verse. It is said there that it is preferred to live within the cage surrounded by fire than to live with the non-devotees. It is preferred.”**

For many reasons—some good, most bad—asramatraining has seriously thinned out in the Society. The result may be that its members will find the ascent through quality sadhanato bhava more difficult and more elusive. Time will tell!

However, Krsna’s method of spiritual advancement is not in need of modernisation, and so it is incumbent upon serious practitioners to seek quality association. It is the only way to rise above the modes of nature and to enter the liberated stage of love.

Narada emphasises this truth to Gopa-kumara:

*nidanam tu param premnah*  
*sri-krsna-karuna-bharah*  
*kasyapy udety akasmad va*  
*kasyacit sadhana-kramat*

**“But the prime cause of pure love for Sri Krsna is Krsna’s full mercy, which in someone may arise spontaneously and in someone else by gradual practice of devotional service.”**

Following the principle of bhaktya sanjataya bhaktya, bhava-bhakti cannot come from practice alone. It must come from a repository of bhava-bhakti.While the treasuries of love include Krsna Himself, His name, His deity, His associates, and bhakti itself, the advantage of sadhu-sangais that Vaisnavas are known to he among the most merciful spiritual benefactors. For that reason, they are likened to and revered as desire trees and oceans of mercy, vancha-kalpatarubhyas ca krpa-sindhubhya eva ca.

Among Vaisnavas, the initiating guruand the instructing gurus are the natural shelters to whom disciples look for spiritual nourishment and emancipation.

For practitioners who are fixed in sadhanait is imperative that they receive guidance from an experienced and realised guru.Such an advanced Vaisnava must be able to guide his dependant through the nuances of bhajanafrom dhyanato samadhi.And when the acaryasees his ward is fully qualified and eager for bhava,he must be able to bless him with his desired aspiration.

The greatly learned Sri Prabuddha described a spiritual master in these terms:

*tasmad gurum prapadyeta*  
*jijnasuh sreya uttamam*  
*sabde pare ca nisnatam*  
*brahmany upasamasrayam*

**“Therefore, any person who seriously desires real happiness must seek a bona fide spiritual master and take shelter of him by initiation. The qualification of the bona fide guruis that he has realised the conclusions of the scriptures by deliberation and is able to convince others of these conclusions. Such great personalities, who have taken shelter of the Supreme Godhead, leaving aside all material considerations, should be understood to be bona fide spiritual masters.”**

The word prapadyeta,“one should take shelter of,” is an impel ative from the same verbal root as prapatti,and indicates that association is not a social affair but that of a continual process of increased surrender to which a sadhakais obliged. And of course, a disciple must be inquisitive, jijnasuh,in order to both prompt and encourage the spiritual master to reveal what he knows, and what the disciple should know.

A disciple should know that the highest good, sreya uttamam, loving devotion, exists, and the gurushould have realised the same. The basis of such realisation is deep knowledge of scripture, sabde, and the truth regarding the Supreme Lord, pare.Needless to say, a qualified spiritual master should be above worldly temptation. How could he confer bhavaon anyone if his heart is full of affection for the impermanent?

And this is the crux of the matter:

**A gurucan only give what he has.**

We have mentioned earlier that Bhaktivinoda Thakura has writ ten that the premi-bhaktahas unlimited power and can bestow his power to another, just as the bhava-bhaktacan bestow his level of attainment or any stage of devotion preceding but not succeeding it. This advanced sadhakacan even bestow taste on a pious non-devotee. However, one still practising sadhanacan only give-faith in and enthusiasm for the stages of sadhana.The acarya has taught that this is how devotional energy is bestowed by one Vaisnava upon another.

In consideration of the above, the ideal spiritual master is the eternally liberated associate of Krsna, or a Vaisnava who has attained loving devotion by ardent effort. These are the uttama-adhikaris who are referred to in the verse above.

However, all gurusmay not be on the topmost level of devotion. And this may very well be the case in a preaching organisation like iskcon. Unfortunately, history has shown that some gurus have fallen down and thus revealed that they were not upasama- asrayam,“fixed in detachment from material affairs.”

These events have weakened the faith of some and fostered misconceptions in others, the most inane deviation being the posthumous rtviktheory.

Srila Prabhupada has written that a lower grade, vulnerable Vaisnava may act as guru,and Vaisnava history attests to that. When Srila Prabhupada’s passing was imminent, he had no alternative but to risk that some of his appointed guruswere still carrying a lot of karma.It was not ideal, but it was the pressing reality. This compromise to the ideal was expressed by Srila Prabhupada in a commentary in The Nectar of Instruction:

**“One should not become a spiritual master unless he has attained the platform of uttama-adhikari.A neophyte Vaisnava or a Vaisnava situated on the intermediate platform can also accept disciples, but such disciples must be on the same platform, and it should be understood that they cannot advance very well toward the ultimate goal of life under his insufficient guidance. Therefore a disciple should be careful to accept an uttama-adhikarias a spiritual master.”**

The obvious question that arises is:

**“If my diksa-gurudoes not have bhava,how will I get it?”**

The answer is:

**“If you are qualified for bhava,Krsna will make arrangement for you to get it.”**

Yet a devotee must be faithful to the path of sadhu-sanga,and his surrender to his pure devotee spiritual master—whatever his level of attainment—should match the description given by saint Prabuddha:

*tatra bhagavatan dharman*  
*siksed gurv-atma-daivatah*  
*amayayanuvrttya yais*  
*tusyed atmatma-do harih*

**“Accepting the bona fide spiritual master as one’s life and soul and worshipable deity, the disciple should learn from him the process of pure devotional service. The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Hari, the soul of all souls, is inclined to give Himself to His pure devotees. Therefore, the disciple should learn from the spiritual master to serve the Lord without duplicity and in such a faithful and favourable way that the Supreme Lord, being satisfied, will offer Himself to the faithful disciple.”**

The sage says that it is the duty of the disciple to serve his guruin such a faithful way that Krsna will offer Himself, atma-dah.The implication of this statement is that the loyalty of an advanced disciple to a guru,who is himself loyal to a self-realised soul, will inspire Krsna to award bhavato the disciple, somehow or another.

There are many alternatives left to Krsna to fulfil the promise that He will not disappoint the sincere sadhaka.In this important verse He reassures us:

*ananyas cintayanto mam*  
*ye janah paryupasate*  
*tesam nityabhiyuktanam*  
*yoga-ksemam vahamy aham*

**“But those who always worship Me with exclusive devotion, meditating on My transcendental form—to them I carry what they lack, and I preserve what they have.”**

At this a reader may ask:

**“How will Krsna bestow His mercy?”**

**“As He best sees fit! Through a siksa-guru,His holy name, His deity, He Himself, or an unseen agent who has been deputed to guard over the sadhaka.”**

But without a douht, when a devotee is qualified for it, Krsna will ensure that His devotee will attain that upon which his heart is set.

And to an obvious question from readers:

**“Can a devotee receive bhavafrom Srila Prabhupada?”**

The answer is:

**“Of course! He is after all the guardian of his Krsna consciousness movement.”**

For his initiated disciples, Srila Prabhupada will most assuredly be the deliverer of prema.Be that as it may, Srila Prabhupada and Krsna cannot be ordered on the means of a devotee’s deliverance. There are many alternatives, which include the aforementioned unseen guardians.

Sanatana Gosvami writes of these unseen agents of deliverance. When the Vaikuntha messengers met Gopa-kumara in the realm of liberation, they gave him many good instructions. Seeing that the boy was doubtful about his ability to apply the many teachings needed to attain his worshipable deity, Madana-gopala, the Vaikuntha-dutas then reassured him that he was not alone on his journey:

*bhakti-prabhavena vicara-jataih*  
*sanjayamanena sadedrsais tvam*  
*vighnati-vighnan kila jesyasiha*  
*sarvatra te hanta vayam sahayah*

**“By the power of bhaktiyou will have many realisations, time and again, and for certain you will conquer your most formidable obstacles. In all circumstances, be assured, we are your helpers.”**

In his commentary Sanatana Gosvami says the Vaikuntha-dutas reassured Gopa-kumara that wherever he went and whatever challenges he faced, the boy would not be alone. The servants of the Lord would accompany him everywhere, they would help resolve every philosophical problem he could not unravel, and help him overcome every stumbling block in his way.

This reassurance was given long after Gopa-kumara had met his diksa-guru,but before his repeated meetings with Narada.

Was Narada the guardian the Vaikuntha messengers were refer ring to, or were there others? Narada and Uddhava were certainly indispensable in resolving Gopa-kumara’s dilemmas. While we are not told more of the spiritual guardians, the words of the Vaikuntha-dutas did not prove false. Gopa-kumara was successful in his quest, and when he needed help he received it from one quarter or another.

We, too, should have faith that in His own wise way, Krsna will ensure that a sincere sadhakawill, like Gopa-kumara, always attain the result of his devotion.

\* \* \* \*

Having spoken at length about the spiritual master, something must be said about the qualification of the disciple. It is not appropriate to solely emphasise the guru’squalification. The sadhakamust be willing, able, and qualified to achieve bhava.

The verse previously mentioned beginning with tatra bhagavatan dharmandescribes the qualification of the disciple. Eligibility for the mercy of Krsna and gurucannot be underestimated, and a lack of advancement in sadhana,or the inaccessibility of bhava, need not be the shortcoming of the guru.Even if they are, unless those shortcomings are severe, a disciple should look to himself for faults. That attitude of humility is what pleases Krsna, the ultimate benefactor.

In commenting on the verse, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura says that even if a disciple has the most advanced spiritual master, if he harbours desires for sense enjoyment or if he is a speculator, he will not advance in sadhana,what to speak of to life’s goal. The disciple’s qualification is that he must be without deceit, amaya.

On the other hand, if a student is simple-hearted and truly accepts his guruas his atma-daivatah,his very life and worshipable deity, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati writes,

“There is absolutely no impediment to the transmission of perfect knowledge and bliss in the devotional service of the Lord.”

To fully avail himself of the company of pure devotees and of his spiritual masters, a Vaisnava must he learned, must serve peers and superiors, and must cultivate the moods of devotion.

Learning does not mean extensive scriptural erudition. It does mean reading at least Srila Prabhupada’s four main compositions and knowing their contents. A devotee serious about transcending the modes of nature must understand the science of pure devotion, the sword that severs the bonds that bind him.

The external aspects of practice are literally the tip of the iceberg.

For example, the numerical aspect of japahas a significant and corresponding internal cultivation that is based on the activities of the antah-karana,the internal senses: the mind, intelligence, and ego. How to control these, how to purify them, how to make them instruments in perfecting nama-sankirtana?These are part of the teachings of Srimad-Bhagavatam.By applying these teachings, a devotee is faithful to Krsna’s repeated request, man-mana:

**“Always think of Me.”**

And to be blessed with bhava,a sadhakamust not only think of Krsna always, but be obsessed by Him, by Sri Radha, by Their associates.

But the vast storehouse of transcendental knowledge contained in Vaisnava texts ultimately concludes in service. The Vraja-vasis are simple villagers whose lives are based on serving Krsna with their skills, belongings, bodies, and hearts.

The eleven bhavasthat define an associate of Krsna may be categorised as their spiritual foundations, their personal services, and their physical attributes. While these characteristics are attained by devotion laced with knowledge, and while they reflect unlimited wisdom and cognisance, erudition itself is not their main manifest trait. Indeed, all eleven bhavashave service, and the mood of service, as their common foundation and purpose.

Since the stage of perfection is revealed through service and through a service attitude, sadhana-bhaktimust feature those same characteristics. Srila Prabhupada would summarise this culture of devotion with the phrase “service and surrender.”

Service means active engagement, and surrender means the favourable moods which makes external activities palatable and pleasing to Krsna.

As a devotee becomes increasingly proficient in service and surrender, his accumulated knowledge becomes correspondingly real ised. And when he transcends the modes of nature, he develops as the personification of knowledge, service, and surrender.

Preceding chapters described a special feature of the mood of devotion, the mood of separation. And humility is the root of vipralambha.

When a devotee feels himself unworthy of Krsna’s mercy, he is able to cry after his Lord. In his tears, a devotee feels him self increasingly distanced from Krsna, a distance that adds to his humility and again deepens his feelings of separation. In this heartbreaking situation, the sadhaka’sonly solace is in incessant nama-sankirtanaand endless thoughts of the Divine Couple’s pas times in the groves of Vraja.

To express his pain, the advanced devotee shares songs of separation composed by great Vaisnavas like Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami. Giving vent to his sorrow offers a ray of hope that his worshipable deity Sri Radha will take notice and answer his plea.

The devotee prays,

*asa-bharair amrta-sindbu-mayaih kathancit*  
*kalo mayati-gamitah kila sampratam hi*  
*tvam cet krpam mayi vidhasyasi naiva kim me*  
*pranair vrajena ca varoru bakarinapi*

**“O Varoru! Somehow, I have spent my time aspiring after oceans of nectar, but if You are not merciful to me, then of what use are life itself, residence in Vraja, or even Krsna Himself?”**

Through the magic of hearing Krsna’s pastimes, the sadhakainherits the legacy of his predecessors, thinking,

**“One day, I too shall enter into these pastimes of wonder.”**

That which is not obtained by brahma or Siva is the sadhaka's ardent hope, a hope that is nurtured by the promise of the acaryas and the sweet vibrations of nama-sankirtana.
