The spiritual science of meeting and separation should be known, and when it is, then devotees can begin to incorporate vipralambhainto their nama-bhajana.That is the mood of chanting, and the only mood of chanting acceptable for the followers of Caitanya Mahaprabhu.

Chapter Thirty-four is dedicated to Caitanya Mahaprabhu as the personification of vipralambha.Although Krsna and Gaura are the same original Supreme Personality of Godhead, the former enjoys pastimes of meeting with Radha, and the latter is absorbed in the mood of Radha separated from Krsna. When Krsna appeared, He wanted people to learn the confidential, spontaneous love with which the Vraja-vasis worshipped Him. However, He was misunderstood, and those who became His devotees worshipped Him with awe and reverence instead of spontaneous love. Therefore in His appearance as Caitanya Mahaprabhu, Krsna assumed the role of a devotee Who personally taught the world how to love Krsna. Of course the means for people’s salvation was nama-sankirtana. hut in addition to the mantrasof Krsna’s names, in His Siksastaka verses Lord Caitanya taught vipralambhaas the mood with which His followers should chant nama-sankirtana.The conclusion, therefore, is that a devotee’s nama-bhajanashould follow the guidance of the verses of Siksastaka.By such smaranaa devotee will eventually awaken all transcendental truths, free himself of all impiety, and perceive the eightfold pastimes enacted within his purified heart.

The following chapter, Thirty-five, describes how practising devotees can cultivate the vipralambhamood, which Srila Prabhupada so much emphasised to his followers. That cultivation begins by understanding the truths of service in separation and how, even though appearing as suffering, vipralambhais actually the source of greatest pleasure. In the beginning a devotee may understand vipralambhaas the chasm that exists between himself in the material world and Krsna in the spiritual world. This is more an intellectually-invoked separation. But as he makes progress in sadhana,the practitioner becomes attached to Krsna, and his sense of being separated from Him actually transforms into the pain that a lover feels in separation from his beloved. Crucial to cultivating these feelings of separation is to read pastimes of separation as enacted by the Vraja-vasis and Caitanya Mahaprabhu. Equally relevant are those books and songs in which great devotees express their pains of sorrow. The primary attainment of vipralambha-seva is that it mysteriously increases attachment to Krsna, and when that attachment matures to real love, then it attracts Krsna into the devotee’s presence and becomes the cause of meeting with Him.

Chapter Thirty-six is entitled “The Perfection of Separation,” and it is a continuation of the previous chapter. Herein we further study the way in which service in separation increases love for Krsna, and we hear of the mula-mantra,the root mantra,for separation which was thus spoken by Madhavendra Puri: “O My Lord! Î most merciful master! Î master of Mathura! When shall I see You again? Because of My not seeing You, My agitated heart has become unsteady. Î most beloved one, what shall I do now?” And as we explore the world of love in separation from Krsna we discover that vipralambhais not only directed to the son of Nanda Maharaja, but to Krsna’s other associates. Among those associates, the one whose company Gaudiya-Vaisnavas most long for is Srimati Radharani. She is Krsna’s feminine counterpart, and more often than not, Gaudiya Vaisnavas envisage their eternal service to Krsna as being a maidservant of Radha. Thus, in addition to many other services to Radha, when Krsna is distant from Vrndavana a perfected devotee can assuage Radha’s sorrow by singing songs about meetings with Krsna.

\* \* \* \*

Part Eight, “Sankalpa for Divine Grace,” studies in the early chapters what saints and scriptures have disclosed about the mysteries of divine grace, and explores the descent of divine grace upon devotees and non-devotees; the chapters attempt to put into words the sublime realisations that transpire during the fulfilment of the purpose of sadhana-bhakti,as realised by the grace of Vaisnavas, and examine the power of the holy name to manifest bhava.

Chapter Thirty-seven introduces the final sankalpaof this book, which is dedicated to paving the steps a devotee must make through sadhanato bhava.Unlike all other sankalpasthat a devotee takes, this final step into transcendence is not within his power. In the way that a traveller may walk a great distance to his destination, upon arrival when he knocks on the door, it must be the residents who open it. Similarly, it is Krsna or His associates who give entrance to bhava,and that is called mercy or divine grace. In this chapter we emphasise that a devotee must have a very clear picture of the abhidheya,or the means to his attainment, as well as of the prayojana,or the attainment itself. The two must be in harmony, and as a sadhakacultivates the stages of smarana,especially beyond dhyana,the affection that he cultivates for Krsna must correspond to the bhavahe covets. It is obvious to Gaudiyas that love for Krsna is their goal, but there must be more specifics about what krsna-premameans! And as it turns out, krsna-prema is the unwedded love for adolescent Krsna in Vrndavana, which, as explained in the previous chapter, is best expressed and most pleasing to Him when offered through His associates, foremost of whom is Srimati Radharani.

But what more exactly is divine grace? Chapter Thirty-eight describes mercy as a transformation of consciousness which occurs when the suffering of another person touches one’s own heart. Thus when the plaintive cries of a sadhakaeager for confidential service to Krsna move the Lord’s heart to the extent that He accepts that devotee into His spiritual family, grace has been granted. But to move Krsna, a devotee must have a clearly defined attachment for Him, and even then, Krsna does not immediately respond, because when He awards the devotee bhava,He awards the means by which He comes under that devotee’s control. Thus Krsna is very thorough in testing His devotee. There are many truths associated with divine grace. The most relevant to the sadhaka'squest is that although Krsna does not feel the suffering of the non-devotee, He does feel the pain of the devotee. Krsna feels the devotee’s pain because He and His devotee are connected by the mutually pervasive potency of bhakti.Krsna’s bhakti-saktimakes Him experience the sorrow a sadhakafeels separated from Him and from love for Him. But the question is: does the practitioner feel a separation intense enough to move Krsna? Attaining such an intense attachment is the practitioner’s goal.

Chapter Thirty-nine goes into further depth on the process by which a devotee actually attains Krsna’s mercy. In short, Krsna’s mercy comes through His devotees. While there are other means by which Krsna may award divine grace, such as directly Himself, His long-standing rule is that His representatives are given the independent power of attorney to distribute bhavato whom they see lit, as and when they see fit. Of the devotees most instrumental in this dispensation are the diksa-and siksa-gurus,and in our Krsna consciousness movement, Srila Prabhupada. Because the blessings of love can be transmitted through instructions, devotees who attentively follow the instructions of Srila Prabhupada, be they his direct initiates or not, may attain his divine grace. However, devotees must be ideal disciples, and among the qualities that Krsna and His representatives look for in a practitioner is atma-daivata, accepting the spiritual master as one’s very life and worshipable deity. When Krsna’s representative is pleased, then either through instructions, blessings, a darsana,or from within the heart, he manifests bhavain the devotee. In this way the love in the heart of the guru,actuated by feelings of compassion, mercifully actuates bhavain the heart of the disciple. Thus, once again we see in action the principle, bhaktibegets bhakti.

The final chapter of the book is Chapter Forty. Finally the devotee attains the goal for which he strived for many years, perhaps many lifetimes. And while much can be said about the glories of bhava-bhakti,the most compelling truth to be emphasised in this closing is that it is not attained without effort. This book is about the relenting effort required to hone the quality and quantity of one’s bhakti,in tandem with the desire to accomplish its perfection. Sadhana-bhaktiis not a lazy man’s business. And Srila Prabhupada’s request to chant a minimum of sixteen rounds is not a minimum achievement. It means: chant sixteen rounds of pure japa,while aspiring in separation for the devotion of the Vraja-vasis,with some, if not complete, feelings of spontaneity born of greed. It may sound like a tall order, but actually that is the minimum. And for devotees dedicated to this goal, grace in the form of help from their guardians, seen and unseen, is assured. And so, too, is assured the darsanaof his worshipable deities, Radha-Krsna in the groves of Vraja. Krsna’s stated practice is that He will, as He did with Narada, give His audience once to the bhava-bhakta,and no more. That one audience will then make the devotee mad with desire to continue sankalpason the path of love, something akin to, but different from, the way that he did in sadhana.And so his devotion grows, and continues to grow even once love and eternal mellow have been attained. After all, the law of bhaktiis that bhaktibegets bhakti,eternally.

## Afterword and Appendices

## Afterword

At the conclusion of His teachings to Rupa Gosvami, Caitanya Mahaprabhu said,

*bhavite bhavite krsna sphuraye antare*  
*krsna-krpaya ajna paya rasa-sindhu-pare*

**“When one thinks of Krsna constantly, love for Him manifests within the heart. Even though one may be ignorant, one can reach the far shore of the ocean of transcendental love by Lord Krsna’s mercy.”**

I have also reached the conclusion of Sankalpa-kaumudi,no doubt with less clarity, conclusiveness, and potency than the Lord to Rupa. In re-reading the manuscript for editing purposes, I found many places where I could have clarified points further, and been more conclusive in both structure and presentation. The book being long enough as it is, and the author, his editor, and co-workers worn out enough as it is, I resisted any additions other than the required corrections.

But more could have been added! I will refrain from listing what that extra content would have been for fear of a lengthy Afterword. My hope is that the time invested in this book was worthwhile, and that readers consider it an asset to their Krsna consciousness and to their nama-bhajana.As with the completion of all of my books, I feel that I have been edified. As Kaviraja Gosvami writes,

**“Whether I know it or know not, it is for self-purification that I write this book.”**

And composing this book has certainly been an educational and purificational process. Like Suddha-bhakti-cintamani,this book was a from-the-ground-up project in terms of concept, structure, and referencing. This kind of undertaking is much different from writing Sri Damodara-janani,for example, wherein the concept and structure are already set by the verses of Srimad-Bhagavatam, and commentators provide most references. In short, Sankalpa kaumudiis much more difficult a composition than was Sri Damodara-janani,and perhaps a better learning experience for me.

If we look back to the verse quoted, we see that Caitanya Mahaprabhu indicates that reaching love for Krsna is a step-by-step pro cess, bhavite bhavite.This book has attempted to present those steps. However, my goal has not been the far side of the ocean of mellows, but the near side, which I take to be bhava-bhakti,the bud of prema.

For a determined and adept sadhana,ecstatic devotion is a goal attainable in this life. Meanwhile, mature premais the goal for the next life, and Goloka-Vrndavana is the final destination in the life after that—the last life, eternal life.

Let me repeat: “Bhavais attainable in this life!” This is my conviction and aspiration, and this was Srila Prabhupada’s expectation of his followers. Moreover, for practitioners Rupa Gosvami defined practice in terms of its goal, bhava.In today’s iskcon, the extremes of faint-hearted sadhanato miracles by divine grace often take precedence over the acquisition of transcendental knowledge and the hard work required to put that knowledge to practice. The attainment of bhavais possible, but not through wishful thinking. It is possible in this life by the grace of guru,Srila Prabhupada, Caitanya Mahaprabhu, and a very determined and systematic approach to sadhana-bhakti.

We must be determined—very determined.

An anonymous source once said,

**“The greatest oak tree was once a little nut who held its ground.”**

And Thomas Edison said,

**“The most certain way to succeed is always to try just one more time.”**

And finally, our Srila Prabhupada wrote,

**“In executing penance, one must be determined to return home, back to Godhead, and must decide to undergo all types of tribulations for that end. Even for material prosperity, name, and fame, one has to undergo severe types of penance, otherwise no one can become an important figure in this material world. Why, then, are there severe types of penance for the perfection of devotional service? An easy-going life and attainment of perfection in transcendental realisation cannot go together. The Lord is more clever than any living entity; therefore He wants to see how painstaking the devotee is in devotional service. The order is received from the Lord, either directly or through the bona fide spiritual master, and to execute that order, however painstaking, is the severe type of penance. One who follows the principle rigidly is sure to achieve success in attaining the Lord’s mercy.”**

This evening of Radhastami, 2020, on the occasion of the appearance of Srimati Radharani, and as the sun sets over the horizon of Krsna Valley, I have completed Sankalpa-kaumudi.I owe my inspiration for this book to Srila Sanatana Gosvami and his Sri Brhad-bhagavatamrta.I pray that I have done justice to the concept of sankalpa,which he has described directly and indirectly. Finally I offer my respectful obeisances at the lotus feet of my divine spiritual master, Om Visnupada 108 Sri Srimad Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada. It is only by his hard work and mercy that I chant Krsna’s holy names and aspire for the bhava-bhaktaof which I have so profusely written of in this book for the benefit of his followers. May His Divine Grace be pleased with this humble effort.

Radhastami 2020

Krsna Valley, Hungary

Sivarama Swami

## Appendix One

**Use Of The Word Adhikari**

(This appendix follows from the study on a devotee’s qualification as discussed in Part One, Chapter Three.)

The term adhikarameans eligibility, and adhikarimeans one who is eligible. The first section of Chapter Three elaborated on the eligibility of devotees for practicing devotional service. The second section was a study of the levels of attainment in devotion achieved by devotees, as described by the sage Havi in Srimad-Bhagavatam.

Caitanya Mahaprabhu instructs Sanatana Gosvami about these two topics—qualification for bhaktiaccording to knowledge and faith, and advancement in bhaktiaccording to attachment and love.

It may well be asked why these two distinct characteristics— qualification and attainment—are identified by the same nomenclature, adhikari.

Bhaktivinoda Thakura, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati, and Srila Prabhupada employed this convention. However, earlier acaryas like Jiva Gosvami and Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura used, for attainment, the different nomenclature bhagavataor bhakta,meaning “devotee.”

Still, adhikariis also a suitable term for defining levels of attainment because it describes the qualification for individuals for being known as a devotee based upon the development of their attraction to Krsna. This convention is further confirmed when we examine the original question posed by King Nimi, in response to which Navayogendra Sri Havi then defines the three levels of devotees:

*atha bhagavatam bruta*  
*yad-dharmo yadrso nrnam*  
*yathacarati yad brute*  
*yair lingair bhagavat-priyah*

**“Now please tell me in greater detail about the devotees of the Supreme Lord. What are the natural symptoms by which I can distinguish between the most advanced devotees, those on the middle level, and those who are neophytes? What are the typical religious activities of a Vaisnava, and how does he speak? Specifically, please describe those symptoms and characteristics by which Vaisnavas become dear to the Supreme Personality of Godhead.”**

The word lingaihin this verse means “by visible symptoms,” which in the context of the question can be restated as “the gradations of eligibility by which devotees are favoured by Krsna.”

To this question the sage Havi then describes uttama, madhyama, and kanisthadevotees according to their level of spiritual advance ment. Therefore, designating these devotees as adhikarisis com pletely consistent with the question posed by the king.

In summary, we see that it is reasonable to use the word adhikari, like the word bhagavata,to indicate the spiritual advancement of Vaisnavas.

That said, it must be admitted that using the term adhikariwithout a clear contextual reference may lend to confusion.

For example, in the statement “That devotee is a madbyama-adbikari,”we do not know whether the devotee in question is a madhyama-adhikariby faith and knowledge for bhakti,or a madhyama-adhikariby an intermediate degree of attraction to Krsna.

However, when the word usage is qualified, then there is no confusion:

**“That devotee is a madhyama-adhikariby qualification for devotion.”**

In Srila Prabhupada’s teachings, the use of adhikariis generally well defined and almost always refers to devotees’ spiritual advancement.

An example where Srila Prabhupada uses adhikariin both ways is in the purport to Sri Upadesamrta 5.After citing verses from Srimad-Bhagavatam on devotee attainment, His Divine Grace quotes some of Lord Caitanya’s teachings on qualification. And in both cases the contextual use of adhikariis clear.

Another example is in the Prema-vivartaof Jagadananda Pandita, wherein the author denotes the three stages of devotees’ advancement with the word adhikari.The following verses define the uttama-adhikari:

*uttamadhikarira aropera nahi sthana*  
*manase aprakrta tattvera paya ta’sandhana*  
*premera udaya haya prema-chakse heri’*  
*pranesvara bhaje purva-aropa dura kari’*

**“Experts \[uttama-adhikaris\] do not practise ascription, they directly perceive spiritual reality within their hearts. Divine love arises in them, and they begin to see with the eyes of that love. They serve the Lord of their heart and give up their previous practice of ascription.”**

Similarly, in contemporary Vaisnava parlance the use of adhikariis generally unqualified and mostly refers to eligibility by attachment; in other words, it refers to devotee’s spiritual advancement.

In this book, when the use of adhikariis not explicitly defined, it is also meant to indicate spiritual advancement.

A final aspect of this topic should be settled, and that is: do the three levels—kanistha, madhyama,and uttama—of the two kinds of adhikdri—eligibility and advancement—correspond?

The answer is “No!” there is no correspondence between the two.

The primary evidence to support our answer is that Caitanya Mahaprabhu described eligibility and advancement separately, making no correlation between the two. Neither, to the best of our knowledge, is any such correlation described by any acarya.

Srila Prabhupada also cites Bhaktivinoda Thakura on the three kinds of qualification for bhakti,and then prior to introducing the topic of levels of advancement he writes,

**“The standard of devotion is also categorised in the same way \[kanistha, madhyama, uttama\].”**

In this way he indicates that the two adhikarisdo not correspond.

Further evidence may be seen by comparing two adhikaris.

Rupa Gosvami identifies Bilvamangala Thakura as a madhyama-adhikari by attachment. However, it is well known that the Thakura was transcendentally situated on the platform of bhava. It would therefore be erroneous to say that his qualification for bhaktiwas intermediate, since devotees at bhavaare fully situated in knowledge, are beyond the four defects, and have deep, unshakeable faith. In other words, if anything, they have superlative qualification for bhakti.

Similarly, devotees who have attained premacannot be uttama- adhikarisby eligibility. Being siddhasin devotion, they cannot simultaneously be candidates for the same. Thus there is no correlation between the two uttama-adhikaris.This is clear when we compare the definition of first class qualification with the definition of a perfected devotee as given below:

*avijnatakhila-klesah*  
*sada krsnasrita-kriyah*  
*siddhah syuh santata-prema-*  
*saukhyasvada-parayanah*

**“Those who experience no suffering at all, who perform all actions while taking shelter of Krsna, and who always taste the happiness of continuous premaare known as the perfected devotees.”**

This concludes a brief analysis of the use of the word adhikari in relation to qualification and attainment, as well as reasoning why the three divisions of the two do not correspond. Finally, a reminder to the reader that in this book, the unqualified use of the word adhikariwill denote spiritual advancement.

## Appendix Two

**Review of Krsna’s Potencies**

(This appendix gives a brief overview of the potencies of the Lord as discussed in Part Two, Chapter Six)

This appendix is a brief review of Krsna’s potencies as they relate to the development of bhava.While many of these terms are defined in the book, their inter-relationship and hierarchy may not be readily perceivable. For the sake of clarity we offer this short summary.

Both srutiand smrtiscriptures describe Krsna as the master of unlimited potencies, a truth the great authority Brahma confirms in this statement:

*tvam adir anto bhuvanasya madhyam*  
*ananta-saktim purusam yam ahuh*  
*kalo bhavan aksipatisa visvam*  
*sroto yathantah patitam gabhiram*

**“O my Lord! You are the beginning, the manifestation, and the ultimate dissolution of the three worlds, and You are celebrated in the Vedas as the reservoir of unlimited potencies, the Supreme Person. O my Lord! As waves attract branches and leaves that have fallen into deep water, You, the supreme eternal time factor, attract everything in this universe.”**

The totality of these unlimited potencies, ananta-sakti,is grouped under the common name “internal potency,” which is also called cit-sakti, svarupa-sakti, antaranga-sakti, or visuddha-sattva.In short these names indicate the Lord’s total spiritual power, which is unlimited and eternal.

In order to manifest a variety of states and to realise that tin- completeness of the Absolute Truth must display existences eternal and temporary, unlimited and limited, the svarupa-saktiacts temporarily as the material energy, called maya-sakti,and limitedló as the living entities, the jivas,also known as the tatastha-saktior marginal potency.

Although the living entity is also spiritual, he is very minute, an infinitesimal particle of svarupa-sakti, called cit-kana. If not under the shelter of the spiritual potency, the jivaidentifies with the temporary maya-sakti,and in that unconstitutional state, suffers.

The svarupa-saktihas three primary subdivisions, which combine in many ways to achieve the Lord’s purposes. Kaviraja Gosvami says,

**“Hladiniis His aspect of bliss; sandhini,of eternal existence; and samvit,of cognisance, which is also accepted as knowledge.”**

A brief review of the constituents of these three potencies and their effects on Krsna and His devotees is instructive:

**The essence of hladiniis love of Krsna, the essence of love is emotion, bhava—which is different from the stage of bhava—and the ultimate expression of emotion is mahabhava.The hladini-sakti gives pleasure to Krsna and His eternal associates, and its material aspect gives happiness to conditioned souls. Jiva Gosvami thus says that it is the foremost of all energies, since it is the purposeful essence of the combined transformations of the svarupa-sakti.**

The essential portion of the sandhinipotency is also known as suddha-sattva—the name by which the svarupa-saktiis known. It is Krsna’s existence potency and thus He and all other things, spiritual and material, directly or indirectly rest upon it.

The essence of the samvitpotency is knowledge of Krsna’s unequalled supremacy, of which all other departments of knowledge are but subsidiary components. The different branches of material knowledge are products of samvit’sshadow.

Of the combinations of these potencies, the most wonderful is a unique blend of the samvitand hladinienergies that resides in Krsna’s eternal associates, inspires them to constantly please the Lord, and is the foundation of their suddha-sattvaexistence.

It is a ray of this same suddha-sattva,comprised of hladiniand samvitthat first manifests in the heart of the accomplished practitioner as bhava.Rupa Gosvami describes this event and its effects in this verse now well-known to the reader:

*suddha-sattva-visesatma*  
*prema-surysamsu-samya-bhak*  
*rucibhis citta-masrnya-*  
*krd asau bhava ucyate*

**“That part of bhaktiis called bhava,whose essence is samvitand hladini-sakti,which is one ray of the sun of premawhich will soon rise in the heart, and which softens the heart with desires to meet, serve, and exchange love with the Lord.”**

As the sadhakacontinues with the devotional activities like chanting and hearing—activities saturated with and a consequence of bbava—ecstasy matures, deepens, and in time enters the realm of full-fledged prema.

In this way the divine energies of Krsna work to re-awaken in conditioned souls their long forgotten love and devotion for Krsna.

## Appendix Three

**Variance in Counting Material Elements**

*(This appendix follows from the study on the material elements as discussed in Part Three, Chapter Eleven)*

The material elements are counted in different ways in different Vedic texts. In Srimad Bhagavatam \[3.26.15\] Lord Kapila counts twenty-five, while also in Srimad-Bhagavatam \[11.19.141 Krsna tells Uddhava that He approves of the knowledge that counts twenty-eight. Later, \[in 11.22.1-3\] Uddhava requests the Lord to clarify how many elements of creation there are, for the very reason that different sages appear to say different things. Krsna then directly answers this enquiry. In short, the Lord explains that because different teachers group the twenty-eight elements differently, there appears to be a divergence in their views, however in the ultimate issue—in the number of elements they group—there is agreement. The exchange between the Lord and His devotee is reproduced here, based on Srimad-Bhagavatam11.22.1-3, 19-25:

**Uddhava enquired, “My dear Lord, Î master of the universe, how many different elements of creation have been enumerated by the great sages? I have heard You personally describe a total of twenty-eight—God, the jivasoul, the mahat-tattva,false ego, the five gross elements, the ten senses, the mind, the five subtle objects of perception, and the three modes of nature. But some authorities say that there are twenty-six elements, while others cite twenty-five or else seven, nine, six, four, or eleven, and even others say that there are seventeen, sixteen, or thirteen. What did each of these sages have in mind when he calculated the creative elements in such different ways? O supreme eternal, kindly explain this to me.”**

After explaining how He counts the twenty-eight material elements, Lord Krsna then comprehensively answers Uddhava’s question:

**“According to some philosophers there are seven elements, namely earth, water, fire, air, and ether, along with the conscious spirit soul and the Supreme Soul, who is the basis of both the material elements and the ordinary spirit soul. According to this theory, the body, senses, life air, and all material phenomena are produced from these seven elements.**

**“Other philosophers state that there are six elements— the five physical elements (earth, water, fire, air, and ether) and the sixth element, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. That Supreme Lord, endowed with the elements that He has brought forth from Himself, creates this universe and then personally enters within it.**

**“Some philosophers propose the existence of four basic elements, of which three—fire, water, and earth—emanate from the fourth, the Self. Once existing, these elements produce the cosmic manifestation, in which all material creation takes place.**

**“Some calculate the existence of seventeen basic elements, namely the five gross elements, the five objects of perception, the five sensory organs, the mind, and the soul as the seventeenth element.**

**“According to the calculation of sixteen elements, the only difference from the previous theory is that the soul is identified with the mind. If we think in terms of five physical elements, five senses, the mind, the individual soul, and the Supreme Lord, there are thirteen elements.**

**“Counting eleven, there are the soul, the gross elements, and the senses. Eight gross and subtle elements plus the Supreme Lord would make nine.”**

The Lord then concludes:

*iti nana-prasankhyanam*  
*tattvanam rsibhih krtam*  
*sarvam nyayyam yuktimattvad*  
*vidusam kim asobhanam*

**“Thus great philosophers have analysed the material elements in many different ways. All of their proposals are reasonable, since they are all presented with ample logic. Indeed, such philosophical brilliance is expected of the truly learned.”**

In summary: Vedic texts and even Srimad-Bhagavatamcount the material elements differently, as a result of which there are different opinions on the number of material elements. Krsna says that differing results will depend on how different sages define, contextualise, and group elements. And provided that such categorisation is comprehensive, these differing counting systems and their results are acceptable to Him.

## Appendix Four

**Nityananda Dasa’s Spiritual Stature Ascertained**

*(This appendix follows from the study on determining one’s stage ofdevotion as discussed in Part Four, Chapter Eighteen)*

The following is the full excerpt from Jaiva-dharma,Chapter Eight, that describes how devotees ascertained Nityananda Dasa’s spiritual status:

Young Nityananda Dasa asked, “Saintly BabajI! What kind of Vaisnava am I? Am I a neophyte Vaisnava or an intermediate Vaisnava? An advanced Vaisnava I certainly am not.”

Saintly Hari Dasa BabajI smiled and said, “Can a person who accepts the name Nityananda Dasa not be an advanced Vaisnava? Our Nityananda is very merciful. Even when He is beaten, He gives love in return. How can words properly glorify a person who chants Lord Nityananda’s name and becomes His servant.”

Nityananda Dasa asked, “I would like to know truthfully what my position is?”

Hari Dasa replied, “Son! Tell me all about yourself. If Lord Nityananda gives me the power to answer your enquiry, then I will tell you.”

Nityananda Dasa then said, “I was born in a lowly family in a village on the bank of the Padmavati. I was married at a young age but bever acquired bad habits. And when my wife died, thoughts of renunciation came to my mind. I thought of giving up the world.

“In my village, Baragaci, I saw many Vaisnavas who had renounced family life, and people were all respectful to them. I too desired to be honoured like that, and inspired by the temporary feeling of renunciation brought by my wife's death, I accepted the garments of a Vaisnava renunciant.

“After some days wickedness came into my mind. A Vaisnava friend of mine who now stays in Vraja was a very good person, and with his association and advice he kept my mind pure. As a result my mind no longer wants to leave the path of saints and instead it prefers to chant a hundred thousand holy names every day.

“I understand that the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Sri Krsna, and His holy name are not different. Both are perfectly spiritual. I observe Ekadasi according to scriptural injunctions, and I water Tulasi-devi every day. When the Vaisnavas sing the holy names together, I join in their sankirtana,and I drink the nectar water that has washed devotees’ feet.

“I read Sri Caitanya-mangala.I do not desire opulent food and clothing, nor do I like to hear gossip. When I see how the Vaisnavas are filled with ecstatic love, I also become ecstatic and I roll in the dust that has touched their feet.

“Yet! In spite of all this, to a certain extent I still desire fame. Now please tell me, to what class of Vaisnava do I belong? And knowing that how should I behave?”

Showing a little smile, Hari Dasa Babaji said to Vaisnava Dasa, “Please give your opinion on what class of Vaisnava Nityananda Dasa belongs to.”

Vaisnava Dasa replied, “From what I have heard, he has left the neophyte stage and became an intermediate devotee.”

Hari Dasa nodded, “I also think that.”

Overjoyed, Nityananda Dasa clapped, “Wonderful! From the mouth of a great soul I now know my true position. Please give your mercy to me so I may gradually become an advanced devotee.”

Hari Dasa commented further, “When you first accepted the garments of a sannyasi,you desired material fame. That inappropriate desire meant that you were still fallen. In spite of that, the mercy of the Vaisnavas brought auspiciousness to you.”

Nityananda Dasa admitted, “I still have a slight desire for fame. In my mind I think, ‘Bewildered by the tears in my eyes and many other symptoms of ecstatic love, people will worship me.’”

Hari Dasa advised, “You must struggle to renounce those thoughts. Do not keep them, for if you do, the danger remains that they will diminish your devotional service. If you allow the desire lor fame to compromise your devotion, you will again become a neophyte devotee.

“Even after lust, anger, and other vices have left, the desire for lame may stubbornly stay with a Vaisnava. It does not easily go away. A single drop of sincere love for the Lord is better than an elaborate ocean of pretense of love.”

Touching the dust of Hari Dasa Babaji’s feet, Nityananda Dasa Babaji begged, “Please have mercy on me.”

Hari Dasa at once embraced him and made him sit down. How wonderful is the result attained by a Vaisnava’s touch! Tears streamed from Nityananda’s Dasa’s eyes.

Taking a blade of grass between his teeth, he said, “I am very fallen and lowly. I am very fallen.”

Hari Dasa Babaji again embraced him and wept. How wonderful it all was! Nityananda Dasa had attained the true goal of life. After a short time, when all the symptoms of ecstatic love had subsided, in his heart Nityananda Dasa accepted Sri Hari Dasa as his spiritual master.

## Appendix Five

**Sri Upadesamrta 8**

*(This appendix follows from the study of the divisions of sadhana and smarana as discussed in Part Six, Chapter Twenty-six)*

This appendix gives in full the verse and purport to The Nectar of Instruction,verse eight. Since this verse is repeatedly referred to in Sankalpa-kaumudi,readers may find it helpful to read Srila Prabhupada’s commentary in its entirety.

*tan-nama-rupa-caritadi-sukirtananu-*  
*smrtyoh kramena rasana-manasi niyojya*  
*tisthan vraje tad-anuragi jananugami*  
*kalam nayed akhilam ity upadesa-saram*

*tat*—of Lord Krsna; *nama*—the holy name; *rupa*—form; *carita- adi*—character, pastimes, and so on; *su-kirtana*—in discussing or chanting nicely; *anusmrtyoh*—and in remembering; *kramena*— gradually; *rasana*—the tongue; *manasi*—and one’s mind; *niyojya*— engaging; *tisthan*—residing; *vraje*—in Vraja; *tat*—to Lord Krsna; *anuragi*—attached; *jana*—persons; *anugami*—following; *kalam*— time; *nayet*—should utilise; *akhilam*—full; *iti*—thus; *upadesa*—of advice or instruction; *saram*—the essence.

**Translation:**

The essence of all advice is that one should utilise one’s full time— twenty-four hours a day—in nicely chanting and remembering the Lord’s divine name, transcendental form, qualities, and eternal pastimes, thereby gradually engaging one’s tongue and mind. In this way one should reside in Vraja \[Goloka Vrndavana-dhama\] and serve Krsna under the guidance of devotees. One should follow in the footsteps of the Lord’s beloved devotees, who are deeply attached to His devotional service.

**Purport**

Since the mind may be one’s enemy or one’s friend, one has to train the mind to become his friend. The Krsna consciousness movement is especially meant for training the mind to be always engaged in Krsna’s business. The mind contains hundreds and thousands of impressions, not only of this life but also of many, many lives of the past. These impressions sometimes come in contact with one another and produce contradictory pictures. In this way the mind's function can become dangerous for a conditioned soul. Students of psychology are aware of the mind’s various psychological changes. In Bhagavad-gita(8.6) it is said:

*yam yam vapi smaran bhavam*  
*tyajaty ante kalevaram*  
*tarn tam evaiti kaunteya*  
*sada tad-bhava-bhavitah*

**“Whatever state of being one remembers when he quits his body, that state he will attain without fail.”**

At the time of death, the mind and intelligence of a living entity create the subtle form of a certain type of body for the next life. If the mind suddenly thinks of something not very congenial, one has to take a corresponding birth in the next life. On the other hand, if one can think of Krsna at the time of death, he can be transferred to the spiritual world, Goloka Vrndavana. This process of transmigration is very subtle; therefore Srila Rupa Gosvami advises devotees to train their minds in order that they will be unable to remember anything other than Krsna. Similarly, the tongue should be trained to speak only of Krsna and to taste only krsna-prasada. Srila Rupa Gosvami further advises, tisthan vraje:one should live in Vrndavana or any part of Vrajabhumi. Vrajabhumi, or the land of Vrndavana, is supposed to be eighty-four krosasin area. One krosaequals two square miles. When one makes Vrndavana his residence, he should take shelter of an advanced devotee there. In this way one should always think of Krsna and His pastimes. This is further elucidated by Srila Rupa Gosvami in his Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu(1.2.294):

*krsnam smaran janam casya*  
*prestham nija-samihitam*  
*tat-tat-katha-ratas casau*  
*kuryad vasam vraje sada*

**“A devotee should always reside in the transcendental realm of Vraja and always engage in krsnam smaran janam casya prestham,the remembrance of Sri Krsna and His beloved associates. By following in the footsteps of such associates and by entering under their eternal guidance, one can acquire an intense desire to serve the Supreme Personality of Godhead.”**

Again Srila Rupa Gosvami states in Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu (1.2.295):

*seva sadhaka-rupena*  
*siddha-rupena catra hi*  
*tad-bhava-lipsuna karya*  
*vraja-lokanusaratah*

**“In the transcendental realm of Vraja \[Vraja-dhama\] one should serve the Supreme Lord, Sri Krsna, with a feeling similar to that of His associates, and one should place himself under the direct guidance of a particular associate of Krsna and should follow in his footsteps. This method is applicable both in the stage of sadhana \[spiritual practices executed while in the stage of bondage\] and in the stage of sadhya\[God realisation\], when one is a siddha-purusa,or a spiritually perfect soul.”**

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura has commented as follows upon this verse:

“One who has not yet developed interest in Krsna consciousness should give up all material motives and train his mind by following the progressive regulative principles, namely chanting and remem bering Krsna and His name, form, quality, pastimes, and so forth In this way, after developing a taste for such things, one should try to live in Vrndavana and pass his time constantly remembering Krsna’s name, fame, pastimes, and qualities under the direction and protection of an expert devotee. This is the sum and substance of all instruction regarding the cultivation of devotional service.

“In the neophyte stage one should always engage in hearing krsna-katha.This is called sravana-dasa,the stage of hearing. Ây constantly hearing the transcendental holy name of Krsna and hearing of His transcendental form, qualities, and pastimes, one can attain to the stage of acceptance called varana-dasa.When one attains this stage, he becomes attached to the hearing of krsna-katha.When one is able to chant in ecstasy, he attains the stage of smaranavastha,the stage of remembering. Recollection, absorption, meditation, constant remembrance, and trance are the five items of progressive krsna-smarana.At first, remembrance of Krsna may be interrupted at intervals, but later, remembrance proceeds uninterrupted. When remembrance is uninterrupted, it becomes concentrated and is called meditation. When meditation expands and becomes constant, it is called anusmrti.By uninterrupted and unceasing anusmrtione enters the stage of samadhi, or spiritual trance. After smarana-dasaor samadhihas fully developed, the soul comes to understand his original constitutional position. At that time he can perfectly and clearly understand his eternal relationship with Krsna. That is called sampatti-dasa,the perfection of life.

“Caitanya-caritamrtaadvises those who are neophytes to give up all kinds of motivated desires and simply engage in the regulative devotional service of the Lord according to the directions of scripture. In this way a neophyte can gradually develop attachment for Krsna’s name, fame, form, qualities, and so forth. When one has developed such attachment, he can spontaneously serve the lotus feet of Krsna even without following the regulative principles. This stage is called raga-bhakti,or devotional service in spontaneous love. At that stage the devotee can follow in the footsteps of one of the eternal associates of Krsna in Vrndavana. This is called raganuga-bhakti. Raganuga-bhakti,or spontaneous devotional service, can be executed in the santa-rasawhen one aspires to be like Krsna’s cows or the stick or flute in the hand of Krsna, or the flowers around Krsna’s neck. In the dasya-rasaone follows in the footsteps of servants like Citraka, Patraka or Raktaka. In the friendly sakhya-rasaone can become a friend like Baladeva, Sridama, or Sudama. In the vatsalya-rasa,characterised by parental affection, one can become like Nanda Maharaja and Yasoda, and in the madhurya-rasa,characterised by conjugal love, one can become like Srimati Radharani or Her lady friends, such as Lalita and Her serving maids (manjaris)like Rupa and Rati. This is the essence of all instruction in the matter of devotional service.”

## Appendix Six

**Krsna Reveals Himself**

*(This appendix follows from the study of qualification for mercy as discussed in Part Six, Chapter Twenty-nine)*

The following four verses of the Bhagavad-gita\[10.8-11\] are known as its essence. In them Krsna reassures the sadhakathat pure efforts to know Him are rewarded. He facilitates a devotee’s efforts at remembering Him, gradually reveals a devotee’s identity, and ultimately, at the stage nearing prema,appears in person. This understanding is elaborately explained in the Sarartha-varsini-tika commentary of Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura, which is presented here in full. In the commentary, the acarya’sphrase-by-phrase explanations are followed in parentheses by the Sanskrit words of the verse.

\[10.8\]

*aham sarvasya prabhavo*  
*mattah sarvam pravartate*  
*iti matva bhajante mam*  
*budha bhava-samanvitah*

**“I am the source of all spiritual and material worlds. Everything emanates from Me. The wise who perfectly know this engage in My devotional service and worship Me with all their hearts.”**

**Commentary:**

Here, Krsna speaks of His vibhutti,which is characterised primarily by His unlimited power. He says,

**“I am the cause of the existence and manifestation of everything material and spiritual \[prabhavah\].Because of Me alone \[mattah\], in the form of Paramatma, the whole material world functions \[pravartate\]. Because of Me alone \[mattah\|, in the form of avataras like Narada Muni, are made possible all the spiritual sadhanas such as bhakti, jnana, tapas,and karma,as well as the goals îf these sadhanas \[sarvam pravartate\].”**

Krsna then describes the yogaknown as ananya-bhakti.

“Having faith and conviction in this knowledge \[iti matva\], the intelligent persons endowed with bhavaworship Me in their preferred moods such as dasya, sakhya,and so on \[bhava-samanvitah\].”

In this way this verse explains the vibhutiand yogamentioned in the preceding verse \[10.7\].

*\[10.9\]*

*mac-citta mad-gata-prana*  
*bodhayantah parasparam*  
*kathayantas ca mam nityam*  
*tusyanti ca ramanti ca*

“The thoughts of My pure devotees dwell in Me, their lives are fully devoted to My service, and they derive great satisfaction and bliss always enlightening one another and conversing about Me.”

**Commentary:**

The Lord continues, “As I have mentioned previously, ananya- bhaktaswho have attained spiritual intelligence \[buddhi-yoga\] by My mercy, also gain factual knowledge of Me. How this takes place is mysterious and difficult to understand.

“Their minds are greedy to remember the sweetness of My form, name, qualities, and pastimes \[ḍṁṣ-cittah\].Such devotees are unable to maintain their lives without Me \[mad-gata-pranah\], just as they are unable to live without food \[anna-gata-prana-nara\].In friendly exchanges they share realisations about the various types of bhakti and the characteristics of those devotions \[bodhayantah\]. They speak of Me as a great ocean of sweet forms, qualities, and pastimes \[kathayantah\],and glorify Me with narrations of these attributes.” Since smarana\[mac-cittah\], sravana\[bodhayantah\], and kirtana \[kathayantah\]are the primary limbs of bhakti,they have been specifically mentioned here. Thus, by ananya-bhaktialone devotees are satisfied and experience happiness. This has been a description of their internal experience.

Another meaning of “satisfaction and enjoyment” is gleaned from the perspective of spontaneous devotion. Well aware of the good fortune that enables them to serve Krsna, even practising devotees are satisfied \[tusyanti\].Moreover, as they relish constant remembrance of Krsna, devotees take great pleasure \[ramanti\]in the reassurance that in the future they will be blessed with prema.

*\[10.10\]*

*tesam satata-yuktanam*  
*bhajatam priti-purvakam*  
*dadami buddhi-yogam tam*  
*yena mam upayanti te*

**“To those who are constantly devoted to serving me with love I give the understanding by which they can come to Me.”**

\[Bhanu Swami’s translation:\] “In the hearts of those who constantly desire to be with Me and who worship Me with love, I appear to bestow My direct association.”

**Commentary:**

It may be asked, “It is understood that devotees’ joy as described in the previous verse is spiritual bliss beyond the modes of nature. But by which method do the devotees gain direct contact with You? Who gives them the method of realising You?”

Anticipating such a question, the Lord speaks this verse.

“I give buddhi-yoga \[bhakti\]to those who are constantly desirous of association with Me \[satata-yuktanam\].”

This means the Lord alone causes buddhi-yoga\[bhakti-yoga\].

“I alone appear within the functions of their minds. This buddhi-yoga cannot be obtained from any other source and it does not appear on its own. In other words, realisation of Me is given by Me alone and received only by the devotee. Through the agency of their pure devotion, My worshippers come near—they gain My direct association \[upayanti\]."

*\[10.11\]*

*tesam evanukampartham*  
*aham ajnana-jam tamah*  
*nasayamy atma-bhava-stho*  
*jnana-dipena bhasvata*

**“To show them special mercy, I, dwelling in their hearts \[in their meditations\], destroy with the shining lamp of knowledge the dark ness born of ignorance.”**

**Commentary:**

It may be asked, “Without transcendental knowledge and other assets, how can devotees even strive after, what to speak of attain, You?” Krsna replies, “Those things are not necessary. Devotees do not need to concern themselves whether they will get My mercy. It is my intention and priority that they receive it. I initiate the effort to avail them of My mercy \[tesam eva anukampartham\]. Situated within the function of their intellects \[atma-bhava-sthah\] I, with the lamp of transcendental knowledge born of bhakti,destroy all darkness produced by ignorance. This knowledge is not the sattvikaknowledge in others like the yogis.It is My internal potency. In short, I alone \[aham eva\]do everything, on My own. Why then should devotees be concerned or strive for this end when I have already said that I take the responsibility to supply all their material and spiritual needs?”

These famous four verses that have been narrated are the essence of all topics in the Gita.They remove all misery and produce complete joy for the jivas.

**“Let Krsna tightly embrace this maidservant who has fallen at His lotus feet, or let Him trample Me or break My heart by never being visible to Me. He is a debauchee, after all, and can do whatever He likes, but still He alone, and no one else, is the worshipable Lord of My heart.”**

## About the Author

Sivarama Swami was born in Budapest, Hungary in 1949, and his family emigrated to Canada during the failed 1956 Hungarian revolution. In 1973 he became a disciple of A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada, the Founder-Acaryaof iskcon, and entered the renounced order of life (sannyasa) in 1979. Sivarama Swami is well known for his deep knowledge of Vaisnava literature and has written many books on Gaudiya Vaisnavism, including the “Krsna in Vrndavana” series and more recently, Nava-vraja-mahima,a nine-volume treatise on the glories of Sri Vrndavana-dhama and its replica in Hungary, New Vraja-dhama through the Vaisnava perspective of pastime, pilgrimage, and philosophy. He served for over three decades as a member of iskcon’s Governing Body Commission and is responsible for projects in Hungary, Turkey, and Romania. He has spent his life travelling and speaking internationally, but now divides his time as much as possible between New Vraja-dhama (Krishna Valley), a replica of Vrndavana and self-sufficient farming project in Hungary’s countryside, and Mayapur, iskcon’s headquarters on the banks of the sacred Ganges River in West Bengal.

## Sanskrit Pronunciation Guide

The system of transliteration used in this book conforms to a system that scholars have accepted to indicate the pronunciation of each sound in the Sanskrit language.

The short vowel a is pronounced like the u in but, long a like the a in far, and short i like the i in pin. Long I is pronounced as in pique, short u as in pull, and long u as in rule. The vowel r is pronounced like the ri in rim. The vowel e is pronounced as in they, ai as in aisle, î as in go, and au as in how. The anusvara (m), which is a pure nasal, is pronounced like the n in the French word bon, and visarga (h), which is a strong aspirate, is pronounced as a final h sound.

The guttural consonants—k, kh, g, gh, and n—are pronounced from the throat in much the same manner as in English. Ê is pronounced as in kite, kh as in Eckhart, g as in give, gh as in dig-hard, and n as in sing. The palatal consonants — c, ch, j, jh, and n—are pronounced from the palate with the middle of the tongue. C is pronounced as in chair, ch as in staunch-heart, j as in joy, jh as in hedgehog, and n as in canyon. The cerebral consonants—t, th, d, dh, and n—are pronounced with the tip of the tongue turned up and drawn back against the dome of the palate. T is pronounced as in tub, th as in light-heart, d as in dove, dh as in red-hot, and n as in nut. The dental consonants—t, th, d, dh, and n—are pronounced in the same manner as the cerebrals but with the forepart of the longue against the teeth. The labial consonants—p, ph, b, bh, and m—are pronounced with the lips. P is pronounced as in pine, ph as in uphill, b as in bird, bh as in rub-hard, and m as in mother. The semivowels—ó, r, l, and v—are pronounced as in yes, run, light, and vine respectively. The sibilants—s, s, and s — are pronounced, respectively, as in the German word sprechen and the English words shine and sun. The letter h is pronounced as in home.

Sankalpa-kaumudi

**A Moonbeam on Determination**

by Sivarama Swami

Inspired by Srila Sanatana Gosvami’s Brhad-bhagavatamrtaand the tireless effort of its central character, Gopa-kumara, to perfect his devotional service, Sankalpa-kaumudi,“A Moonbeam on Determination,” casts a unique light on four aspects of sadhana-bhaktithat arise from the pages of Brhad-bhagavatamrta: Sankalpa,the determination that enables progress through the stages of devotional service; ekagrata,the careful attention needed for each successful Sankalpa; bhava-seva,the underlying mood of a Sankalpacorresponding to the mood of vraja-bhakti;and krpa,the divine grace by which practice finally transforms to ecstasy. Sankalpa-kaumudiis an attempt to elaborate on these four themes.

Extracting the philosophical essence from the writings of Srila Prabhupada and the previous acaryas,Sivarama Swami brings together their teachings with a unique analysis of bhaktiin a most practical and digestible style that everyone—from aspiring sadhakasto pure devotees—will find inspiring, revealing, and life-changing.

Based on the commentaries of Rupa Gosvami, Sanatana Gosvami,

Jiva Gosvami, Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura, Bhaktivinoda Thakura, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura, and Srila A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada.
